docs.title: replay_data
docs.text:
Recordings for the replay-to-sim workflow (RFC-0006 part 8): one camera's video plus whatever the source knows.

A Recording is the common input of every replay step: RGB frames and times, and when the source has them depth, intrinsics, the camera pose, the robot's joint positions, TCP poses (hylo.core.robot convention: +x approach, +y closing axis, origin between the pads) and gripper opening (1 open, 0 closed), the task text, and for our own simulated episodes ground truth (object poses and sizes, segmentation, success) used only for evaluation.

Sources (load_source): DIR a saved recording (DIR/recording.npz + DIR/recording.json) panda:TASK:SEED record an episode now: mujoco.panda_table with its privileged oracle, RGB-D camera on hf:REPO:EPISODE one episode of a LeRobot dataset on Hugging Face (fetched by replay_fetch.py in its own uv environment), converted with a profile: libero, droid or video (camera images only) FILE.mp4 | FRAME_DIR a video (e.g. a human hand demonstration); the hand becomes a parallel gripper later

Profiles say how a dataset's state maps to the robot: LIBERO (robosuite Panda: eef position, axis-angle, two finger positions; world frame with the robot base at about (-0.66, 0, 0.912)), DROID (Franka: end-effector position and XYZ Euler angles in the robot base frame, gripper position 0 open .. 1 closed).

docs.title: replay_geom
docs.text:
Geometry, checks, video and the simulation client of replay-to-sim (RFC-0006 part 8), all without MuJoCo.

MuJoCo runs in the isolated worker replay_sim.py (uv run --script, like the hylo-tools and motion workers), so it never enters the agent's process. SimClient writes the objects' meshes, sends one request per call (build the scene, kinematic replay, physics replay) and reads the arrays back. Here: meshes (OBJ I/O, convex hulls, boxes, extrusion to the table), pose and size errors, event checks of the simulation, final-state success and the side-by-side video.

docs.text:
The perception and rendering tools the replay workflow calls, behind one small interface.

RealTools runs the hylo-tools workers (each in its own uv environment, on the CPU): segment (SAM 3), depth (MoGe-2, a persistent worker for whole videos), gravity (GeoCalib), mesh (SAM 3D Objects when access is granted, else depth carving), convex (CoACD + MJCF), hands (WiLoR, else MediaPipe) and render (Blender Cycles or MuJoCo offscreen). docs.title: replay_track
docs.text:
Perception for replay-to-sim (RFC-0006 part 8): lift a recording to 3D, track objects, detect contact events, register the camera to the robot and retarget a human hand to a parallel gripper.

Frames. Tracking runs in a "frame" F with +z up and the table at z = table_z: the replay world itself when the recording knows its camera pose (our episodes), otherwise the gravity-levelled camera frame (GeoCalib roll / pitch, refined by the RANSAC table normal) shifted so the table is at z = 0. register then finds the similarity (scale, yaw about +z, translation) from F to the robot's world by aligning the carried object's track with the TCP path while the gripper holds it (the constant hand-object offset is absorbed by the translation).

Tracking (per object): a model point set from the first frame's mask; per frame the mask is propagated by projecting the model at the predicted pose (a box around it), keeping pixels that match the object's colour histogram (when it is discriminative), lie above the table and near the predicted surface, and are closer to this object than to any other; the pose is refined by trimmed ICP (translation + yaw by default, or full 6-DoF). A frame whose fit fails keeps the prediction and is marked lost.

Events: closed-gripper intervals from the opening signal (hysteresis relative to the open level); grasp (with the object that moves in the interval), lift (2 cm above its rest height), release, place (at rest after the release). The same detector runs on the simulation, so recorded and simulated events compare like for like.

docs.title: research
docs.text:
Research sessions (RFC-0006 part 5): a model develops a program on development cases, then it is frozen.

The model works in one persistent namespace across episodes of the benchmark's search split (development cases). Besides the toolkit (robot, on the live episode) it has:

cases            the development cases: [{"case": i, "instruction": ...}]
reset(case=None) end the live episode, return its outcome (success, steps, reason), start `case` (default: again)
submit(source=None)  validate a program defining solve(robot) (default: the imports, functions and constants the
                 blocks defined) and run it, without the model (code.program), on a
                 fresh episode of every development case; returns each case's outcome and printed output
finish()         end the session

The submission with the most development successes (the earliest on a tie) is frozen into a sealed program artifact (provenance: the search split only) and becomes a Candidate(kind="code") whose patch sets agent.type: code.program and the artifact: from there it is an ordinary candidate (search_val, gate, held-out, approval). The model never sees anything but development cases. Budgets: turns, model tokens and cost, resets, submissions. Everything goes to the session directory:

log.jsonl            one record per turn, reset, submission and the end (images as PNG files under images/)
live/                traces of the live episodes
submissions/sub-NN/  solve.py, results.json and the traces of each submission's runs
frozen/<name>/       the sealed program artifact
summary.json         turns, usage, dev outcomes per submission, the frozen program and the candidate

docs.title: SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
SYSTEM = 'You are developing a Python program that makes a robot solve a family of tasks. You experiment on
development cases, then submit programs; the best submission is frozen and later evaluated on unseen cases of the
same family that you will never see.

{robot}

Toolkit API (`robot`, acting on the live development episode):
{api}

{rules}

Research functions (in your namespace):
- `cases`: the development cases, a list of {{"case": i, "instruction": ...}}. A live episode of one case is running.
- `reset(case=None)`: ends the live episode and returns its outcome {{"case", "success", "steps", "reason"}}, then
  starts case `case` (default: the same case again). Your variables survive resets.
- `submit(source=None)`: submits a program that defines `solve(robot)`; it is validated, then run without you on a
  fresh episode of every development case. `submit()` with no argument submits what your blocks defined at the top
  level: every import, function definition and constant assignment (the latest of each name), which must include
  `solve(robot)`. Or pass the complete program as a string. The program does not see your other variables. Defining
  `solve` does not submit it: only submit() evaluates it. Returns {{"submission", "successes", "cases", "results": [per case: success,
  steps, reason, output, error]}}. A program can call finish() to end its episode early; returning also ends it.
- `finish()`: ends the session. The submission with the most development successes is frozen.

Write general code: read the instruction from robot.status()["instruction"], measure the scene every time, and never
hard-code positions seen in one case.{skills}{demo}{parent}{guidance}'

docs.title: robot_surface
docs.text:
The robot as typed tools (RFC-0007 part 2): what the tools.llm agent calls, built on the manipulation toolkit.

Read tools look, measure and compute; they never move the robot and several may share one model reply. Act tools are action proposals: each is bound to the observation step it was decided on, recorded (agent.tool.proposal), planned and executed through the kernel and the SafetyShield, and answered with a measured receipt (agent.tool.receipt): status (refused / arrived / stopped_short / episode_ended), steps, residual TCP error, hand state, holding. A refusal that moved nothing does not count as a decision. finish ends the episode with an outcome the agent states; the task's own success check stays the verdict and is never shown.

Frames and units: world frame, metres, +z up; orientations are quaternions in (x, y, z, w) order; the TCP follows hylo.core.robot (+x approach, +y closing axis). Targets and grasp options are named handles (t1, g3) valid for the observation they came from: after the robot moves they are stale and must be measured again.

docs.title: roles
docs.text:
Role campaigns (RFC-0008 part 9): a coordinator works through a set of tasks with worker and verifier roles over a tool surface, keeps a ledger of every tool call, and admits skills only after an independent replay.

hylo roles run CAMPAIGN.yaml [--model ollama:qwen3.5:35b-a3b] [--out runs/roles/NAME]
hylo roles status OUT

A campaign file lists tasks, each a stage (a hylo.stage/v0.1 file the task starts from), a request for the worker, a goal (a check predicate) and a partition:

  dev       pending -> working -> verifying -> done        a worker session works until its check holds
                              \-> retrying -> blocked       one retry, with the failure reasons and matching skills
            after a dev task is done, its worker's successful tool calls become a proposed skill (a recipe) with the
            failure signature the task started with; a verifier (no model) replays the recipe on a fresh copy of the
            task and checks the goal, at most twice; only a passing replay promotes the skill into the library
  heldout   pending -> heldout -> done | failed            evaluated last, with the library frozen; never used to
            propose or verify skills, and never shown to a dev worker

Rules: every task runs on its own copy of its stage (the campaign's stage root), so tasks never see each other's changes; every tool call goes into ledger/<task>/<run>.jsonl (tool, argument digest, ok, error code, receipt status) and counts against the task's budget (max_tool_calls; the call that crosses it fails with campaign_budget_exceeded); the coordinator takes the pending dev task with the fewest goal atoms first. Progress is written to status.json after every transition.

docs.title: sandbox
docs.text:
A restricted namespace for model-written Python (RFC-0006: "programs are data until gated").

Every block is parsed and checked against an allow-list before it runs
  • imports: only math and numpy (and numpy.linalg / random / fft)
  • no names or attributes that start with an underscore (no dunders, no private toolkit state)
  • no open / exec / eval / compile / globals / getattr / ... (they are not in the builtins either)
  • no frame, generator or code-object internals, no numpy file I/O
  • no class definitions, no async code

Builtins are a small allow-list; print writes to a buffer the agent returns to the model. The namespace persists between blocks (one per episode or research session). Each block has a wall-clock limit that excludes the time the robot spends executing (paused(), used around Executor.run): on expiry an exception is raised inside the running thread (CPython async exception), so a busy loop stops; a call stuck inside C code stops when it returns.

This is a guard against mistakes and casual escapes by a model, not an OS-level jail: run untrusted models in a container as well. Memory use is not limited.

docs.title: scene_check
docs.text:
The scene checker (RFC-0006 part 8): is a hylo.scene/v0.1 file a fair task for the robot?

report = check_scene("scene.json")           # env "mujoco.panda_scene", seeds (0, 1)
report.ok, [p.message for p in report.problems]

Checks, in order (later ones need the earlier ones to pass):

  1. schema the file parses and validates against hylo.core.scene.Scene
  2. static names and labels unique, references resolve, no attachment cycles, the predicate can hold at all (hylo.core.scene.scene_problems)
  3. physics per seed, through the Environment contract with privileged observations: the scene loads; start poses fit (no free position in a region, overlaps deeper than 3 mm); after settling 2 s nothing fell off, nothing moved more than 2 cm or tilted more than 10 degrees, joints stayed put, nothing penetrates (objects, table, robot); the success predicate is false at the start and stays false while settling
  4. reach on the settled state, with hylo-manip's IK on the env's RobotSpec: every movable object has a top-down (or side) grasp the arm reaches, with a pre-grasp 10 cm back, and fits the open hand; every jointed part is reachable at its centre and at the end of its travel; every place target (b of on / inside / above, inside regions, near points) is reachable 5 cm above its top

Problems are hylo.core.scene.Problem records (code, message, objects, severity); warnings do not fail a scene.

docs.title: scene_free
docs.text:
Free-form scene building (RFC-0006 part 8, free mode): task text -> a scene program -> checked -> solved.

hylo scene build --free "lift the cable by both ends" --out runs/scenes_free/cable [--model SPEC] [--attempts 6]
hylo scene check runs/scenes_free/cable            (a directory with scene.py, or the .py itself)
hylo scene solve runs/scenes_free/cable [--model SPEC] [--turns 30]

The fixed format (hylo.scene/v0.1, scenes.py) describes a scene as data: primitives on a Panda's table and a predicate from a small language. Free mode lets the model write the task as a Python program instead (hylo.freescene/v0.1, run by the env mujoco.free_scene): it chooses the robot (Panda, the two ALOHA arms or the G1 humanoid), builds the world with MuJoCo's model editor or MJCF (cables, cloth, tendons, equality constraints, hinged and sliding parts: anything MuJoCo compiles, except actuators and keyframes), and writes success(sim) over the simulation state. Optional demo(sim) proves the task can be done with invisible hands; the checker runs it.

build: the code agents' turn loop (turns.CodeLoop) with a scene-program runner in place of the robot sandbox. Each turn the model replies with one ```python block holding the whole program; the runner validates it with a wider allow-list than robot programs (scene programs may import mujoco and use the model editor; still no files, no underscores, no exec), saves it, and runs the free checker (scene_free_check.py) under a time limit. The checker's numbered problems are what the model reads next, until the program passes or the attempt budget is spent. Writes DIR/scene.py (the last attempt), DIR/attempts/NN.py and DIR/build.json (per attempt: problems, tokens, latency).

solve: code.llm on mujoco.free_scene with privileged state: PrivilegedFreeTools adds robot.scene() (rigid bodies, cable nodes, flex vertices, joint values and sites from the simulator), robot.points(name), robot.top_down(xyz) and robot.scene_table(). Two-arm robots use the toolkit's multi-arm verbs (arm=..., robot.run({arm: plan}, sync=True)). Writes DIR/solve/trace, DIR/solve/turns.jsonl, DIR/solve.json and DIR/front.mp4, like the fixed-format solve (scene_episode.run_recorded_episode). agent= runs another agent instead, e.g. code.program with a scripted solution (written to DIR/.json and DIR/.mp4).

Modules: scene_free_check (the program allow-list and the checker), scene_free_prompt (what the model is told), scene_free_tools (the privileged toolkit); this file only orchestrates.

docs.title: scene_free_check
docs.text:
The checker for free-form scene programs (hylo.freescene/v0.1, env mujoco.free_scene).

report = check_free_scene("runs/scenes_free/cable/scene.py")
report.ok, report.text()

A free scene has no schema to validate against and no predicate language to reason about, so the checks are behavioural: build it, run it, and try to satisfy it. Stages, in order (later ones need the earlier ones to pass):

  1. program the source passes the scene-program allow-list (validate_scene_program, below) and defines ROBOT, INSTRUCTION, build(scene) and success(sim)
  2. load the environment builds the scene with the robot and compiles it (build errors, MuJoCo compiler errors, actuators or keyframes added, randomize errors come back with the program's own lines)
  3. physics per seed: no deep start overlaps (scene-scene, scene-table, scene-robot at its home posture); 2 s of doing nothing: the simulation does not diverge, nothing falls off the table, rigid bodies stay within 2 cm and 10 degrees, cable nodes and cloth vertices within 5 cm, joints stay put, and nothing is still moving at the end; success(sim) runs, returns a bool, is False at the start and stays False
  4. reach on the settled state, with hylo-manip's IK on the robot's RobotSpec: every movable thing (free body, cable, cloth, hinged or sliding part) has a point some arm reaches with a top-down or side approach and a pre-pose 8 cm back, and so does every point the program's targets(sim) names
  5. satisfiable demo(sim) runs with invisible hands (physics only, the robot holds still) and success(sim) becomes True during it or after the hands let go; every point a hand grabbed is reachable by an arm. Without a demo the stage is a warning ("unverified")

What it cannot verify: that the success function means what the instruction says (a demo that satisfies a wrong function passes), that a real gripper (rather than an invisible hand) can hold a thin cable or a cloth corner, and that both arms can act at once where a task needs two hands at the same time (each point is checked on its own).

docs.title: SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
SYSTEM = 'You write simulation tasks for robot manipulation as Python programs. A program builds a MuJoCo world
around a robot at a table, states the task, and judges success from the simulation state. A checker loads it, lets
it settle on several seeds, checks reach and runs your demo; then a separate agent tries to do the task with the robot.

## The program (format hylo.freescene/v0.1)
Top level (plain constants and functions only):
    ROBOT = "panda" | "aloha" | "g1"        the robot that fits the task (see Robots)
    INSTRUCTION = "..."                     what the robot must do, naming each object as it looks
    MAX_STEPS = 900                         control steps at 20 Hz (100 .. 4000)
    LABELS = {{"rope": "red rope"}}           optional: words for bodies, cable prefixes and flexes
    def build(scene): ...                   required: add the world's things
    def success(sim): ...                   required: return a plain bool, False at the start
    def demo(sim): ...                      strongly recommended: do the task with invisible hands (checker only)
    def randomize(sim, rng): ...            optional: vary the start per seed (sim.set_body / set_joint)
    def targets(sim): ...                   optional: {{name: xyz}} points a robot hand must be able to reach
Imports allowed: math, numpy (as np), mujoco. No files, no classes, no names starting with "_".

build(scene):
    scene.add_mjcf(xml, pos=None)  add an MJCF document (<mujoco> with worldbody, asset, default, tendon, equality,
                                   contact, extension sections); names stay as written. Angles in this MJCF are
                                   DEGREES (the MJCF default) unless you add <compiler angle="radian"/>.
    scene.spec                     the mujoco.MjSpec being built (you may also use the model editor directly)
    scene.table_top                z of the table surface; scene.table = {{"x": (lo, hi), "y": (lo, hi), "top"}}
    scene.arms                     {{arm: {{"base": xyz, "x": (lo, hi), "y": (lo, hi)}}}}: where each arm works best
    scene.opening                  the gripper's max opening (m); scene.rgba("red") -> [r, g, b, 1]
success(sim) / randomize(sim, rng) / demo(sim) / targets(sim) read the state through sim:
    sim.pos(body) (3,)   sim.quat(body) (w,x,y,z)   sim.xmat(body) (3,3)   sim.speed(body) m/s
    sim.bounds(body) -> (min (3,), max (3,)) world box of the body and its children
    sim.joint(name) value (radians for hinges, metres for slides)   sim.joint_range(name)
    sim.nodes(prefix) (N,3) a composite cable's bodies in order (prefix+"B_first" ... prefix+"B_last")
    sim.flex(name) (N,3) flex vertices (cloth)   sim.site(name)   sim.geom(name)   sim.bodies(prefix="")
    sim.touching(a, b) contact between two things: body, cable prefix, flex name, "table", "robot" or "hand"
    sim.held(thing) touched by the robot's fingers   sim.table_top   sim.time
randomize and demo may also edit: sim.set_body(body, pos=None, quat=None) (free-joint bodies), sim.set_joint(name, v).
demo(sim) moves things with invisible hands while the physics runs (the robot stays still):
    sim.grab(body, hand=0)  hold a body at its frame origin   sim.move(hand, xyz, seconds=1.0) straight line
    sim.move_together({{0: xyz, 1: xyz}}, seconds)   sim.release(hand)   sim.wait(seconds)   sim.hand(hand) -> xyz
  success must become True during the demo or within 1 s after the hands let go. Grab only where a real gripper
  could (an end of a cable, a corner or edge of cloth, a handle, a small object): those points must be reachable.

## The world
- Metres, kilograms, +z up. Every object is a named body; a body with <freejoint/> can move freely, a body without
  joints is fixed to the world, a child body with a hinge or slide joint is an articulated part (give it a range,
  damping, and armature="0.001").
- Objects rest ON their support at the start: z = support top + half height (+0.001). Nothing may overlap anything
  else or the robot; leave 3 cm between objects.
- Put everything the robot must touch inside an arm's zone (scene.arms), and things that must be picked up at most
  scene.opening - 0.01 m wide where they are grasped, at most 0.3 kg.
- Deformables:
  * cable / rope: <composite prefix="rope" type="cable" curve="s" count="N 1 1" size="L" offset="x y z"
    initial="free"> with <plugin plugin="mujoco.elasticity.cable"> (declare <extension><plugin
    plugin="mujoco.elasticity.cable"/></extension>), <joint kind="main" damping="0.02"/> and <geom type="capsule"
    size="R" density="..."/>. It runs along +x from offset; bodies are rope+"B_first", rope+"B_1", ..., rope+"B_last".
    Use initial="free" (initial="none" fixes the first end to the world). N 15-30, R 0.008-0.012, z = top + R.
  * cloth: <flexcomp name="cloth" type="grid" count="8 8 1" spacing="0.025 0.025 0.025" pos="x y z" radius="0.004"
    dim="2" mass="0.04"> <edge equality="true" damping="0.01"/> <contact selfcollide="none" condim="3"/>
    </flexcomp>: centred at pos, flat in xy; vertex bodies cloth_0, cloth_1, ... (row by row); at most 10 x 10.
  * a gripper's fingertips keep its centre (TCP) about 1.5 cm above whatever it reaches down to, so it cannot pinch
    a thin cable or cloth lying flat on the table: give a cable radius >= 0.012, or start the part to be grasped on
    a raised support (a low block or pad, 2-4 cm) with an end or edge overhanging it.
  * also allowed: <tendon> (spatial / fixed), <equality> (connect, weld, joint), springs (stiffness / springref).
- No <actuator> and no <keyframe>: the robot is the only actor.

## Robots
{robots}

Reply with one or two sentences of plan, then the complete program in ONE ```python block.

## Example 1: "slide the green gate to the other end of the rail"
```python
{example1}
```

## Example 2: "put the end of the rope in the bowl"
```python
{example2}
```'

docs.title: EXAMPLE_1 module-attribute
docs.text:
EXAMPLE_1 = 'ROBOT = "panda"
INSTRUCTION = "slide the green gate to the other end of the rail"
MAX_STEPS = 600
LABELS = {"rail": "grey rail", "gate": "green gate"}

def build(scene):
    t = scene.table_top
    scene.add_mjcf(f"""
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="rail" pos="-0.02 0.0 {t + 0.01}">
      <geom type="box" size="0.03 0.14 0.01" rgba="0.5 0.5 0.5 1"/>
      <body name="gate" pos="0 -0.07 0.05">
        <joint name="gate_slide" type="slide" axis="0 1 0" range="0 0.12" damping="3" armature="0.001"/>
        <geom type="box" size="0.006 0.05 0.04" rgba="0.2 0.7 0.3 1" mass="0.1"/>
        <geom name="knob" type="box" size="0.012 0.012 0.012" pos="0 0 0.052" rgba="0.1 0.1 0.1 1" mass="0.01"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
  <contact><exclude body1="rail" body2="gate"/></contact>
</mujoco>""")

def success(sim):
    return bool(sim.joint("gate_slide") > 0.1)

def demo(sim):
    sim.grab("gate", hand=0)
    sim.move(0, sim.pos("gate") + np.array([0.0, 0.115, 0.0]), seconds=1.5)
    sim.release(0)

def targets(sim):
    return {"knob": sim.geom("knob")}
'

docs.text:
EXAMPLE_2 = 'ROBOT = "panda"
INSTRUCTION = "put the end of the red rope in the bowl"
MAX_STEPS = 900
LABELS = {"rope": "red rope", "bowl": "bowl", "step": "grey step"}

def build(scene):
    t = scene.table_top
    walls = "".join(
        f'<geom type="box" size="{sx} {sy} 0.025" pos="{x} {y} 0.03" rgba="0.3 0.4 0.8 1"/>'
        for x, y, sx, sy in ((0.055, 0, 0.005, 0.06), (-0.055, 0, 0.005, 0.06), (0, 0.055, 0.06, 0.005), (0, -0.055, 0.06, 0.005)))
    scene.add_mjcf(f"""
<mujoco>
  <extension><plugin plugin="mujoco.elasticity.cable"/></extension>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="bowl" pos="0.05 0.18 {t}">
      <geom type="box" size="0.06 0.06 0.005" pos="0 0 0.005" rgba="0.3 0.4 0.8 1"/>{walls}
    </body>
    <body name="step" pos="0.0 -0.2 {t + 0.015}"><geom type="box" size="0.05 0.05 0.015" rgba="0.6 0.6 0.6 1"/></body>
    <composite prefix="rope" type="cable" curve="s" count="20 1 1" size="0.38" offset="-0.33 -0.2 {t + 0.04}" initial="free">
      <plugin plugin="mujoco.elasticity.cable">
        <config key="twist" value="5e4"/><config key="bend" value="5e4"/><config key="vmax" value="0"/>
      </plugin>
      <joint kind="main" damping="0.02"/>
      <geom type="capsule" size="0.01" rgba="0.8 0.15 0.1 1" density="300" condim="4"/>
    </composite>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>""")

def success(sim):
    lo, hi = sim.bounds("bowl")
    end = sim.pos("ropeB_last")
    return bool(lo[0] < end[0] < hi[0] and lo[1] < end[1] < hi[1] and end[2] < hi[2])

def demo(sim):
    end = sim.pos("ropeB_last")
    lo, hi = sim.bounds("bowl")
    above = np.array([(lo[0] + hi[0]) / 2, hi[1] - 0.035, hi[2] + 0.06])
    sim.grab("ropeB_last", hand=0)
    sim.move(0, end + np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.1]), seconds=1.0)
    sim.move(0, above, seconds=2.0)
    sim.move(0, above - np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.09]), seconds=1.0)
    sim.release(0)
'

Example (one arm: lift the end of a cable and lay it at a point):
    s = robot.scene(); table = robot.scene_table()

    up = out["tcp"]["arm"].copy(); up[2, 3] += 0.10
    robot.run(robot.plan(robot.Goal("move", tcp=up), table))
    to = robot.top_down([0.1, 0.2, table.height + 0.05], yaw)
    robot.run(robot.plan(robot.Goal("move", tcp=to, hand=robot.spec.arms[0].hand.open), table))

FREE_TWO_ARM_EXAMPLE = '
Example (two arms: take both ends of a cable and lift them together):
    s = robot.scene(); table = robot.scene_table()
    n = s["cables"]["rope"]["nodes"]
    plans = {}
    for arm, i, j in (("left", 0, 1), ("right", -1, -2)):
        d = n[i] - n[j]; yaw = math.atan2(d[1], d[0]) + math.pi / 2
        p = n[i].copy(); p[2] = max(p[2], table.height + 0.017)
        plans[arm] = robot.plan(robot.grasp_at(robot.top_down(p, yaw), arm=arm), table)
        if plans[arm] is None: print(arm, robot.why())
    out = robot.run(plans); print(out.get("error"), out["tcp_error"])
    st = robot.status(); ups = {}
    for arm in ("left", "right"):
        t = st["tcp"][arm].copy(); t[2, 3] += 0.15
        ups[arm] = robot.plan(robot.Goal("lift", arm, tcp=t), table)
    out = robot.run(ups, sync=True)
    print(robot.scene()["cables"]["rope"]["nodes"][[0, -1]])

docs.title: scenes
docs.text:
The scene builder workflow (RFC-0006 part 8): task text -> scene file -> checked -> solved with privileged state.

hylo scene build "put the ball in the cup" --out runs/scenes/ball-cup [--model SPEC] [--attempts 6]
hylo scene solve runs/scenes/ball-cup [--model SPEC] [--turns 30] [--seed 0] [--no-video]
hylo scene check runs/scenes/ball-cup/scene.json

build: a chat model writes a hylo.scene/v0.1 file (hylo.core.scene) from the task text; the scene checker (scene_check.py: schema, static, physics, reach) answers with a numbered list of problems, which go back to the model until the scene passes or the attempt budget is spent. Writes DIR/scene.json (the last attempt), DIR/attempts/NN.json and DIR/build.json (per attempt: problems, tokens, latency; totals; built or not).

solve: code.llm on mujoco.panda_scene with the scene, with PRIVILEGED state: the env runs with privileged_obs: true (part of the env params, so of any digest) and the toolkit is PrivilegedSceneTools, which adds robot.scene() (simulator object poses, extents, joint states), robot.object_points(name) and robot.scene_table(). The trace names the toolkit and every turn's code. Writes DIR/solve/trace (the episode trace), DIR/solve/turns.jsonl, DIR/solve.json (outcome, turns, usage, wall time) and DIR/front.mp4 (front camera, when imageio-ffmpeg is installed).

Free mode (scene_free.py): hylo scene build --free TASK --out DIR has the model write a Python scene program (hylo.freescene/v0.1: any robot of panda / aloha / g1, any MuJoCo feature, its own success function) instead of a scene file; check and solve recognise a directory holding scene.py (or a .py path) and use the free checker (scene_free_check.py) and the free-scene privileged toolkit.

SPEC is a chat-model spec (JSON or shorthand, see hylo.reasoners.llm.chat); default: Ollama qwen3.5:35b-a3b. Task-agnostic: nothing here knows a task; the prompt teaches the format with two examples of its own.

docs.title: SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
SYSTEM = 'You write simulation scenes for a robot manipulation benchmark. A scene is one JSON document in the
format hylo.scene/v0.1 (its JSON Schema is below). The simulator turns it into a MuJoCo world: a Franka Panda arm
with a two-finger gripper at one end of a table, and your objects on the table. A checker loads your scene, lets it
settle, checks that the robot can reach everything and that the goal is not already met; then a separate agent
tries to solve the task with the robot.

The world
- Units: metres and kilograms; ANGLES IN DEGREES. +z is up; the table top is z = 0.
{robot}
- Keep every object the robot has to touch, and every place it has to put something, inside the area the arm
  serves best (above). Do not put objects in a straight line between the arm base and the area.
- The gripper opens {opening:.2f} m: whatever must be picked up needs a horizontal side of at most 0.06 m (blocks of
  0.04 m, balls and cylinders of radius 0.02-0.03 m), mass at most 0.3 kg.
- Typical sizes: block 0.04 m cube, 0.05 kg; ball radius 0.02 m; tray [0.14, 0.14, 0.04]; cup [0.045, 0.08].

Objects
- Every object has a unique `name` (identifier) and a unique `label`: the words the instruction uses for it.
- Give `shape` and `size`, or `parts` (primitives placed in the object's own frame) for a built thing (a cabinet).
  `tray` and `cup` are ready-made open containers: use them for a box, bin, bowl, basket or cup to put things in.
- Start pose: `pose` with pos [x, y] rests the object on the table, or on the object named in `on`. Use `region`
  (x and y ranges about 0.08-0.15 m wide, yaw range) for objects the robot moves, so every episode starts a bit
  differently. A region must leave room for the object next to everything else.
- `fixed: true` for things that must not move (cabinet, button housing, a bin fixed to the table).
- Moving parts (drawer, door, lid, button) are separate objects with `parent` (what they are attached to) and a
  `joint` (slide: metres along `axis`; hinge: degrees about `axis` through `anchor`). Their `pose.pos` is
  [x, y, z] in the parent's frame. A part does not collide with its parent: its joint range is what stops it.
  The parent of a drawer or door is usually fixed.
- Objects must not overlap at the start; leave at least 0.03 m between them.
- Make it physically what the task says: something to put things in is hollow (tray, cup, or walls and a floor
  from parts), a drawer is a hollow box on a slide joint, a sliding lid uses a slide joint, a door or flap a hinge.

Success predicate (`success`, field `op`)
- on(a, b): a rests on top of b (b may be "table"). inside(a, b): a's centre inside container b (or `region`).
  near(a, b or point, max_dist). above(a, b). upright(a, axis). lifted(a, height). row(objects, axis): in a line,
  in the listed order of increasing x or y. joint_at_least / joint_at_most(object, value or fraction of range).
  not(term). all_of(terms). any_of(terms). sequence(terms): each becomes true after the previous ones.
- Relations about an object need it at rest and released by the gripper (unless released: false).
- The predicate must be FALSE at the start. Use only object names that exist.
- The instruction names every object the robot must act on by its label.

Reply with one or two sentences of plan, then the complete scene in ONE ```json block (no comments in the JSON).

JSON Schema of the format:
{schema}

Example 1: "put the green cylinder in the tray"
```json
{example1}
```

Example 2: "press the button, then put the blue block on the yellow block"
```json
{example2}
```'

docs.title: PRIVILEGED_REFERENCE module-attribute
docs.text:
PRIVILEGED_REFERENCE = '## Privileged simulator state (this run is flagged privileged)
This run gives you the simulator's ground truth: start with robot.scene() and use its exact poses and sizes
instead of look / find / objects (perception is still there if you want to look).
robot.scene() -> dict
    {name: {"label", "shape", "pos", "quat", "yaw", "size", "extent", "bounds": (min, max), "top", "movable",
    "fixed", "parent", "joint": {"type", "value", "range", "units"}, "interior": {"centre", "half"}}}: exact object
    poses and sizes from the simulator, fresh at every call. Prefer it to perception.
robot.object_points(name, spacing=0.006) -> (N, 3) points on the object's oriented bounding box (world), usable
    wherever the toolkit takes observed object points.
robot.scene_table(height=None) -> Table: the table, or a support plane at `height` for place_at.

Example (pick an object and put it on another one):
    s = robot.scene(); table = robot.scene_table()
    pts = robot.object_points("red_block"); box = robot.box(pts, table)
    plan = robot.plan(robot.grasps("arm", pts, table), table)
    out = robot.run(plan); print(out["tcp_error"], robot.holding("arm"))
    up = out["tcp"]["arm"].copy(); up[2, 3] += 0.12
    robot.run(robot.plan(robot.Goal("lift", "arm", tcp=up), table))
    obj_in_tcp = np.linalg.inv(plan.goal.tcp) @ box.pose
    local = (pts - box.pose[:3, 3]) @ box.pose[:3, :3]
    goal = robot.place_at("arm", obj_in_tcp, local, xy=s["plate"]["pos"][:2], table=robot.scene_table(s["plate"]["top"]))
    robot.run(robot.plan(goal, table))
    retreat = robot.status()["tcp"]["arm"].copy(); retreat[2, 3] += 0.1
    robot.run(robot.plan(robot.Goal("retreat", "arm", tcp=retreat), table))
For a drawer, door or lid: grasp its handle with robot.grasp_at (a TCP pose you build from scene() numbers) and move
along the joint with robot.Goal("push", ...) (a straight line from the current TCP).'

docs.title: session
docs.text:
Tool sessions (RFC-0008 part 7): a chat model works with any registered tool surface (group hylo.surfaces) on a request, outside an episode: build a scene, run robots in it, record data.

hylo world chat "put a Go1 on the floor next to a table with a red cube and walk it 1 m forward" \
    [--stage lab] [--root runs/stages] [--model ollama:qwen3.5:35b-a3b] [--vision] [--out runs/world-chat]
hylo world chat                  (no request: read requests from the terminal, one session that remembers)
hylo world tools                 the tool manual of the surface

The loop is the one of tools.llm without an environment: every model call sends the projected conversation (tool_context) and every tool; read calls of a reply run first, then act calls in order (each tool checks its own preconditions: stage revisions, world generations); after any act the after_act read tool (the world's free view) is called so a vision model sees the result. Events go to a hash-chained trace (hylo watch OUT follows it): agent.tool.start / turn / result / operator / summary. An inbox file lets a person steer the session.

docs.title: WORLD_SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
WORLD_SYSTEM = 'You work in a 3D robotics workspace through tools: a stage (the scene as entities, edited by
patches with revisions) and a MuJoCo world built from it (robots from packs, cameras, people), which you run with
actions and check with predicates.

How to work:
- Read before you write: stage_show gives the revision stage_edit needs; world_state gives the generation every
  robot action needs. A conflict or a stale refusal means: read again, then retry.
- Edits change the stage, not the running world: call world_build after editing, then act.
- Build scenes in metres, +z up, the floor at z = 0. A box's size is its half extents. A table top at height h with
  half thickness t has its centre at z = h - t. Put objects on surfaces (centre z = surface + half height).
- Robots come from packs (packs tool): check a pack's controls before choosing actions. Arms move their tool point
  with tcp actions; grasp from above: move above the object, descend, close the gripper, lift.
- stage_edit ops is a JSON array, never a JSON-encoded string. Keep patches small (up to six operations) and use
  the revision returned by each patch for the next one. Robot fields are nested, for example an add operation:
  {"op":"add","entity":{"id":"arm","pose":{"pos":[0,0,0]},"robot":{"pack":"panda","base":"fixed"}}}.
  Shapes likewise use pose.pos and shape {type,size,rgba}; kind, pack and pos are not top-level entity fields.
  On a validation error, correct the fields named by the error; do not repeat the same invalid arguments.
- Look at the result (view or capture) and check goals with check: a receipt says what the robot did, a check says
  whether the goal holds. Report what you measured.
- Do one thing at a time and keep replies short; finish with a summary of what exists and what was verified.'

docs.title: tool_agent
docs.text:
tools.llm (RFC-0007): a chat model operates the robot through typed tools with native tool calls.

agent: {type: tools.llm, params: {model: {backend: ollama, model: qwen3.5:35b-a3b, vision: true},
        max_decisions: 40, max_calls: 150, inbox: runs/steer/inbox.jsonl}}

Each model call sends the projected conversation (tool_context) and every tool of the surface (robot_surface plus read_artifact). Read calls of one reply run in order; an act call must be alone in its reply, runs through the kernel and the SafetyShield, and the next message carries its receipt and fresh images. finish ends the episode; the task's success check stays the verdict and is never shown.

Budgets: decisions (act calls that moved or could have moved the robot; refusals that moved nothing do not count), model calls, calls without an action, tokens, cost, wall time. Replies without a tool call get a reminder; after max_idle_replies in a row the episode ends.

Steering: with inbox, a JSON-lines file a person (the Studio, hylo watch --say) appends {"message": ...} to, each new message is shown to the model before its next call as operator guidance. A run that received any is marked human_assisted in its summary event and must not be counted as autonomous.

Trace events: agent.tool.start (surface and prompt digests), agent.tool.turn (per model call: projection stats, reply, tool calls, usage), agent.tool.result (per call), agent.tool.proposal / agent.tool.receipt (per act), agent.tool.operator, agent.tool.finish, agent.tool.summary.

docs.title: tool_context
docs.text:
Context for a tool-calling model (RFC-0007 part 3): the conversation is kept whole; what is sent is a projection.

The canonical history is append-only. Before every model call ToolContext.project() builds the request:

  head       the system message and the task message, always verbatim
  tail       the last `tail_decisions` actions (an action = an act call and everything after it up to the next
             act) verbatim, images included for the last `image_decisions`
  older      tool results longer than `inline_chars` become references: {"stored": "ref:<id>", "preview": ...};
             their images become a note naming the reference; identical results are stored once
  pressure   when the estimated request exceeds `compact_tokens`, everything between the head and the tail is
             replaced by a summary the model wrote in a separate call (no tools), plus the list of references
             it covered; the exact turns stay readable through `read_artifact`

Nothing is lost: every stored item is in self.artifacts (and in the trace), and the model can open it again with read_artifact (a character range of a text, or an image). Tool calls and their results always travel together, so a projection is always a valid conversation for the provider.

docs.title: SUMMARY_PROMPT module-attribute
docs.text:
SUMMARY_PROMPT = "You are condensing your own earlier work on a robot task so you can continue with less context. Write ONE JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list of short strings:
  progress     what has been achieved so far, in task terms
  confirmed    facts established by measurement or by an action's receipt
  ruled_out    beliefs that turned out wrong
  attempts     each failed attempt as 'what failed / evidence / what to change'
  constraints  limits that still apply (reach, collisions, objects that must not move)
  avoid        calls or plans not to repeat
  next_checks  what to measure again before acting (positions go stale after motion)
Do not copy coordinates or other numbers: they are stale; re-measure instead. At most 250 words in total. Reply with the JSON object only."

docs.title: tool_prompt
docs.text:
The prompt of the tools.llm agent (RFC-0007 part 4), in named layers so a run records exactly what the model was told (bundle_digest, and one digest per layer):

  protocol     how turns work: read tools batch, one act call alone per reply, receipts, handles go stale
  evidence     how to treat what you know: seen, measured, inferred, executed, confirmed; what to do when unsure
  boundary     what the agent cannot see or decide: simulator state, the task's own success check
  embodiment   the robot, generated from its RobotSpec: arms, hands, TCP convention, frames, cameras, notes
  task         the instruction (first user message), with the opening images

docs.title: PROTOCOL module-attribute
docs.text:
PROTOCOL = 'You operate a robot through tools. You cannot see or touch anything except through them.

How a turn works:
- Read tools (look, locate, pixel_to_world, world_to_pixel, calc, grasp_options, reach_check, robot_state,
  read_artifact) only measure or compute. Call several in one reply when they do not depend on each other.
- Act tools (move_tcp, grasp, place, gripper, recover, wait) move the robot. An act call must be the ONLY call in its
  reply. It ends your turn: the next message brings its receipt (status, measured errors, holding) and new images.
- finish ends the episode. Call it when the evidence shows the task done, or when it cannot be done.
- Every reply should contain at least one tool call. Think briefly in text, then call.

Handles and staleness:
- locate returns target handles (t1, t2, ...) and grasp_options returns option handles (g3, ...). They describe the
  moment they were measured. After any motion they are stale: measure again before using positions.
- Images arrive with each observation. Earlier results and images may be stored to save context; they show the
  past. read_artifact opens one; for the present, call the tool again.

Numbers:
- Derive every number with calc (offsets, midpoints, rotations, distances). Quaternions are [x, y, z, w].
- World frame: metres, +z up. The TCP of a hand: +x is the approach direction, +y the closing direction.
'

docs.title: EVIDENCE module-attribute
docs.text:
EVIDENCE = 'Evidence rules:
1. Know how you know. A fact is seen (in an image), measured (a tool returned it), inferred (you reasoned it),
   executed (a receipt says the motion ran) or confirmed (an observation after the motion shows the effect). Only
   confirmed facts show that the task is done.
2. A receipt says what the robot did, not what happened to objects. After a grasp, holding_after_lift tells you the
   hand stopped on something; the next images and a fresh locate tell you whether the object came along.
3. When two pieces of evidence disagree, get a third: another camera, another measurement, a small diagnostic motion.
4. A failed call teaches something. Do not send the same call with the same arguments again on an unchanged scene:
   change the arguments, measure something new, or try another approach. After repeated failures of one approach,
   change the approach.
5. If you are missing something, say which tool can get it: positions (locate, pixel_to_world), whether a point is
   hidden (world_to_pixel), whether a pose is reachable (reach_check), what changed (look after acting).
6. If the instruction is ambiguous, choose the reading most consistent with the scene and say which you chose.
'

docs.title: BOUNDARY module-attribute
docs.text:
BOUNDARY = "Boundary:
- You do not have the simulator's state, object ground truth or the task's success check. The task's own check
  decides success after the episode; finish only states your view.
- Objects can move without a command (they roll, slide, fall). Something missing from one image may be hidden.
- Tools refuse unsafe or impossible motions; a refusal that moved nothing costs no decision.
- Budgets limit decisions (act calls), model calls and time. The latest message says what is left.
"

docs.title: watch
docs.text:
hylo watch: follow a tool-agent episode in the terminal, replay a finished one, or steer a running one.

hylo watch RUN_DIR [--episode ID]        print the newest episode (or ID) and keep following it while it runs
hylo watch RUN_DIR --replay [--speed 4]  replay a finished episode on its recorded timing
hylo watch RUN_DIR --raw                 the episode's agent events as JSON lines
hylo watch --say "MESSAGE" --inbox PATH  send a message to a running tools.llm agent (its `inbox`)
hylo watch RUN_DIR --inbox PATH --interactive   follow, and send every line typed to the agent (Ctrl-D stops typing)

One line per thing that happened: the model's words, each tool call with a condensed result, each action's receipt, operator messages, and the verdict, with a footer of calls, decisions, tokens and cost. Read-only, except --say.

docs.title: cli
docs.text:
hylo: the command dispatcher. Each package registers its own subcommands.

A subcommand is an entry point in the group "hylo.commands": a name and a callable taking the remaining arguments and returning an exit code. The first line of the callable's docstring is its help line.

[project.entry-points."hylo.commands"]
bench = "hylo.bench.cli:main"          # hylo bench ...  (hylo-bench)

So hylo only has the commands of what is installed: on a robot computer with hylo-core and hylo-serve, hylo serve; on a workstation with the harness, hylo run, hylo evolve, hylo learn, ...; with hylo-bench also hylo bench.

docs.title: codec
docs.text: JSON-safe encoding for numpy arrays and arbitrary payloads. No pickle anywhere (RPent's socket RPC unpickles arbitrary frames; DSPy's .pkl programs execute code on load).

docs.title: compat
docs.text:
Bind-time compatibility check between an Agent and an Environment.

Unlike vla-eval (mismatch -> logger.warning), errors here stop the run. Severity split follows inspect-robots compat.py: control mode / rotation / dimensionality are errors; frame and gripper conventions are warnings.

docs.title: contract
docs.text:
Base class and field types for data contracts.

Rules: - Data that crosses a boundary (process, file, version, plugin) is a frozen pydantic model with extra="forbid", so typos fail loudly and every contract has a JSON Schema. - Runtime objects that hold callables or live handles (EpisodeContext, SafetyContext) stay plain dataclasses; they are never serialized. - numpy arrays use NDArray; free-form payloads that may contain arrays use JsonAny. Both round-trip through JSON via core.codec, so model_dump(mode="json") / model_validate is the whole wire format. - Formats written before the rename to Hylo (2026-11-01) carry wc.<name>/v<x> schema ids and refer to worldcurrent.* modules. They are read as hylo.<name>/v<x> and hylo.* (current_schema, current_module), so recorded runs, artifacts, configs and profiles stay readable; nothing is rewritten on disk.

docs.title: MemoryEvent
docs.text:
Bases: Contract

One observed event, not one model guess or one repeated image.

Producers assign stable IDs and a total (step, order) ordering. A completed action is an observed transition, not an action request. _gap marks missing observation coverage. Evidence references identify agent-visible frames/receipts retained in the trace.

docs.title: errors
docs.text:
Error taxonomy (semantics follow inspect-robots errors.py and vla-eval EpisodeError.phase).

  • AgentError: the agent failed; the episode is marked error and not scored.
  • EnvironmentFault: the env/sim failed; infra problem, counted as infra_invalid.
  • SafetyAbort: a guard, the operator (stop, e-stop) or the realtime watchdog halted the episode. Guard and operator stops are scored as safety_abort; a watchdog abort (no new actions for max_hold_steps) is the agent's failure: error.
  • IncompatibleComponents: bind-time contract mismatch; the run never starts. The partial episode record travels on exc.record so nothing collected so far is lost.

docs.title: wire
docs.text:
msgpack-numpy wire format (the one openpi uses), shared by the policy server (hylo-serve) and the openpi client.

msgpack frames in which numpy arrays are maps {b"ndarray": True, b"data": raw bytes, b"dtype": dtype.str, b"shape": shape} (and numpy scalars {b"npgeneric": True, b"data": item, b"dtype": dtype.str}). Written from the format, not copied; like openpi and core.codec it never falls back to pickle, so object / void dtypes are refused.

docs.title: workcell
docs.text:
Workcell API (hylo.workcell/v0.1): what a workcell serves and a control plane calls.

A workcell (hylo-serve) runs next to a robot or simulator and executes episodes with a remote policy. A control plane (the playground in hylo-studio) starts episodes and relays operator input. Both sides use the models here, so neither imports the other.

GET  /healthz                                  liveness, no auth
GET  /status                                   the workcell's state (dict; see WORKCELL_STATES)
POST /episodes   StartEpisode  -> EpisodeStarted     409 while an episode runs or a fault is latched
POST /operator   OperatorEvent -> OperatorAck        400 for an unknown or malformed event
WS   /events                                   the live event stream: one JSON event per message

Auth, when the workcell has a token: Authorization: Bearer <token> on HTTP, ?token=<token> on the WebSocket.

docs.title: ws
docs.text:
WebSocket transport for the EnvServer / AgentServer protocols: run a simulator or a policy on another machine, container or GPU box, with the same JSON messages as the stdio transport (handlers.py).

# serve (in the component's own venv; binds localhost unless --host is given)
python -m hylo.core.remote.ws env  libero --params '{"image_size": 256}' --port 8765
python -m hylo.core.remote.ws agent lerobot --params '{...}' --port 8766 --token-env HYLO_TOKEN

# use from any experiment config
env:   {type: remote.ws, params: {url: "ws://gpu-box:8765"}}
agent: {type: remote.ws, params: {url: "ws://gpu-box:8766", token_env: HYLO_TOKEN}}

Each connection gets its own component instance (parallel workers = parallel connections, as with stdio subprocesses). docs.title: stage
docs.text:
Stage contract (hylo.stage/v0.1): an open world as an entity tree that a person, a model or a program edits through patches, with every revision kept. A world engine (bench: hylo.envs.mujoco.world) compiles a stage into a running simulation; tools (hylo-agents hylo.agents.worldtools) read and change it.

It differs from the table-top hylo.scene/v0.1 on purpose: a scene is one manipulation task written as data (objects on a table and a success predicate); a stage is a general workspace (robots of any kind from packs, mounted on each other or on fixtures, meshes, cameras, people) that changes while someone works in it.

Frames and units: metres, radians in quaternions; world frame +z up; quat is (w, x, y, z) like MuJoCo.

  entity      id, parent (an entity id or none: the world), label, pose in the parent's frame, locked
              and components, each optional:
    shape     a primitive (box, sphere, cylinder, capsule, plane): size, rgba
    mesh      a mesh file (obj, stl) with a scale; its collision geometry comes from `collision`
    body      physics: dynamic (has a free joint) or static, mass or density, friction
    collision how the visual geometry becomes contact geometry: the primitive itself, the convex hull, convex
              parts (a decomposition file) or voxel boxes (hylo-tools `physicalize` writes them)
    robot     a robot from a pack (hylo.pack/v0.1): pack name, base fixed or free, `mount` onto a body of
              another entity, initial joint values
    camera    a camera: vertical field of view, image size, depth on/off; `body` names the body it rides on
    light     a directional or spot light
    human     a walking person (hylo.envs.mujoco.humans): route, speed, appearance

A patch is a list of operations with the revision it was written against (compare and swap): add an entity, remove one (with its children when cascade), update some of its fields, reparent it. The store applies a patch to a copy, refuses it if the stage changed in between or an operation touches a locked entity, validates the result and writes it as the next revision; old revisions are never changed, and restore(n) commits revision n again as the newest.

docs.title: tooling
docs.text:
Typed tool surfaces (hylo.tools/v0.1): what a tool-calling model may call, declared once and checked on every call.

A Surface is an ordered set of ToolDefs. Each tool has

  name         lower_snake_case, unique in the surface
  kind         read  (looks, measures, computes: never changes the world; several may share one model reply)
               act   (changes the world: must be the only call of its reply; ends the model's turn)
               end   (ends the episode or session)
  help         purpose, when to use it, what it changes, what it returns, what it does not do, its errors:
               rendered into one description, so every tool explains itself the same way
  params       a closed JSON Schema object (no unknown keys; every field described); optional fields also accept
               null, which means "not given"
  fn           fn(args) -> dict (the result) or ToolOutput (a result with images); raises ToolError

Surface.call(name, args) checks the arguments against the schema (types, enums, bounds, required fields, unknown keys), runs the tool and returns a ToolReply (ok, result or error, images). A failure is a structured ToolError (code, message, field, whether retrying with the same arguments can help) that goes back to the model as data, never an exception out of the agent loop. Surface.digest() hashes the declarations as the model sees them, so a run records exactly which surface it had.

docs.title: bringup
docs.text:
Bring-up policy: small sinusoidal moves around the pose the arm is in, joint by joint.

Not a task policy. It checks the chain (policy server -> workcell -> adapter -> motors) with motions that stay within a few degrees of the measured pose, so the shield's limits and the robot's own limits are never near. The motion is a function of executed steps (counted in on_step), not of policy calls: under asynchronous execution the runtime drops the actions that went stale during inference, and a chunk indexed by steps stays continuous with the one before it.

docs.title: env
docs.text:
A real robot as a Hylo Environment, through LeRobot's Robot interface (S3).

Any LeRobot robot works (SO-100/101 and Koch followers, LeKiwi, OpenArm, ...; ROS 2 robots through LeRobot's third-party plugins such as lerobot_robot_ros2_zenoh), and so does SimulatedArm for bring-up without hardware.

What the adapter adds on top of LeRobot's Robot: - an EnvSpec: observation keys grouped into named state vectors (default: joint_pos and gripper), cameras renamed, an action box with explicit limits and semantics (joint_pos in the robot's units, continuous gripper), the control rate, and real_robot=True so the SafetyShield aborts on any modification; - reset: connect if needed, move to the home pose by interpolation (home_steps small steps, each within the shield's limits), then hand over. The scene is the operator's job: the workcell waits for "reset_done"; - success is never claimed (None): the operator's verdict or a calibrated judge labels the episode; - hold_action: the current measured position (the robot stays where it is), used by the workcell runtime when the policy is late; stop(): hold immediately (e-stop path, in addition to the robot's own hardware e-stop).

env:
  type: lerobot.robot
  remote: {runtime: robot}            # the profile's runtime: the venv with lerobot and the robot SDK
  params:
    robot: {type: so101_follower, params: {port: /dev/ttyACM0, id: arm1, max_relative_target: 10}}
    cameras: {front: agentview, wrist: wrist}
    action_low: [-110, -100, -100, -100, -160, 0]
    action_high: [110, 100, 100, 100, 160, 100]
    home: [0, -90, 90, 0, 0, 10]
    control_hz: 30

docs.title: sim_arm
docs.text:
SimulatedArm: a stand-in with LeRobot's Robot interface, for bringing up a workcell without hardware.

Five revolute joints and a gripper, in degrees and 0-100 like LeRobot's SO follower, with first-order motor dynamics (each joint closes a fraction of the gap to its target per step), a per-step limit on the commanded change (LeRobot's max_relative_target) and an overhead camera that draws the arm's projected joint positions. It never claims success: on a real robot the operator (or a calibrated judge) decides.

docs.title: env
docs.text:
LIBERO Environment adapter. Runs inside the simulator venv (hf-libero, robosuite 1.4) behind an EnvServer; the main process never imports LIBERO.

Conventions match LeRobot's LIBERO integration so LeRobot-trained policies see what they saw in training: - images: agentview and wrist cameras, rotated 180 degrees (robosuite renders them upside down); - state: eef position (3), eef axis-angle from the xyzw quaternion (3), gripper qpos (2); - reset: load the task's stored init state (index = seed % 50), then 10 no-op steps; - action: 7-D OSC delta pose in [-1, 1], last dim gripper (-1 open, +1 close); - success: LIBERO's BDDL goal predicate (env.check_success()); the episode ends on success.

The robot contract (RFC-0006, hylo.core.robot) for tool-using agents: params control: joint_position and tool_obs: true (the defaults keep the VLA mode above, unchanged). - action: 7 joint-position targets (rad) + hand command in [0, 1] (0 closed, 1 open), through robosuite's JOINT_POSITION controller (delta to the target each step, unscaled; gains kp, damping_ratio); the hand command is a target opening, approached at robosuite's gripper speed (full stroke in 8 steps); - observation: q.arm, hand.arm (measured opening in command units), RGB-D per camera (agentview, wrist; upright images, depth in metres), <cam>.seg and extra["segments"] with segmentation: true, intrinsics and OpenCV-frame camera poses in extra["cameras"], object poses in extra["privileged"] with privileged_obs: true; - EnvSpec.robot: the Panda exported from robosuite into the asset cache (see robot.py). The contract's world frame is the robot base frame (LIBERO scenes place the robot at different heights).

Perturbed tasks (perturb.py): perturb (env param, applied to every task) and TaskSpec.params["perturb"] (from the benchmark's perturb param) name the changes: position, task, language, object, camera, noise, robot_init. What was changed is reported in extra["perturbation"] of every observation.

docs.title: libero
docs.text: LIBERO (Liu et al. 2023) for Hylo: environment adapter and benchmark suites.

docs.title: robot
docs.text:
The robot contract (hylo.core.robot) for LIBERO: the RobotSpec, human labels for the BDDL objects, camera intrinsics and poses (pure Python: numpy only). The simulator side (the Panda model exported from robosuite, the segmentation render) is in sim.py.

World frame of the robot contract: the robot's base frame (robosuite body robot0_base), +x forward, +z up. LIBERO places the robot differently per scene (kitchen and study tables: base 0.91 m above the floor; living room: 0.42 m; floor scenes: on the floor) while EnvSpec.robot is fixed for an environment, so every pose the contract reports (camera poses, TCP, privileged object poses) is relative to the base; ArmSpec.base_in_world is then the identity and the support surface is always within a few centimetres of z = 0. extra["libero"]["base_in_sim"] gives the base in LIBERO's own world frame.

docs.title: aloha_oracle
docs.text:
oracle.aloha_table: a privileged scripted agent for mujoco/bimanual-v0 (an upper bound, not a method).

It reads object poses and the goal from extra["privileged"] (env param privileged_obs: true) and moves both arms with ordinary joint-position actions, so it proves each task is solvable by the two simulated arms:

  • handover: the arm on the object's side picks the bar near one end and lifts it to the middle of the table, turned along y; the other arm grasps the free end from above, the first lets go and leaves, the second puts the bar in the zone;
  • lift_box: both arms grasp the box's end handles from above at the same time, close together and lift along straight lines of identical timing, then hold;
  • two_bins: each arm picks the block on its side and drops it in the bin on its side, both at once. Param sequential: true runs the same motions one arm after the other (the baseline the step limit rules out).

docs.title: aloha_table
docs.text:
Two ViperX 300 arms facing each other across a table: mujoco.aloha_table (RFC-0006 part 3, two-arm tasks).

The arms, their parallel grippers and their joint-position servos are the MuJoCo Menagerie aloha model (BSD-3-Clause, fetched at a pinned commit into the asset cache on first use, see assets.py); the table, the objects, the fixed cameras and the pinhole wrist cameras are ours. Arm bodies compensate gravity (as the real servos do with their integral terms), so the position servos track planned motions closely.

World frame: +z up, table top at z = 0, the left arm's base at x = -0.469 and the right arm's at x = +0.469 (both at y = -0.019), facing each other along x; the operator stands at -y. Each arm reaches top-down grasps over x in [-0.5, 0.1] (left) or [-0.1, 0.5] (right): only the middle strip is reachable by both.

Control: joint-position targets at control_hz (20 Hz; 25 physics steps of 2 ms). Action = left arm 6 joint targets (rad), left gripper command (0 closed .. 1 open), right arm 6 joint targets, right gripper command. Observation: q.left, hand.left, q.right, hand.right (measured opening in command units: 0 when the pads touch), RGB-D from overhead, front, left_wrist, right_wrist, segmentation and privileged state on request.

Cameras need an OpenGL backend (MUJOCO_GL=egl, or osmesa on CPU); cameras=[] needs none.

docs.title: arm_table
docs.text:
Shared machinery of the table environments with several arms (mujoco.aloha_table, mujoco.g1_table).

A subclass supplies the robot (an MjSpec it attaches to the scene, its arms as ArmIO records, its RobotSpec), its cameras and its object pool; this base runs everything else the same way for every robot:

  • one compiled model holds a pool of objects; an episode activates the ones its task needs (colour, size, mass) and parks the rest inside the table, so the model never changes shape and snapshots stay cheap;
  • control is joint-position targets per arm plus a hand command per arm, at control_hz;
  • observations follow hylo.core.robot: q.<arm>, hand.<arm> (measured, command units), RGB-D per camera, <cam>.seg with segmentation=True, camera intrinsics and poses in extra["cameras"], and with privileged_obs=True object poses and the goal in extra["privileged"] (oracles only);
  • snapshots carry the episode record and the full integration state.

The task family (sampling and success predicates) is a module with sample_episode(params, rng) and evaluate(env), named by the subclass.

docs.title: assets
docs.text:
Third-party simulation assets, fetched on first use into the asset cache and never vendored.

The cache is $HYLO_ASSETS (default ~/.cache/hylo/assets). Each asset is one upstream folder pinned to one commit and verified file by file against a digest list kept beside this module (a <name>.json manifest: source, commit, folder, licence, sha256 per file, the upstream LICENSE among them), so a cached copy that was changed or truncated is refused rather than loaded.

assets("menagerie_panda")     -> Path   MuJoCo Menagerie `franka_emika_panda` (Apache-2.0)
assets("menagerie_aloha")     -> Path   MuJoCo Menagerie `aloha`: two ViperX 300 6-DoF arms (BSD-3-Clause)
assets("menagerie_g1_hands")  -> Path   MuJoCo Menagerie `unitree_g1` with the three-finger hands (BSD-3-Clause)
assets("menagerie_allegro")   -> Path   MuJoCo Menagerie `wonik_allegro`: the Allegro hand, left and right
                                        (BSD-2-Clause)
panda_assets() / panda_assets_dir()     the Panda shortcuts used since the first environment

Manifests that pin folders of the same repository at the same commit share one cache folder per upstream folder; a manifest may list only some files of it. Files a manifest needs that are missing from an existing cached folder are fetched into it (same commit, verified digests), so one manifest never disturbs another's files.

Offline machines: put the upstream folder at assets_dir(name) by hand; it is verified the same way.

Other GitHub repositories (e.g. a robot model and pretrained policies published with a training framework): a manifest with "repo": "<owner>/<name>" is fetched from that repository's raw files at its commit into <cache>/github/<owner>_<name>/<commit12>/<folder>; "paths": {rel: path from the repository root} names files that live outside the folder (its LICENSE at the root).

docs.title: bimanual_tasks
docs.text:
The mujoco/bimanual-v0 task family on mujoco.aloha_table: tasks that one arm cannot do.

Each task samples a layout from the episode seed (positions, yaw, sizes, masses, colours, which side starts) and realises a natural-language instruction. Each arm reaches only up to about 10 cm past the middle of the table, which the layouts use to make a second arm necessary.

Task Success Why one arm is not enough handover the bar rests in the named zone, released the bar starts where only one arm reaches and the zone lies where only the other reaches: one arm must pass it to the other lift_box the box held at least the named height off the table and level (tilt under 0.2 rad) for one second the box is wider than a gripper opens; its two end handles are 22 cm apart, and lifted by one handle it tips two_bins each block in the bin on its side, both released, within the step limit each block and its bin lie on one arm's side only, and the step limit is shorter than two pick-and-place motions one after the other

Failures end the episode early: an object falls off the table, or the box is dropped after it was lifted.

docs.title: checks
docs.text:
Checks on a stage world (RFC-0008 part 4): goals as predicates over the world's state, answered with reasons.

A check never steps the simulation. Each failed atom says what was expected, what was measured and a reason code, so an agent (or a skill matched by reason code, RFC-0003) knows what to do next:

  atom          fields                                   fails with
  in_box        entity, min [x,y,z], max [x,y,z]         POSE_OUTSIDE_BOX
  near          a, b (entities or [x,y,z]), max_m        DISTANCE_NOT_MET
  apart         a, b, min_m                              DISTANCE_NOT_MET
  above         a, b, min_m (a's centre higher than b's) NOT_ABOVE
  contact       a, b (entity ids; b "any")               CONTACT_MISSING
  no_contact    a, b                                     CONTACT_PRESENT
  joint_range   robot, joint, min, max                   JOINT_OUT_OF_RANGE
  settled       entity, max_speed (m/s)                  NOT_SETTLED
  upright       entity (a robot base or an object), min_cos  NOT_UPRIGHT
  lifted        entity, min_z                            NOT_LIFTED
  reachable     robot, point, margin_m                   UNREACHABLE (beyond the pack's reach from its base)
  no_penetration  max_mm                                 PENETRATION_PRESENT
  all / any / not   terms (all, any) or term (not)

An atom that cannot be evaluated (an entity that does not exist, a robot without a reach) is unverifiable (ENTITY_MISSING, OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE): not of it stays unverifiable and all with it is not true. The spec gate (gate) refuses a goal whose entities are missing and reports SPEC_ALREADY_SATISFIED when the goal already holds before anything was done.

docs.title: compose
docs.text:
A stage (hylo.stage/v0.1) as one MuJoCo model, built with MjSpec (RFC-0008 part 2).

Entities are built parents first. Each becomes a body named by its id (robots: the pack's model attached under a frame with the prefix "/", so a robot's joints, actuators, sites and bodies are "/"):

  shape    a body with one primitive geom; `body.dynamic` adds a free joint; collision `none` makes it visual only
  mesh     a body with a mesh geom (MuJoCo collides with its convex hull); collision `parts` (convex pieces) or
           `voxels` (boxes) from a physicalize file become collision-only geoms and the mesh stays visual only
  robot    the pack's model: fixed base (its free joint removed) attached at the pose, or onto `mount.entity`'s
           body `mount.body`; free base keeps (or gains) a free joint; the pack's physics options carry over
           (elliptic cones, impratio, integrator) when it asks for them
  camera   a camera on the parent's body (or `camera.body` of a robot parent); MuJoCo convention: it looks along
           its -z axis with +y up (Pose of a camera = that frame; `look_at` builds one)
  light    a directional or spot light
  human    a kinematic person (mocap body: capsule legs, torso, head) moved by the crowd controller

The home posture of every robot (its keyframe) is applied after compiling, by joint and actuator name, so robots from different models never mix keyframes. A free-base robot's pose gives x, y and yaw; its base starts at the pose's z plus the keyframe's base height (without a keyframe: plus the model's own base height).

docs.title: controllers
docs.text:
Controllers of the stage world (RFC-0008 part 3): each turns one action into actuator commands, step by step.

A robot's actuators keep a target (Robot.target, one value per actuator, in ctrl units for position servos and in joint units for torque motors, where the world closes a PD loop with the pack's gains). A controller moves those targets over time and reports when it is done and what it measured:

  JointMove    linear interpolation from the current targets to new joint targets over a duration, then a short
               settle; measured: the largest joint error at the end
  GripperMove  the gripper actuator to its open or closed value (or a fraction); measured: whether the fingers
               stopped short of the command (something is held)
  TcpMove      damped least squares IK of the arm joints for a tool-point pose, then a JointMove
  Walk         an open-loop trot for quadrupeds: diagonal leg pairs in antiphase, thigh swing proportional to the
               commanded forward speed (minus / plus a turn term on the left / right legs), calf flexion lifts the
               swing foot; measured: base displacement, heading change, whether the robot tipped over
  Fly          drones: position PD -> desired force -> attitude PD -> body wrench -> actuator commands through the
               allocation matrix measured from the model (works for body-thrust and per-rotor drones alike)
  BaseMove     mobile bases driven through x, y, yaw joints: interpolation like JointMove
  Hold         keep every target for a while

docs.title: crowd
docs.text:
People in a stage world (RFC-0008 part 6): kinematic walkers that follow routes, plan around obstacles and stop for what is in front of them.

Each human entity is a mocap body (built by compose.py from capsules). Every step:

  route      the next waypoint of its route (looping or not); at a waypoint it stands for `dwell` seconds
  path       a path to that waypoint on a planar grid (A*, 8 neighbours, no corner cutting, then shortened by line of
             sight) around the floor footprints of every other body, inflated by the person's radius; planned when a
             waypoint is chosen and again after being blocked for half a second
  sensing    three rays at chest height (straight ahead and 25 degrees to each side, 0.7 m): a hit on anything but the
             floor makes the person stop (a robot, a box, another person): people never walk through things
  motion     walking speed along the path, turning at most 180 degrees per second, a small vertical bob

Commands: goto(id, [x, y]) (a one-waypoint route), stop(id), resume(id). state() reports each person's position, heading and whether they are walking, waiting or blocked.

docs.title: dex_table
docs.text:
A floating dexterous hand above a table with objects of several shapes: mujoco.dex_table.

The robot is one hand from MuJoCo Menagerie (hands.py: the Unitree G1 three-finger hand or the Allegro hand, left or right) on a six-joint base (x, y, z slides, then yaw, pitch and roll hinges), every joint position-controlled and gravity-compensated, so the toolkit plans and runs the base like an arm (one ArmSpec named "hand" with the hand's dexterous HandSpec). At zero base joints the TCP points straight down. The table, objects and cameras are ours.

Objects (one of each in the pool, all free): box (5 cm cube), cylinder (r 2.5 cm, 10 cm tall), sphere (r 3 cm), mug (r 3.5 cm, 9 cm tall, a handle: concave, a cup of wall segments) and rock (an irregular solid of three overlapping lumps, seeded), each a set of convex mesh parts (shape(kind), also what a planner can be given as ground truth).

World frame: table top at z = 0, object centres within 6 cm of the origin, the hand's home 30 cm above it. Observation: q.hand (base joints), hand.hand (finger joints), RGB-D from front, side and back, segmentation and privileged state on request. docs.title: free_program
docs.text:
Scene programs (hylo.freescene/v0.1): loading one Python file into a restricted namespace.

A scene program is a Python file with top-level declarations and functions:

ROBOT = "panda" | "aloha" | "g1"     INSTRUCTION = "..."     MAX_STEPS = 900     LABELS = {...}   (optional)
def build(scene): ...                 required: adds the task's things to scene.spec (free_model.SceneHandle)
def success(sim) -> bool: ...         required: judges the state (free_world.SimView)
def randomize(sim, rng): ...          optional: per-seed changes to the start (free_world.SimEdit)
def demo(sim): ...                    optional: a scripted proof with invisible hands (checkers only)
def targets(sim) -> {name: xyz}: ...  optional: points a robot hand must reach

program_problems(source) lists what keeps a source from loading (imports other than math / numpy / mujoco, names or attributes starting with an underscore, file and code-loading calls, classes); SceneProgram(path) checks, runs the top level with a small set of builtins and exposes the declarations. The code agents check programs the same way before they reach an environment (hylo.codeagents.scene_free_check.validate_scene_program); this second check guards files written by hand. Neither is an OS-level jail: run untrusted programs in a container.

docs.title: free_scene
docs.text:
mujoco.free_scene: a task written as a Python scene program (hylo.freescene/v0.1) instead of a scene file.

The program (free_program.py) picks the robot, states the instruction, builds the world with MuJoCo's model editor or MJCF (free_model.py) and judges success from the simulation state (free_world.py). This module is the environment: it mixes the free scene into the robot environments themselves, so the robot, table, cameras, control, observation layout, RobotSpec and snapshots are those of mujoco.panda_table, mujoco.aloha_table or mujoco.g1_table, unchanged; what it adds is the program's model, reset (home posture, randomize, settle), the program's success function after every step, privileged free-form state and, for checkers, the demo's invisible hands.

env = FreeSceneEnv(scene="runs/scenes_free/cable", privileged_obs=True)       # or registry type mujoco.free_scene
obs = env.reset(task); obs.extra["privileged"]["cables"]["cable"]["nodes"]

Params: scene (a scene.py or the directory holding it; a task's params["scene"] may switch programs but must keep the robot), demo_hands (invisible hands for demo(); checkers only, 0 otherwise), and the robot environment's cameras, width, height, segmentation, privileged_obs, control_hz, depth, mesh_detail.

Checker-only methods (never reachable by an agent through the Environment contract): run_demo(), program_targets(), contacts(), model_xml().

docs.title: free_world
docs.text:
The free-form state of a compiled free scene, and the sim views scene programs read and edit it through.

world = SceneWorld(model, scene_bodies, robot_bodies, finger_bodies, labels)
world.state(data)            -> {"bodies", "joints", "cables", "flexes", "sites"}   (privileged, JSON-ready)
world.touching(data, "rope", "hand"); world.contacts(data, depth=0.003)
SimView(world, data, table_top)                 `sim` in success(sim) and targets(sim): read-only
SimEdit(world, data, table_top, forward, hands)  `sim` in randomize(sim, rng) and demo(sim): edits too
DemoHands(world, n)          invisible mocap hands that hold a body through a ball-joint equality (demo only)

Nothing here knows a robot or an episode: SceneWorld indexes the program's part of the model once (rigid bodies, composite cables found by their <prefix>B_first body, flexes and their vertex bodies, hinge / slide joints, one segmentation group per cable, flex and rigid root), and every query takes the MjData to read.
