docs.title: flow
docs.text:
policy.flow: a flow-matching action head (the objective of pi0's and SmolVLA's action experts).

Training: for a demonstration chunk x1 (normalised) and noise x0 ~ N(0, I), x_tau = (1 - tau) x0 + tau x1, and an MLP v(x_tau, tau, obs) regresses the velocity x1 - x0. Sampling: start from seeded noise (times noise_scale) and integrate dx/dtau = v from tau = 0 to 1 with Euler steps. Different seeds give different, plausible chunks, so the policy can be steered (seeded noise, sample-and-select) like the large flow-matching VLAs.

docs.title: reference
docs.text:
Reference policies: one small implementation per policy family, numpy only, no downloaded weights.

They are trained from your own runs (development splits only, sealed as artifacts with provenance) and run through the same agents, safety shield, benchmarks and gate as any other policy. They are meant for teaching, testing the stack end to end in seconds, and as baselines on low-dimensional state; they are not the published architectures at scale. For those, use the LeRobot policies (ACT, Diffusion, VQ-BeT, pi0, SmolVLA, ...) or openpi servers.

Plugin Family Idea (reference) Stochastic policy.knn retrieval / non-parametric nearest neighbours in observation space, average their chunks (VINN) no policy.bc regression behaviour cloning MLP from observation to an action chunk, MSE (BC with chunking) no policy.flow generative, flow matching velocity field from noise to the chunk, Euler integration (pi0, SmolVLA action experts) yes policy.tokens tokenized actions each action dimension binned, categorical heads, sampled (RT-1, OpenVLA-style discretization) yes policy.mpc model-based planning cross-entropy method over action sequences in a learned world model (MPC, TD-MPC without the value) yes

Run any of them with the "policy" agent, ACT-style with "temporal_ensemble", or steer the stochastic ones with "steered" (seeded noise, sample-and-select). Learners of the same names build the artifacts: hylo learn job.json with {"learner": "policy.flow", "inputs": ["runs/demos"], "out": "artifacts/flow"}.

docs.title: mpc
docs.text:
policy.mpc: model-predictive control with a learned world model (the planning half of TD-MPC / PETS, without a learned value function).

Each decision runs the cross-entropy method over horizon-step action sequences in the world model (an artifact of the "world_model.state" learner): sample sequences from a Gaussian (seeded), roll them out with the ensemble, keep the best elites, refit, repeat. The objective is either the model's learned success probability ("success"), or a task cost given as data, {"reach": ["tip_pos", "target_pos"]}: the distance between two state entries. uncertainty_penalty > 0 adds the ensemble's disagreement to the cost, keeping plans where the model has data (off by default: it slowed reaching on MuJoCo planar reach).

Train the world model on data that explores: expert runs alone cover too few actions, and the planner then exploits the model's errors. On MuJoCo planar reach (40 held-out episodes): expert-only data 0.88 success, expert + random-action runs 0.95 in 44 steps, with these defaults; 64 samples x 3 iterations, re-planning every 2 steps: 0.42 / 0.75.

policy: {type: policy.mpc, params: {world_model: artifacts/wm, objective: {reach: [tip_pos, target_pos]}}}

docs.title: experience_agent
docs.text:
LeRobot flow policies with experience memory (RFC-0003 M1).

PriorLeRobotSampler extends LeRobotAgent with the PriorSampler protocol: - the retrieval key is the policy's own visual tokens (SigLIP embeddings of each real camera, 2x2 grid-pooled, concatenated, L2-normalised), captured from the forward pass the policy runs anyway; - prior_fn(key) is called between the prefix computation and the denoising loop; if it returns a prior, the Euler integration starts at x_t0 = (1 - t0) * normalise(prior) + t0 * noise and runs t0 -> 0 with the policy's unchanged velocity field. With no prior (or t0 = 1) the result is bit-identical to LeRobotAgent.sample. Implemented by wrapping embed_image and euler_integrate for the duration of one call; LeRobot is not modified.

agent: {type: remote, params: {ref: hylo.policies.lerobot.experience_agent:make_experience_agent,
        params: {repo_id: lerobot/smolvla_libero, memory: {type: action_bank, params: {path: ...}}, ...}}}

docs.title: export
docs.text:
Export Hylo traces to a LeRobotDataset (v3) for training (imitation, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, RL warm starts). Runs in a venv with lerobot (envs/libero).

Each frame pairs the observation seen before an action with the action actually executed (after the SafetyShield), plus next.reward / next.done / next.success. Video features need traces recorded with trace.image_every = 1; episodes without per-step images are skipped and reported. A provenance file maps every exported episode back to its run, episode id, status and agent, and the dataset is sealed as a dataset artifact (RFC-0004). Gate and held-out runs are refused whatever --splits says.

python -m hylo.policies.lerobot.export --runs runs/<run_dir> ... --out data/<name>         [--only-success] [--state-keys eef_pos eef_axis_angle gripper_qpos] [--cameras agentview wrist]

docs.title: memory_build
docs.text:
Build a frozen ActionBank from Hylo traces, with keys from the policy's own visual tokens (RFC-0003 M1).

python -m hylo.policies.lerobot.memory_build --runs runs/<search runs> ... --out runs/memory/<name>         [--repo-id lerobot/smolvla_libero] [--workers 8] [--task-prefix libero/libero_10/]

Only chunks of simulator-verified successful episodes from development splits are stored (search / search_val; gate and held-out never). Replays of identical episodes (common random numbers across runs) are stored once. Writes bank.npz / bank.json plus build_report.json with nearest-neighbour similarity statistics, which is what memory_steer.sim_floor should be calibrated against, and seals the directory as an action_memory artifact (RFC-0004). docs.title: selftrain
docs.text:
Expert iteration for a LeRobot VLA (RFC-0002 L4): fine-tune the policy on its own successful episodes.

python -m hylo.policies.lerobot.selftrain --runs runs/<search-run> ... --out runs/selftrain/<name>         --pretrained lerobot/smolvla_libero --steps 300 --batch-size 8
  1. export: successful episodes of development-split runs (search / search_val only; gate and held-out data must stay unseen) -> LeRobotDataset v3, cameras named as the policy expects, with provenance;
  2. pin normalisation: the dataset's state/action statistics are replaced by the pretrained policy's own, so fine-tuning changes weights, not the input/output scaling (lerobot-train otherwise re-normalises with the new dataset's stats);
  3. fine-tune with lerobot-train (action expert only by default: cheap on CPU, little room to overfit);
  4. write selftrain.json: dataset + weights digests, training arguments, and the config patch that turns the result into an improvement candidate (it is then gated like any other candidate); the weights directory is sealed as a policy_weights artifact (RFC-0004) whose provenance lists the runs and the dataset artifact. Runs in the policy venv (envs/libero/.venv: lerobot + torch).

docs.title: proposer
docs.text:
LLM proposer for steering candidates (RFC-0002 step 3).

The model reads what the search split shows (failure buckets, per-episode timelines of grasps and stalls, a few successes for contrast), the current steering config with its schema bounds, and the archive's earlier hypotheses with their verdicts. It never sees search_val, gate or held-out numbers. Every proposal must validate against SteeringConfig (field bounds, rule schema); invalid proposals are dropped and counted.

docs.title: SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
SYSTEM = 'You improve a frozen robot manipulation policy (a VLA) WITHOUT changing its weights, by editing the
configuration of a steering wrapper around it. You see diagnostics from failed and successful episodes and propose
a few alternative steering configurations, each with ONE falsifiable hypothesis about which failures it fixes and why.

The steering wrapper:
- samples action chunks from the policy with seeded noise; n_samples > 1 draws several chunks and selector
  "gripper_vote_medoid" executes the medoid of the gripper-majority samples (cost grows linearly with n_samples);
- executes `execution_steps` actions of each 50-step chunk before asking the policy again (null = all 50);
- noise_scale scales the policy's sampling noise (1.0 = as trained);
- rules: runtime triggers. feature in [still_steps, grasp_attempts, disagreement, steps], op in [>=, >, <=, <],
  action "resample" (params: noise_scale) or "backoff" (params: steps, dz, open_gripper); cooldown and max_fires
  are in control steps / per episode. disagreement requires n_samples >= 2.

Experience (when present): `lessons` are notes distilled from earlier episodes, each with an id and helpful/harmful
votes; `skills` are earlier steering configurations with a status: verified (shown to help), refuted (shown not to
help), proposed (tried, not yet shown either way). Build on verified skills and well-supported lessons, do not
re-propose refuted ones, and list the ids of the lessons each candidate relies on in "lessons_used".

Rules of the game: propose changes that plausibly generalise across tasks and init states; do not repeat an
earlier hypothesis that was refuted; keep each candidate a coherent single idea.
Reply with JSON only: {"candidates": [{"hypothesis": "...", "steering": {<complete steering config>},
"lessons_used": ["<lesson id>", ...]}]}'

docs.title: reflector
docs.text:
LLM reflector (RFC-0003 M4): distil lessons from the search split's successes and failures.

Like ReasoningBank it learns from failures as well as successes (pitfalls next to strategies); like ExpeL / ACE it never rewrites the lesson book, it emits operations (ADD / UPVOTE / DOWNVOTE / EDIT / RETIRE) that LessonBook applies deterministically. It reads exactly what the steering proposer reads (search-split diagnostics and timelines), never search_val, gate or held-out data, so lessons cannot carry selection-split information into proposals. Every ADD must cite episodes it was shown; uncited or out-of-scope operations are dropped.

docs.title: SYSTEM module-attribute
docs.text:
SYSTEM = 'You maintain a lesson book for a robot manipulation agent (a frozen VLA policy with a steering wrapper).
From episode timelines (grasp steps, still periods, end-effector heights, outcome) you extract short, reusable
lessons: "strategy" lessons describe what successful episodes did, "pitfall" lessons describe failure patterns to
avoid. A lesson is useful only if it is specific (names the phase, object or signal) and could change a decision.

You may only:
- ADD a new lesson: {"op": "ADD", "scope": "global" | "task:<task id from the input>", "kind": "strategy"|"pitfall",
  "title": "<= 12 words", "content": "<= 60 words", "evidence": ["<episode id from the input>", ...]}
- UPVOTE or DOWNVOTE an existing lesson the new episodes confirm or contradict: {"op": "UPVOTE"|"DOWNVOTE",
  "id": "<lesson id>", "evidence": ["<episode id>"]}
- EDIT an existing lesson's content: {"op": "EDIT", "id": "<lesson id>", "content": "..."}
Do not restate existing lessons as new ones; vote on them instead. Use scope "global" only for patterns seen in
several tasks. Reply with JSON only: {"ops": [...]}'

docs.title: chat
docs.text:
Chat models for tool-using agents (RFC-0006 part 7): one interface, images, per-call accounting.

model = build_chat({"backend": "ollama", "model": "qwen3.5:35b-a3b", "vision": True})
reply = model.chat([{"role": "system", "content": "..."},
                    {"role": "user", "content": "...", "images": [rgb_array]}])
reply.text, reply.tokens_in, reply.tokens_out, reply.latency_s, reply.cost_usd

Backends (the backend key of a spec): openai any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint (vLLM, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, ...); the key is read from the environment variable named by api_key_env; price gives USD per million tokens ollama the same against a local Ollama server (http://localhost:11434/v1), price 0 anthropic the Anthropic Messages API (key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unless api_key_env says otherwise) claude_code the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess (claude -p --output-format json, prompt on stdin) codex the Codex CLI as a subprocess (codex exec ... -, prompt on stdin) scripted a deterministic fake for tests: canned replies, or a function of the conversation

Messages are dicts {"role": "system" | "user" | "assistant", "content": str, "images": [...]}; an image is an (H, W, 3) uint8 array or PNG bytes, sent only to models with vision. Keys never appear in configs or traces. Standard library only (and Pillow for PNG encoding).

Native tool calls (RFC-0007): chat(messages, tools=[ToolSpec | {"name", "description", "parameters"}]). The reply's tool_calls are ToolCall(id, name, arguments); a call whose arguments are not a JSON object keeps them in raw with error set, so the agent can answer it instead of crashing. The conversation stays in one neutral shape and each backend translates it at the wire:

{"role": "assistant", "content": "...", "tool_calls": [{"id", "name", "arguments"}], "reasoning": "..."}
{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "...", "name": "...", "content": "<result text>", "images": [...]}

OpenAI-compatible endpoints get tools as functions (images of tool results follow in a user message, since tool messages carry text only there); replay_reasoning sends an assistant turn's reasoning back as reasoning_content (needed by endpoints that continue a reasoning chain across tool calls). Anthropic gets tool_use / tool_result blocks. Backends without tool support (the coding-agent CLIs) are wrapped by TextTools, which describes the tools in the system message and parses fenced tool blocks from the text.

docs.title: control
docs.text:
Joint-position control and the hand command on robosuite (pure numpy; robosuite objects are only touched through their attributes, so this runs with robosuite 1.4 and 1.5).

robosuite's parallel grippers keep a finger set-point (gripper.current_action: [-1, +1] closed, [+1, -1] open) that their own actions only push towards open or closed at the gripper's speed. The contract's hand command is a target opening in [0, 1] (0 closed, 1 open): the set-point moves towards it at that same speed each control step and the gripper's own action is 0 (keep the set-point).

docs.title: env
docs.text:
RobosuiteContractEnv: the robot contract (hylo.robot/v0.1) over a robosuite environment, as a base class. An adapter subclasses it with what is specific to its suite (which scene to build for a task, the arms' layout, the labels, success); this class does the contract's side once:

  • action: per arm, in RobotSpec.arms order, 7 joint-position targets (rad) then a hand command in [0, 1] (0 closed, 1 open). robosuite's JOINT_POSITION controller takes the targets as absolute goals (robosuite15.make); the hand command is a target opening that the gripper's set-point approaches at the gripper's own speed (control). Other robot parts (a mobile base, a torso) get zero commands: they stay where they are. Arms without fingers ignore the hand command;
  • observation: q.<arm>, hand.<arm> (measured opening in command units), RGB-D per camera (upright images, depth in metres), <cam>.seg and extra["segments"] with segmentation: true, intrinsics and OpenCV camera poses in extra["cameras"], object poses in extra["privileged"] with privileged_obs: true;
  • world frame: the body world_body (robot0's base): every pose is relative to it; extra[<suite>]["base_in_sim"] maps it into the simulator's world;
  • reset: start_episode (reseed and reset), the layout checked once against what the RobotSpec published, the arms moved to ready_posture() if the suite gives one, then settle_steps steps holding the joints with the hands open;
  • step: success() ends the episode, and so does failed() (a suite's own failure condition).

The import is pure (numpy, hylo-core): simulator code runs only inside methods, in the simulator's venv.

docs.title: labels
docs.text:
Instance ids and human labels for the geoms of a robosuite scene (pure numpy: works on name lists, so suites test their rules without MuJoCo).

Id 1 is the support (a table, a counter), id 2 the robot, then one id per label in the order the rules list them (so ids do not depend on the scene's contents); 0 is background (walls, floor, scenery no rule names). Rules are tried in this order for each geom:

  1. attached: (regex on the body name, label): things fixed into the robot's own model (a peg on a hand);
  2. the robot: bodies whose top-level ancestor (or own name) starts with one of robot_prefixes;
  3. parts: (regex on the geom or body name, label): a handle on a pot, a knob on a stove;
  4. objects: {name: label} for objects whose bodies are named <name>_... (longest name first);
  5. bodies: {body name: label}, matched against the body or its top-level ancestor (bins, pegs);
  6. markers: {body name prefix: label} (many small bodies under one label, e.g. dirt spots);
  7. support: body names (exact, or starting with one of support_prefixes) that make up the support.

docs.title: robosuite_contract
docs.text:
The robot contract (hylo.robot/v0.1) on robosuite-based simulators, shared by the robosuite and RoboCasa adapters (and written so the LIBERO adapter, on robosuite 1.4, can adopt it).

Modules (pure: importable in the main process; worker-side: only inside a simulator venv):

  • geometry (pure): 4x4 poses, pinhole intrinsics, OpenCV camera poses, MuJoCo depth in metres.
  • panda (pure): the Franka Panda's limits and home posture, robosuite's naming of arm i and its gripper, and the RobotSpec builder.
  • control (pure): the hand command as a gripper set-point, the measured hand opening, joint-target clipping.
  • labels (pure): instance ids and human labels for a scene's geoms from name rules.
  • splits (pure): seeded RFC-0002 / standard evaluation splits.
  • env (pure at import): RobosuiteContractEnv, the Environment base class (spec, reset, observe, step) that the adapters subclass with their task lists, scene builders and label rules.
  • export (worker-side, MuJoCo): the arm's MJCF exported into a content-addressed asset folder and the TCP measured on it.
  • render (worker-side, MuJoCo): RGB-D and instance segmentation of a camera in the contract's conventions.
  • robosuite15 (worker-side, robosuite 1.5): absolute joint-position controllers, cheap offscreen rendering, reseeding, the Panda's XML as a task builds it.
  • runs (main process): one-command program evaluation, code.llm runs, summaries and captioned videos re-simulated from traces, for any adapter that describes itself with a runs.Suite.

docs.title: panda
docs.text:
The Franka Panda as robosuite models it, for the robot contract (pure Python: numpy and hylo-core).

robosuite 1.5 names arm i's joints robot{i}_joint1..7 and attaches its gripper as the arm's "right" part with the prefix gripper{i}_right_: the hand frame is the gripper's root body (gripper{i}_right_right_gripper for the PandaGripper), the fingers gripper{i}_right_finger_joint1/2, the pads gripper{i}_right_finger{1,2}_pad_collision.

docs.title: runs
docs.text:
One-command evaluation for a robosuite-family suite with the robot contract (main process; pure at import).

An adapter describes itself with a Suite and calls main(suite) from its examples/run.py:

run.py smoke                       one episode of one task, through `hylo run` (the real code path)
run.py programs [--tasks ...]      the solve(robot) programs, --n episodes per task (validation seeds)
run.py code-llm [--tasks ...]      the code.llm agent (one model session at a time by default), zero-shot
run.py summarize OUT               rewrite OUT/results.md from the runs under OUT
run.py video OUT [--task T]        re-simulate a recorded episode from its trace into a captioned MP4

Every run is a hylo run process on a generated experiment config (kept under OUT/configs/), one task per experiment (an environment instance serves one task). The simulator process imports hylo-core, this package and the adapter from the checkout running this script (PYTHONPATH), so a runtime venv built from another checkout still runs this code. Videos need the workspace's demo dependency group (Pillow, imageio-ffmpeg).

docs.title: policy
docs.text:
Policy server (S1): any Hylo agent as a network service, for robots and for other harnesses.

One WebSocket server, two protocols, chosen by path: - /hylo the Hylo agent protocol (hylo.agentserver/v0.1, JSON): spec / reset / act / on_step / on_episode_end. reset carries the client's EnvSpec and the session is refused there, before any motion, if the agent is not compatible with it (core.compat). Client: core.remote.ws.WSAgent. - /openpi openpi's protocol (msgpack-numpy): the server sends its metadata, then answers every observation dict with {"actions": (H, A), "server_timing": {...}}, so openpi clients (DROID, RoboArena, openpi's own examples) can run our agents. openpi has no reset message: the agent is reset on connect, when the prompt changes, or when the client sends {"reset": true}. - /healthz liveness, /meta the served agent's spec as JSON.

One session at a time (a robot talks to one policy; a second client is refused with code 1013, like LeRobot's admission). The agent is built once and reused across sessions. With campaign, the server follows that campaign's active version through its active.json (core.deployment): between sessions, never during one, it rebuilds the agent when a promotion or rollback changed it.

hylo serve policy --agent '{"type": "lerobot.steered", ...}'      # or --config EXP.yaml / --campaign DIR

docs.title: workcell
docs.text:
Workcell service (S2): runs next to the robot (or simulator) and executes episodes with a remote policy.

It owns the environment, the SafetyShield, the real-time runner and the trace, so safety never depends on the network: if the policy server stalls the robot holds and the watchdog aborts; an e-stop is latched here until an operator clears it. The policy is reached over the network (policy.protocol: "hylo" = the Hylo agent protocol, "openpi" = openpi's). Episodes are recorded as an ordinary run (split deployment by default, which no learner reads unless asked) so replay, judges and the catalog work on them.

hylo serve workcell --config workcell.yaml --port 8100

name: sim-libero
env: {type: libero, remote: {...}}                     # any env plugin: a simulator or a robot adapter
benchmark: {type: libero, params: {suite: libero_10}}  # optional: named tasks and init states
policy: {url: "ws://gpu:8000/hylo", protocol: hylo}
runtime: {clock: wall, refill_steps: 10, max_hold_steps: 40, require_reset_confirm: true, verdict_timeout_s: 60}
safety: {max_delta: 0.5}

HTTP API: hylo.workcell/v0.1 (core.remote.workcell): GET /healthz, GET /status, POST /episodes, POST /operator, WS /events (live stream).

docs.title: gravity
docs.text:
gravity: one image -> camera gravity direction (roll, pitch) and focal length (GeoCalib, on the CPU).

hylo tool gravity IMAGE [--weights pinhole|distorted] [--focal-prior PX] [--out DIR]
Python

g = gravity(rgb) # Gravity: roll, pitch (rad), gravity_cam (3,), R_level_cam (3, 3), K (3, 3), vfov_deg

Conventions (GeoCalib's): with g the unit gravity (down) in the camera frame (OpenCV), roll = atan2(g_x, g_y) (positive when the image content is rotated counter-clockwise) and pitch = -asin(g_z) (positive looking up). R_level_cam turns camera-frame (OpenCV) vectors into a level frame (z up); with a known camera height h it gives a camera pose for a single image: T_world_cam = [[R_level_cam, (0, 0, h)], [0, 1]] (yaw fixed: camera looks along +x).

docs.title: hands
docs.text:
hands: video -> per-frame 3D hand poses (WiLoR with MANO; MediaPipe Hands keypoints while MANO is missing).

hylo tool hands VIDEO [--backend auto|wilor|mediapipe|detect] [--max-hands 2] [--fov 60] [--out DIR]
hylo tool hands --status                     which backend would run, and what is missing for WiLoR

Backends (VIDEO: a video file, a folder of images or a (T, H, W, 3) .npy): - wilor: WiLoR (CVPR 2025, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0): YOLO hand detector -> ViT -> MANO pose, shape, camera-frame keypoints and vertices. Needs MANO_RIGHT.pkl from https://mano.is.tue.mpg.de (registration; see MANO_ACTION) at $HYLO_MANO_DIR/MANO_RIGHT.pkl (default ~/.cache/hylo/tools/body_models/mano/MANO_RIGHT.pkl). - mediapipe: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (Apache-2.0): 21 keypoints per hand, image and metric hand-centred 3D, placed in the camera frame by fitting the 2D projection (approximate; depends on the intrinsics). - detect: WiLoR's hand detector only (boxes and handedness), the part of the WiLoR path that runs without MANO. - auto (default): wilor when the MANO file is present, else mediapipe.

Python

track = hands("clip.mp4") # HandTrack: kp2d (T, Hn, 21, 2), kp3d_cam (T, Hn, 21, 3), handedness, valid

docs.title: human
docs.text:
human: video -> world-grounded human motion (GVHMR with SMPL-X; MediaPipe Pose 3D keypoints meanwhile).

hylo tool human VIDEO [--backend auto|mediapipe|gvhmr] [--fov 60 | --K fx,fy,cx,cy] [--pitch DEG --roll DEG]
hylo tool human --status                     what GVHMR still needs (files and where to put them)

Backends (VIDEO: a video file, a folder of images or a (T, H, W, 3) .npy): - gvhmr: GVHMR (SIGGRAPH Asia 2024; non-commercial licence), gravity-view world-grounded SMPL-X motion. Blocked: needs the SMPL and SMPL-X body models (registration) and GVHMR's checkpoints (GVHMR_FILES), and GVHMR's own environment is CUDA-only today (a pytorch3d CUDA wheel, .cuda() calls); status() lists what is missing. - mediapipe: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker heavy (Apache-2.0), 33 keypoints per frame: image, metric hip-centred 3D, camera frame (projection fit) and an approximate world frame (static camera, pitch/roll given or level, ground plane z = 0 under the feet). Pass pitch/roll from the gravity tool for a better ground. - auto (default): mediapipe until the GVHMR path is available.

Python

motion = human("clip.mp4") # HumanMotion: joints_world (T, 33, 3), root_world (T, 3), kp2d, valid

One person per frame, 33 MediaPipe keypoints (JOINTS). Metres. joints_world: z up, ground z = 0, x/y centred on the first frame's root (approximate grounding, see the module docstring); joints_cam: camera frame (x right, y down, z forward); joints_local: hip-centred.

docs.title: tools
docs.text:
Hylo tool adapters (RFC-0006 part 8): perception and motion models, each run as a worker in its own uv environment on the CPU (a GPU only makes them faster).

  • runner: worker processes, file exchange (JSON, .npz, .png, .glb, .mp4), timing, provenance, persistent workers
  • segment: text prompts -> instance masks (SAM 3); Sam3Segmenter implements the hylo.manip segmenter interface
  • depth: one image -> metric depth, points, normals, intrinsics (MoGe-2)
  • gravity: one image -> gravity direction (roll, pitch) and focal length (GeoCalib)
  • mesh: image + mask -> object mesh (SAM 3D Objects when access is granted; depth back-projection fallback)
  • convex: mesh -> convex collision parts (CoACD) and an MJCF snippet
  • hands: video -> per-frame 3D hand poses (WiLoR with MANO; MediaPipe Hands keypoints fallback)
  • human: video -> human motion (GVHMR with SMPL; MediaPipe Pose 3D keypoints fallback)
  • text_motion: text -> humanoid joint trajectories and a retargeting hook
  • render: MuJoCo scene / trajectory -> MP4 (Blender Cycles on the CPU; MuJoCo offscreen fallback)

docs.title: mesh
docs.text:
mesh: image + mask -> object mesh (.glb and .obj).

hylo tool mesh IMAGE MASK [--depth DEPTH.npz] [--backend auto|sam3d|depth] [--method carve|hull|relief]
               [--scale S] [--out DIR]

Backends behind one interface: - sam3d: SAM 3D Objects (facebook/sam-3d-objects, gated). Used when the weights are accessible; while access is pending (403) auto says so and falls back. - depth (CPU fallback): metric depth (the depth tool, MoGe-2, unless a depth map is given) -> masked back-projection -> cleaned point cloud, back completed by reflection across the silhouette plane -> closed surface (frustum carving + marching cubes, or convex hull) with vertex colours, in metres in the camera frame (or world, with T_world_cam). scale corrects a known metric scale error of the depth (e.g. from a known object size or table distance).

MASK: a (H, W) bool .npy, a PNG (white = object) or a masks.npz from segment (--instance picks one; default union).

docs.title: physicalize
docs.text:
physicalize: a visual mesh -> collision geometry for a stage entity (one box, the hull, convex parts or voxel boxes).

hylo tool physicalize MESH [--strategy auto|box|hull|parts|voxels] [--density 500] [--mass KG] [--out DIR]
Python

p = physicalize("chair.obj") # Physical: path (collision.json), strategy, info

auto measures the mesh: one box when it fills at least 90% of its oriented bounding box, its convex hull when it is nearly convex (concavity = 1 - volume / hull volume below 0.25), convex parts (CoACD) when it is concave, and voxel boxes (filled voxels merged greedily into boxes) when a closed mesh would need more than 16 convex parts. Mass comes from the mesh volume and the density unless given.

docs.title: render
docs.text:
render: a MuJoCo scene or trajectory -> MP4 and a still, rendered offline on the CPU with a better look than MuJoCo's default (Blender Cycles; MuJoCo offscreen fallback).

hylo tool render SCENE.xml [--trajectory traj.npz] [--simulate SECONDS] [--camera orbit|fixed|track|NAME]
                 [--backend auto|blender|mujoco] [--width 640 --height 360 --fps 30 --samples 32] [--out DIR]
Python

r = render("scene.xml", simulate=2.0) # Rendering: video, still, backend, frames, result r = render("scene.xml", trajectory={"qpos": qpos, "time": t}, camera="track")

Trajectory: .npz (or a dict) with qpos (T, nq) and optionally time (T,) seconds or fps; resampled to --fps. Without a trajectory the scene is simulated for --simulate seconds, or shown static for --duration seconds with the camera path. Camera paths: orbit (eased arc of --orbit-degrees around the scene), fixed, track (follows the moving bodies), or a camera of the MJCF.

Backends: blender runs the external Blender program ($HYLO_BLENDER, default ~/.local/opt/blender/blender; extra shared libraries from $HYLO_BLENDER_LIBS, os.pathsep-separated) with Cycles on the CPU: principled materials, soft area lights, a sky gradient, ground plane, AgX colour, OpenImageDenoise. mujoco uses MuJoCo's offscreen renderer (OSMesa or EGL; the user-space OSMesa under ~/.local/mesa is used when MUJOCO_GL is unset) with a three-light rig, 4096 shadow map, 8x MSAA, 2x supersampling, sky and floor. auto (default): blender, falling back to mujoco.

docs.title: runner
docs.text:
The common runner: every tool runs as a worker script in its own uv environment, on the CPU.

A worker is a standalone Python script under workers/ with inline PEP 723 dependencies (uv run --script), so heavy and conflicting dependencies (torch, transformers, mediapipe, coacd, ...) never enter the Hylo environment. The exchange is files: the runner writes the inputs (images as PNG, arrays as .npz, meshes as they are) and a request JSON into a work directory; the worker writes result.json and its output files (.npz, .png, .glb, .obj, .mp4, .xml) next to it. Each result carries timing and provenance (model id, revision, licence, backend, device).

Two ways to run a worker:

run_worker("segment", {"prompts": ["red can"]}, inputs={"image": rgb})      # one shot: new process per call
with ToolServer("segment") as srv:                                         # persistent: load the model once
    srv.call({"prompts": [...]}, inputs={"image": rgb})
Environment variables

HYLO_TOOLS_CACHE work directories and small model files (default ~/.cache/hylo/tools) HYLO_TOOLS_THREADS CPU threads per worker (default 32) HYLO_TOOLS_UV the uv executable (default: uv on PATH)

Model weights go to the default Hugging Face / torch caches.

Model: facebook/sam3 (gated: request access on Hugging Face and log in). About 4 s per prompt on a 558 x 558 image with 32 CPU threads once loaded; the image encoder runs once per image, each prompt reuses it.

docs.title: text_motion
docs.text:
text_motion: text -> humanoid motion (NVIDIA Kimodo on the CPU) with a retargeting hook for robot humanoids.

hylo tool text_motion "a person walks forward and waves" [--duration 4] [--model soma|g1] [--steps 100]
                      [--seed 0] [--no-retarget] [--no-render] [--out DIR]
Python

mo = text_motion("a person jumps twice", duration=3) # Motion: joints (T, J, 3), names, parents, fps, robot rob = retarget(mo, KeypointIKRetargeter(xml, mapping)) # any MuJoCo humanoid: map skeleton joints to its sites

Models (open weights, NVIDIA Open Model License; code Apache-2.0): Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1.2 (77-joint SOMA skeleton, joint positions directly, no SMPL files needed) and Kimodo-G1-RP-v1 (Unitree G1 joint angles directly: model="g1" returns MuJoCo qpos). The text encoder is LLM2Vec on Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct (gated on Hugging Face: accept the Llama 3 licence at https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct and log in); it runs on the CPU in fp32 (about 32 GB RAM). Output coordinates: metres, z up, x forward (MuJoCo convention).

Retargeting: the worker maps SOMA motion to a built-in MuJoCo humanoid by keypoint IK (retarget=True); in Hylo, retarget(motion, retargeter) runs any Retargeter (KeypointIKRetargeter needs mujoco).

docs.title: retarget
docs.text:
retarget(motion: Motion | tuple[ndarray, Sequence[str], float], retargeter: Retargeter | None = None) -> RobotMotion

The retargeting hook: map a skeleton motion to robot joint targets. Default: keypoint IK onto the built-in humanoid (needs mujoco in this environment). Pass a KeypointIKRetargeter(xml, mapping) for another robot, or any callable (joints, names, fps) -> RobotMotion.

No simulator handles, evaluators or model dependencies hylo.core.errors Error taxonomy (semantics follow inspect-robots errors.py and vla-eval EpisodeError.phase) hylo.core.events Typed events and a synchronous event bus hylo.core.experience Experience contracts (RFC-0003): action memory, lessons and skills. Contracts and protocols only; stores live in hylo.core.improvement The generators plugin contract (hylo.generator) and the records of an improvement campaign hylo.core.instrument Instruments (RFC-0004): learned components that measure or label instead of act hylo.core.kernel Execution kernel: the one episode loop, used for evaluation, learning rollouts and deployment hylo.core.learning Learning pipeline contracts (RFC-0004): data source -> labeler -> learner -> sealed artifact -> candidate -> gate hylo.core.memory Memory contracts (schema from our research notes) hylo.core.plugins Contract versions and plugin metadata (RFC-0005 part 4) hylo.core.policy Policies (plugin group "policies"): action-chunk generators that agents run, steer and compose hylo.core.profile Execution profiles (hylo.profile/v0.1): where components run on this machine, kept out of experiment configs hylo.core.reasoning Reasoning plugin contracts, one per role (each its own plugin group and version): hylo.core.registry Plugin registry: explicit registration, module:attr references (vla-eval style) and hylo.core.remote hylo.core.remote.agent_client RemoteAgent: an Agent proxy for an AgentServer subprocess (e.g. a VLA in its own torch venv) hylo.core.remote.agent_server AgentServer: hosts one Agent in its own process (and venv), mirroring the EnvServer hylo.core.remote.client RemoteEnvironment: an Environment proxy for an EnvServer subprocess hylo.core.remote.handlers Transport-agnostic request dispatch for the EnvServer and AgentServer protocols hylo.core.remote.protocol EnvServer protocol hylo.envserver/v0.1: newline-delimited JSON over a subprocess's stdio hylo.core.remote.server EnvServer: hosts one Environment in its own process (in practice its own venv/container), so hylo.core.remote.wire msgpack-numpy wire format (the one openpi uses), shared by the policy server (hylo-serve) and the openpi client hylo.core.remote.workcell Workcell API (hylo.workcell/v0.1): what a workcell serves and a control plane calls hylo.core.remote.ws WebSocket transport for the EnvServer / AgentServer protocols: run a simulator or a policy on another hylo.core.robot Robot description contract (hylo.robot/v0.1): what a manipulation environment tells tool-using agents about its hylo.core.safety SafetyShield: the single, non-bypassable checkpoint between any Agent and any Environment hylo.core.scene Table-top scene contract (hylo.scene/v0.1): a manipulation task written as data, so a model can author it, a hylo.core.scorecard Scorecards (hylo.scorecard/v0.1): the result of running one policy under one benchmark protocol hylo.core.scoring The scorers and gate_tests plugin contracts (hylo.scorer, hylo.gate_test) and the data they exchange hylo.core.seal Run evidence: hash-chain checks, run seals and a scan of what models were shown (RFC-0007 part 5) hylo.core.stage Stage contract (hylo.stage/v0.1): an open world as an entity tree that a person, a model or a program edits through hylo.core.stage_cli hylo stage: stages (hylo.stage/v0.1) on disk, with their revisions hylo.core.store Run and artifact store (hylo.store/v0.1): global ids, references instead of paths, deletion protection, sync hylo.core.task Task contracts. A TaskSpec covers both LIBERO-style declarative tasks with fixed init states and hylo.core.tooling Typed tool surfaces (hylo.tools/v0.1): what a tool-calling model may call, declared once and checked on every call hylo.core.trace Event-sourced, replayable episode trace hylo.core.types Core data contracts shared by every layer (design/interfaces/environment.md, agent.md) hylo.testing Test fixtures shipped with core: the test double environment (testing.point_reach) and the conformance kit hylo.testing.conformance Conformance kit: contract checks every plugin must pass (design/plugin-system.md §6) hylo.testing.learners A dependency-free learner for tests and conformance: summarises development runs into a sealed artifact hylo.testing.point_reach Test double: a deterministic 2-D point-mass environment ("testing.point_reach") for unit and conformance tests hylo.testing.setup Where plugin checks run: a real simulator when one is installed, the test double otherwise

docs.title: Benchmarking
docs.text:
Benchmarking provides validation evidence for the robot-skill lifecycle. Protocols score the agent or policy implementing a task capability under fixed conditions. Keep the task, robot, observations and implementation version with each result; a scorecard alone does not create a verified skill-library record.

To compare agents fairly, score each under the same evaluation protocol: a frozen, versioned experiment that fixes everything except the agent being scored (the agent usually wraps a policy). Each run writes a scorecard. The scorecards of one protocol form a leaderboard, and any two can be compared episode by episode.

The agent is passed as --policy. Despite the flag's name, it takes an agent spec.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Commands on this page run from bench/.

cd bench
uv run hylo bench list                     # built-in protocols, their versions and digests
uv run hylo bench show mujoco-reach        # one protocol, with its digest

Score a baseline and a candidate under the same protocol:

uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name ik-0.02 \
    --policy '{"type": "baseline.planar_ik", "params": {"kp": 0.02}}'
uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name ik-0.3 \
    --policy '{"type": "baseline.planar_ik", "params": {"kp": 0.3}}'
Output of the second run
{
  "scorecard": "scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.3.json",
  "success_mean": 1.0,
  "success_ci95": [0.963, 1.0],
  "n": 100
}

hylo bench run writes the run to OUT/runs/ and the scorecard to OUT/scorecards/<protocol>/<name>.json. --out sets OUT; the default is the working directory. All options are in the CLI reference.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
uv run hylo bench compare scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.3.json scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.02.json
Output
{
  "candidate": "ik-0.3",
  "baseline": "ik-0.02",
  "n_pairs": 100,
  "candidate_wins": 59,
  "parent_wins": 0,
  "p_value": 1.734723475976807e-18
}

hylo bench compare CANDIDATE BASELINE pairs the episodes both scorecards share by task and seed (n_pairs; an episode either side abstained on is dropped). A one-sided exact McNemar test on the pairs where exactly one agent succeeded (candidate_wins, parent_wins) asks whether the candidate wins more often. Two agents whose intervals overlap can still differ clearly this way (example). Scorecards with different protocol digests are refused.

The success interval is the 95% Wilson score interval, which stays inside [0, 1]: 100 successes in 100 episodes give [96.3%, 100%].

docs.title: Scorecards
docs.text:
A scorecard is a self-contained JSON file:

Field Content protocol, protocol_version, protocol_digest what was measured policy, agent the name given with --name, and the agent spec that ran metrics success_mean, steps_mean, safety_interventions_mean, n_episodes, n_scored, ... success_ci95 the 95% Wilson score interval on the success rate per_task success and episode count per task episodes per-episode success keyed task#seed, which compare pairs on run_dir, config_digest, code the run it came from on this machine, its config digest, and the git commit and package versions that ran notes, created_at free text (--notes), and when it was written

docs.title: Evaluation setup
docs.text:
An experiment config says what to run: benchmark and split, environment, agent, safety, trace, timing. A protocol is an experiment with the agent left out:

Experiment config Evaluation protocol Agent part of the config the only free input (--policy) Who writes it anyone, for any run built in, or your own YAML; a change is a new version Identity config digest protocol name, version and digest Result a run (evallog.json, traces) a run plus a scorecard Comparable with runs with the same config digest and code versions scorecards with the same protocol digest

The protocol digest does not cover package versions. Each scorecard records them under code (the digest).

docs.title: Next
docs.text:

  • The built-in protocols, and how to write your own.

  • Put several agents on a leaderboard.
  • Improve an agent with a campaign, whose gate uses the same paired test by default.

docs.title: Compare agents
docs.text: A leaderboard is every scorecard of one evaluation protocol (name, version and digest), ranked by success. There is no server: scorecards are JSON files, and hylo bench leaderboard collects them from directories.

docs.title: Run evaluations
docs.text:
Commands on this page run from bench/. --policy takes an agent spec, in one of three forms: JSON, an experiment config YAML (its agent is used), or a plugin name.

Agent specExperiment configPlugin name 
uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name ik-0.3 \
    --policy '{"type": "baseline.planar_ik", "params": {"kp": 0.3}}'

uv run hylo bench run libero-10-heldout --name smolvla-steered \
    --policy examples/configs/libero10_steered.yaml --workers 12

uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name random --policy baseline.random
Option Meaning --name the agent's name on the leaderboard; the scorecard file is the name with other characters than A-Za-z0-9_.- replaced by -, and a name that maps to an existing file overwrites it --out DIR runs go to DIR/runs, scorecards to DIR/scorecards (default: the working directory) --workers N parallel episodes --set KEY=VALUE execution settings only (which keys) --notes TEXT stored in the scorecard

Use digest-pinned store ids for artifacts so the scorecard names the exact weights.

docs.title: Compare results
docs.text:
uv run hylo bench leaderboard                          # ./scorecards
uv run hylo bench leaderboard runs/policies/scorecards --json
uv run hylo bench compare scorecards/mujoco-reach/flow-steering-4.json scorecards/mujoco-reach/bc.json

The leaderboard prints one Markdown table per protocol digest: rank, agent name, success %, 95% interval, scored episodes, mean steps. compare prints the paired result:

{
  "candidate": "flow+steering-4",
  "baseline": "bc",
  "n_pairs": 100,
  "candidate_wins": 18,
  "parent_wins": 5,
  "p_value": 0.005311012268066406
}

candidate_wins and parent_wins count episodes only the candidate or only the baseline solved (the key name is shared with campaigns). The test is explained in compare two scorecards.

docs.title: Reference policies
docs.text:
Published rankings now live in Research → Benchmarks. The MuJoCo reach benchmark separates the recorded protocol versions and links their source records.

To generate your own reference-policy scorecards, run from bench/:

uv run python examples/policies/compare.py --out runs/policies
uv run hylo bench leaderboard runs/policies/scorecards

Compare only scorecards with the same protocol name, version and digest. A published historical ranking may use a different digest from your current installation.

docs.title: Share results
docs.text:
• A scorecard is the unit to share.
  • run_dir is a path on your machine. To share the traces too, keep the run in the store and copy it to the other side with hylo store push.
  • Report held-out protocols for anything a campaign improved (libero-10-heldout, not libero-10).

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text: An evaluation protocol is a YAML file that fixes everything except the agent being scored (the agent usually wraps a policy). hylo-bench ships four, named by file name. You can also pass the path of your own (hylo bench run path/to/protocol.yaml ...).

docs.title: Built-in protocols
docs.text:
Protocol Scores Episodes Timing Requires mujoco-reach MuJoCo planar reach, standard held-out seeds 20000–20049 100: a fixed and a random target sync hylo-env-mujoco libero-10 LIBERO-10, all 50 stored init states per task 500 sync hylo-env-libero, envs/libero/setup.sh libero-10-heldout LIBERO-10, init states 40–49 100 sync as above libero-10-heldout-realtime as libero-10-heldout 100 realtime, virtual clock, 0.5 s per chunk as above 
cd bench
uv run hylo bench list        # names, versions and current digests

mujoco-reach. A planar two-link arm reaching a fixed and a random target, 50 seeds each. It takes a few seconds per agent on a CPU and is deterministic. Campaigns never use these seeds (two held-out sets).

libero-10. The standard LIBERO-10 evaluation: all 50 stored init states of each of the 10 long-horizon tasks. Campaigns tune on init states 0–39, so for a policy a campaign improved, report libero-10-heldout instead.

libero-10-heldout. Only init states 40–49, the campaigns' held-out split (splits).

libero-10-heldout-realtime. The same 100 episodes in realtime timing with a fixed 0.5 s latency on a virtual clock, so the score does not depend on the machine. The gap to libero-10-heldout shows what that delay costs a policy.

The LIBERO protocols need the libero-sim runtime (installation).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field In digest Meaning schema_version yes the protocol format version name, version yes the identity shown on leaderboards benchmark yes {type, split, params}: the benchmark plugin, the split that is scored, its parameters env yes, except env.remote {type, params} of the environment plugin; remote says where the simulator runs safety yes the safety shield config: max_delta, guards: [{type, params}] (safety) trace yes record_privileged, image_every timing yes, unless it is the default sync (default) or realtime, with its clock, latency and refill settings seed yes base seed of the run description no what the protocol is for workers no parallel episodes: how fast, not what requires no what must be installed or set up, for people

To change anything in the digest, write a new protocol version.

docs.title: Comparability
docs.text:
hylo bench show NAME prints the protocol and its current digest: the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over the fields marked "yes" above. Renaming a protocol or changing its version changes it. env.remote (where the simulator runs) is placement, not measurement, and is left out entirely. The digest does not cover code or package versions; each scorecard records those under code.

A scorecard keeps the digest it was written with, and leaderboards group scorecards by name, version and digest. A protocol edited without a new version therefore starts a new board instead of mixing incomparable numbers.

hylo bench run --set accepts only keys outside the digest: env.remote.*, workers and output_dir. Anything else is refused, because the scorecard would no longer belong to the protocol.

docs.title: Create a protocol
docs.text:
Copy a built-in protocol and change what you measure:

protocols/mujoco-table.yaml
schema_version: hylo.protocol/v0.1
name: mujoco-table
version: "1"
description: |
  MuJoCo table reach: held-out seeds of every table task.
benchmark: {type: mujoco/table-v0, split: heldout}
env: {type: mujoco.table_reach}
safety: {max_delta: 0.5}
trace: {record_privileged: true, image_every: 0}
workers: 8
requires: [hylo-env-mujoco]

uv run hylo bench show protocols/mujoco-table.yaml          # check the digest
uv run hylo bench run protocols/mujoco-table.yaml --policy composable.object_reach --name object-reach
  • If campaign-improved agents will be scored, use a split that no campaign learns from or gates on. The standard heldout split of a MuJoCo benchmark is disjoint from the campaign seeds.
  • Bump version for any change to a field in the digest, and say what changed in description.

To ship a protocol with hylo-bench, add the YAML file to bench/packages/hylo-bench/src/hylo/bench/protocols/.

docs.title: hylo tool
docs.text:
perception and motion tool adapters (segment, depth, gravity, mesh, convex, hands, human, text_motion, render)

All commands

`hylo tool`: run a perception or motion tool adapter on the CPU in its own environment.

    hylo tool list                     the tools, their models and licences
    hylo tool NAME [ARGS ...]          run one tool (hylo tool NAME --help for its arguments)

tools:
  segment      `segment`: text prompts -> instance masks and scores (SAM 3 through transformers, on the CPU).  [facebook/sam3, SAM License (Meta; custom, gated)]
  depth        `depth`: one image -> metric depth, camera-frame points, normals and intrinsics (MoGe-2, on the CPU).  [Ruicheng/moge-2-vitl-normal, MIT (code and weights)]
  gravity      `gravity`: one image -> camera gravity direction (roll, pitch) and focal length (GeoCalib, on the CPU).  [GeoCalib (geocalib-pinhole), Apache-2.0 code; CC-BY-4.0 weights]
  mesh         `mesh`: image + mask -> object mesh (.glb and .obj).  [SAM 3D Objects (facebook/sam-3d-objects) | fallback: MoGe-2 depth + frustum carving, SAM License (gated) | fallback: MIT (MoGe-2), BSD-3 (scikit-image), Apache-2.0]
  convex       `convex`: mesh -> convex collision parts (CoACD) and an MJCF snippet for MuJoCo.  [CoACD, MIT]
  physicalize  `physicalize`: a visual mesh -> collision geometry for a stage entity (one box, the hull, convex parts or voxel boxes).  [CoACD + trimesh, MIT]
  hands        `hands`: video -> per-frame 3D hand poses (WiLoR with MANO; MediaPipe Hands keypoints while MANO is missing).  [WiLoR (rolpotamias/WiLoR) + MANO; fallback MediaPipe Hand Landmarker, WiLoR CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 + MANO licence (non-commercial); fallback Apache-2.0]
  human        `human`: video -> world-grounded human motion (GVHMR with SMPL-X; MediaPipe Pose 3D keypoints meanwhile).  [GVHMR + SMPL-X (blocked); fallback MediaPipe Pose Landmarker (heavy), GVHMR non-commercial + SMPL/SMPL-X licences; fallback Apache-2.0]
  text_motion  `text_motion`: text -> humanoid motion (NVIDIA Kimodo on the CPU) with a retargeting hook for robot humanoids.  [nvidia/Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1.2 (+ nvidia/Kimodo-G1-RP-v1), NVIDIA Open Model License (weights), Apache-2.0 (code); text encoder Llama 3 Community License (gated)]
  render       `render`: a MuJoCo scene or trajectory -> MP4 and a still, rendered offline on the CPU with a better look than  [Blender Cycles (CPU) / MuJoCo offscreen, Blender GPL-3.0-or-later (external program); MuJoCo Apache-2.0]
