docs.title: Campaign configuration
docs.text:
Fields for an improvement campaign. Follow Campaigns for setup and execution.

Campaign keys:

Key Default Meaning experiment required the experiment config to improve, relative to the campaign file experiment_overrides {} dotted-path overrides applied to it proposer rule.steering the generator ({type, params}) diagnosis {} options for sorting failures, for example stall_steps, regrasp protocol see below the gate settings cycles 1 maximum cycles stop_after_no_progress 2 stop after this many consecutive cycles without a promotion budget_s none wall-clock limit for the campaign, checked before each cycle approval auto or manual out_dir runs/evolve the campaign directory, relative to the working directory

Gate settings (protocol:):

Key Default Meaning alpha 0.05 false-promotion rate per cycle, Holm-corrected across that cycle's candidates stage1_pairs 10 pairs used for early rejection stage1_max_deficit 2 reject in stage 1 when parent wins minus candidate wins is this or more gate_top_k 1 candidates sent to the gate gate_looks 1 sequential looks; the benchmark must provide gate_r1, ... spending_rho 3.0 alpha spent by look k is alpha * (k/K)^rho futility_stop true stop a candidate once it no longer leads the parent on the gate max_task_regression 0.15 veto: success on any task may not drop by more than this max_safety_increase 1.0 veto: mean safety interventions per episode may not rise by more than this max_candidates 8 candidates evaluated per cycle budget_s none wall-clock limit per cycle, checked before each candidate prescreen none {env: {type: world_model, params: {path}}, split, margin}: reject candidates a world model predicts below parent minus margin gate_test {type: mcnemar} the paired statistic (gate_tests plugin), for example {type: sign, params: {metric: steps, direction: lower}}

docs.title: Deployments repository
docs.text: A lab's robot setup (robot names, network addresses, joint limits, safety limits) belongs to the lab. Keep it in a private <lab>-deployments repository created from the deployments template. The repository holds YAML only; every environment, agent and guard it names comes from an installed Hylo package.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/HyloAI/hylo-deployments-template.git mylab-deployments
cd mylab-deployments
git remote set-url origin <your lab's private repository>

<lab>-deployments/
├── README.md
└── workcells/
    ├── sim_arm.yaml          a simulated arm, no hardware: bring-up and operator flow
    ├── so101.yaml            an SO-101 arm through LeRobot's Robot interface
    └── libero10_sim.yaml     LIBERO-10 in simulation, with the realtime runner

Add one workcell file per robot or simulator. Set up the robot computer first (deployment, step 2).

docs.title: Workcell
docs.text: Copy a template for your robot and set its port, identity, cameras, action limits and home pose. See Workcell configuration for the YAML example, field defaults and safety-limit settings.

docs.title: Safety limits
docs.text: Review changes to robot action limits and safety settings before starting a workcell. See workcell safety fields and Safety.

docs.title: Machine settings
docs.text: Keep out of the repository Put it here instead tokens, including a policy endpoint's token an environment variable or a secret store, passed when the workcell or the episode starts interpreter paths, environment variables the robot computer's execution profile motor calibration LeRobot's calibration files on the robot computer

docs.title: Start a workcell
docs.text:
From the deployments repository:

uv run hylo serve workcell --config workcells/sim_arm.yaml --port 8102
uv run hylo serve workcell --config workcells/so101.yaml --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100 --token "$HYLO_TOKEN"

A workcell listens on 127.0.0.1:8100 by default. Bind it to 0.0.0.0 only on a robot network, and always with --token (security). The workcell takes the token only as --token VALUE, so it is visible in the robot computer's process list.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: The variables Hylo reads, and the third-party variables its setup relies on.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
In the profile (recommended)In a config (one-off)In the shell

Set a component's variables on its runtime in the execution profile. set-runtime replaces the whole runtime, so pass every variable again:

uv run hylo profile set-runtime robot --python ~/robot/.venv/bin/python \
    --env HF_HOME=~/hf --env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

For LIBERO, run bench/envs/libero/setup.sh instead: it registers the full set.

env:
  type: libero
  remote: {runtime: libero-sim, env: {OMP_NUM_THREADS: "2", LP_NUM_THREADS: "4"}}

MUJOCO_GL=osmesa PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/.local/mesa/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
    uv run pytest bench/adapters/hylo-env-mujoco

Variables in the profile or a config reach only that component's subprocess. Set HYLO_PROFILE, HYLO_STORE and the contributor variables in the shell: Hylo reads them before it starts any component.

docs.title: Hylo
docs.text: Variable Read by Meaning Default HYLO_PROFILE every hylo command path of this machine's execution profile ~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml HYLO_STORE every hylo command the store directory; overrides store: in the profile the profile's store:, else ./runs HYLO_NO_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD the plugin registry 1: ignore installed plugin packages; only module:attr references and plugins registered in code work unset: installed plugins load

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text: Hylo has no fixed token variable. hylo serve env and hylo serve agent take --token-env NAME, and a remote.ws agent takes token_env: NAME in its params, so the token never appears on a command line. hylo serve policy, hylo serve workcell and hylo playground take --token VALUE, which shows in the machine's process list. The templates keep the token in HYLO_TOKEN. Security covers each service.

docs.title: Rendering and simulators
docs.text: Variable Used by Meaning MUJOCO_GL MuJoCo, LIBERO renderer: osmesa (CPU, user-space Mesa) or egl (GPU). Unset: no off-screen rendering, so no image observations PYOPENGL_PLATFORM LIBERO (robosuite) must match MUJOCO_GL (osmesa) LD_LIBRARY_PATH the libero-sim runtime where the user-space libOSMesa.so is LIBERO_CONFIG_PATH LIBERO the non-interactive LIBERO config that setup.sh writes OMP_NUM_THREADS, LP_NUM_THREADS numpy, OSMesa (llvmpipe) threads per simulator process; kept low because benchmarks run many workers

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Variable Used by Meaning HF_HOME LeRobot, Hugging Face Hub the model and dataset cache (bench/envs/hf-home in the lerobot runtime) HF_HUB_OFFLINE LeRobot 1: never download, use the cache. Set in the lerobot runtime TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM tokenizers false: no fork warnings in worker processes TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE torch 1: no torch.compile

docs.title: Program development
docs.text:
Variable Read by Meaning Default HYLO_ASSETS robot and motion asset loaders cache for downloaded robot/character assets, robot packs and policy files ~/.cache/hylo/assets HYLO_STAGES hylo stage where stages are kept runs/stages HYLO_TOOLS_CACHE tool runner worker requests, outputs and small model assets ~/.cache/hylo/tools HYLO_TOOLS_THREADS tool runner CPU threads per worker 32 HYLO_TOOLS_UV tool runner uv executable used for independent worker environments uv on PATH

Choose chat endpoints, model names and budgets in the model/session specification. API backends can read provider credentials from environment variables; keep credentials out of configs and recorded prompts. Model access and body-model registration requirements are backend-specific. See Developing programs.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Variable Read by Meaning Default HYLO_GIT_BASE harness/dev/bootstrap.sh clone missing repositories from $HYLO_GIT_BASE/hylo-<name>.git unset: missing repositories are skipped HYLO_HARNESS bench/envs/libero/setup.sh the harness checkout to install into the LIBERO venv ../harness, side by side HYLO_TEST_LLM the LLM reasoner tests 1: run the tests that call a local Ollama server unset: skipped

docs.title: Execution profiles
docs.text: Anything that depends only on the machine (interpreters, renderers, model caches, the store) goes in its execution profile, not in the experiment config.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
uv run hylo profile show                         # the profile and where it is
uv run hylo profile set-runtime robot --python ~/robot/.venv/bin/python --env HF_HOME=~/hf
uv run hylo profile remove-runtime robot
cd bench && uv run hylo store init runs          # record bench/runs as this machine's store

set-runtime replaces the entire runtime. Pass every --env you want to keep, or the ones you leave out are gone. --env KEY=VALUE can be repeated, and values are stored as given. --python is stored as an absolute path without resolving symlinks, so the interpreter stays in its venv.

bench/envs/libero/setup.sh builds the LIBERO and LeRobot venv and registers two runtimes, libero-sim and lerobot, with the paths of the bench checkout it ran in. Run it again to re-register them.

docs.title: Profile file
docs.text:
Each machine has one profile: ~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml, or wherever $HYLO_PROFILE points. A machine without a profile has no runtimes.

~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml
schema_version: hylo.profile/v0.1
runtimes:
  libero-sim:                                    # the LIBERO simulator
    python: /home/me/hylo/bench/envs/libero/.venv/bin/python
    env:
      MUJOCO_GL: osmesa
      LIBERO_CONFIG_PATH: /home/me/hylo/bench/envs/libero/config
store: /home/me/hylo/bench/runs                  # the run and artifact store

Environment variables lists the variables a runtime usually carries.

docs.title: Runtimes
docs.text:
A named runtime is a Python interpreter plus environment variables, for a component that needs its own venv: a simulator with pinned dependencies, a policy stack with its own torch, a robot SDK. Configs name it, never a path:

env:
  type: libero
  remote: {runtime: libero-sim}                  # run the environment in a subprocess with this runtime

A remote agent names its runtime the same way (experiments). The runtime: block of a workcell config is something else: it holds the workcell's realtime timing settings.

When a component starts in a runtime:

  1. Hylo looks up the name in this machine's profile. An unknown name is an error that lists the known runtimes and the set-runtime command that registers the missing one.
  2. An explicit python or env in the config overrides the runtime's values, for a one-off.
  3. ~ and $VARS in environment values, and in a python written by hand, are expanded when the component starts.
  4. The subprocess gets the parent's environment plus the runtime's variables.

docs.title: Store
docs.text: Hylo finds the store in this order: --root on hylo store, then $HYLO_STORE, then store: in the profile, then ./runs. hylo store where prints the one in use. See the store.

docs.title: Lab setup
docs.text:
Machine Typical runtimes Store workstation libero-sim, lerobot the main store, where campaigns and benchmarks write GPU machine lerobot (policy server, learners) its own, synced with hylo store push and pull robot computer robot (the robot SDK venv) where the workcell writes, pulled by the workstation

The profile belongs to one machine and is not committed anywhere. What a lab shares (workcell configs, safety limits) belongs in the deployments repository.

docs.title: Workcell configuration
docs.text: Fields read by hylo serve workcell --config FILE, defined by hylo.serve.workcell.WorkcellConfig. For setup and operator steps, use Deployment. Keep shared YAML files in a deployments repository.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
hylo serve workcell takes --config (required), --host (default 127.0.0.1), --port (default 8100) and --token. Its config:

Field Default Meaning name required the workcell's name; its run is <output_dir>/workcell-<name> env required any environment plugin, local or in another venv (remote: {runtime: ...}) benchmark none a benchmark whose validation tasks can be started by task_id; without it, free-form instructions only policy none default policy endpoint: url, protocol (hylo or openpi), token, params runtime see below the episode loop's timing safety {} safety shield config: max_delta, guards (safety) image_every 10 keep every n-th camera frame in the trace; every frame is streamed live split deployment the split recorded episodes get max_steps 600 step limit for free-form instructions; benchmark tasks have their own output_dir runs/workcell where the run is written, relative to the working directory

The workcell's runtime: block holds the episode loop's timing. It takes the keys of an experiment's timing:, with these differences:

Key Workcell default Meaning mode realtime experiments default to sync clock virtual set wall on hardware (robot setup) require_reset_confirm false wait for the operator's reset_done before the move to home verdict_timeout_s 0 how long to wait for a verdict when the environment cannot judge success record_privileged true store privileged state, when the environment has any

runtime.image_every has no effect: the top-level image_every decides which frames the trace keeps.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The template for a real arm:

workcells/so101.yaml
name: so101
env:
  type: lerobot.robot
  remote: {runtime: robot}              # named runtime from this machine's profile: the venv with lerobot + feetech
  params:
    robot:
      type: so101_follower
      params: {port: /dev/ttyACM0, id: arm1, max_relative_target: 10.0}
    cameras: {}                         # e.g. {front: agentview, wrist: wrist} with configured cameras
    action_low: [-110, -100, -100, -100, -160, 0]
    action_high: [110, 100, 100, 100, 160, 100]
    home: [0, -90, 90, 0, 0, 10]
    home_steps: 90
    control_hz: 30
policy: {url: "ws://gpu-box:8000/hylo", protocol: hylo}   # protocol: the policy wire protocol (hylo or openpi)
runtime:                                # realtime execution settings, not a named runtime
  clock: wall                           # the default is virtual: always set wall on hardware
  refill_steps: 10
  max_hold_steps: 30
  require_reset_confirm: true
  verdict_timeout_s: 120
safety: {max_delta: 8.0}
image_every: 5
max_steps: 900
output_dir: runs/workcell

Set clock: wall on hardware

The runtime: block's clock defaults to virtual. A real robot needs clock: wall.

What Where Notes motor calibration LeRobot's own calibration, keyed by the robot id (arm1) made with LeRobot's tools on the robot computer; Hylo does not store it joint limits (the action box) env.params.action_low, action_high in the robot's units (degrees, gripper 0-100); required for a real robot per-step limit in the robot env.params.robot.params.max_relative_target LeRobot clamps each commanded change; keep it home pose env.params.home, home_steps reset moves there by interpolation; each step is clipped to the action box only and does not pass through the safety shield (safety) cameras env.params.cameras robot camera name to observation name (agentview, wrist) control rate env.params.control_hz the wall-clock loop rate

docs.title: Safety limits
docs.text: safety: can only add guards or tighten limits. The action box itself comes from action_low and action_high in this file, so review changes there as safety changes. Safety describes every guard.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Serve package: configuration models and runtime implementation.
  • Workcell API: HTTP endpoints and request types.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text: This page maps Physical RSI, Worlds, Agents, Memory and Skills to their implementation: execution, recorded evidence, evaluation, improvement and deployment.

docs.title: Concepts and components
docs.text: Concept Implementation Details RSI learning jobs, candidate generation, evaluation gates, version registry Campaigns, Learning Worlds stage descriptions, robot packs, simulator environments and goal checks Worlds Agents policy agents, programs and typed tool calls through the episode loop Agents Memory spatial facts, scoped events, episode video, action banks and lesson books, with distinct consumers and lifetimes Memory Skills versioned library records, verification evidence, retrieval and application by supported agents Skills

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text: Goal Design response A light core hylo-core holds contracts, the episode loop, the safety shield, the trace and the plugin registry, and depends on a few small libraries; it contains no simulator, model, memory backend, scorer or improvement algorithm No simulator is required an environment is a contract; simulators and robots are plugins, and those with conflicting dependencies run in their own runtime behind the same contract Not tied to a language model or a VLA the episode loop knows only agents; policies, reasoners, memory and world models are parts of an agent Reasoning, memory and improvement can each be replaced separate packages that meet only through core contracts and the trace Scores independent of the agent scorers read traces only Reproducible results versioned configs with a digest, a run manifest, and seeds partitioned so that no seed crosses splits Evidence from real simulators a test double serves unit and conformance tests only; every example, protocol and campaign runs on a real simulator Works with existing tools an openpi-compatible policy server, LeRobot policies, robots and datasets

docs.title: From runs to deployed versions
docs.text:
The data flow behind Run, Improve, Verify and Deploy: the workcell's episodes become new runs.

Experiments produce runs and traces. Evaluation scores them; learners turn permitted data into sealed artifacts. Campaigns propose changes, test candidates and record promotions in active.json. A policy server can follow that version, and a workcell records new episodes as ordinary runs. Promotion alone changes nothing on a robot: the server and workcell must be configured, and hardware deployment requires human review and target validation. See Campaigns and Deployment for the operational rules.

docs.title: One episode loop
docs.text: One episode loop runs every episode: in evaluation, in Studio's live sandbox and in a workcell next to a robot. It passes every action through the safety shield, and every step emits events that a trace store writes per episode. Replay, scoring, judges, learners and Studio all read these traces. Timing (sync by default, or realtime) is part of what an experiment measures (timing). Realtime uses a deterministic virtual clock by default; on hardware, set clock: wall (deployment).

docs.title: Three rules
docs.text:
1. The episode loop only knows contracts. It runs an agent against an environment. Policies, memories, reasoners and world models live inside agents. Any simulator, robot or policy stack plugs in as a plugin.
  2. Every action passes the safety shield. Agents cannot bypass it, and campaign candidates may not change the safety settings. Overrides you write into a campaign config yourself are not checked (what is protected).
  3. Scoring reads traces only. A scorer sees what happened, never the agent's internals.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Each boundary in the picture stops one kind of coupling:

  • Agents and environments meet only in the loop. An agent never touches an environment, and an environment never calls an agent. The loop passes observations one way and approved actions the other, so the shield cannot be bypassed and privileged simulator state can go to the trace without reaching the agent.
  • Evaluation sees episodes, not agents. It decides which tasks and initial states run and scores the traces afterwards. Any agent is scored the same way, and a score can be recomputed from stored traces.
  • Improvement works through evaluation. A campaign never measures anything itself: it asks the evaluation layer to run splits, and its only output is a version that becomes the agent. Improvement methods can be added without touching how anything is measured.
  • Packages depend downwards only. Agents, memory, evaluation and improvement depend on the core, never on each other's internals; a boundary check enforces it.

docs.title: What an episode records
docs.text: Event Written by Used for episode.start episode loop task digest, seed, split, agent component versions, guards observation episode loop replay, training-data export agent.chunk episode loop what the policy proposed, with latency and provenance agent.decision the agent's reasoner or planner following its reasoning, diagnosing failures memory.retrieval, memory.write the agent's memory whether memory helped or misled the agent safety.review safety shield proposed and approved action, and why it was changed action episode loop the action actually executed step.result episode loop reward, termination, success, info privileged.state environment ground truth for scorers and diagnosis only error episode loop what failed, in which phase episode.end episode loop success, failure, error, safety abort or invalid infrastructure

docs.title: Measurement vs placement
docs.text: An experiment's identity is what it measures. Configs name runtimes and store ids, never paths, and each machine resolves them (profiles, store). So an experiment has the same digest on every machine; the one placement detail that is hashed is a remote.ws URL. The digest does not cover code versions or unpinned artifacts (when two runs are comparable). A result in simulation does not by itself predict the result on a robot.

docs.title: Packages and repositories
docs.text:
The harness is the base, and the leaf repositories depend on it only.

Repository Package What it holds hylo-harness hylo-core contracts, episode loop, safety shield, traces, plugin registry, store, hylo command hylo-eval benchmarks, splits, runner, scorers, paired statistics, gate tests hylo-agents agents that run a policy: plain, ensembled, steered; baselines hylo-policies reference policies, one per family, trained from your runs hylo-memory action memory, lessons, skills hylo-reasoners rule-based reasoners and choosers hylo-instruments success judges, value models, world models: they never act hylo-learn learner jobs, judge calibration and labelling, external data hylo-evolve campaigns: generators, the cascade, the gate, approvals, active versions hylo-catalog read-only queries over runs, campaigns and artifacts hylo-cli the harness's hylo subcommands hylo-manip robot tools: perception, kinematics, grasping and planning; current kinematics backend: MuJoCo adapters hylo-code-agents, hylo-tools, hylo-policy-lerobot, hylo-policy-openpi, hylo-policy-simplememvla, hylo-reasoner-llm, hylo-proposer-llm, hylo-data-video hylo-bench hylo-bench evaluation protocols, scorecards, leaderboards, paired comparison hylo-robosuite-contract shared robot-contract mapping for robosuite-based environments adapters hylo-env-mujoco, hylo-env-libero, hylo-env-robosuite, hylo-env-robocasa hylo-serve hylo-serve the policy server and the workcell adapters hylo-env-lerobot-robot: LeRobot robots and a simulated arm hylo-studio hylo-playground research/session record viewer, run explorer, web UI and workcell control plane hylo-plugins hylo-plugin-examples example plugins, written as a third party would hylo-docs (no code) this site hylo-deployments-template (no code) a template for a lab's private workcell configs and safety limits

Leaves never import each other, and serve's packages depend on hylo-core alone. Leaves cooperate only through formats defined in hylo-core: traces, artifact manifests, store ids, scorecards, active.json and the workcell API. A boundary lint enforces this (contributing).

docs.title: Key decisions
docs.text: Decision Why A light core with contracts and plugins; heavy stacks out of process No simulator, LLM or VLA is mandatory. Components with conflicting dependencies run in their own venvs. Improvement is a gated experiment A change is kept only if a paired test on unseen initial states agrees (campaigns). Experience as memory and skills, not only weights Retrieved successes, lessons and skills steer a frozen policy and are cheap to roll back. Persistent experience banks and libraries are built from development data and frozen during evaluation; episode-local spatial, event and video memory can record permitted observations (memory). A model decides what; deterministic layers decide what is valid and what happened A language model edits a world through checked patches, acts through controllers, and learns the result only from measured receipts and checks, so its mistakes cannot make the world inconsistent (worlds). Looking is separate from acting A tool-calling agent may measure freely, but each action is a proposal tied to what was seen, answered by a measured receipt; the task's check, hidden from the model, decides success (tool-calling agents). Everything learned is a sealed artifact with a role Each role earns trust its own way, and provenance travels with the artifact (learning). Measurement separated from placement; one episode loop; store ids The same identity on every machine, and the loop a robot runs. One base repository and leaves Changes to the base are atomic, the leaves stay independent, and the robot side stays small.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Choice Alternative Why not The episode loop owns execution the benchmark owns the loop, or a language-model framework does a benchmark-owned loop gives up per-step control, injected disturbances, isolation of privileged state and shadow replay; a model framework leaves safety and timing to code Hylo does not control The agent is the only intelligence the loop knows the loop orchestrates a reasoner and a policy itself that builds one cognitive architecture into the core, and end-to-end models need no reasoner An own event-sourced trace a training-dataset format, service-tracing spans, or chat-model evaluation logs none of them records reasoning, memory and safety and can also be replayed step by step; they are export targets instead A plain loop, not an agent-graph framework running control through a graph-execution framework its per-step overhead does not fit control at 5 to 50 Hz, and it brings a heavy dependency into the core Declarative candidates letting a model generate and run code directly without an isolated runtime that is unsafe; code enters only as sealed programs through research sessions, in a restricted namespace Typed contracts that refuse unknown fields plain data classes a typo fails loudly, every contract has a JSON schema, and one serialisation path serves traces, protocols and configs; the cost was about 5 µs per step against a 20 ms budget One base repository with leaf repositories one repository per package, or a single package per-package repositories need coordinated releases for every contract change; a single package cannot enforce layering or let anyone install the core alone No pickle in any protocol pickle for convenience loading pickle runs code; arrays travel as typed, whitelisted data

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Model-assisted development has recorded successes on specific simulated tasks. The promoted stacking program improves a deliberately weak parent; from-scratch local-model research remains unsuccessful. Free-scene and motion-free showcases and formal robosuite/RoboCasa program evaluations remain unrun.
  • Program execution uses an in-process restricted namespace. Artifact/candidate validation and guard ordering have known gaps; see Security and demos.
  • Campaigns run in the foreground of the shell that started them. Studio starts jobs as local subprocesses; it does not queue them.
  • The robot path has run with a simulated arm. No physical robot has been connected.

docs.title: Add a generator
docs.text: You will write a generator that proposes controller-gain changes, then run a campaign to test whether a candidate passes the gate. To build a model from runs instead, write a learner. You need the development workspace with hylo-bench.

docs.title: 1. Create a package
docs.text:
From the workspace root, create the package in plugins/packages/:

uv run hylo plugin new generator my-gain --dir plugins/packages

This creates plugins/packages/hylo-plugin-my-gain with the module wc_my_gain. Add license = "Apache-2.0" (or your licence) under [project] in its pyproject.toml. Then add it to the workspace and install it, as in adding a policy. From here on, run commands from bench/:

uv run python harness/dev/workspace.py
uv sync                                     # add the --group options you used in Installation
cd bench
uv run hylo plugins | grep my-gain

generators   my-gain                        hylo.generator/v0.1  unverified      Apache-2.0

docs.title: 2. Write propose()
docs.text:
A generator has a name and one method, propose(diagnosis, cfg, parent_id, archive), which returns (Candidate, hypothesis) pairs (contracts). The scaffold scales one numeric config value. Update its hypothesis to state the expected improvement:

src/wc_my_gain/plugin.py
from __future__ import annotations

from hylo.core.improvement import Candidate


class MyGainProposer:
    name = "my-gain@0.1"

    def __init__(self, path: str = "agent.params.kp", factors: tuple[float, ...] = (1.5,)) -> None:
        self.path, self.factors = path, factors

    def propose(self, diagnosis, cfg, parent_id, archive):
        node = cfg.model_dump(mode="json")
        for k in self.path.split("."):
            node = node[k]
        return [(Candidate(patch={self.path: float(node) * f}, rationale=f"scale by {f}", parent_id=parent_id,
                           generator=self.name), f"scaling {self.path} by {f} raises the success rate")
                for f in self.factors]

What propose() receives:

  • diagnosis: the parent's search results, including failure summaries and the run_dir for reading traces.
  • cfg: the parent's experiment config. parent_id names the parent.
  • archive: previous candidates and their results, including gate results (what generators see).

Each Candidate is a patch of dotted config paths, a rationale, the parent_id and the generator name. A patch may not touch the protected settings.

docs.title: 3. Validate
docs.text:
uv run hylo plugin check generator my-gain

generator my-gain@0.1: PASS
  [  ok] proposes (Candidate, hypothesis) pairs: 1 candidates
  [  ok] candidates stay outside protected scopes and apply to the config
  [  ok] candidates name their generator

The check calls propose() once with a MuJoCo planar reach diagnosis. A PASS means the candidates are well formed and allowed, not that they help.

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
A campaign configures its generator under the proposer key. Save this in bench/:

gain_campaign.yaml
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach-my-gain
experiment: examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi}, agent.params.kp: 0.02}
proposer: {type: my-gain, params: {factors: [4.0, 10.0]}}
cycles: 1
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-my-gain

The parent starts with a weak gain, kp: 0.02.

uv run hylo evolve run gain_campaign.yaml

[cycle 1] parent-search                      search     success=0.450 n=80 (2s)
[cycle 1] parent-search_val                  search_val success=0.400 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] cand-71e72a5f60-search_val         search_val success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] cand-223390d4c4-search_val         search_val success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] parent-gate                        gate       success=0.350 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] cand-71e72a5f60-gate               gate       success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] cand-71e72a5f60-heldout            heldout    success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] parent-heldout                     heldout    success=0.400 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] done: promoted=cand-71e72a5f60 heldout={...}

docs.title: 5. Inspect
docs.text: runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-my-gain/archive.jsonl has one entry per candidate. kp: 0.08 (factor 4) passed the gate and was promoted. kp: 0.2 (factor 10) succeeded on search_val but was archived without entering the gate (read the result).

docs.title: Add a learner
docs.text:
You will write a learner, build a sealed artifact from development runs, and let a campaign's gate decide on a candidate that uses it. A learner turns recorded runs into an artifact. For success judges see learning; for generators that propose changes directly, adding a generator.

You need the development workspace with hylo-bench.

docs.title: 1. Create a package
docs.text:
From the workspace root, create the package in plugins/packages/:

uv run hylo plugin new learner my-recap --dir plugins/packages

This creates plugins/packages/hylo-plugin-my-recap with the module wc_my_recap. Add license = "Apache-2.0" (or your licence) under [project] in its pyproject.toml. Then add it to the workspace and install it, as in adding a policy. From here on, run commands from bench/:

uv run python harness/dev/workspace.py
uv sync                                     # add the --group options you used in Installation
cd bench
uv run hylo plugins | grep my-recap

learners     my-recap                       hylo.learner/v0.1    unverified      Apache-2.0

Record some runs to learn from: 80 episodes of the planar IK controller with kp: 0.3 on a development split.

uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml --split search --output runs/demos \
    --set benchmark.params.protocol=rsi

docs.title: 2. Implement the contract
docs.text:
A learner has a name and one method, fit(job) -> ArtifactManifest. This example groups development runs by the agent's gain and seals an artifact that records the gain with the highest success rate:

src/wc_my_recap/plugin.py
"""Learner plugin: development runs in, one sealed artifact out."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from hylo.core.artifact import ArtifactManifest, Provenance, development_runs, write_manifest


class MyRecapLearner:
    name = "my-recap@0.1"

    def fit(self, job) -> ArtifactManifest:
        param = job.params.get("param", "kp")                         # the agent parameter to recap
        sources = development_runs(job.inputs, job.splits)           # gate / held-out are refused or skipped
        outcomes: dict[float, list[bool]] = {}
        for rd, _ in sources:
            value = json.loads((rd / "manifest.json").read_text())["config"]["agent"]["params"].get(param)
            samples = json.loads((rd / "evallog.json").read_text())["samples"]
            if value is not None:
                outcomes.setdefault(value, []).extend(s["status"] == "success" for s in samples)
        rates = {v: sum(ok) / len(ok) for v, ok in outcomes.items()}
        best = max(rates, key=rates.get)                             # the value with the highest success rate
        out = Path(job.out)
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (out / "recap.json").write_text(json.dumps({"param": param, "success_rate": {str(v): r for v, r in rates.items()}}))
        return write_manifest(out, kind="policy_params", role="behaviour",
                              metrics={"episodes": sum(map(len, outcomes.values())), "best": best, "best_success": rates[best]},
                              provenance=Provenance(builder=self.name, sources=[r for _, r in sources], params=dict(job.params)))

Three rules:

Read inputs with development_runs development_runs(job.inputs, job.splits) returns (run_dir, SourceRef) pairs for development runs only (which runs a learner may read). Write your files, then seal Write everything into job.out and call write_manifest last. The manifest records a content digest over the files and every source run. Changing a file afterwards makes the artifact fail verification. Choose kind and role role="behaviour" means the artifact changes what the robot does, so only a promotion may activate it. role="instrument" means it measures, and it is trusted only after calibration (artifact roles).

docs.title: 3. Validate
docs.text:
uv run hylo plugin check learner my-recap

learner my-recap: PASS
  [  ok] runs and seals a verifiable artifact: policy_params / behaviour, digest e3d96ccc61cef0ae
  [  ok] provenance lists development data only: splits ['search', 'search_val']
  [  ok] refuses gate / held-out splits
  [  ok] an identical job reuses the artifact

The check records the search, search_val and gate runs of MuJoCo planar reach and runs your learner on them. A PASS means it seals a valid artifact from development data and refuses gate data; whether the artifact is useful is step 5's job. The generated test in tests/ runs the same check under pytest.

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
A job names the learner, inputs, output and params (train an artifact):

recap.json
{"learner": "my-recap", "inputs": ["runs/demos"], "out": "runs/artifacts/recap"}

uv run hylo learn recap.json

{
  "out": "runs/artifacts/recap",
  "kind": "policy_params",
  "role": "behaviour",
  "digest": "e3d96ccc61cef0ae",
  "splits": ["search"],
  "metrics": {"episodes": 80, "best": 0.3, "best_success": 1.0}
}

A job that asks for gate data is refused before anything is read:

leak.json
{"learner": "my-recap", "inputs": ["runs/demos"], "out": "runs/artifacts/x", "splits": ["search", "gate"]}

hylo learn: SplitLeak: gate / heldout data must never be used to build anything that is gated on it: ['gate']

Look up the artifact's store id. The artifact must be inside your store, which is bench/runs after Installation:

uv run hylo store ref runs/artifacts/recap

artifact:recap@e3d96ccc61cef0ae

Configs reference artifacts by this id; keep the @digest (use ids in configs).

docs.title: 5. Integrate
docs.text:
The built-in learn generator connects a learner to a campaign. Each cycle it runs your learner on development runs, checks the artifact's metrics, and proposes a config patch that uses them. A campaign configures its generator under the proposer key. Save this in bench/:

recap_campaign.yaml
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach-recap
experiment: examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi}, agent.params.kp: 0.02}
proposer:
  type: learn
  params:
    learner: my-recap
    params: {param: kp}
    data_roots: [runs/demos]
    patch: {agent.params.kp: "{metrics.best}"}
    require: {best_success: 0.9}
    hypothesis: "a gain of {metrics.best}, the best in the development runs, reaches more targets in time"
cycles: 1
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-recap
data_roots More runs to learn from. The generator always adds this cycle's own development runs. patch The patch to propose. {metrics.best} is replaced by the value from the artifact's metrics. require Floors on the metrics. When one is not met, the generator proposes nothing.

The parent starts with a weak gain, kp: 0.02. The other parameters are in the hylo-evolve API.

uv run hylo evolve run recap_campaign.yaml

[cycle 1] parent-search                      search     success=0.450 n=80 (2s)
[cycle 1] parent-search_val                  search_val success=0.400 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] cand-77ee16b64c-search_val         search_val success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] parent-gate                        gate       success=0.350 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] cand-77ee16b64c-gate               gate       success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] cand-77ee16b64c-heldout            heldout    success=1.000 n=40 (0s)
[cycle 1] parent-heldout                     heldout    success=0.400 n=40 (1s)
[cycle 1] done: promoted=cand-77ee16b64c heldout={...}

The learner read runs/demos and the parent's search and search_val runs from this cycle; by default the learn generator reads both development splits (splits). It found kp: 0.3 best, so the candidate's patch is {"agent.params.kp": 0.3}. It passed the gate and was promoted. The archive entry in runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-recap/archive.jsonl links the verdict to the generator learn.my-recap@0.1 and the sealed artifact (read the result).

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
Online learnerHeavy dependencies

An online learner learns by acting: each iteration it returns agent specs, the runner evaluates them on a development split, and the learner updates from the results. hylo plugin new online_learner NAME scaffolds one, and online: true in the learn generator runs it. examples.cem (hylo-plugins) is the reference (extending Hylo).

A learner that needs torch runs in that venv: uv run hylo learn job.json --python /path/to/venv/bin/python, or python: in the learn generator. Install your package and Hylo's learning packages into that venv.

docs.title: Add a policy
docs.text:
You will write a policy, run it on MuJoCo planar reach, and end with its scorecard on the mujoco-reach leaderboard next to a baseline. You need the development workspace with hylo-bench.

A policy is the model inside an agent; built-in agents decide how its chunks run (policies). If your decision logic is more than drawing chunks from one model, write an agent instead (hylo plugin new agent NAME).

docs.title: 1. Create a package
docs.text:
From the workspace root, create the package in plugins/packages/:

uv run hylo plugin new policy my-reacher --dir plugins/packages

plugins/packages/hylo-plugin-my-reacher/
├── pyproject.toml              # dependencies and entry points
├── src/wc_my_reacher/
│   ├── __init__.py             # META: contract version and maturity
│   └── plugin.py               # MyReacherPolicy
└── tests/test_wc_my_reacher.py # conformance, and "it reaches the target"

Add a licence line under [project] in pyproject.toml, for example license = "Apache-2.0". Then add the package to the workspace and install it:

uv run python harness/dev/workspace.py      # adds every package in plugins/packages/ to the workspace
uv sync                                     # add the --group options you used in Installation
cd bench
uv run hylo plugins | grep my-reacher

policies     my-reacher                     hylo.policy/v0.1     unverified      Apache-2.0

A package in plugins/packages/ is a workspace member, so every uv sync keeps it installed, editable. Do not use the uv pip install -e hint that hylo plugin new prints: the next uv sync removes a package installed that way. From here on, run commands from bench/. META and maturity: extending Hylo.

docs.title: 2. Implement the contract
docs.text:
A policy provides four methods and inherits from nothing (contracts). The generated policy drives the planar arm with two-link inverse kinematics plus seeded noise. These are the methods you change:

src/wc_my_reacher/plugin.py (excerpt)
class MyReacherPolicy:
    def __init__(self, gain: float = 0.3, horizon: int = 8, noise: float = 0.05, l1: float = 0.3, l2: float = 0.25,
                 max_step: float = 0.05) -> None:
        self.gain, self.horizon, self.noise, self.l1, self.l2, self.max_step = gain, horizon, noise, l1, l2, max_step

    def spec(self) -> AgentSpec:
        # what it reads and what its actions mean: checked against the environment before the first step
        return AgentSpec(name="my-reacher", version="0.1", required_state=("qpos", "target_pos"),
                         action_semantics=ActionSemantics(control_mode="joint_delta", frame="base"), action_dim=2,
                         components={"policy": "my-reacher@0.1"})

    def reset(self, ctx: EpisodeContext) -> None:
        pass

    def default_execution_steps(self) -> int:
        return max(1, self.horizon // 2)

    # _ik(x, y): two-link inverse kinematics, as generated

    def sample(self, observation: Observation, seeds: list[int] | None, noise_scale: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        s = observation.state
        err = (self._ik(*np.asarray(s["target_pos"], float)[:2]) - np.asarray(s["qpos"], float) + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi
        a = np.clip(self.gain * err / self.max_step, -1.0, 1.0)
        rngs = [np.random.default_rng(x) for x in seeds] if seeds else [np.random.default_rng()]
        return np.stack([np.clip(a + self.noise * noise_scale * r.standard_normal((self.horizon, 2)), -1.0, 1.0)
                         for r in rngs])                                    # (N, T, A)
spec() The policy's identity and assumptions. Every key in required_state and required_cameras must exist in the environment's observations, and action_dim and the action semantics must match its action space. Before the first step, the episode loop compares this with the environment. A different control mode, rotation or action size stops the run. A different frame or gripper convention only warns. reset(ctx) Clears per-episode state. ctx.emit(type, payload) writes your own events into the trace. default_execution_steps() How many actions of a chunk run before the next call, unless the agent overrides it. It must not exceed the chunk length T. sample(observation, seeds, noise_scale) Returns (N, T, A) chunks, one per seed (N = 1 when seeds is None). Draw all randomness from seeds. Agents derive each seed from the task, the chunk index and the sample index, so a candidate and its parent see the same noise on the same init state. The campaign's paired tests rely on this. A deterministic policy ignores the seeds and returns N identical chunks. noise_scale scales the noise; 1.0 is the policy's own level.

Units and bounds

Chunks are in the units of the environment's action space: here, normalised joint deltas in [-1, 1]. The safety shield clips anything outside the bounds and counts larger excursions as interventions (safety).

docs.title: 3. Validate
docs.text:
uv run pytest ../plugins/packages/hylo-plugin-my-reacher/tests
uv run hylo plugin check policy my-reacher

2 passed in 0.23s
policy MyReacherPolicy: PASS
  [  ok] spec is compatible with the environment: my-reacher
  [  ok] sample returns finite (N, T, A) chunks of the action shape: chunk 8 x 2
  [  ok] the same seeds give the same chunks: stochastic (seeded)
  [  ok] default_execution_steps is within the chunk

The generated tests run the conformance check and one full episode that must reach the target. hylo plugin check checks only the interface and warns about missing metadata. Neither measures quality; step 5 does. More options are in testing.

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
Save an experiment config in bench/ (experiments). The policy agent runs your policy:

my_reacher.yaml
schema_version: hylo.experiment/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach-my-reacher
benchmark: {type: mujoco/reach-v0, split: validation}
env: {type: mujoco.planar_reach}
agent: {type: policy, params: {policy: {type: my-reacher}}}
output_dir: runs

uv run hylo run my_reacher.yaml

{
  "run_dir": "runs/mujoco-reach-my-reacher-validation-76e6326fbd816822-13c8a6",
  "config_digest": "76e6326fbd816822",
  "success_mean": 1.0,
  "safety_interventions_mean": 0.0,
  "steps_mean": 35.85,
  "n_episodes": 20,
  "n_scored": 20
}

The policy never knows which agent runs it. temporal_ensemble and steered take the same policy (choose an agent):

agent: {type: steered, params: {sampler: {type: my-reacher, params: {noise: 0.2}}, steering: {n_samples: 4, selector: medoid}}}

docs.title: 5. Evaluate
docs.text:
An evaluation protocol fixes everything except the agent being scored. Score the agent that runs your policy, and the planar IK baseline, under the mujoco-reach protocol:

uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name my-reacher \
    --policy '{"type": "policy", "params": {"policy": {"type": "my-reacher"}}}'
uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name planar-ik --policy baseline.planar_ik
uv run hylo bench leaderboard scorecards
uv run hylo bench compare scorecards/mujoco-reach/my-reacher.json scorecards/mujoco-reach/planar-ik.json

### mujoco-reach v1  (`a76c7037efb84660`)

| # | policy | success % | 95% CI | episodes | mean steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | my-reacher | 100.0 | 96.3–100.0 | 100 | 37 |
| 2 | planar-ik | 100.0 | 96.3–100.0 | 100 | 36 |

{
  "candidate": "my-reacher",
  "baseline": "planar-ik",
  "n_pairs": 100,
  "candidate_wins": 0,
  "parent_wins": 0,
  "p_value": 1.0
}

No episode separates the two, so p_value is 1.0 (compare two scorecards).

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
Learned weights. The constructor takes a path to a sealed artifact and loads the weights from it. Configs reference the artifact by its store id, spec() reports the artifact's digest in components, and weights_license names the licence of the weights (learning, store).

A model with its own stack. Three ways keep its dependencies out of the workspace venv:

In another venvBehind a serverAs a Hylo policy server 
agent:
  type: remote
  params: {ref: lerobot.steered, runtime: lerobot, params: {repo_id: lerobot/smolvla_libero}}

runtime names an interpreter from this machine's profile. Install your package, hylo-core and hylo-agents into that venv.

agent: {type: openpi, params: {url: "ws://gpu-box:8000", preset: libero, execution_steps: 5}}

A client of openpi's own policy server. The episode loop, the safety shield and the trace stay on this machine.

uv run hylo serve policy --config my_reacher.yaml --port 8001

agent: {type: remote.ws, params: {url: "ws://gpu-box:8001/hylo"}}

Serves the config's agent over WebSocket, one session at a time (deployment).

docs.title: Add an environment
docs.text:
You will add a simulator and end with a scorecard under your own evaluation protocol. The example, slider, is a point on a rail that must reach a goal. hylo-env-mujoco and hylo-env-libero in hylo-bench are the full references. You need the development workspace.

An environment is the simulator plus the task logic. It decides success; the agent never does.

docs.title: 1. Create a package
docs.text:
There is no hylo plugin new template for environments. From the workspace root, create the package by hand in plugins/packages/:

plugins/packages/hylo-env-slider/
├── pyproject.toml
└── src/hylo_env_slider/
    ├── __init__.py       # META
    └── env.py            # SliderEnv, slider_benchmark, SliderPolicy
pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "hylo-env-slider"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["hylo-core", "numpy>=1.24"]
license = "Apache-2.0"

[project.entry-points."hylo.envs"]
"slider" = "hylo_env_slider.env:SliderEnv"

[project.entry-points."hylo.benchmarks"]
"slider-v0" = "hylo_env_slider.env:slider_benchmark"

[project.entry-points."hylo.policies"]
"slider.p" = "hylo_env_slider.env:SliderPolicy"

[project.entry-points."hylo.meta"]
"hylo-env-slider" = "hylo_env_slider:META"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.24"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/hylo_env_slider"]
src/hylo_env_slider/__init__.py
META = {"contracts": {"envs": "hylo.env/v0.1", "benchmarks": "hylo.benchmark/v0.1", "policies": "hylo.policy/v0.1"},
        "maturity": "unverified"}

META and maturity: extending Hylo.

docs.title: 2. Implement the environment
docs.text:
An environment has four methods: spec, reset, step and close (contracts).

src/hylo_env_slider/env.py
"""A point on a rail that must reach a goal: the smallest useful Environment."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from hylo.core.agent import AgentSpec, EpisodeContext
from hylo.core.benchmark import Benchmark, rsi_splits
from hylo.core.task import TaskInstance, TaskSpec
from hylo.core.types import (Action, ActionSemantics, BoxSpace, EnvCapabilities, EnvSpec, Observation,
                             ObservationSpec, StepResult)

MAX_STEP = 0.02           # metres per control step at |action| = 1
SEMANTICS = ActionSemantics(control_mode="eef_delta_pos", frame="base", dim_labels=("x",), max_step=(MAX_STEP,))


class SliderEnv:
    def __init__(self, control_hz: float = 20.0) -> None:
        self.control_hz = control_hz
        self.pos = self.goal = 0.0
        self.task: TaskInstance | None = None

    def spec(self) -> EnvSpec:                            # cheap: no simulator work here
        return EnvSpec(
            name="slider", version="0.1",
            observation=ObservationSpec(state={"pos": (1,), "goal": (1,)}, units={"pos": "m", "goal": "m"}),
            action=BoxSpace(shape=(1,), low=(-1.0,), high=(1.0,), semantics=SEMANTICS),
            control_hz=self.control_hz,
            capabilities=EnvCapabilities(seedable=True))

    def reset(self, task: TaskInstance) -> Observation:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(task.seed)            # everything random comes from the seed
        self.task = task
        self.pos = float(rng.uniform(-0.5, 0.5))
        self.goal = float(task.spec.params.get("goal", rng.uniform(-0.5, 0.5)))
        return self._observe()

    def _observe(self) -> Observation:
        return Observation(state={"pos": np.array([self.pos]), "goal": np.array([self.goal])},
                           instruction=self.task.spec.instruction)

    def step(self, action: Action) -> StepResult:
        self.pos += float(np.asarray(action.data).reshape(-1)[0]) * MAX_STEP
        if not np.isfinite(self.pos):                     # an infrastructure fault, not a policy failure
            return StepResult(observation=self._observe(), reward=None, terminated=False, truncated=True,
                              info={"sim_error": "position is not finite"})
        if abs(self.pos) > 1.0:
            return StepResult(observation=self._observe(), reward=None, terminated=True, truncated=False,
                              success=False, info={"fail_reason": "left the rail"})
        success = abs(self.pos - self.goal) < 0.01
        return StepResult(observation=self._observe(), reward=-abs(self.pos - self.goal), terminated=success,
                          truncated=False, success=success)

    def close(self) -> None:
        pass

The rules this follows:

spec() declares observations and actions It builds no simulator and must serialize to JSON. Declare every state key with its shape and units, cameras as (H, W, 3) uint8, and the action box with its real bounds and semantics. max_step says what the units mean at |action| = 1. An environment can also declare an always-on workspace limit in EnvSpec.workspace. reset() depends on the seed only Draw all reset randomness from task.seed: the same seed must give the same init state, so a candidate and its parent face the same situations. Splits are sets of seeds; if several seeds share one stored state (LIBERO loads seed % 50), keep the splits disjoint in states, not only in seeds. step() separates success from ending success is the task predicate. terminated means the episode is over for task reasons; add info["fail_reason"] when it failed for good. truncated means it stopped for other reasons. success: None means the environment cannot judge. Simulator faults are not policy failures Return truncated=True with info["sim_error"], or raise EnvironmentFault. The episode is then infra_invalid, which scoring and campaigns keep apart from failures.

How the last step becomes an episode status is in execution lifecycle. Optional capabilities, such as snapshots or privileged state, are declared in EnvSpec.capabilities (interfaces: environment).

docs.title: 3. Define tasks
docs.text:
A TaskSpec describes one task: a globally unique id, version, instruction, max_steps, environment-specific params and tags. A Benchmark is tasks plus splits.

src/hylo_env_slider/env.py (continued)
def slider_benchmark(protocol: str = "rsi", n_states: int = 50) -> Benchmark:
    tasks = (TaskSpec(id="slider/reach", version="1", instruction="reach the goal", max_steps=100, tags=("slider",)),)
    splits = rsi_splits(n_states, (20, 30, 40)) if protocol == "rsi" else {"validation": tuple(range(1000, 1020))}
    return Benchmark(id="slider-v0", version="0.1", tasks=tasks, splits=splits)

The protocol argument chooses a split scheme, not an evaluation protocol; the name follows the built-in benchmarks. rsi_splits gives the four splits that campaigns need: search, search_val, gate and heldout, here 20, 10, 10 and 10 init states.

docs.title: 4. Validate
docs.text:
A conformance check needs an agent. Add this proportional controller, a policy, to env.py:

src/hylo_env_slider/env.py (continued)
class SliderPolicy:
    """A proportional controller: move a fraction `gain` of the remaining distance each step."""

    def __init__(self, gain: float = 0.5) -> None:
        self.gain = gain

    def spec(self) -> AgentSpec:
        return AgentSpec(name="slider.p", version="0.1", required_state=("pos", "goal"),
                         action_semantics=SEMANTICS, action_dim=1, components={"policy": "slider.p@0.1"})

    def reset(self, ctx: EpisodeContext) -> None:
        pass

    def default_execution_steps(self) -> int:
        return 1

    def sample(self, observation: Observation, seeds: list[int] | None, noise_scale: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        s = observation.state
        a = np.clip(self.gain * (s["goal"] - s["pos"]) / MAX_STEP, -1.0, 1.0)     # deterministic: seeds unused
        return np.tile(a.reshape(1, 1, 1), (len(seeds) if seeds else 1, 1, 1))   # (N, T=1, A=1)

Add the package to the workspace and install it, as in adding a policy. From here on, run commands from bench/:

uv run python harness/dev/workspace.py
uv sync                                     # add the --group options you used in Installation
cd bench
uv run hylo plugins | grep slider

envs         slider                         hylo.env/v0.1        unverified      Apache-2.0
policies     slider.p                       hylo.policy/v0.1     unverified      Apache-2.0
benchmarks   slider-v0                      hylo.benchmark/v0.1  unverified      Apache-2.0

Save an experiment config in bench/ and check it:

slider.yaml
schema_version: hylo.experiment/v0.1
name: slider-p
benchmark: {type: slider-v0, split: search_val}
env: {type: slider}
agent: {type: policy, params: {policy: {type: slider.p}}}
output_dir: runs

uv run hylo conformance slider.yaml --agent

environment SliderEnv: PASS
  [  ok] spec() is cheap and typed: 0.0 ms
  [  ok] spec survives JSON (wire format)
  [  ok] reset returns an Observation matching the spec: instruction='reach the goal'
  [  ok] reset is deterministic in the seed
  [  ok] step returns StepResult with separate success/terminated/truncated: 5 steps
  [skip] snapshot/restore reproduces the trajectory
  [  ok] close() works
agent PolicyAgent: PASS
  [  ok] spec is compatible with the environment: slider.p
  [  ok] act returns finite chunks of the env's action shape
  [  ok] reset leaves no state behind (same seed, same episode)

A PASS means the contract holds; it does not check your success predicate. The snapshot check skips because slider does not declare snapshot. Options for slow or nondeterministic simulators are in testing.

docs.title: 6. Add a protocol
docs.text:
An evaluation protocol fixes everything except the agent being scored:

slider-v1.yaml
schema_version: hylo.protocol/v0.1
name: slider-reach
version: "1"
description: |
  The slider reaches its goal: the 10 held-out init states (seeds 40-49).
benchmark: {type: slider-v0, split: heldout, params: {protocol: rsi}}
env: {type: slider}
trace: {record_privileged: false, image_every: 0}
workers: 4
requires: [hylo-env-slider]

uv run hylo bench show slider-v1.yaml          # digest: 1fdbb3364711b868
uv run hylo bench run slider-v1.yaml --name slider.p \
    --policy '{"type": "policy", "params": {"policy": {"type": "slider.p"}}}'
uv run hylo bench leaderboard scorecards

### slider-reach v1  (`1fdbb3364711b868`)

| # | policy | success % | 95% CI | episodes | mean steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | slider.p | 100.0 | 72.2–100.0 | 10 | 14 |

Ten episodes give a wide interval. The built-in protocols use 100 (MuJoCo reach) and 500 (LIBERO-10).
