docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: The rules for changing code in the Hylo repositories, and how to commit. Architecture shows how the repositories fit together.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
Follow installation: it checks the repositories out side by side and installs every package editable into one venv. After you add or remove a package, regenerate the workspace file from the workspace directory (the script needs Python 3.11 or later):

uv run --no-project --python '>=3.11' python harness/dev/workspace.py .
uv sync

The boundary lint fails while the workspace file is stale.

docs.title: Repository rules
docs.text:
harness/dev/repos.toml lists the repositories and what each may depend on. harness/dev/test_boundaries.py enforces these rules:

  1. Package layering. Every hylo.* import in a package's src/, and every module:attr or -m module string, targets a package allowed for it in the lint's ALLOWED map (package layering). Heavy libraries (torch, jax, mujoco, ...) are imported only in the adapter that wraps them.
  2. Repositories. A package imports or declares only packages of its own repository and of the repositories it depends on. The leaves (bench, serve, studio, plugins) depend on the harness and never on each other. The harness depends on no leaf.
  3. Robot side. serve's packages declare no Hylo dependency except hylo-core, so a robot computer needs no other Hylo package.
  4. No ../<repo>/ paths. Code and configs never point into a sibling repository. Shell scripts that need a sibling checkout read it from an environment variable such as HYLO_HARNESS.
  5. The workspace file is current.

docs.title: Add a package
docs.text:
1. Create it under packages/, or under adapters/ if it wraps a third-party stack, in the right repository. Give it a pyproject.toml (hatchling, src/ layout, a license), src/ and tests/.
  2. Register its plugins under the hylo.<group> entry-point groups. Declare their contract versions and maturity under hylo.meta (plugin system, plugin catalogue).
  3. Add its module prefix to OWNER and its allowed dependencies to ALLOWED in harness/dev/test_boundaries.py.
  4. Regenerate the workspace file (above) and run uv sync.
  5. Write its tests as described in testing, and run them.

A plugin outside the Hylo repositories is a package of its own. uv run hylo plugin new <group> <name> scaffolds one that passes its conformance check as generated (extending).

docs.title: Commits
docs.text:
• Run the tests and the boundary lint (testing). Both must pass.
  • One logical change per commit, in the repository it belongs to.
  • State what changed in the summary line. In the body, say why, and which tests or real runs you checked.
  • When you copy third-party code, record its source URL, commit and licence next to the copied code.
  • Discuss a change to a contract, a format or what an experiment measures with the maintainers before you write it. Bump the format's version when the change is not backward compatible (versioning).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Docs live in hylo-docs; its README says how to build them. A repository's own reference docs live in its docs/ directory. The harness's are rendered on this site under Developer Guide.

docs.title: Execution model
docs.text: How execution, evaluation, learning and deployment fit together. For a first run, use the quickstart; for system boundaries, read Architecture.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text:
One episode loop for everything. Evaluation, campaigns, the Studio's sandbox and a workcell next to a robot run the same loop. When deployment had a loop of its own, what the gate approved in simulation was not what the robot ran; with one loop it is.

Everything an episode does is recorded, and everything else reads the record. Each episode writes an append-only event stream: observations, the agent's chunks and decisions, memory retrievals, every safety review, every executed action, results. Scoring, diagnosis, replay, learners and the Studio read only these traces. Formats made for training data, for service calls or for chat messages each miss some of this (reasoning, memory, safety) or cannot be replayed, so the trace is Hylo's own and those formats are export targets.

An experiment's identity is what it measures. The digest covers the benchmark, environment, agent, safety, trace and timing settings, and leaves out where the experiment runs: output directories, worker counts, interpreters and paths. Configs name runtimes and store ids, and each machine resolves them, so the same experiment has the same identity on a workstation, a GPU machine and a robot computer.

Timing is part of the experiment. In sync timing the world waits for every policy call; in realtime it does not, and actions that went stale while the policy computed are dropped. A slow policy behaves differently on a robot than in a waiting simulation, so the difference is something to measure, not to hide. Realtime runs on a deterministic virtual clock in simulation, so it can be repeated.

Problems surface before the first step. The agent and the environment are checked for compatibility (control mode, rotation format, action dimensions) when they are bound, and privileged simulator state goes to the trace for scoring, never to the agent.

docs.title: Policy agents
docs.text:
The loop knows only agents. The episode loop calls an agent and nothing else. Policies, reasoners, memory and world models live inside agents. Building a reasoner-plus-policy loop into the core would fix one way of thinking about robots in place, and an end-to-end model that needs no reasoner would then be the odd one out.

A policy proposes, an agent decides. A policy samples action chunks from an observation. An agent decides how to use them: how many to sample, which to take, how many steps to run before asking again, when to resample, whether memory or a critic biases them. These components compose when their observation, action and conditioning interfaces match. A technique that needs flow noise, critic inputs or video context requires a compatible policy.

Randomness comes only from seeds. A stochastic policy may draw its noise only from the seeds it is given, and agents derive the seeds from the task, the chunk and the sample. Two agents compared on the same initial state draw matching noise when the runtime uses the same draw order and batching protocol. Keep those conditions fixed in paired comparisons: changing batch composition can change a shared RNG stream even with the same scene seeds.

Heavy stacks stay out of process. A policy with its own dependencies runs in its own runtime behind the same contract, and its trace events are relayed to the episode. No simulator, model framework or vision-language-action model is required by the core.

The contract is checked, not assumed. A conformance check runs every policy through shape, finiteness and seed determinism before it is used.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
Only the agent may differ. A comparison means something only when everything except the agent was the same: the tasks and their initial states, the environment, the safety settings, the timing, the scorers. A protocol fixes all of these and leaves the agent as its single free input. It is versioned and digested, and changing anything in it makes a new protocol rather than a different result under the old name.

Scorers read traces, never agents. A scorer sees what happened in an episode, recorded in its trace, and nothing of the agent's internals. A vision-language-action model, a language-model agent and a hand-written program are therefore scored in exactly the same way, and a score can be recomputed later from the stored traces. Privileged simulator state goes into the trace for scoring and is never shown to the agent.

Pair, do not pool. Two agents are compared on the same tasks with the same seeds, episode by episode. Which situations happened to be hard then cancels out, and only the pairs where exactly one agent succeeded carry information. That is why two agents whose intervals overlap can still differ clearly, and why the same paired test decides promotion in campaigns.

Honest intervals at the edges. Success rates are reported with Wilson intervals, which stay inside 0 to 1 and do not collapse to a point at 100 of 100.

What is measured, not where. The digest covers what defines the measurement and leaves out where it ran (machine paths, interpreters, worker counts), so the same protocol has the same identity on every machine. Code versions are recorded beside each scorecard rather than inside the digest. Scorecards from different protocol digests are refused, not compared.

Timing is part of the measurement. A policy that waits for the world (sync) and one that runs while the world moves (realtime) are different measurements. A protocol can score what a robot would run, with a fixed latency; never with a measured one, which would depend on the machine and its load.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
An improvement is an experiment, not an edit. A rule, a learner or a language model can propose a change; none of them is trusted. A change is kept only when a paired test on initial states that played no part in proposing or choosing it agrees, and every kept change can be undone. The proposer's confidence counts for nothing.

Four splits, one job each. Data that has been used to make a decision is no longer an independent test of that decision. So the initial states are divided by job: search to diagnose failures (proposers see these), search_val to choose among candidates, gate for one confirmatory test of the chosen candidate, and heldout for the report to the person who approves, never used to choose. Choosing on gate data would turn the gate into one more selection step; reporting on selection data would overstate the gain.

Spend episodes where they can matter. Episodes are the expensive resource, so the cascade orders its checks by cost. Stage 0 costs nothing: protected settings, validity, novelty, the provenance of any artifact the candidate names. Stage 1 runs a few pairs to drop clear losers. Stage 2 screens on all of search_val. Only the best reach the gate.

Pair everything. Parent and candidate use matched initial states and episode seeds. Keep the model, controller, batching and RNG protocol fixed when attributing a difference to memory or program changes. Scene seeds alone do not guarantee identical policy noise under different batch schedules. The default paired success test uses the pairs in which exactly one version succeeded.

One error budget per cycle. A cycle tests several candidates and may look at the gate more than once. Holm correction across candidates and an alpha-spending schedule across looks keep the chance of promoting a change that does not help at alpha per cycle.

Better on average is not enough. A candidate that raises the mean but breaks one task, or needs more safety interventions, is vetoed: success on any task may not fall beyond a tolerance, and interventions may not rise beyond one per episode.

Changes are declarative, and the goalposts are protected. A candidate is a config patch, which may name a sealed artifact or a sealed program. It may not touch safety, the benchmark, the trace, the scorers, the environment or the campaign's own settings: a change that raises its score by loosening safety or editing the scorer has improved nothing.

Cheap and reversible first. Improvements form a ladder by cost and risk. A frozen policy is improved from the bottom up, and every rung passes the same gate.

Every promotion can be undone. A candidate can be promoted only over the version that is active; the ledger records every promotion and rollback, with who and why. Configure approval: manual for hardware deployment so a person can review the held-out report before activation; the current campaign default is auto.

docs.title: Learning
docs.text:
One pipeline for everything learned. Learning from the agent's own runs, from demonstrations, from video, and learning judges or world models all take the same path: data, an optional labeller, a learner, a sealed artifact, a candidate, the gate. Before this pipeline, each learner had its own export, its own split guard and its own output format; now a new learner only has to read runs and write an artifact.

The trace store is the only source of truth. Everything learned is derived from recorded runs, and a sealed artifact records which runs and splits it read, which builder made it, with which parameters, and its content digest. Persistent experience artifacts can use the same provenance pipeline as learned weights. Episode-local observation memory has a separate lifecycle, described in Memory.

Three roles, three ways to earn trust. What an artifact is allowed to influence decides how it must be trusted.

An instrument never decides a gate verdict: in simulation the gate scores with ground truth, and a world model may only decide which candidates are worth real episodes. An instrument is never calibrated on, and never labels, the data it was built from. A model used in two roles is approved separately for each.

Split integrity is enforced twice. When an artifact is sealed, a guard refuses any provenance that includes gate or held-out runs. When a candidate reaches the gate, stage 0 checks again that every artifact it names still has its digest and never saw those splits. One bias is accepted and recorded: an artifact built from search_val can favour itself in the screen that uses search_val; the gate split stays clean.

Outside data comes in as runs. External datasets and videos enter as runs under their own split, with origin, licence and how their labels were made, and are checked against the gate and held-out initial states, so they follow the same rules as everything else.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Three roles in three places. Computation goes where the accelerators are (the policy server); safety, timing and the record go where the robot is (the workcell); people can watch and operate from anywhere (the control plane), but the control plane holds nothing that moves and never sends actions. The roles can share one laptop or use three machines without changing anything else.

The robot runs the loop the gate approved. The workcell runs the same episode loop as evaluation, in realtime timing. What a campaign promoted in simulation is executed by the same code on the robot.

The robot keeps moving while the policy thinks. Inference takes time, and a robot can neither stop the world nor execute actions that were planned for a moment that has passed. An action queue is refilled before it runs out, actions that went stale during inference are dropped, the arm holds its position when the queue is empty, and a watchdog ends the episode when the policy stops answering.

Promotion changes nothing on a robot by itself. A promoted version reaches the robot only when a policy server follows the campaign's active version and a workcell connects to that server. Anything that runs on hardware should be approved by a person first.

Robot episodes never claim success. There is no ground truth on a robot. An episode is labelled by the operator's verdict or by a calibrated judge, and the label records which.

The robot side stays small. The serving package depends on the core alone, so the robot computer installs little, and its episodes come back to the workstation as ordinary runs that can be scored, learned from and improved on.

docs.title: Tool-calling agents
docs.text:
Looking is separate from acting. Read tools (locate, measure, compute, ask for grasp poses) can be batched in one reply and change nothing. An action must be the only call in its reply. It is recorded as a proposal tied to the observation it was decided on, runs through the kernel and the safety shield, and is answered with a measured receipt and fresh images. The model therefore sees the effect of every action before it decides the next one.

Measurements expire. A target or grasp handle is tied to the moment it was measured. Once the robot has moved, an old handle is refused as stale and the model has to measure again: positions taken before a motion may no longer be true after it.

Refusing is not failing. An action the shield or the planner refuses, and that moved nothing, does not count as a decision, so a model is not punished for asking for something impossible and then correcting itself. Three identical refusals in a row end the episode, so it cannot loop forever.

The task decides success. finish(success) records what the model believes. The episode is scored by the task's own check, which the model never sees: a model that could see the check could stop the moment it passed, or argue with it.

Nothing is dropped from the record. Long episodes outgrow the model's context, so what the model is sent is a projection: recent turns verbatim, older results as references it can reopen, and under pressure a structured summary. The conversation itself is append-only, and everything left out of the projection stays in the trace.

The evidence holds up. The prompt is recorded layer by layer with digests, every trace line carries the hash of the line before it, and a sealed run can be checked later for any change. A person can steer a running episode, but any message marks it as human-assisted, and such episodes are kept out of autonomous results and training exports.

Tools are declared once. Each tool is one declaration (a kind, a closed argument schema and structured help). The same declaration serves native tool calls, a text protocol for models without them, the MCP server and these docs, so they cannot drift apart.

The same execution path as every agent. A tool action becomes action chunks that the episode kernel executes step by step through the safety shield, exactly as it does for a policy or a code agent. A model's run is therefore scored, traced and limited in the same way as any other agent's, and the results can be compared directly.

Under the hood
  • Tool surface. Every tool is typed: a name, a kind (read, act or end), a closed JSON schema for its arguments, and help in six parts (purpose, when to use, effect, returns, limits, errors). Calls are checked against the schema before they run; a bad call returns a structured error, not an exception.
  • Model backends. Messages use one neutral format with tool calls and tool results; adapters translate it for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including reasoning replay for models that need it) and the Anthropic API. Models without native tool calls write fenced tool blocks, which are parsed into the same calls.
  • Prompt layers. The system prompt is built from four layers (protocol, evidence rules, boundary, robot description), each recorded with its digest.
  • Context. Older tool results are stored and replaced by references the model can reopen with read_artifact; under token pressure older turns are folded into a summary with seven fixed keys (progress, confirmed, ruled_out, attempts, constraints, avoid, next_checks). A tool call and its result are always kept or dropped together.
One recorded episode, call by call

The stack episode in the video, with qwen3.5:35b-a3b running locally:

Call The model The robot and the tools 1 locates both blocks in one reply: two read calls purple block t1 and green block t2, measured in 3D at step 0 2 asks for grasp options on t1 options that fit the open hand; g3 is top-down with no IK error 3 grasps with g3: an action, alone in its reply proposal tied to step 0; receipt after 84 steps: closed with 0.6 mm error, lifted with 4.0 mm, holding before and after the lift 4 locates the green block again, since the robot has moved and t2 would now be refused as stale the same block as t7, measured at step 84 5 places on t7 lowered and released with 1.4 mm error; the episode ends, and the task's check reports success

Five model calls, two decisions, no refusals, 127 control steps, 93 seconds of wall time.

docs.title: Worlds
docs.text:
The design starts from a division of labour. A language model is good at deciding what a scene should contain and what to do next; it is unreliable at exact geometry, at remembering field names, and at judging its own results. A simulator is exact, but knows nothing about what anyone wants. So the model decides what, and a chain of deterministic layers turns that into a simulation and turns the simulation back into measured facts. Each layer accepts only what it can check, and each boundary is there to stop one kind of mistake.

Language to patches. The model never writes a scene file. It edits through tool calls whose arguments are checked against a closed schema: add, remove, update or move one entity. A scene file written in one piece is long, fails as a whole, and cannot be compared or merged with someone else's change. A patch is small, says exactly what it changes, and can be checked before anything happens.

Patches to stage revisions. The stage is the single description of the scene, shared by the model, the Studio and a person. A patch is validated as a whole (unique names, existing parents, no mounting cycles, valid rotations, one geometry per entity) and applied to the revision it was based on. A valid patch makes a new revision; an invalid or outdated one changes nothing. Because every revision is kept, every step can be undone.

Stage to compiled model. A robot is named, not described: the stage says pack: go2, and the pack supplies the model files at a pinned commit, the home posture, the drive, the gripper and the controls. Compilation attaches each robot under its own prefix in one MuJoCo model, together with the shapes, meshes, cameras, lights and people. A language model cannot be expected to write a robot model, and a robot model written anew for each scene would never be the same twice.

Compiled model to world. A build starts a new generation of the world and reports what is hard to see in data: which entities are fixed in place and which can move, and which parts overlap at the start. Problems surface before anything moves, and the generation is what every later action is bound to.

Actions through controllers. The model asks for intents at its own pace: walk forward at this speed, move the tool point there, fly to this point, run this walking policy. Controllers turn each intent into control at the simulation rate (a trot gait, inverse kinematics, attitude control, a pretrained policy). A model decides once every few seconds; a robot needs commands hundreds of times a second, so the model is never asked for joint torques.

World to receipts and checks. What happened is measured by the simulation and returned as receipts (distance, turn, joint error, whether the gripper holds something). Goals are predicates evaluated on the world, and a failure names what was expected, what was measured and why (NOT_LIFTED, DISTANCE_NOT_MET). These are the model's only source of facts about the result, and the feedback it corrects itself with: a refused patch is fixed, an overlap is moved apart, a failed check leads to another action.

The model can be wrong at every step without the world becoming inconsistent: a bad patch is refused, a stale action is refused, an impossible request returns as a failed receipt, an unmet goal is reported with its measurements. What the layers cannot prevent is a model that misreports its result or rewrites its own goal (a local model was recorded lowering its own threshold until the check passed). That is why a goal that decides success is defined outside the session, as in role campaigns, and why results are read from receipts and checks rather than from the model's summary.

Actions are bound to what was seen. A model decides on a picture of the past. An action names the generation it was decided on, and after a rebuild or a reset an old action is refused as stale. An action id makes retries safe: the same id never runs twice. Several robots' actions in one call start in the same step.

Time passes only during actions. While the model thinks, the world stands still, so a slow model sees the same world as a fast one and a session can be replayed.

Robots come from pinned sources, and weights are never executed. Robot models are fetched from their public repositories at a fixed commit and checked file by file; nothing is vendored. Pretrained walking policies are read from their files as tensors and run with numpy, and a policy is refused when its joints or timing do not match the robot.

The same tools for everyone. A chat model, a person in the Studio, a coding agent over MCP and a role campaign all use the same tools, so whatever a model claims it did can be checked with the same calls.

docs.title: Program repair
docs.text:
Experimental

Recorded real-model probes produced no promoted candidate. Use the probe results to assess this path. For the standard workflow, follow Program skills.

docs.title: Phase-guided repair
docs.text:
harness.program is an optional proposer in hylo-code-agents. It uses phase-scoped program repair and notes within Hylo's research runtime and campaign gate.

The model proposes observable phases, repairs solve(robot) on search cases, and can distill notes connecting a failed case to a successful replay in the selected program. All selected development cases must pass before a candidate is returned. Invalid notes are discarded without discarding an otherwise valid program.

proposer:
  type: harness.program
  params:
    model: {backend: ollama, model: gpt-oss:20b, reasoning_effort: low}
    dev: 6
    budget: {turns: 40, submits: 6, resets: 12}
    out_root: runs/harness-program/proposals
    repair_campaigns: [runs/harness-program]

Use this block within a campaign configuration. The alias requires the updated adapter entry-point metadata; the equivalent module reference is hylo.codeagents.harness_evolution:HarnessEvolutionProposer.

Completed program revisions are automatically submitted within the budget. Unchanged collected source and explicit submissions are not duplicated. The ordinary research.llm proposer retains its explicit-submission behavior. Planning and optional distillation share the total model-call budget with development.

Repair notes and their evidence share the sealed program artifact. Recall checks both artifact integrity and the digest recorded in the admitted candidate, and reads only active promoted lineages. A gate-passing candidate awaiting approval contributes no notes. Rollback removes the retired branch's notes from subsequent recall. A note's transfer to another task remains unverified even when its containing program passed a gate.

The phase plan is guidance for generated code, not a centrally enforced phase interpreter. Using a frozen VLA requires a toolkit that exposes one; there is no automatic SimpleMemVLA handover. The recorded real-model probes produced no promoted candidate. See the phase-guided example and probe results before choosing this experimental path.

The example campaign, workflow diagram and probe runner are under harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/harness_evolution/ in the workspace. See the code-agent API and campaign guide for the surrounding runtime and version lifecycle.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Every package tests itself. A test double lets the harness check its contracts without a simulator. The real simulators check what the double cannot. A boundary lint keeps the repositories apart.

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
Run these from the workspace directory, not from bench/:

uv run pytest harness/packages harness/adapters harness/tests harness/dev \
    bench/packages bench/adapters serve/packages serve/adapters studio/packages plugins/packages
uv run pytest harness                           # one repository
uv run pytest harness/packages/hylo-core        # one package
uv run pytest harness/dev                       # the boundary lint only
uv run pytest -rs                               # also list why tests skipped

Tests that need a missing repository skip. To check that a repository stands on its own, build a workspace from fresh clones:

mkdir /tmp/ws && cd /tmp/ws
git clone /path/to/harness harness && git clone /path/to/bench bench      # any subset that includes the harness
bash harness/dev/bootstrap.sh                                             # writes pyproject.toml, runs uv sync
uv run pytest

List only directories present in your checkout. Explicit paths avoid collecting upstream tests in downloaded simulator source trees such as bench/envs/robocasa/src-robocasa. Some code-agent and example tests automatically call Ollama if a configured local model is reachable; the explicit path list above does not disable them. HYLO_TEST_LLM controls the reasoner tests, not every live-model test. Review those tests before a network-free run.

There is no CI. Before pushing, run the project test directories in a workspace with the repositories you changed, and uv run hylo conformance CONFIG --agent on the MuJoCo example configs.

Unit tests run on the test double or on recorded data, finish in seconds, and need nothing but the venv. Tests in bench, plugins and the CLI templates run MuJoCo episodes. The LIBERO test starts the simulator in its own venv.

docs.title: Skipped tests
docs.text: Test Skips unless To enable hylo-env-libero: test_remote_libero_episode_runs_end_to_end the libero-sim runtime is in the profile (or bench/envs/libero/.venv exists), and user-space OSMesa is installed bench/scripts/install-osmesa-user.sh, then bench/envs/libero/setup.sh (installation) hylo-env-mujoco: test_vision_variant_adds_camera_images_only_while_visible MUJOCO_GL is egl or osmesa MUJOCO_GL=osmesa PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/.local/mesa/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu uv run pytest bench/adapters/hylo-env-mujoco hylo-reasoner-llm: the live LLM chooser test HYLO_TEST_LLM=1 a local Ollama server with the configured model, then HYLO_TEST_LLM=1 uv run pytest harness/adapters/hylo-reasoner-llm hylo-cli: the policy and agent template tests hylo.envs.mujoco is importable check out hylo-bench next to the harness hylo-plugin-examples: all hylo.envs.mujoco is importable hylo-bench hylo-playground: the control-plane test with a real workcell hylo.serve is importable (a fake workcell is used otherwise) hylo-serve hylo-playground: test_playground.py httpx is importable the workspace's dev dependency group, which uv sync installs

docs.title: Package tests
docs.text:
1. Put tests in <package>/tests/, importing the package by its installed name.
  2. Call the conformance check for each plugin the package registers (see below). The hylo plugin new templates generate tests that already do.
  3. Use check_experiment() for environment-dependent checks, so the tests run with the harness alone and on MuJoCo when bench is present.
  4. Skip, with a reason, what needs hardware, a model download, a network service, another repository or an optional dependency (pytest.importorskip(..., reason=...), pytest.mark.skipif(..., reason=...)). Never skip for a missing required dependency: that is a packaging error, and the test should fail.
  5. Keep tests that run a simulator small (a few episodes, short max_steps), seeded, and asserting on outcomes that do not depend on timing. A realtime test uses timing: {mode: realtime, clock: virtual} with a fixed latency_s, so it is deterministic.

The steps for creating the package itself are in contributing.

docs.title: Test doubles
docs.text:
hylo.testing ships with hylo-core. Its plugins are named testing.*, are declared test-double in the plugin catalogue, and are hidden from hylo plugins unless --all is given.

Plugin Group Package testing.point_reach envs hylo-core testing/reach-v0 benchmarks hylo-eval testing.p_controller, testing.landmark agents hylo-agents testing.rule_landmark reasoners hylo-reasoners testing.summary learners hylo-core

A test double, not an evaluation environment

It exists so contract tests run without a simulator. Examples, protocols, campaigns and published numbers use real simulators (MuJoCo, LIBERO).

hylo.testing.setup.check_experiment(experiment=None, prefer="auto") chooses where environment-dependent checks run. An explicit experiment (a config path or an ExperimentConfig) always wins.

prefer Result "auto" MuJoCo planar reach (with the IK controller) when hylo-bench's mujoco.planar_reach is registered, else the test double "mujoco" MuJoCo planar reach, or RuntimeError: MuJoCo planar reach is not installed (hylo-bench: hylo-env-mujoco) "double" the test double

A conformance test for a policy. MyPolicy stands for your own class:

from hylo.testing.conformance import check_policy
from hylo.testing.setup import check_experiment, env_and_task

def test_conformance():
    env, task = env_and_task(check_experiment())
    try:
        report = check_policy(MyPolicy(), env, task)
        assert report.ok, report.summary()
    finally:
        env.close()

docs.title: Conformance kits
docs.text:
Every contract has a check that a plugin's own tests call. The checks live in hylo.testing.conformance (hylo-core), hylo.eval.conformance, hylo.learn.conformance and hylo.evolve.conformance. The CLI runs the same checks on any registered plugin or config:

Contract Check From the CLI environment check_environment hylo conformance CONFIG agent check_agent hylo conformance CONFIG --agent, hylo plugin check agent NAME policy check_policy hylo plugin check policy NAME guard check_guard hylo plugin check guard NAME memory store check_memory_store scorer check_scorer gate test check_gate_test (hylo-eval) hylo plugin check gate_test NAME learner, online learner check_learner (hylo-learn) hylo plugin check learner NAME, hylo plugin check online_learner NAME data source check_datasource (hylo-learn) hylo plugin check datasource NAME success judge check_judge (hylo-learn) hylo plugin check judge NAME generator check_generator (hylo-evolve) hylo plugin check generator NAME

hylo plugin check builds the plugin with --params (JSON). It runs environment-dependent checks on --experiment, else MuJoCo planar reach when installed, else the test double. It also warns when the plugin's declaration (contract version, maturity, licence) is missing.

uv run hylo plugin check policy policy.flow --params '{"path": "artifact:policy.flow"}'
uv run hylo plugin check learner my-recap
uv run hylo conformance bench/examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml --agent

The learner and generator checks record runs on the search, search_val and gate splits. With --experiment, name a config whose benchmark has those splits (on MuJoCo: benchmark: {..., params: {protocol: rsi}}). bench/examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml uses the standard splits, so the learner check fails on it with KeyError: 'search'.

docs.title: Boundary lint
docs.text: harness/dev/test_boundaries.py runs one test per repository and package rule; uv run pytest harness/dev -v lists them. The path rule reads code and config files (.py, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .ts, .tsx, .json) in the code repositories. It does not read shell scripts, hylo-docs or the deployments template.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Where What <repo>/<packages or adapters>/<dist>/tests/ a package's own tests, next to its code; they import the package as installed harness/tests/integration/ cross-package checks inside the harness: remote environments and agents in another process, memory used through the episode loop harness/dev/test_boundaries.py the boundary lint for every repository that is checked out bench/packages/hylo-bench/tests/testing-reach.yaml a protocol over the test double, for hylo-bench's own tests only (not shipped)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Error messages as Hylo prints them, why they happen, and what to do. Paths in messages are shortened with .... Commands run from bench/ unless an entry says otherwise.

Message starts with Section ... pyproject.toml is stale, AssertionError: run python harness/dev/workspace.py, ModuleNotFoundError, ValidationError ... extra_forbidden Installing and setting up KeyError: "runtime '...' is not in ... Installing and setting up EnvironmentFault, KeyError: "no ... plugin named, IncompatibleComponents, watchdog: Running an experiment ValueError: overrides ..., ValueError: different protocols, KeyError: "unknown protocol Benchmarks and scorecards SplitLeak, ... content digest ... != manifest, a candidate rejected at stage 0 Learning and campaigns artifact:... not found, ... is referred to by, sync refused, rsync The store [Errno 98] ... address already in use, HTTP 401 or 409 from a workcell Serving and workcells IncompatiblePlugin, cannot build ..., warning: ... declares no contract version Writing plugins

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
.../pyproject.toml is stale: run python harness/dev/workspace.py . or AssertionError: run python harness/dev/workspace.py

Cause: the workspace file no longer matches the repositories present. A repository or package was added or removed, or workspace.py changed. workspace.py --check prints the first message; the boundary lint under pytest prints the second.

Fix: in the workspace directory, run:

uv run --no-project --python '>=3.11' python harness/dev/workspace.py .
uv sync

Check: uv run pytest harness/dev passes test_the_workspace_file_matches_the_repositories.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hylo.envs.mujoco' (or another Hylo package)

Cause: the repository that provides it is not checked out next to the harness, or uv sync has not run since it was added.

Fix: run harness/dev/bootstrap.sh in the workspace directory. It clones missing repositories when HYLO_GIT_BASE is set, and reinstalls everything (installation).

pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: ... Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden ...]

Cause: the config contains a key Hylo does not know. The line before names it, for example worker instead of workers.

Fix: correct the key. uv run hylo schema experiment prints the experiment schema.

KeyError: "runtime 'libero-sim' is not in ~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml (known: -); register it with: hylo profile set-runtime libero-sim --python PATH [--env KEY=VALUE ...]"

Cause: the config names a runtime this machine's profile does not have.

Fix: for libero-sim and lerobot, run bench/envs/libero/setup.sh, which builds the venv and registers both. For any other runtime, register its venv with uv run hylo profile set-runtime NAME --python PATH. If you keep the profile elsewhere, set HYLO_PROFILE in the shell.

Check: uv run hylo profile show lists the runtime. See execution profiles.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
EnvironmentFault: env server exited with code 1, after a traceback

Cause: a remote environment's process (env.remote) died before it answered. Its own traceback is printed above. Common causes:

  • the runtime's venv lacks the environment's package;
  • rendering is not set up: LIBERO needs MUJOCO_GL=osmesa, PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa and LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at user-space OSMesa;
  • LIBERO_CONFIG_PATH does not point at the config setup.sh wrote.

Fix: for LIBERO, rerun bench/scripts/install-osmesa-user.sh and bench/envs/libero/setup.sh. They install the package and register the libero-sim runtime with these variables.

Check: uv run hylo conformance CONFIG starts the environment and checks it. The same failure mid-episode shows as remote <method> failed: ..., and the episode is infra_invalid.

A LeRobot policy fails to load its weights with an offline error from huggingface_hub

Cause: the lerobot runtime sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and HF_HOME to bench/envs/hf-home, so nothing is downloaded during a run. The checkpoint is not in that cache.

Fix: download it once with the runtime's HF_HOME and with HF_HUB_OFFLINE unset, or point repo_id at a cached checkpoint (environment variables).

KeyError: "no policies plugin named 'policy.nope'; known: [...]"

Cause: no installed package registers that name in that group.

Fix: check the spelling against uv run hylo plugins (--all adds the test doubles). A plugin package you installed with uv pip install -e PATH is removed by the next uv sync, because it is not a workspace member: put it under plugins/packages/ and make it a member (adding a policy, step 1). If HYLO_NO_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 is set, installed plugins are not loaded at all: unset it.

IncompatibleComponents: action dim: agent 7 != env 2

Cause: the agent's spec and the environment's spec disagree. Hylo checks this before any episode runs. The same check reports env does not provide state keys [...], env does not provide cameras [...], control_mode: agent ... != env ... and rotation_repr: ....

Fix: pick an agent made for this environment, or adapt the agent's spec. uv run hylo conformance CONFIG --agent shows both specs.

Episodes end with error, safety_abort or infra_invalid instead of success or failure

Cause: see episode statuses. error and infra_invalid episodes are left out of the metrics, and error includes the agent's own exceptions and timeouts, so check these counts before reading the score.

Fix: read the episode's termination_reason (reading a run).

watchdog: no new actions for N steps in realtime runs

Cause: in realtime timing the action queue ran empty for more than max_hold_steps (default 100) consecutive steps. The policy is too slow for control_hz, or it stopped answering.

Fix: compare latency_s or the measured latency with refill_steps, or raise max_hold_steps for slow policies on a simulator (timing).

no target to hold for absolute control (the environment must provide hold_action)

Cause: a realtime episode with absolute actions needs the environment's hold_action to know what "hold still" means.

Fix: implement hold_action in the environment, or use delta actions.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
ValueError: overrides ['agent.params.kp'] would change what the protocol measures; only env.remote.*, workers

Cause: hylo bench run --set may change how a protocol runs, never what it measures.

Fix: change the agent (--policy), or write a new protocol.

ValueError: different protocols: mujoco-reach@1 vs ...

Cause: hylo bench compare pairs episodes only within one protocol digest.

Fix: re-evaluate the older agent under the current protocol before comparing. hylo bench show NAME prints the current digest.

KeyError: "unknown protocol 'nope'; built in: libero-10, libero-10-heldout, libero-10-heldout-realtime, mujoco-reach"

Fix: use a built-in name (uv run hylo bench list) or a path to a protocol YAML.

docs.title: Artifacts and campaigns
docs.text:
.../b/gain: content digest ca22895f89be761f != manifest 7c0e3c577ceeacab (modified after sealing)

Cause: a file in a sealed artifact changed after artifact.json was written, so it is no longer what its id names. Mutable artifacts (a lesson book while curating) are not checked.

Fix: rebuild it (rerun the learner job), or restore the original files.

Check: uv run hylo artifact PATH verifies the artifact and prints its manifest.

<id>: <path> now holds digest <d>

Cause: a config or candidate references artifact:<name>@<digest>, and the directory the store resolves holds a different digest.

Fix: reference the current digest, or restore the content.

SplitLeak: gate / heldout data must never be used to build anything that is gated on it: ['gate_r1']

Cause: a learner or judge was asked to read a gate* or heldout* split. Variants of the same guard: <run> is a 'gate' run; only ['search', 'search_val'] may be used (an explicit list of runs given to a learner) and refusing to seal <dir>: source <run> is a 'gate' run (at sealing).

Fix: build from development splits (search, search_val) only. See which runs a learner may read.

A candidate rejected by the stage-0 checks is recorded in the campaign archive with the reason:

behaviour artifacts with unknown provenance: [...]

Cause: the candidate references a behaviour artifact adopted without its training runs (hylo store adopt without --source). The stage-0 checks cannot rule out that it was trained on gate or held-out data.

Fix: rebuild the artifact with a learner, or adopt it again with --source for each run it was built from.

candidate <id> touches protected scope '<path>' or duplicate of an archived candidate

Cause: the generator proposed a change to a protected path, or a patch the archive already holds.

Fix: none needed: the stage-0 checks are working.

prescreen: world model predicts 0.40 vs parent 0.65

Cause: the campaign's gate settings (protocol.prescreen) turn on a world-model prescreen, and the model predicted the candidate to be worse than the parent by more than the margin (default 0.1).

Fix: none needed. If it rejects candidates you expected to pass, raise protocol.prescreen.margin or remove the prescreen.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
artifact:l10-trace-v2 not found in the store at .../runs

Cause: no run or sealed artifact with that id is under the store directory, even after the index was rebuilt. If another digest of the name exists, the message lists it: ...; with that name: [...].

Fix: check which store this machine uses: hylo store where prints it (lookup order). hylo store ls --name l10-trace-v2 lists what has the name. If the artifact is on another machine, hylo store pull HOST:PATH ID.

'l10-trace-v2' is not a store id (run:<id> or artifact:<name>[@<digest>])

Fix: ids start with run: or artifact:. hylo store ref PATH prints the id of a directory.

artifact:gain is ambiguous: ['artifact:gain@0c15194f963398b2', 'artifact:gain@7c0e3c577ceeacab']; add the digest

Cause: a bare name works only when exactly one artifact has it.

Fix: add the digest. Eight hex characters are enough.

artifact:gain@0c15194f963398b2 was removed at Sun Nov 1 04:19:38 2026 (superseded)

Cause: the entry was deleted with hylo store rm. The tombstone records when and why.

Fix: rebuild the artifact, pull it from a machine that still has it, or change the reference.

run:r1 is referred to by ['artifact:gain@0c15194f963398b2']; remove those first or pass force (with a reason)

Cause: something still uses this entry: an artifact built from it, or a campaign that names it.

Fix: hylo store show ID lists them. Remove those first, or force it with hylo store rm ID --force --reason "..." (the referrers are recorded).

sync refused, 1 conflict(s): [{'path': 'b/gain', 'here': 'artifact:gain@7c0e...', 'there': 'artifact:gain@fd51...'}]

Cause: the same path holds different content on the two machines. Sealed artifacts are never overwritten, so nothing was copied.

Fix: rename or remove one side (hylo store rm there), then sync again.

cannot list the store at robot:/data/runs: ..., rsync failed (N): ..., rsync is needed to sync with another machine

Cause: syncing with HOST:PATH runs ssh HOST hylo store --root PATH ls --json, then rsync.

Fix: the other machine needs ssh access without a prompt and hylo on its PATH. Otherwise pass --remote-command /path/to/hylo. This machine needs rsync.

Check: ssh HOST hylo store where prints the remote store.

run:<id>: indexed at <path> but missing in <store>

Cause: the index lists the entry, but its directory is gone, even after a rebuild.

Fix: remove <store>/.hylo-store/index.json and run hylo store index.

docs.title: Serve and Studio
docs.text:
ERROR: [Errno 98] error while attempting to bind on address ('127.0.0.1', 8765): address already in use

Cause: another process holds the port. The message comes from uvicorn.

Fix: stop that process, or start on another --port. Default ports: policy server 8000, workcell 8100, Studio (hylo playground) 8765, and hylo serve env / hylo serve agent also 8765.

A workcell episode ends at once; /status shows "state": "idle" and "last": {"error": "..."}

Cause: the episode failed to start or run, for example because the policy endpoint does not answer. The message is also broadcast on /events as {"type": "failed", ...}. The workcell stays up.

Fix: check the policy server (hylo serve policy) and the URL in the workcell config or the request.

HTTP 409 from POST /episodes: latched fault: e-stop by operator; clear it first / an episode is running / no policy endpoint (in the request or the workcell config)

Cause and fix:

  • An e-stop latches until an operator posts {"type": "clear_fault"} to /operator.
  • Only one episode runs at a time. Wait for it to end.
  • A policy endpoint is required, in the request or in the workcell config.
HTTP 401 missing or wrong token

Cause: the workcell or Studio was started with --token, and the request has no token or the wrong one.

Fix: send Authorization: Bearer <token> to a workcell (and ?token= on /events). Studio takes the x-token header or ?token=. See security.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
IncompatiblePlugin: policies plugin 'x' (pkg 1.2.0) implements hylo.policy/v1.0; this core implements hylo.policy/v0.1

Cause: the plugin declares a contract version this core cannot run: another major version, or a newer minor one.

Fix: install a plugin version written for this core, or upgrade the harness. See versioning.

cannot build policy 'policy.knn': TypeError: KNNPolicy.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'path'

Cause: hylo plugin check builds the plugin with --params (JSON), and this plugin needs a parameter.

Fix: pass it, for example hylo plugin check policy policy.knn --params '{"path": "artifact:policy.knn"}'.

warning: <dist> declares no contract version ... from hylo plugin check

Cause: the package has no hylo.meta declaration, or the declaration lacks maturity or licence. The plugin still loads.

Fix: add the declaration (extending, versioning).

docs.title: Inspect a run
docs.text:
Experiments lists the files of a run directory.

uv run hylo trace runs/<run_dir>                        # aggregate results, status counts, episode ids
uv run hylo trace runs/<run_dir> <episode_id>           # event counts and the episode.end payload

The episode.end event carries status and termination_reason. The termination_reason tells failure modes apart: max_steps, terminated, truncated, sim_error, or the text of the error that ended the episode. An error event carries phase and message.

docs.title: Report a bug
docs.text:
Include:

  1. the command and its full output: the traceback, and the child process's traceback for remote components;
  2. manifest.json of the run, which records the config, its digest, package versions, git commit, Python and platform;
  3. uv run hylo plugins --json for the plugins involved, and uv run hylo profile show;
  4. for one bad episode, uv run hylo trace RUN_DIR EPISODE_ID, and the episode's .jsonl if it is small;
  5. whether it reproduces on the test double or on MuJoCo (hylo plugin check ... --experiment), which separates a plugin problem from a simulator problem.

Before you send it, remove secrets from everything you attach: command lines and output, manifests, configs and the profile. Tokens can appear in all of them, for example as --token arguments or a policy endpoint's token.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
This page lists what carries a version or a digest, and what changes it.

Kind Example Answers Contract version hylo.policy/v0.1 can this plugin run on this core? Format schema version hylo.scorecard/v0.1 can this file or message be read? Digest config_digest: 2342f91d706e83e9 is this the same experiment, protocol or content? Package version 0.1.0.dev0 which code is installed?

Until the first release, contracts and formats may change without a deprecation period.

docs.title: Contract versions
docs.text:
Every plugin group is a contract with a version, named hylo.<name>/v0.1 after the group in the singular (envs is hylo.env/v0.1, gate_tests is hylo.gate_test/v0.1). All are at v0.1. The plugin system lists the groups.

A plugin package declares the versions it implements in a META dictionary, registered under the hylo.meta entry-point group (extending):

META = {"contracts": {"policies": "hylo.policy/v0.1", "learners": "hylo.learner/v0.1"}, "maturity": "implemented"}

A declared version runs on this core when it names the same contract, has the same major version, and its minor version is not newer than the core's:

Plugin declares Core implements Loads? hylo.policy/v0.1 hylo.policy/v0.1 yes hylo.policy/v1.0 hylo.policy/v1.3 yes: the core still supports what v1.0 plugins use hylo.policy/v1.4 hylo.policy/v1.3 no: the plugin may use features this core lacks hylo.policy/v0.1 hylo.policy/v1.0 no: another major version

The plugin registry checks the declaration before it imports an entry point, and raises IncompatiblePlugin on a mismatch. A plugin without a declaration still loads and is listed as undeclared, and hylo plugin check warns. module:attr references are not checked, because there is no package to ask.

docs.title: Schema versions
docs.text:
Files read through a Hylo contract (experiment configs, profiles, protocols, artifact manifests, scorecards, the store index, campaign configs) carry their schema version. They are refused when the version or a key is unknown, rather than misread. Old wc.* ids are renamed first (see Older data). Workcell configs have no version field but also refuse unknown keys. evallog.json is read as plain JSON: its version key is not checked.

Format Version Written as Experiment config hylo.experiment/v0.1 config YAML; the run's manifest.json Execution profile hylo.profile/v0.1 ~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml Store index hylo.store/v0.1 <store>/.hylo-store/index.json Artifact manifest hylo.artifact/v0.1 artifact.json Trace events hylo.trace/v0.1 episodes/<id>.jsonl, recorded in manifest.json Eval log hylo.evallog/v0.1 (key version) evallog.json Scorecard hylo.scorecard/v0.1 scorecards/<protocol>/<policy>.json Protocol hylo.protocol/v0.1 protocol YAML Campaign config hylo.evolve/v0.1 campaign YAML Active version hylo.active/v0.1 a campaign's active.json Workcell API hylo.workcell/v0.1 HTTP and WebSocket messages; workcell run manifests Env server protocol hylo.envserver/v0.1 the hello line of a remote environment Agent server protocol hylo.agentserver/v0.1 the hello of a remote agent or policy server Ingested runs hylo.external/v0.1 manifest.json of an external-data run

The remote protocols are matched exactly: a client that receives another hello fails with protocol mismatch .... Artifact payloads carry their own versions, and each loader refuses another version. hylo schema NAME prints the JSON Schema of the experiment config, task, env spec, agent spec, candidate, memory item and benchmark (formats).

docs.title: Digests
docs.text:
A digest names what something is, so that two results can be compared and an artifact cannot change unseen. All are SHA-256, truncated to 16 hex characters.

Digest Over Left out Experiment (config_digest) what the experiment measures (rules) where results go, workers, placement Benchmark id, version, every task's digest, the splits Task the whole task spec Protocol the protocol definition (rules) description, workers, requirements, placement Artifact content every file under the artifact directory, with its relative path artifact.json itself Learner job the learner, inputs, splits and params the output directory Candidate the patch, the parent and the kind its random id

Store ids are artifact:<name>@<content digest>, and stage 0 of a campaign re-verifies the content of every artifact a candidate references.

Changing what a digest covers changes it for every new run. Older runs and scorecards keep the digest they were recorded with, so they no longer compare.

docs.title: Older data
docs.text:
Hylo reads data written under its former name:

  • schema ids wc.<name>/v<x> are read as hylo.<name>/v<x>;
  • module references worldcurrent.* are read as hylo.*, and wc_examples as hylo_examples;
  • the policy server still answers on /wc as well as /hylo;
  • a workcell config's protocol: wc is read as hylo.

Nothing is rewritten on disk. Experiment and protocol digests recorded under the old name differ from the digests the same definitions get now, because the schema id is part of what is hashed. The same holds for runs recorded before placement (env.remote) was left out of the digest. To compare with such a run, run the older agent again. Artifact content digests did not change, so older store ids still resolve.

docs.title: Package releases
docs.text:
There are 23 packages, all at 0.1.0.dev0. Nothing is released to PyPI, and the repositories have no tags. Install from the GitHub repositories (https://github.com/HyloAI/hylo-<name>), as installation describes. In a development workspace every package is installed editable from its checkout, so the version does not tell two installs apart.

A run's manifest.json records the versions of the main Hylo packages and the git commit of the directory the run started in. When that directory is not inside a git repository, as with the workspace directory, the commit is empty.

docs.title: Retired memory prototype
docs.text: The experimental model-managed Working Memory runtime, agent wrapper and dedicated prompt campaign were removed on 2026-11-04. MemoryPromptCampaign is not an available API. Event memory, SimpleMemVLA and the bounded in-process working store are separate, supported components. See Memory for current choices and their evaluation boundaries.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Inspect the checks behind execution, safety boundaries, evaluation and deployment. These records describe the implementation and conditions tested; they are not a hardware certification or a general capability ranking.

Mechanism Validation record Action bounds, deterministic replay and process placement Core Control deadlines, watchdog, emergency stop and version changes Runtime External guards, effect-size gates and learner integration Plugins Judges, learned world models and critics Instruments Upstream parity and regression episodes Video-memory integration

docs.title: Run a check
docs.text:
Run from the workspace root:

uv run python harness/examples/core/02_safety_shield.py --quick
uv run pytest harness/tests/test_examples_core.py

The linked records identify source scripts, full-run conditions and known failures. Their results are dated observations; use the scripts to check a different implementation or environment.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: For analysis and measured outcomes, visit Research and Benchmarks. The reproduction records retain full tables and commands next to the originating scripts.

docs.title: Recorded issues
docs.text:
The earlier system measurements reported these implementation gaps; consult the current code and issue records before assuming they have been resolved:

  • A WebSocket environment changes the configuration digest.
  • A later guard can undo a rate-limit guard.
  • A mutable behaviour artifact skips the tamper check.
  • A malformed generator candidate can stop the campaign cycle.
  • The skill-derivation CLI recognises only the remote steering path.

docs.title: Agent examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/agents/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Agents that run any policy, choose with any reasoner and evaluate candidates without letting them act (hylo-agents, hylo-reasoners, hylo-reasoner-llm, hylo-policies). Each script measures one effect on MuJoCo reach or table tasks (from hylo-bench, referenced by registry name only), writes result.json and prints a results table. Run from the repository root:

uv run python examples/agents/01_chunk_execution.py [--quick] [--out DIR] [--workers N]

Output goes to runs/examples/agents/<slug>/ (traces, artifacts, result.json); --quick runs a small version in under a minute. Numbers below are from full runs on 2026-11-01 (128-core CPU, no GPU, 16 worker processes); policies are evaluated on held-out init states that no learner saw.

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_chunk_execution.py one policy, four execution strategies by config: open loop, replan interval, ACT temporal ensemble uv run python examples/agents/01_chunk_execution.py policy.bc: open loop 90%, replan every 4 steps 93%, every step 81% (+4/-13 vs open loop, p = 0.05), temporal ensemble 93% with 31% smoother actions (jerk 0.054 vs 0.078) at 4.8x the policy queries; policy.flow: 88% open loop, 93% ensembled; other differences within the 95% intervals 50 s (quick 10 s) 02_reasoner_swap.py the same agent with a rule, LLM or VLM chooser, one config line apart (table reach, language goals, pads visible for 5 steps) uv run python examples/agents/02_reasoner_swap.py rule chooser 76.7% (indirect phrasing 30%); chooser.llm qwen3.5:35b-a3b 100%, 2.3 s per decision; gpt-oss:20b 100%, 2.6 s; chooser.vlm (top-camera image only) 100%, 2.0 s; no-language baseline 0% (60 episodes each) 5 min live, 15 s cached (quick 10 s) 03_reference_policies.py reference policies trained from your own runs: leaderboard and data efficiency uv run python examples/agents/03_reference_policies.py expert 100%, mpc-cem 98%, bc + temporal ensemble 93%, bc 93%, flow + steering 92%, flow 89%, tokens 67%, knn 63%; from 20 demonstrations: bc 55%, flow 46%, knn 31%, tokens 25% 70 s (quick 16 s) 04_shadow_agent.py candidates run in shadow next to the acting IK controller: disagreement, no actions sent, latency uv run python examples/agents/04_shadow_agent.py executed actions identical to the controller alone in all 7 shadow runs (3747 decisions each); disagreement does not predict how a candidate acts (Spearman -0.15): flow is closest to the controller (mean abs. difference 0.022) yet acts worse than bc (89% vs 93%); a CEM-MPC shadow adds 7.1 ms per decision inline, 0.03 ms in the background 75 s (quick 16 s)

docs.title: Chunk execution
docs.text:
policy.bc and policy.flow (chunks of 8 actions, 300 demonstrations), 100 held-out episodes per row; jerk = mean |a_t - a_(t-1)|; "vs open loop" = episodes won / lost against the same policy run open loop, exact two-sided McNemar test on the same seeds.

policy strategy success % 95% CI steps queries / episode jerk vs open loop bc open loop (8) 90 83-94 49.1 9.6 0.078 - bc replan every 4 93 86-97 46.6 14.7 0.083 +6/-3, p 0.51 bc replan every 2 88 80-93 51.4 27.7 0.087 +6/-8, p 0.79 bc replan every 1 81 72-88 58.8 58.8 0.066 +4/-13, p 0.05 bc temporal ensemble m=0.01 93 86-97 45.7 45.7 0.054 +4/-1, p 0.38 bc temporal ensemble m=0.5 90 83-94 49.5 49.5 0.054 +3/-3, p 1.00 flow open loop (8) 88 80-93 50.6 7.2 0.082 - flow replan every 1 90 83-94 49.1 49.1 0.081 +7/-5, p 0.77 flow temporal ensemble m=0.01 93 86-97 45.3 45.3 0.061 +7/-2, p 0.18

Receding horizon with one step is the worst choice for the deterministic BC policy here; averaging overlapping chunks is the best for both policies and the smoothest, but the planar reach task has no disturbances, so the gains are small. result.json has every row, including flow with replan intervals 4 and 2.

docs.title: Reasoner swap
docs.text: The agent is composable.object_reach in every row; only chooser: changes. Grounding accuracy (the first choice is the instructed pad, checked against the trace's privileged state) equals the success rate in every row: once the right pad is chosen, spatial memory and the IK policy always finish the task. The rule chooser understands colour words only; for indirect phrasing ("the colour of a ripe tomato") it falls back to the nearest pad (30%, about chance with three pads). Latency is the median of live calls, one at a time, on the CPU Ollama server; 20 of the 60 calls per LLM row are answered from the cache because the push task shares its scenes with the direct task.

docs.title: Reference policies
docs.text: Demonstration subsets are balanced over the two tasks (the search split of a smaller protocol, whose seeds are a prefix of the full one's). The curve is not monotonic (bc 74% at 60, 69% at 120 demonstrations): neighbouring points overlap within their intervals. The MPC planner uses a world model learned from expert and random-action runs and costs 7 ms per decision against 0.05 ms for bc. Compare with bench/examples/policies for the same families scored under the mujoco-reach benchmark protocol.

docs.title: Shadow agent
docs.text:
candidate (in shadow) mean abs. difference decisions with max difference > 0.25 acting: success % acting: steps policy.flow (from its runs) 0.022 0.6% 89 49.4 policy.knn (from its runs) 0.030 4.2% 63 77.0 policy.bc (from its runs) 0.033 0.9% 93 46.6 IK controller kp=0.1 0.097 30.5% 100 46.9 IK controller kp=0.03 0.325 82.3% 100 107.3 mpc-cem (world model) 0.442 83.6% 100 42.8 random actions 0.826 96.3% 0 150.0

In shadow, a candidate only ever sees the states the acting agent produces, so the imitation policies look close to it while their compounding errors when acting (knn: 63%) stay invisible, and good controllers that act differently (MPC, slower gains) look far. Shadow disagreement tells where a candidate would act differently, not whether it is better; promotion still needs the gate.

docs.title: Showcase
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-bench: examples/showcase/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Four runnable examples of the evaluation layer, each with a measured result. Run them from the bench repository root; each writes result.json (and figures) to runs/examples/<slug>/ and prints a results table.

uv run python examples/showcase/01_leaderboard.py        [--quick] [--out DIR]
uv run python examples/showcase/02_pairwise.py           [--quick] [--out DIR]
uv run python examples/showcase/03_parallel_workers.py   [--quick] [--out DIR]
uv run python examples/showcase/04_libero_recorded.py    [--quick] [--out DIR] [--store DIR] [--run]

Measured on 2026-11-01, 128-core CPU, no GPU. All MuJoCo numbers are under the built-in mujoco-reach protocol (100 held-out episodes, digest a76c7037efb84660) and are deterministic: a rerun gives the same numbers.

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_leaderboard.py protocol -> scorecards -> leaderboard (table + PNG); a hand-edited protocol (same name and version, safety.max_delta: 0.05) gets another digest and is refused for ranking uv run python examples/showcase/01_leaderboard.py 9 agents ranked: expert-ik 100%, ik-weak-gain 87%, flow+steering-4 84%, bc+temporal-ensemble 83%, flow 83%, bc 71%, tokens 68%, knn 64%, random 0%. bc under the edited protocol (digest 7311c7b72f04043f) scores 36%: it lands on a second board, compare raises "different protocols", and the same change passed as an override is refused; workers leaves the digest unchanged 51 s (quick 17 s) 02_pairwise.py episode-by-episode comparison: discordant pairs, one-sided exact McNemar, against overlapping Wilson intervals and an unpaired Fisher test uv run python examples/showcase/02_pairwise.py flow+steering-4 vs bc: 84 vs 71%, intervals overlap, discordant 18–5, McNemar p = 0.0053 (unpaired Fisher p = 0.021). bc+temporal-ensemble vs bc: 14–2, p = 0.0021. flow+steering-4 vs flow: 5–4, p = 0.50 (no evidence that steering helps flow). A/A control (bc scored twice): 0–0 28 s (quick 9 s) 03_parallel_workers.py the same protocol with 1 / 4 / 16 workers: identical scorecards and identical action sequences (hashed from the traces); wall-clock time in-process and with a remote (out-of-process) agent uv run python examples/showcase/03_parallel_workers.py all 8 runs identical to their 1-worker reference (100/100 episodes, same actions). Workers are threads: in-process agents get slower, IK 2.0 -> 3.1 s (0.6x), MPC 43.5 -> 74.4 s (0.6x). MPC as a remote agent (one process per worker): 47.8 -> 12.4 s (4 workers, 3.9x) -> 4.8 s (16 workers, 9.9x), same 89% and same episodes as in-process 206 s (quick 9 s, identity check only) 04_libero_recorded.py SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_libero, CPU) on LIBERO from recorded runs (no re-simulation): success per suite with Wilson intervals, per-task outcomes, an episode strip; --run adds a 2-episode live check uv run python examples/showcase/04_libero_recorded.py --run recorded 2026-10-30, 50 episodes per suite (10 tasks x 5 validation init states): spatial 70% (56–81), object 66% (52–78), goal 78% (65–87), LIBERO-10 42% (29–56); pooled 64% (128/200). LIBERO-10 per task 0/5 to 4/5. Live check: 2/2 succeeded (82 and 109 steps; recorded 79 and 109) 1 s (live check +40 to 70 s)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Parallel workers. The evaluator runs workers as threads. On MuJoCo reach a run is bound by Python in one process, so more threads make it slower. The mujoco-reach protocol's default workers: 16 slows in-process agents down by about 1.5x. A speed-up needs the agent (or the simulator) out of process, as LIBERO configs do. Results do not change with the worker count either way.
  • LIBERO. The numbers come from runs recorded with an earlier checkout, before the package rename (the manifests list wc-* packages). The script reads them from this machine's run store (hylo profile show) or from --store. They are 50-episode validation runs, not the official libero-10 protocol (500 episodes). Live SmolVLA on CPU is not bit-reproducible: in an earlier live run of the same two episodes, one failed (280 steps).
  • Reference policies. 01, 02 and 03 retrain the policies they need (deterministic, cached under the output directory), using the same recipe as examples/policies/compare.py.

docs.title: Core examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/core/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Six small scripts, one per capability of hylo-core: the kernel, the SafetyShield, traces and replay, remote components and the wire codecs, conformance with sealed artifacts and the store, and the kernel's timing modes with the operator channel. Each script runs real episodes, measures something, prints a short results table and writes result.json.

The environments are the MuJoCo tasks of hylo-bench (mujoco.planar_reach, mujoco.table_reach, from hylo-env-mujoco). The scripts refer to them only by their registry name, so they need that package installed in the venv. The development workspace installs it.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
From the harness repository root:

uv run python examples/core/01_first_episode.py            # full run
uv run python examples/core/01_first_episode.py --quick    # under 60 s (here: 2-3 s)
uv run python examples/core/01_first_episode.py --out /tmp/x
uv run pytest tests/test_examples_core.py                  # every example with --quick

Output goes to runs/examples/core/<slug>/ (gitignored): result.json, any figure, and the run directories with their traces. Seeds are fixed, so the numbers below reproduce, except wall-clock timings.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Full runs on 2026-11-01, on a 128-core CPU with no GPU.

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_first_episode One episode through EpisodeRunner by hand, then a whole split as an ExperimentConfig (run_experiment, as hylo run does), hylo trace, a second identical run uv run python examples/core/01_first_episode.py Episode by hand: success in 30 steps, final distance 0.0195 m, 183 trace events (8 types), guards finite -> bounds. Experiment, 100 episodes on 8 workers: success 1.00, 36.2 steps on average (fixed target 30.0, random 42.4), 1.4 s. Second run: same status and steps on 100/100 episodes, largest action difference 0 4 s 02_safety_shield A noisy agent with spikes up to 5x the bounds, under the mandatory guards, a rate limit (max_delta: 0.25), and norm_limit + delta_limit in both orders, with a well-behaved control agent. Then four ways to try to get around the shield uv run python examples/core/02_safety_shield.py 100 episodes per config. Proposed actions reach 9.42 and executed ones never pass 1.00. Largest step-to-step jump of the executed action: 2.00 with the mandatory guards, 0.25 with a rate limit. Peak joint speed 2.52 -> 1.66 rad/s, peak acceleration 32.7 -> 14.2 rad/s² (norm+rate: 1.31 rad/s, 13.8 rad/s²). In the wrong order (max_delta first, then norm_limit) the jump reaches 0.28. Success stays 1.00 in every config. Control agent: 3.0 interventions per episode. Bypass attempts: a guard plugin that multiplies actions by 10 still gives max |a| 1.00, a NaN ends the episode as safety_abort (every action that reached the env was finite), guard order stays finite -> ... -> bounds, and a real-robot shield aborts at the first proposal 12 s 03_trace_replay A language + memory agent on the MuJoCo table, every episode re-simulated from its recorded actions alone, a 1e-9 sensitivity check, and a replay GIF rendered from the trace uv run python examples/core/03_trace_replay.py 90 episodes, 3985 steps, success 0.77. Traces: 10.7 MiB, 2.8 KB per step, 11 event types (including 759 memory.retrieval and 180 agent.decision). Replay: 90/90 episodes bit-exact, largest observation and reward deviation 0, same outcomes, 2709 steps/s. First action changed by 1e-9: 0/90 episodes stay bit-exact (largest deviation 5.6e-10) 8 s 04_remote_env The same experiment in five placements: in-process, stdio env, stdio env + agent, WebSocket env, WebSocket env + agent. Latency of a single step call, and the two wire codecs uv run python examples/core/04_remote_env.py 50 episodes, 1840 steps per placement, identical everywhere: same status and steps, largest action difference 0. Time per step inside episodes: 0.126 ms in-process, +0.105 ms stdio env, +0.239 ms stdio env + agent, +0.326 ms ws env, +0.747 ms ws env + agent. Single env.step call, median: 22 µs direct, 63 µs through stdio, 161 µs through WebSocket. One step on the wire: 152 B request, 644 B reply. Observation with a 224x224 image: 196 KiB and 0.63 ms (JSON codec) vs 147 KiB and 0.017 ms (msgpack wire) 8 s 05_conformance_artifacts hylo conformance --agent in-process and over stdio, the kit on a broken environment, a dataset artifact sealed from a run, hylo artifact before and after a 1-bit change, the split guard, store ids, references and deletion protection uv run python examples/core/05_conformance_artifacts.py Conformance: 10/10 checks pass in-process. Over stdio 9 pass and 1 is skipped (snapshot). BrokenEnv: 2 of 7 checks fail (seeded reset, snapshot/restore). Artifact reach-pairs@d2d609810e833160: 371 pairs, sealed in 0.5 ms, verified in 0.2 ms. One flipped bit: hylo artifact exits 1 (digest mismatch); with the bit restored it exits 0. Sealing a gate-split build is refused. The artifact id resolves only while the content matches, and hylo store rm of the source run exits 1 because the artifact refers to it 3 s 06_realtime_timing sync vs realtime timing (virtual clock) for an agent that plans 10-step chunks, over a policy latency of 0 to 0.8 s, then an e-stop through the OperatorChannel uv run python examples/core/06_realtime_timing.py 100 episodes per timing. Sync: success 1.00, 36.2 steps. Realtime: success 1.00 up to a 5-step latency (59.7 steps, 13.6 holds), 0.89 at 6 steps, 0.00 from 7 steps (150-step timeouts). From 10 steps (the chunk horizon) every episode ends in a watchdog abort. E-stop posted after step 10: safety_abort at step 10 with no action sent after it. The next episode is refused (latched fault). After clear_fault: success in 51 steps 40 s
