docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• A WebSocket placement changes the config digest. ExperimentConfig.measured() drops env.remote and a remote agent's runtime, so a stdio env has the same digest as in-process (05c573fe1309dd6d). A WebSocket env is {type: remote.ws, params: {url}} instead, so the digest changes, and it includes the URL: with --port 0 it is different on every run. A stdio agent (type: remote) also gets its own digest. Results do not depend on placement (example 04), so comparing runs by digest across placements does not work today.
  • Guard order matters. Guards run in the order they are listed, and the max_delta shorthand is always inserted first. With max_delta plus a norm_limit guard, the norm scaling runs after the rate limit and produces step-to-step jumps of up to 0.28, above the 0.25 limit. Listing norm_limit and then delta_limit as guard plugins keeps the jumps at 0.25 (example 02, both orders measured).
  • The unsafe stream does not lower success here. On planar reach the noisy agent succeeds in every config. What the shield changes is the motion: smaller steps, lower peak speed, lower peak acceleration. Interventions count every modified step, so a stricter config shows more interventions.
  • Realtime fails well before the latency reaches the chunk horizon. With 10-step chunks, success drops to 0 at a 7-step latency, not at 10. The aligned merge drops the first t - s actions of a chunk, which assumes the robot followed the previous plan in the meantime. While the queue is empty the robot holds instead, and the rest of a P-controller rollout is small, so the arm only crawls. The watchdog catches the case where nothing is left to execute (latency of 10 steps or more).
  • The stdio env proxy has no snapshot/restore. RemoteEnvironment does not forward snapshot/restore, so that conformance check is skipped over stdio. In-process, MuJoCo passes it.
  • Reusing an episode id appends to its trace file. TraceStore opens episode files in append mode. The scripts that use fixed episode ids clear their trace directory first.

docs.title: Evolution examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/evolve/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

For architecture, strategy selection, validation and rollback, see the Self-Evolution README.

Runnable examples of the evolution layer (hylo-evolve, the paired statistics of hylo-eval, hylo-proposer-llm) on MuJoCo planar reach. Each script shows one capability and measures its effect. All run from the harness repository root, write result.json and print a results table:

uv run python examples/evolve/01_campaign_reach.py [--quick] [--out DIR]

The default output directory is runs/examples/evolve/<slug>/. --quick finishes in under a minute. The MuJoCo environment comes from hylo-env-mujoco (hylo-bench) and is referenced only by its registry name, mujoco.planar_reach. Large evaluations run in up to --workers processes (default 24).

Most examples improve one parent: a flow-matching policy trained in the script from 120 IK-expert demonstrations (the search and search_val init states, as in hylo-bench's examples/policies), run with too much sampling noise (noise_scale: 3.0, about 45% success). Gate and held-out init states are never used for training.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-11-01 on a 128-core CPU without a GPU, full mode (no --quick).

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_campaign_reach.py A full campaign (run_campaign): diagnosis, rule.gain candidates, cascade, 2-look gate, held-out report, promotion, cycle after cycle; then every version on fresh episodes uv run python examples/evolve/01_campaign_reach.py 3 cycles, 2 promotions (noise 3.0 → 1.5 → 0.75), stopped when cycle 3 found nothing better. On 500 fresh held-out episodes: 0.440 → 0.726 → 0.762 (vs base 190:29, p = 1.7e-30) 48 s 02_protected_scope.py Adversarial candidates (loosen safety, change benchmark, trace, env, gate settings, code kind, doctored artifacts, duplicates) refused at stage 0 uv run python examples/evolve/02_protected_scope.py Removing the speed limit would raise success 0.505 → 1.000 (counterfactual run outside the gate). 11 of 14 candidates refused before any rollout, 0 episodes spent on them. Gap found: a behaviour artifact forged as mutable passes stage 0 16 s 03_gate_power.py False promotions of an A/A change vs alpha, and power against the number of episodes, for the paired test and for the whole campaign cycle uv run python examples/evolve/03_gate_power.py A/A promoted in 0.3–2.9% of draws (test alone) and 0.6–0.9% of whole cycles (alpha 0.05). At the default split sizes (40 episodes per split) the cycle promotes +29 pts 99%, +18 pts 75%, +10 pts 26%, +4 pts 6.5% of the time. 80% power needs 80 pairs for +18 pts, 320 for +10, 1280 for +4 1.5 min 04_field_rollback.py Manual approval, deployment through active.json, a field monitor, rollback() uv run python examples/evolve/04_field_rollback.py The gate promoted noise 1.0 in simulation (0.450 → 0.805). In the 10 Hz field cell it regressed (parent 0.265, candidate 0.055). The monitor fired after 40 field episodes (0:8 discordant pairs, p = 3.9e-3) and rolled back to the base version 34 s 05_llm_vs_rule.py llm.steering (qwen3.5:35b-a3b via Ollama) against rule.steering and rule.gain, 2 cycles of at most 3 candidates each uv run python examples/evolve/05_llm_vs_rule.py Each promoted once. On 500 fresh held-out episodes (parent 0.496): LLM 0.724 (noise 1.5, the same candidate rule.gain found), rule.gain 0.724, rule.steering 0.542 (4-sample vote; vs parent p = 0.07). The LLM used 2 calls (26–28 s each), 520 episodes, and 3 of its 6 proposals were invalid 2 min

01: the active version after each cycle on 500 fresh held-out episodes (95% Wilson intervals). Circles are the candidates on search_val; filled circles were promoted.

docs.title: The gate's power
docs.text:
The project's main open problem is power. 03_gate_power.py runs each arm once on 6000 episodes (2 tasks × 3000 fresh seeds), then replays gate decisions on random subsets of those episodes:

Left: the one-sided exact McNemar test alone. Right: the whole campaign cycle (run_cycle) at 0.5× to 8× the default split sizes. Effects are the arms' true differences on the pool.

Arm True effect Pairs for 80% power (test alone) Whole cycle, default sizes A/A (fresh noise stream, same policy) −0.5 pts never (false promotions 0.3–2.9%) 0.9% noise 2.75 +4.1 pts 1280 6.5% noise 2.5 +9.9 pts 320 26.4% noise 2.0 +18.3 pts 80 74.9% noise 1.0 +29.2 pts 40 98.9%

The gate is safe: the A/A change is promoted far less often than alpha, because the exact test is conservative and the cycle adds a screen and alpha spending. It is also underpowered: a 10-point gain, the size most real improvements have, is confirmed in about one cycle in four at the default 40 episodes per split. On LIBERO-10 (recorded, docs/our research notes) a candidate that helped by 8 to 12 points on three disjoint sets of init states failed the gate at p = 0.068 for the same reason.

Common random numbers (parent and candidate share seeded policy noise) did not help here: the same +18-point effect on a fresh noise stream has the same power. The policy's trajectories diverge too quickly for shared noise to keep outcomes correlated.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• 03_gate_power.py replays decisions on a finite pool of real episodes (a bootstrap). As the number of pairs nears the pool size, rates converge to the pool's realised difference. That is why the A/A rate drifts down at 1280 and 2560 pairs.
  • 04_field_rollback.py simulates the field as a different control rate (10 Hz instead of 20 Hz). The flow policy was trained on 20 Hz data. The lower-noise candidate is better in simulation and much worse in the field. The monitor pairs each field episode with the parent's recorded field baseline on the same task instance and tests one-sided at 0.01 per look (10 looks at most, so at most 0.1 overall by the union bound).
  • 05_llm_vs_rule.py caches LLM replies under <out>/llm-cache, so a rerun into the same directory reproduces the proposals without the model. It needs an Ollama server at http://localhost:11434 (--model, --base-url). Without one, the LLM arm is skipped and reported in result.json. One run per generator: this does not show that either kind of generator is better. On this task the best single change is a smaller noise scale, which a one-knob rule finds directly. The LLM's steering prompt is written for LIBERO grippers. All 3 invalid proposals were trigger rules without the required name field, which the prompt does not mention. The LLM latencies (26–28 s per call) are from the first, uncached run; result.json of a cached rerun records 0 calls.
  • Shadow mode (shadow_config) is not covered. Its divergence report treats the last action dimension as a gripper, which does not fit the 2-dimensional joint actions of planar reach.

docs.title: Capability results
docs.text: Recorded measurements previously embedded in the usage guides. These are observations under the conditions below, not expected output for a new run. The reproduction records link to the source scripts and full experiments; Research provides the analysis.

docs.title: Spatial memory
docs.text:
On the MuJoCo table with targets visible for only the first 5 steps, composable.object_reach went from 0.00 to 0.75 success with spatial memory (300 pairs, p = 4e-68); per task, 0.99 on direct and push instructions and 0.27 on indirect ones ("the colour of a ripe tomato"), which the rule-based chooser cannot resolve with or without memory. With targets always visible, memory changed nothing (0.75 both ways). In a single traced episode, the recalled positions matched the true ones exactly and the agent switched from seen to remembered objects at step 5.

uv run python examples/memory/01_spatial_memory_occlusion.py      # in the harness repository
uv run python examples/memory/02_observable_retrieval.py          # one episode's writes and retrievals

Usage guide · Source records

docs.title: Action memory
docs.text:
Setting Result MuJoCo planar reach, revisited scenes 0.75 → 0.81 (p = 0.29) MuJoCo planar reach, new scenes 0.69 → 0.75 (p = 0.24) Six sessions on the same workcell, each extending the bank +4, +5, +7, +11, +1 points in sessions 2–6; pooled +5.6 LIBERO-10, SmolVLA, bank from other start states 0.54 → 0.46 LIBERO-10, same scenes, fixed t0 0.2 0.54 → 0.62 (p = 0.10)

On MuJoCo the key is the policy's 8-dimensional state, so a neighbour from another scene is still informative. On LIBERO the key is pooled image features, which carry no information about the outcome on an unseen layout. Looser retrieval (k 10, floor 0.95) with a well-tuned policy made results worse on MuJoCo in a development run. Treat action memory as an experiment to measure on your task, not a default.

uv run python examples/memory/03_action_memory_scene_recall.py    # in the harness repository
uv run python examples/memory/05_memory_across_sessions.py

Usage guide · Source records

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
Two experience campaigns on MuJoCo planar reach wrote, read and credited a lesson book with llm.reflector on a local model. The effect of lessons on promotion has not been measured separately: it needs a language model in the loop and enough rounds to compare with and without lessons.

Usage guide · Source records

docs.title: Skill library
docs.text:
On MuJoCo planar reach, a campaign proposed four noise-scale changes. One passed its gate (+0.42, p = 3e-12) and became a verified skill; three stayed proposed. The skills agent then applied it on fresh scenes, disjoint from every campaign split: 0.47 → 0.86 (200 pairs, p = 6e-19), with skill.applied in all 200 episodes.

On LIBERO-10, the library built from two campaigns holds eight skills, none verified: the two most promising (+8 and +9 points on the gate) were not significant and are recorded as proposed.

uv run python examples/memory/04_skill_library.py      # in the harness repository

docs.title: Action-memory diagnostics
docs.text:
SmolVLA's velocity field pulls hard towards its own action: on LIBERO, a prior almost one standard deviation away moves the result about 40% of the way at t0 = 0.1 and hardly at all from t0 = 0.4. Useful guidance therefore lives at small t0.

The noise-memory variant on unseen LIBERO start states scored 0.55 and 0.54 against a 0.54 baseline.

Each decision emits memory.retrieval. From a recorded MuJoCo episode: five candidates above the floor, four kept, started at a fixed t0 of 0.3, with the source episode, step and similarity of each kept segment.

docs.title: Instrument examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/instruments/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Instruments measure or predict but never act (hylo-instruments): success judges, world models and chunk value models, trained by hylo-learn jobs from your own runs. Each script trains an instrument on MuJoCo planar reach (from hylo-bench, referenced by registry name only), where the simulator's verdict is known, checks the instrument against it, writes result.json and prints a results table. Run from the repository root:

uv run python examples/instruments/01_success_judge.py [--quick] [--out DIR] [--workers N]

Output goes to runs/examples/instruments/<slug>/; --quick runs a small version in under a minute. Numbers below are from full runs on 2026-11-01 (128-core CPU, no GPU, 16 worker processes).

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_success_judge.py judge.trace trained on development runs, calibrated (hylo calibrate) on unseen runs against the simulator outcome; four choices of what the judge observes uv run python examples/instruments/01_success_judge.py fingertip + target: AUC 0.986 (random-target task 0.974), recall 0.69 at precision 0.95; all state: AUC 0.960 (0.884): with joint velocities it learns a termination shortcut instead of the target; proprio only 0.958; positions only 0.889 (0.697); 400 calibration episodes, base rate 0.36 80 s (quick 14 s) 02_world_model.py world_model.state fitted from runs, used as an environment (env: {type: world_model}) to rank 9 controllers, compared with MuJoCo uv run python examples/instruments/02_world_model.py open-loop fingertip error 3.9 cm after 10 steps (no-motion baseline 17.5 cm); ranking vs MuJoCo: Spearman 0.91 on success, 0.83 on mean steps; but optimistic (kp 0.01: 80% in the model, 0% real) and it picks kp 0.1 as best where MuJoCo picks kp 0.3 1 min (quick 9 s) 03_chunk_critic.py a chunk value model (ChunkCritic) from flow-policy traces: offline accuracy and steering with it (CriticSteeredAgent) uv run python examples/instruments/03_chunk_critic.py null result: AUC 0.828 for state + chunk vs 0.831 for state alone; same-state pair accuracy 0.61 +- 0.05 (n = 102); online, critic selection 88% vs medoid 92% (+3/-7, p = 0.34) on 100 held-out episodes 90 s (quick 12 s)

docs.title: Success judge
docs.text:
Training data: IK controllers too slow for the 150-step budget (kp 0.015, 0.02, 0.03) and random actions, 800 search episodes; calibration: the 400 search_val episodes, which no judge saw.

judge observes AUC AUC, fixed target AUC, random target Brier ECE threshold for precision 0.95 recall there ready to label fingertip + target 0.986 0.998 0.974 0.066 0.120 0.661 0.69 yes all state (joints, velocities, fingertip, target) 0.960 0.992 0.884 0.085 0.091 0.635 0.68 yes proprio only (no target) 0.958 0.993 0.873 0.088 0.084 0.613 0.68 yes positions only (no velocities, no target) 0.889 0.987 0.697 0.137 0.142 0.620 0.63 yes

Given every state entry, the judge does no better than without the target: successful episodes end the moment the fingertip arrives, still moving, so joint velocity separates the outcomes on the training distribution and the judge never learns the target relation. Without velocities and target it falls to 0.70 on random targets. The same trap as episode length in LIBERO (hylo-docs, success judges on LIBERO-10): choose what a judge may observe by what decides the task, then calibrate it. The labelling workflow with a calibrated judge is in examples/learn.

docs.title: World model
docs.text:
Model: 3-member ensemble, 37189 transitions from 300 expert and 300 random-action episodes (29 s to train); one-step validation MSE 7.2e-3 against 2.95e-2 for predicting no change. Candidates on the gate split, 100 episodes each:

candidate MuJoCo success % model success % model states, simulator predicate % MuJoCo steps model steps IK kp=0.01 0 80 0 150.0 103.9 IK kp=0.015 0 85 1 150.0 76.5 IK kp=0.02 41 89 0 143.4 59.3 IK kp=0.03 100 97 1 105.3 38.4 IK kp=0.05 100 99 3 67.9 30.5 IK kp=0.1 100 100 16 45.8 31.2 IK kp=0.3 100 100 62 36.8 35.1 IK kp=1.0 100 100 92 37.8 36.7 random actions 0 0 1 150.0 150.0

The model separates the bad from the good (random and slow gains fail in MuJoCo and take longest in the model), which is what pre-screening uses it for; it cannot pick the winner. Two error sources: the learned completion classifier fires near the target, so slow controllers "succeed" too early; and the dynamics are not precise enough for the 2 cm success radius (the simulator's predicate on model states, which ranks steps with Spearman 0.89, rarely fires for slow controllers). The fine ranking is also fragile: retraining the same model with a different BLAS thread count changed Spearman on success from 0.93 to 0.91 and the model's best candidate from kp 0.05 to kp 0.1.

docs.title: Chunk critic
docs.text:
Behaviour data: policy.flow on the development splits at noise scales 1.0, 1.4 and 1.8 (97%, 93%, 87% success; 900 episodes, 11631 chunks). Offline, grouped 5-fold cross-validation over init states:

model AUC (chunk value vs episode outcome) critic: state + chunk 0.828 state only 0.831

The critic predicts outcomes from the state, not from the chunk: on 102 same-state pairs (first chunks from the identical reset state, one success and one failure) it ranks the successful chunk higher 61% +- 5% of the time. Online, steering with it does not help:

flow policy, 4 seeded samples per decision success % 95% CI steps vs medoid 1 sample 89 81-94 49.4 +0/-3, p 0.25 first sample 89 81-94 49.4 +0/-3, p 0.25 medoid 92 85-96 46.5 - critic (beta 0.5) 88 80-93 52.3 +3/-7, p 0.34

The critic's chunk summary was designed for 7-D end-effector actions with a gripper; on 2-D joint actions it keeps only coarse motion features, which is one plausible reason for the null result.

docs.title: Learning examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/learn/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Runnable examples of the learning layer (hylo-learn: learner jobs and sealed artifacts, judge calibration and labelling, external-data ingestion, online learning) on MuJoCo planar reach. Each script shows one capability and measures its effect. All run from the harness repository root, write result.json and print a results table:

uv run python examples/learn/01_learner_job.py [--quick] [--out DIR]

The default output directory is runs/examples/learn/<slug>/. --quick finishes in under a minute. The MuJoCo environment comes from hylo-env-mujoco (hylo-bench) and is referenced only by its registry name, mujoco.planar_reach. Large evaluations run in up to --workers processes (default 24). Held-out evaluations use the standard heldout seeds (20000+), which no learner reads.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-11-01 on a 128-core CPU without a GPU, full mode (no --quick).

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_learner_job.py TrainJob + run_job for kNN, BC and flow matching: sealed artifacts, tamper and split-guard checks, held-out evaluation, success against the number of demonstrations uv run python examples/learn/01_learner_job.py On 300 held-out episodes: kNN 0.620, BC 0.783, BC + temporal ensemble 0.837, flow 0.847, flow + 4-sample steering 0.873 (expert 1.000). Flow vs demonstrations: 10 → 0.397, 20 → 0.463, 40 → 0.610, 80 → 0.750, 160 → 0.847. A changed byte and a job asking for gate runs were refused; a rerun was skipped 32 s 02_judge_calibration.py judge.trace learner jobs, calibrate_judge against simulator outcomes, ingest of a run without outcomes, label_run uv run python examples/learn/02_judge_calibration.py Calibrated on 720 unseen episodes: proprio + target judge AUC 0.993, recall 0.990 at 0.95 precision; proprio-only judge AUC 0.910, recall 0.724. On 400 ingested episodes from another cell, labels were less precise than calibrated: 0.821 (45 false labels) and 0.909. An uncalibrated judge and a simulator run were refused 86 s 03_online_cem.py An online learner (CEM over steering settings) through run_online: rollouts on search, a sealed artifact listing every rollout run, held-out check uv run python examples/learn/03_online_cem.py 6 iterations × 8 settings × 80 episodes (48 rollout runs, 3840 episodes). Population mean on search 0.606 → 0.848. On 500 held-out episodes: start 0.458, CEM mean 0.778, best setting 0.836 (198:9 vs start, p = 8e-48). The best setting scored 0.887 on search. A job rolling out on gate was refused 83 s

01: the flow policy's held-out success against the number of demonstrations (95% Wilson intervals). The dotted line is the IK controller it imitates.

03: success of every setting tried (grey), population and elite means on search, and the held-out success of the starting setting and of the final CEM mean.

docs.title: Readings
docs.text:
• Judges are trustworthy only on the distribution they were calibrated on. The proprio + target judge reached 0.95 precision at threshold 0.537 on search_val, but labelled the other cell's episodes (other agents, other seeds, base rate 0.53) at 0.821 precision. label_run enforces the calibrated threshold, but it cannot tell that the data has shifted. The threshold is also the lowest one reaching the target on the calibration set, which is optimistic. The proprio-only judge has the higher threshold (0.732) and kept 0.909.
  • The recorded LIBERO-10 judges give the same picture with images (docs/our research notes, recorded, not rerun here): judge.trace AUC 0.93 and recall 0.55 at 0.95 precision, ready to label. The VLM judge reached AUC 0.61 and was not ready.
  • Selecting on few episodes is optimistic. CEM's best setting scored 0.887 on the 80 search episodes it was picked on and 0.836 held out. The demonstrations come from init states disjoint from the rollouts, so the gap is selection, not memorisation. The online artifact is a behaviour artifact: only the gate can activate it.
  • Temporal ensembling (ACT-style) and 4-sample steering each add a few points over their base policy, but the 95% intervals of neighbouring rows overlap. Compare two policies with a paired test (see ../evolve/03_gate_power.py).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• 02_judge_calibration.py trains state-only judges (cameras: []): planar reach has no camera. A judge sees only the last observation of an episode, never its length or termination reason. The "other cell" is the IK controller with gain 0.02 and a noisy flow policy on the standard train seeds. They are ingested as external:other-cell with outcomes withheld, and the withheld outcomes score the labels afterwards.
  • 03_online_cem.py writes its learner in the script and passes it to run_online. A plugin learner would be referenced by name in a job file and run with hylo learn.

docs.title: Memory examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: examples/memory/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Runnable examples for the memory layer (hylo-memory) and the agents that use it (hylo-agents: the composable agent with spatial memory, MemorySteeredAgent, the skills agent). Each script shows one capability and measures its effect against the same agent without it, on the same episodes (paired by task and seed).

uv run python examples/memory/01_spatial_memory_occlusion.py [--quick] [--out DIR] [--workers N]
uv run python examples/memory/make_figures.py          # assets/memory_results.png from the full runs
uv run pytest tests/test_examples_memory.py            # every example with --quick

Run from the harness repository root. Results go to runs/examples/memory/<slug>/ (a result.json, the runs with their traces, banks and libraries). Seeds are fixed, so a re-run gives the same numbers. The examples need hylo-bench's MuJoCo adapter (mujoco.table_reach, mujoco.planar_reach), referenced by registry name only. _common.py holds the shared helpers, including PriorFlowSampler, which adds the RFC-0003 prior protocol to the reference flow policy so MemorySteeredAgent can drive it. No LLM is used.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Full runs on 2026-11-01: 128-core CPU, no GPU, 16 worker threads. p-values are exact two-sided McNemar tests on the discordant pairs (+wins / -losses).

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01 spatial memory under occlusion composable.object_reach on mujoco.table_reach, pads visible for 5 steps; sqlite spatial memory off vs on; visibility sweep uv run python examples/memory/01_spatial_memory_occlusion.py 300 pairs: 0.00 [0.00, 0.01] → 0.75 [0.70, 0.80], +225 / -0, p = 4e-68. Per task: direct 0.00 → 0.99, push 0.00 → 0.99, indirect 0.00 → 0.27 (the rule chooser cannot resolve "the colour of a ripe tomato"; memory does not fix language). Pads always visible: 0.75 vs 0.75, memory adds nothing 86 s 02 observable retrieval one episode: the memory.write / memory.retrieval / agent.decision timeline from the trace, then the SQLite file queried directly (by key and by radius, with scores) uv run python examples/memory/02_observable_retrieval.py 1 write (3 ADD), 6 retrievals; decisions switch from seen to remembered at step 5; recalled pad positions match privileged state exactly (error 0.000 m); success in 21 steps vs failure after 150 steps without memory ("no objects perceived or remembered") < 1 s 03 action memory: revisited vs new scenes ActionBank of verified chunks from 3 earlier visits to each search_val scene; MemorySteeredAgent (Retrieve-then-Steer) on a noisy flow policy uv run python examples/memory/03_action_memory_scene_recall.py revisited: 0.75 → 0.81 (+14 / -8, p = 0.29); new (held-out): 0.69 → 0.75 (+12 / -6, p = 0.24). Memory produced a prior at 67% of decisions on revisited scenes vs 41% on new ones, but the outcome effect is the same: the LIBERO shape (+8 revisited / -8 new) was not reproduced, both effects are not significant 48 s 04 skill library campaign (RFC-0002 gate) → archive → skills with evidence-based status → frozen library → skills agent around the unchanged parent uv run python examples/memory/04_skill_library.py 4 skills: 1 verified (noise scale 3.0 → 0.99; gate +0.42, p = 3e-12), 3 proposed (not gated or not significant). Campaign held-out report 0.56 → 0.84. On fresh scenes (standard validation seeds, disjoint from all campaign splits, 200 pairs): 0.47 [0.40, 0.53] → 0.86 [0.81, 0.90], +85 / -6, p = 6e-19; skill.applied in 200 of 200 episodes 51 s 05 memory across sessions one process per session on a fixed workcell (the same 100 scenes); each session loads the bank the previous one saved (frozen, digest), then appends its verified successes; a SQLite journal carries session summaries uv run python examples/memory/05_memory_across_sessions.py session 1 (empty bank) equals the control by construction; sessions 2-6: +4, +5, +7, +11 (p = 0.035), +1 points; pooled +0.056, +63 / -35 (p = 0.006, naive: the scenes repeat across sessions). A small, mostly non-significant per-session gain that grows with the bank until session 6 64 s

Notes on the numbers:

  • 03 and 05 use the same memory steering settings (k 5, similarity floor 0.99, fixed t0 0.3), picked from a sweep of four settings on example 03's splits; treat their p-values as exploratory. With looser retrieval (k 10, floor 0.95) and the well-tuned policy (noise 1.0, 0.88 success), memory hurt on both revisited (-0.11, p = 0.03) and new scenes (-0.12, p = 0.002) in a development run.
  • Why 03 differs from LIBERO: here the retrieval key is the policy's own 8-dimensional state (joint angles, fingertip, target position), so a neighbour from another scene is still informative and the prior acts like a kNN denoiser everywhere. LIBERO's keys are pooled image features that carry no outcome information on an unseen layout.
  • 04 needs a proposer that suggests a noise change: the built-in rule.steering candidates (voting over 4 samples, longer execution) were not promoted on this task, so the script registers a small noise-scale proposer, standing in for the LLM proposer of the recorded maturity campaign.

docs.title: Recorded LIBERO-10 results
docs.text:
Recorded, not re-run here (frozen SmolVLA, 100 paired search_val episodes, from docs/our research notes in hylo-docs):

Bank Success vs control 0.54 unseen init states (102 search successes) 0.46 -0.08 (+6 / -14, p = 0.115) same scenes, confidence t0 0.55 +0.01 (+8 / -7, p = 1.0) same scenes, fixed t0 0.2 0.62 +0.08 (+13 / -5, p = 0.096)

The skill library built from the two LIBERO-10 campaigns holds 8 skills, none verified (the two execution_steps 25 candidates were +8 / +9 points on the gate split, p 0.07 / 0.09: recorded as proposed).

docs.title: Not covered
docs.text:
• The lesson book (lesson_book): lessons change behaviour only through an LLM proposer or planner that reads them, so a measured effect needs an LLM in the loop; recorded runs used llm.reflector with a local Ollama model.
  • hylo skills ARCHIVE --out LIB only recognises the steering path of a remote agent (agent.params.params.steering); example 04's local campaign patches agent.params.steering, so the script calls the same functions (skill_from_entry, classify) with that path.
  • MemorySteeredAgent aggregates the last action dimension as a gripper (gripper_dim, no "none" option); the planar arm has no gripper, so stored segments carry a constant gripper channel that the sampler drops again.

docs.title: Harness Program Evolution
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/harness_evolution/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

For the shared campaign lifecycle, strategy options and version management, see the Self-Evolution README.

harness.program is an optional Hylo evolution strategy inspired by HarnessPAI's program-repair and phase-scoped skill-memory design. It independently implements phase planning, iterative program development and evidence-linked repair recall. It performs no weight training and coexists with research.llm, steering proposers and memory strategies.

The pinned HarnessPAI source has no project license. This implementation uses Hylo's own research sessions, kernel, artifact format and promotion protocol; no HarnessPAI source, prompts or templates are copied. It is a design adaptation, not a reproduction of the authors' benchmark result or a drop-in implementation of their runtime.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    active["Active program and development instructions"] --> plan["Model proposes observable phase plan"]
    recall["Repair notes from active promoted lineages"] --> plan
    plan --> session["Research session writes and tests solve(robot)"]
    session -->|"Failed development cases"| repair["Model diagnoses and edits the program"]
    repair --> session
    session -->|"All selected development cases succeed"| distill["Model proposes evidence-linked repair notes"]
    distill --> seal["Seal program, phase plan and accepted notes together"]
    seal --> gate["Existing Hylo selection and independent gate"]
    gate -->|"Passed and approved"| publish["Activate candidate version"]
    publish --> recall
    gate -->|"Rejected"| archive["Archive only; no repair recall"]
    publish --> rollback["Rollback restores the parent lineage"]
    rollback --> recall
  1. Read instructions from the benchmark's search cases. A supplied diagnosis must also have a search manifest; selection, gate and held-out data are not sent to the model.
  2. Retrieve relevant admitted repair notes and ask the model for named phases, observable completion conditions, fallback behavior and step budgets.
  3. Run a bounded Hylo ResearchSession: inspect the parent program, submit alternatives, inspect development outcomes and repair failures. All selected development cases must succeed before this strategy returns a candidate. This strategy enables auto_submit: after a completed block changes the collected program, evaluate it and send the results back to the model. Explicit submissions are not duplicated; unchanged programs and revisions beyond the submission budget are not automatically evaluated. Other research proposers retain their existing explicit-submission behavior.
  4. Distill repair notes only when failed submissions exist. Each note must reference a real failed case and a successful replay of that case in the selected program. Invalid notes are discarded; the otherwise valid program can still proceed without notes.
  5. Seal the program, plan, notes and evidence into a new artifact. The existing campaign performs selection, independent paired validation, reporting and configured approval.
  6. Recall notes only from promoted candidates on each configured campaign's current active lineage. A gate-passing candidate awaiting manual approval remains invisible. Rollback automatically removes the retired branch's notes from subsequent queries.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Source Responsibility harness_evolution.py Strategy orchestration, phase planning, development and repair distillation phase_memory.py Typed phase plans and repair notes, evidence checks, active-lineage retrieval research.py Existing interactive development, program submissions and observation/tool execution skills.py Existing sealed programs and program-skill integration test_harness_evolution.py Failed-program repair, gate, approval, recall, corruption and rollback tests

A phase contains name, goal, completion, fallback and step_budget. The phase plan is guidance for code generation. Generated code must implement the phase checks and bounded loops; this release does not introduce a centrally enforced phase-state-machine interpreter. The existing kernel and research runtime enforce their overall episode, execution-time and session budgets. Evaluator outcomes, rather than program exit or printed claims, determine development and gate success.

A repair note contains phase, trigger, repair, limitation, failure_refs and success_refs. It is advice tied to a program that passed a gate; it is not an independently verified transferable skill. Recall reports program_gate_passed: true and transfer_verified: false. Retrieval uses lexical overlap and an optional exact phase-name boost, not embeddings. The files and provenance are checked against the sealed digest, which must also match the artifact digest recorded in the admitted candidate.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Use the registered generator after installing the updated adapter:

proposer:
  type: harness.program
  params:
    model: {backend: ollama, model: gpt-oss:20b, reasoning_effort: low}
    dev: 6
    budget: {turns: 40, submits: 6, resets: 12}
    out_root: runs/harness-program/proposals
    repair_campaigns: [runs/harness-program]

repair_campaigns names campaign directories, not arbitrary note folders. Sharing several campaign directories enables cross-task retrieval while retaining the active-lineage rule for each source. It does not establish that a retrieved repair transfers to another task.

The example campaign uses a module reference, which also works before reinstalling entry-point metadata. It targets the CPU toy environment, with an intentionally inactive baseline and an existing local Ollama model. From the workspace root, with Hylo and that model service already available:

.venv/bin/python -m hylo.core.cli evolve run \
  harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/harness_evolution/campaign.yaml

To retain the resolved protocol, relevant source snapshots and campaign outcome in a new directory, use the probe runner:

.venv/bin/python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/harness_evolution/run_probe.py \
  --out runs/harness-program-probe --model gpt-oss:20b

The probe uses 16 total model calls, four submissions, four resets, a 180,000-token budget and a 90-second per-request timeout. It refuses to reuse an existing output directory.

The strategy makes one planning call, a bounded research session and at most one distillation call. budget.turns includes all three stages; two calls are reserved for planning/distillation. Token and reported-cost budgets are shared across stages and checked between calls. Unknown model prices remain unknown in accounting. No model or simulator dependencies are installed by the strategy.

docs.title: Runtime Boundary
docs.text:
Programs use the configured Hylo robot toolkit and its kernel action path. The strategy asks for observation-based completion checks and does not supply evaluator traces from gate or held-out splits to the coding model. Observation permissions still depend on the chosen environment/toolkit; a phase plan is not an isolation mechanism.

HarnessPAI's model/code handover is represented here as a code-generation design: a program may call a frozen action-model tool when the configured toolkit provides one. This release does not add a general VLA driver or automatically turn a SimpleMemVLA agent into such a tool. The bundled CPU example uses manipulation tools, not a VLA. Video diagnosis, per-phase capability estimation and expert-data collection for VLA training are outside this implementation.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The CPU integration test uses a scripted reasoning model and the actual Hylo kernel and campaign gate: a no-movement program fails, a repaired program succeeds, the candidate waits for approval, its repair becomes retrievable on promotion and disappears on rollback. Other tests reject fabricated repair evidence, mismatched cases, corrupted artifacts and gate-split diagnostic inputs. A program that does not solve all selected development cases does not become a candidate. These tests establish mechanics, not autonomous model ability. Automatic submission tests cover omitted submit() calls, duplicate program definitions and exhausted submission budgets. An integrity test also rejects a changed artifact that was resealed at the same path after its candidate was admitted.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/tests/test_harness_evolution.py \
  harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/tests/test_research.py \
  harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/tests/test_real_toolkit.py \
  harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/tests/test_prompt_context.py \
  harness/packages/hylo-evolve/tests/test_campaign.py \
  harness/packages/hylo-evolve/tests/test_protocol.py -q

Local CPU checks on 2026-11-04 passed: 33 strategy and regression tests, followed by all 11 strategy tests after adding the artifact-replacement case (34 distinct tests in total). The scripted integration test's perfect toy scores are not an autonomous learning result. Real-model probe outcomes and remaining limitations are recorded in docs/docs/our research notes in the workspace.

docs.title: Design Sources
docs.text:
The existing source study pins Darwin-Agent/HarnessPAI at 3af7d561d531ce3e3a3884a3f801c41b8b98e2fe. The following are design references, read statically:

  • Generated phase programs and model/code handover: references/memory/HarnessPAI/harnesspai/code_library/TEMPLATE.md:20 and :187.
  • Development rollout followed by code promotion and repair-summary writeback: references/memory/HarnessPAI/harnesspai/evolution/loop.py:793 and :839.
  • Phase-scoped repair retrieval: references/memory/HarnessPAI/harnesspai/memory/skill/query.py:44 and :112.
  • Post-write structural checks: references/memory/HarnessPAI/harnesspai/memory/skill/writeback.py:389.

Paths above are relative to the docs research workspace. Its HarnessPAI worktree is unpopulated; the study and this implementation's design check used read-only git show at the recorded commit. Hylo adds its existing independent gate and digest-bound notes, with recall tied to active versions, rather than treating development success as promotion.

docs.title: Plugin examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-plugins: examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Configs and campaigns that use the example plugins of packages/hylo-plugin-examples, and one script that measures what each plugin changes against a run without it. Everything runs on MuJoCo planar reach, so hylo-bench (hylo-env-mujoco) must be in the workspace. Run from the plugins repository root.

uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_guarded.yaml              # each config / campaign on its own
uv run hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml
uv run python examples/01_plugin_effects.py [--quick] [--out DIR]  # every plugin with and without, one table each

01_plugin_effects.py writes runs/examples/plugin-effects/result.json and cem.png. Its comparisons with mujoco-reach use bench's protocol (100 held-out episodes). The others use the configs' validation split (20 episodes).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-11-01, 128-core CPU, no GPU. Runs are deterministic: a rerun gives the same numbers.

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime configs/mujoco_reach.yaml the baseline the others build on: the IK controller (kp 0.3) uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml success 1.00, 35.3 steps, 0 interventions (20 episodes) < 1 s configs/mujoco_guarded.yaml guard examples.slow_zone: the fingertip slows to 25% within 10 cm of the fixed target uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_guarded.yaml success 1.00, 52.2 steps, 35.2 interventions/episode. Against no guards (01_plugin_effects.py): mean fingertip speed in the zone 0.242 -> 0.052 m/s (max 0.463 -> 0.351), 6.6 -> 35.3 steps spent in the zone, episodes 35.2 -> 52.2 steps. Per episode, slow_zone fires 17.7 times, norm_limit 17.5 (also without the zone), and the shield's delta_limit 15.0, because each scaled action jumps from the previous one by more than max_delta: 0.5 < 1 s configs/mujoco_mixture.yaml policies examples.ik_reacher + examples.mixture: 4 seeded samples from two members, medoid executed uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_mixture.yaml success 1.00, 37.0 steps (20 episodes). Under mujoco-reach every variant succeeds 100/100, so the effect shows in steps: member A (gain 0.3, noise 0.05) 36.6, member B (gain 0.1, noise 0.3) 47.7, A steered 36.4, B steered 46.1, mixture steered 38.0, mixture in mean mode 40.0. The steered mixture takes fewer steps than B in 100 of 100 episodes (sign test p = 8e-31) but more than A (A fewer in 54, mixture fewer in 5): it does not beat its better member < 1 s evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml the gate's statistic is a plugin (sign on steps); both gains always succeed uv run hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml kp 0.1 -> 0.2 promoted: fewer steps in 40 of 40 gate pairs, p = 9.1e-13. The same campaign with mcnemar or examples.min_effect archives the candidate (0 discordant pairs on success) 4 s gate test examples.min_effect McNemar promotes a real but small gain; min_effect also requires a net win rate uv run python examples/01_plugin_effects.py IK kp 0.0265 vs 0.025 under mujoco-reach: 95 vs 87%, 8–0 discordant, net effect 0.08. mcnemar p = 0.0039 (passes); min_effect 0.1: p reported as 1 (blocked); min_effect 0.05: p = 0.0039 (passes) in the script evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml online learner examples.cem as a candidate generator uv run hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml 10 rollouts of 80 search episodes over 2 iterations: CEM converged before the configured 3. Search success at kp 0.01 / 0.017 was 0.00 / 0.17, and 1.00 from kp 0.064 up. Best kp 0.228 (mean 36.6 steps). Gate on unseen init states: 1.00 vs parent (kp 0.02) 0.35, 26–0, p = 1.5e-8, promoted; held-out (report only) 1.00 vs 0.40 22 s 01_plugin_effects.py all of the above, with and without each plugin, in one run uv run python examples/01_plugin_effects.py the numbers in the rows above 46 s (quick 38 s, without the three gate campaigns) hylo plugin new + check scaffold a policy plugin and check it without installing it uv run hylo plugin new policy my-policy --dir /tmp/p package created in 0.2 s. Its 2 template tests pass (PYTHONPATH=/tmp/p/hylo-plugin-my-policy/src uv run pytest /tmp/p/hylo-plugin-my-policy/tests). hylo plugin check policy wc_my_policy.plugin:MyPolicyPolicy passes 4 of 4 checks. The check by entry-point name (my-policy) needs uv pip install -e first < 1 s

hylo plugin check on the shipped plugins also passes: examples.slow_zone (guard, 4 checks), examples.min_effect (gate test: type-I 0.025, power 0.81 at 40 pairs), examples.ik_reacher and examples.mixture (policy, 4 checks each), examples.cem (online learner, 4 checks, about 8 s). The online learner check needs --params with a space, for example --params '{"space": {"kp": {"path": "params.kp", "low": 0.01, "high": 1.0}}, "population": 4, "iterations": 2}'. Without it, the check fails with KeyError: 'space'.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-serve: examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Runnable examples of the runtime layer: hylo serve policy and hylo serve workcell started as real subprocesses on free ports, driven through the workcell API (hylo.workcell/v0.1) the way the playground's Operator page drives them, and measured from the recorded traces. Every workcell episode is an ordinary run that hylo trace reads.

uv run python examples/01_sim_arm_end_to_end.py [--quick] [--out DIR]    # from the serve repository

Each script writes result.json and prints a results table; the default output is runs/examples/<slug>/. --quick takes under 30 s. The simulated arm comes from the deployments repository (workcells/sim_arm.yaml: 30 Hz wall clock, watchdog after 60 holds, reset confirmation, operator verdict), found through $HYLO_DEPLOYMENTS or the side-by-side deployments-template checkout.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-11-01 (128-core CPU, no GPU), full mode.

Example What it shows Command Measured result Runtime 01_sim_arm_end_to_end.py Policy server and workcell on the simulated arm, 5 operated episodes (reset confirmed, verdict given), control-loop timing from the traces uv run python examples/01_sim_arm_end_to_end.py 1500 steps at 30.00 Hz (target 30); period jitter 0.32 ms std, worst p99 deviation 2.75 ms, longest interval 36.4 ms, 0 deadline misses (interval > 1.5 periods); policy round trip p50 3.6 ms, p99 8.7 ms; 1 hold per episode (step 0, before the first chunk) 52 s (--quick 11 s) 02_watchdog_and_hold.py A fault-injecting proxy between workcell and policy: 100 ms latency, a 1 s stall, a 3 s stall, a dropped connection uv run python examples/02_watchdog_and_hold.py 100 ms latency: 4 stale actions dropped per chunk, episode completes. 1 s stall: 29 holds (streak 28), the arm stays still (0.00 deg/step while holding, 1.05 deg/step while moving), episode completes. 3 s stall: first hold 162 ms after the fault, watchdog abort after 61 holds, 2162 ms after the fault. Dropped connection: episode ends with an error 30 ms after the drop; all five episodes are in the run 38 s (--quick 23 s) 03_operator_channel.py E-stop mid-episode (10 trials), the latch, reset confirmation, the operator verdict uv run python examples/03_operator_channel.py 0 actions after the e-stop in 9 of 10 trials, 1 in the other (1.5 ms after the press, already in the loop); abort in the trace at most 34.7 ms after the press (one period is 33.3 ms). New episodes refused with 409 at once and still after 3 s, until clear_fault. 0 actions during 2 s of awaiting_reset, first action 12 ms after reset_done. Verdict "partial" recorded as label {verdict: partial, by: operator:operator} 22 s (--quick 11 s) 04_campaign_hot_switch.py hylo serve policy --campaign: a manual approval and a rollback reach the robot between sessions, never during one uv run python examples/04_campaign_hot_switch.py Held-out MuJoCo planar reach through the policy server: base (kp 0.02) 0.42 success, 144 steps; a 200-episode session during which the candidate was approved kept serving the base (0.415); after the approval the candidate (kp 0.04) 1.00, 81.5 steps; after hylo evolve rollback the base again, identical episode for episode (0.42) 31 s (--quick 20 s)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Example 01's numbers depend on machine load: the full run above shared the machine with other jobs; a quick run on a quiet machine measured 0.05 ms jitter std and a 2.8 ms round trip p50.
  • In example 02, after the 3 s stall the watchdog aborts at about 2.2 s, but episode.end is written only when the late reply arrives (3 s): the runtime waits for an in-flight policy call before closing the episode. The arm is stopped at the abort.
  • A dropped policy connection ends the episode with status error, not safety_abort, so the env's stop() is not called; with no new commands the arm keeps its last target.
  • In example 03, a "partial" verdict counts as a failure (success value 0) with the verdict kept in the label.
  • Example 02 found a bug, fixed in packages/hylo-serve/src/hylo/serve/workcell.py (_Instruction.on_episode_end): when the policy connection was lost, the closing on_episode_end call raised after episode.end had been written, so the episode was missing from the run's evallog.json and the operator saw "failed". The error is now kept in the status (last.policy_error) and the episode is recorded.

docs.title: Free-form scenes
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

Free mode of the scene builder: the model writes the task as a Python scene program (hylo.freescene/v0.1) in place of a scene file. The program chooses the robot (Panda, ALOHA or G1), builds the world with MuJoCo's model editor or MJCF (including cables, cloth, tendons, equality constraints and articulated parts), and defines its own success function and a demo with invisible hands. The checker builds the scene, settles it on three seeds, checks reach for every arm, and runs the demo. Details, the checker's limits and the task list are in scenes_free/README.md.

uv run hylo scene build --free "drape the cloth over the box" --out runs/scenes_free/cloth
uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/scenes_free/run_all.py     # every showcase task

The showcase runs have not been run yet: every result in scenes_free/results.json is "not run yet".

docs.title: LIBERO
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

The LIBERO adapter has a second mode for tool-using agents: joint-position control plus the robot contract (depth, camera poses, segmentation, and a Panda model exported from the simulator). The same toolkit therefore runs on LIBERO scenes unchanged. Four programs (pick and place, open a drawer, turn on the stove, drawer then place) cover the task types, and code.llm runs zero-shot. Full details are on hylo-env-libero/examples/README.md.

uv run python bench/adapters/hylo-env-libero/examples/programs/run_programs.py --out runs/libero-programs --n 10
uv run python bench/adapters/hylo-env-libero/examples/run_code_llm.py run --out runs/libero-code-llm \
    --tasks libero_spatial:0 libero_object:0 --episodes 3 --parallel 2
Suite Programs (10 init states per task) SmolVLA (recorded, 50 episodes) libero_spatial 98/100 = 0.98 0.70 libero_object 96/100 = 0.96 0.66 libero_goal 81/100 = 0.81 (push the plate: 4/10) 0.78 libero_10 66/100 = 0.66 0.42

code.llm with qwen3.5:35b-a3b, zero-shot, at most 16 turns:

Task Success Turns (mean) libero_object: pick up the alphabet soup and place it in the basket 3/3 2.7 libero_spatial: pick up the black bowl between the plate and the ramekin and place it on the plate 0/3 9.7 libero_goal: put the wine bottle on the rack 1/1 5

Left: the open_drawer.py program on libero_goal "open the middle drawer of the cabinet" (init state 0, 88 steps, success). Right: qwen3.5 writing code zero-shot on libero_object "pick up the alphabet soup and place it in the basket" (init state 1, 3 turns, 165 steps, success). Both are re-simulated from the traces at 512x512.

Limitations.

  • The comparison with SmolVLA is not like for like. The programs use the simulator's segmentation (privileged) and were written while looking at these tasks; SmolVLA sees RGB only.
  • "Open the top drawer and put the bowl inside" fails 0/10 (the opened drawer blocks every approach to the bowl).
  • libero_10: four tasks at 10/10, but the microwave task fails 0/10 (no skill for putting an object inside an enclosure and closing its door), and flat boxes (cream cheese, butter) and moka pots slip out of the grasp (3/10, 2/10 and 6/10 on the tasks that need them). A grasp mode for flat objects is missing from the toolkit.
  • Push the plate: 4/10; the fingertips slide over the low rim, or the plate ends 6 to 12 cm short.
  • code.llm ran on only 7 episodes, and failed all three on the bowl task.

docs.title: Tool agents live code as policy runs
Live code-as-policy runs
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

code.llm writes one Python block per turn against robot, sees the printed output and images, and calls finish() when it thinks the task is done. The task's score is never shown to it. Six mujoco/manip-v0 tasks, validation seeds 10000 to 10004; full details in RESULTS.md.

uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/llm/run_code_llm.py run --out runs/code-llm \
    --model ollama:gpt-oss:20b --modes zero one --episodes 5
Task gpt-oss:20b zero-shot gpt-oss:20b one-shot qwen3.5:35b-a3b zero-shot Claude Sonnet 5.5 zero-shot pick_place 5/5 5/5 1/1 1/1 stack 4/5 3/5 1/1 1/1 put_in_bowl 5/5 3/5 0/1 1/1 push_to_zone 0/5 0/5 0/1 1/1 press_by_number 0/5 0/5 0/1 1/1 sort_by_colour 0/5 1/5 0/1 0/1 Total 14/30 12/30 2/6 5/6

gpt-oss took 1 to 3 turns on the tasks it solved; 60 episodes in 4.1 h at $0. The six Claude episodes took 9 min and cost $0.98 in total. The one-shot demonstration comes from a different task family.

docs.title: Skill reuse
docs.text:
The program promoted by the campaign is stored as the verified skill stack@1. When an episode's instruction matches it, code.llm is told the skill exists and can import it. gpt-oss:20b then called skills.stack(robot) in its first turn in 10 of 10 fresh stack episodes, all successful, with 49 output tokens per episode (zero-shot without the skill: 4/5). qwen3.5 called it in 2 of 3 episodes, both successful. Before the skill was retrieved by the episode's own instruction and named in the first message, no model called it (0 of 12).

Left: gpt-oss:20b with the promoted skill, "stack the purple block on the green block": one turn, out = skills.stack(robot), 48 output tokens, success. Right: gpt-oss:20b zero-shot on put_in_bowl, written from scratch in the episode (Blender Cycles).

Limitations.

  • No local model solved push_to_zone or press_by_number (0/30 for gpt-oss): it builds push and press goals with the hand pointing sideways and loops on "unreachable". Claude solved both.
  • Models often call finish() without checking; on sort_by_colour, 0 to 2 of 3 or 4 blocks end in the right tray.
  • From scratch, six 30-turn research sessions (gpt-oss and qwen3.5, on stack, press_by_number and sort_by_colour) froze no program. Research worked when it improved an existing program.
  • qwen3.5 ran one episode per task only, because the shared CPU model server queued its turns for 20 to 30 min.

docs.title: Tool agents motion characters and free mode
Motion characters and free mode
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

The motion studio's final motion can be retargeted to any humanoid described by a short mapping file. There are eight: Unitree G1 and H1, Booster T1, Apptronik Apollo and Fourier N1 from MuJoCo Menagerie, Hylo's capsule figure, and two CC0 rigged characters (Kenney, Quaternius) driven in Blender. Every character gets the source's proportions and reports its keypoint error, limb angle error and joint-limit hits; --characters all shows the final motion on all of them in one video grid. In free mode (hylo motion --free) the model writes its own scripts in the run directory, in a guarded process, calling the studio's tools through a kit and doing its own processing with numpy and scipy.

The code and its tests are finished; the five showcase requests have not been run yet. Commands, characters, licences and design: motion_free/README.md.

The G1 runs above used one uniform scale for the whole skeleton. Retargeting now gives each character its own proportions, so their keypoint errors are not directly comparable with new runs.

docs.title: Motion studio
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

A request (text, an image of a pose, or a reference video) becomes a motion for the Unitree G1 humanoid. A model writes Python against motion tools: NVIDIA Kimodo for text to motion, MediaPipe for pose from images and video, motion edits, retargeting to the G1, a check, and a renderer. The check reports kinematic problems (self-collision, joint limits, ground penetration, foot skate) and, separately, a physics rollout in which position servos track the trajectory with no balance controller.

uv run hylo motion "wave with the right hand, then bow" --robot g1 --side-by-side --out runs/motion/wave_bow
uv run hylo motion "strike the pose shown in the image and hold it for a second" --image pose.jpg --robot g1 \
    --out runs/motion/image_pose

Model: qwen3.5:35b-a3b (vision). From motion/runs.json. "Upright" is how long the G1 stays up in the physics rollout; "with ankle strategy" is the same rollout with the check's ankle strategy switched on.

Request Turns Wall min Clip Keypoint error Upright With ankle strategy How it falls "wave with the right hand, then bow" 2 35 5.0 s 5.6 cm 1.48 s 4.35 s right wrist touches the floor "walk forward four steps and turn around" 3 38 9.0 s 4.5 cm 1.22 s 1.13 s pelvis drops below 40% of its start height "a short dance" 2 6 4.0 s 3.9 cm 1.68 s 2.68 s right knee touches the floor "jump in place twice" 2 23 5.0 s 6.8 cm 1.44 s 1.70 s pelvis drops "do what the person in the reference video does" (jumping jacks) 6 95 2.8 s 4.2 cm 1.05 s 1.12 s left knee touches the floor "strike the pose shown in the image and hold it for a second" 3 46 1.0 s 4.2 cm 0.97 s (whole clip) 0.97 s no fall within the clip, but the centre of mass is outside the support in every frame

All six motions have no self-collision and no joint-limit violation.

"wave with the right hand, then bow": the generated human motion (left) and its retargeting to the G1 (right). Kinematic playback, Blender Cycles.

"walk forward four steps and turn around": 9 s, 5.9 m of path, about 175 degrees of turn. Kinematic playback; under physics this motion falls after 1.2 s.

Limitations.

  • Every motion is kinematically clean, but none stays balanced under physics. With no balance controller, five of the six fall within 1.7 s (within 4.35 s with the ankle strategy). The 1 s held pose does not fall within its clip, but its centre of mass is outside the support the whole time.
  • The videos are kinematic playback, not the physics rollout.
