Perception and motion tools
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

Each tool is a model wrapped as a worker in its own uv environment, so torch and the other heavy dependencies never enter the Hylo environment. Every result records the model, its revision and licence, and its timing. All of them were run on this workstation's CPU (32 threads). Full details are on hylo-tools/README.md.

uv run hylo tool list
uv run hylo tool segment frame.png -p basket -p "soup can" --out out/
uv run hylo tool text_motion "a person walks forward and waves" --duration 5 --out out/
Tool Model on the CPU CPU time (32 threads) Status segment SAM 3 3 prompts on a 387x387 frame: 11.9 s wall works depth MoGe-2 480x480: 4.3 s inference, 11.2 s with loading works gravity GeoCalib 480x480: 0.5 s inference, 4.3 s with loading works mesh SAM 3D Objects (gated); fallback MoGe-2 depth, carving and marching cubes fallback: 11.3 s fallback only (no access to SAM 3D yet) convex CoACD open cup: 2.5 s, 28 parts works hands WiLoR + MANO; fallback MediaPipe Hand Landmarker 32 frames: 1.1 s (MediaPipe) fallback only (MANO not registered) human GVHMR + SMPL; fallback MediaPipe Pose Landmarker 24 frames: 1.4 s (MediaPipe) fallback only (SMPL not registered, no CPU port) text_motion NVIDIA Kimodo (Llama 3 8B text encoder) 5 s clip: 57 s wall works render Blender 5.2.3 Cycles; fallback MuJoCo 30 frames at 480x272: 11.4 s works

Left: SAM 3 masks for the prompts "basket", "soup can" and "milk carton" on a LIBERO frame. The "milk carton" prompt also matches two other boxes, at scores 0.61 to 0.73. Right: MoGe-2 depth and normals for the same scene.

Left: Kimodo text to motion, retargeted to a small MuJoCo humanoid. Right: MediaPipe hand keypoints on a test video, in the image and in 3D.

Limitations. Three primary models are blocked by access or registration (SAM 3D Objects, WiLoR with MANO, and GVHMR with SMPL), so those tools run on their fallbacks. On a rendered tabletop, MoGe-2's metric scale is 3.8 times too large.

docs.title: Program improvement
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

A campaign on stack starts from a hand-written parent that is deliberately weak: it stacks two blocks only and never retries. The generator research.llm gives gpt-oss:20b a research session with three development cases, in which it rewrites the parent. The campaign's gate then compares the new program with the parent on unseen initial states. The model never sees the gate or held-out results. Full details are on campaign/README.md.

uv run hylo evolve run harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/campaign/campaign.yaml
uv run hylo evolve status runs/campaign/campaign
Step Split (episodes) Candidate Parent Wins / losses (pairs) p Research session search, 3 dev cases 3/3 (each of 3 submissions) Stage 1: early rejection first 10 of search_val 6 / 0 (10) Stage 2 search_val (20) 1.00 0.30 14 / 0 (20) 6.1e-5 Gate (McNemar, alpha 0.05) gate (20) 0.95 0.50 9 / 0 (20) 0.002 Held-out report heldout (20) 1.00 0.60 8 / 0 (20) 0.0039

The candidate was promoted as sealed artifact 0a1ee96b2f810ab6. The campaign took 44 min (a 22 min session and 22 min of rollouts) and used 30 model calls with 406,698 input and 7,082 output tokens, for $0.

Held-out seed 30080, "build a tower: the blue block at the bottom, then the green block, then the orange block on top". Left: the parent stops after one level (failure, 177 steps). Right: the promoted program builds all three levels (success, 424 steps). Blender Cycles.

Limitations.

  • This is one campaign on one task, against a parent that was weakened on purpose.
  • From scratch, the local models did not get this far: three gpt-oss research sessions without a parent produced no program that solved a development case (see RESULTS.md, section 2).
  • The promoted program wastes a motion: it lifts the bottom block and drops it back before stacking on it. The gate did not penalise this.

docs.title: Replay to simulation
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

From one recorded episode (ours, a LeRobot dataset episode, or a human video), the pipeline names the objects with a vision model, masks them with SAM 3, and lifts them to 3D with recorded depth or MoGe-2. It then tracks them, builds collision meshes (mesh and convex-decomposition tools), places them in a MuJoCo scene with the Panda (or a free-floating gripper for a human hand), and replays the motion in physics. The checks compare simulated object poses with the tracked ones and match contact events (grasp, lift, place) to the recording.

uv run hylo replay panda:stack:3 --out runs/replay/panda_stack_3            # one of our episodes, recorded now
uv run hylo replay hf:physical-intelligence/libero:1280 --profile libero --camera image --out runs/replay/libero_1280

From replay/results.json. Object error is the simulated pose against the tracked pose, mean / final, in mm.

Source Episode Events matched Final state reproduced Object error, mean / final ours, Panda pick_place 1 3/3 yes 6.0 / 2.1 ours, Panda pick_place 2 3/3 yes 5.8 / 0.4 ours, Panda stack 3 6/6 yes 2.7 / 5.4 and 4.7 / 3.1 (two blocks) ours, Panda put_in_bowl 4 3/3 yes 8.0 / 5.0 ours, Panda push_to_zone 5 no events yes 3.3 / 10.5 LIBERO 1280 1/2 no 21 to 45 / 34 to 75 (the bowl to move got no mask) LIBERO 379 none no registration failed (scale 0.057) LIBERO 813 0/2 no 9.4 / 19.8 (basket; no carried object found) DROID 21 3/3 no 53 / 97 human video mug 0 0/2 no 69 / 120

For our episodes, where ground truth is known, the largest error of a reconstructed object's size is 5.3 to 10.6 mm per episode.

With --agent, a model drives the same steps instead of the fixed order. qwen3.5:35b-a3b ran pick_place 2 in 12 turns (1,558 s of model time, 28,411 input and 1,104 output tokens, $0) and called the steps in the suggested order. It reproduced the outcome as the fixed pipeline did: the same labels and masks, 3/3 events, a simulated object error of 6.1 mm mean and 1.2 mm final against the ground truth (5.9 mm and 0.7 mm for the fixed pipeline). The run shows the agent loop working, not the model correcting anything: it kept every default, never looked at the overlays, skipped the video step, and described its events as matched to the ground truth when they were matched to the recording.

Panda stack 3, "build a tower: the blue block at the bottom, then the green block, then the yellow block on top". Left: the recording. Right: the physics replay, in which the blocks move only by contact. 6 of 6 events matched, and the tower stands at the end.

A failure: LIBERO episode 1280. The registration scale came out at 0.39, the replayed robot (right) does not line up with the reconstructed scene, and the black bowl it should move was never masked.

Both videos are rendered with MuJoCo, on purpose: the replay uses the recording's camera, so the two views line up.

Limitations.

  • Only our own Panda episodes reproduce. They come from our simulator, with recorded depth and a known camera pose.
  • No external episode (3 LIBERO, 1 DROID, 1 human video) reproduces. Monocular depth, registration and the hand-to-gripper mapping are each off by centimetres or more.

docs.title: Robot toolkit
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

hylo-manip gives a program one object, robot, with stateless verbs over any robot described by a RobotSpec: look, find (masks for text labels), objects, box, grasps, place_at, plan (IK plus a collision-free path) and run, the only verb that moves the robot. The six reference programs in programs/ each define solve(robot) for one mujoco/manip-v0 task. They see the front, side and wrist cameras with the environment's segmentation and no privileged object state, and they run as code.program (no model) through hylo run.

uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/programs/run_programs.py --out runs/manip-programs
Task Success Episodes Steps (mean) Wall s per episode pick_place 1.00 20 141 23.7 stack 1.00 20 236 57.5 put_in_bowl 1.00 20 148 24.2 push_to_zone 1.00 20 93 24.0 press_by_number 1.00 20 235 38.3 sort_by_colour 1.00 20 596 184.4

Validation split, seeds 10000 to 10019; 322 s of wall time for all 120 episodes with 48 workers.

The reference sort_by_colour program on validation seed 10015, "sort the blocks by colour into the matching trays": the orange block goes into the orange tray, then both red blocks into the red tray (11 motions, 433 steps, success). The caption numbers the motions and shows what the program printed: the trays and blocks it found with the cameras. Rendered with Blender Cycles on the CPU from the recorded joint positions.

Limitations.

  • The programs were written by hand while looking at these tasks, so they show what the toolkit can do, not what an agent finds on its own.
  • Segmentation comes from the simulator. It is a declared observation and part of the config digest, but it is still privileged perception.
  • These numbers are for one robot, the Franka Panda, on one benchmark.

docs.title: Scene builder
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

A model writes a hylo.scene/v0.1 file from a one-line task: objects, their shapes and start regions, and a success predicate. A checker runs five stages on it: schema; static (names and references); physics (the scene loads and settles, nothing falls or penetrates, and the predicate is false at the start); reach (every object has a grasp the arm reaches, and every place target is reachable); and satisfiable (objects placed where the predicate asks make it true). The problems it finds go back to the model until the scene passes. code.llm then solves the scene with privileged state: robot.scene() returns the simulator's object poses and joint states.

uv run hylo scene build "put the ball in the cup" --out runs/scenes/ball_cup --attempts 6
uv run hylo scene solve runs/scenes/ball_cup --turns 10 --reply-tokens 2500

Model: qwen3.5:35b-a3b (vision) for both building and solving, from scenes/results.json.

Task Build attempts (problems in the failed ones) Solved Turns Steps Model time size_tower: "stack the three blocks into a tower ordered by size: the largest block at the bottom and the smallest on top" 2 (a timed-out model call) yes 6 423 66 min ball_cup: "put the ball in the cup" 2 (timeout) yes 3 159 37 min slide_lid: "slide the lid of the box open so that the box is uncovered" 3 (timeout; predicate true at start) yes 2 87 17 min drawer_block: "open the drawer and put the red block in it" 6 (unstable; predicate true at start, twice; unsatisfiable; unstable) no 10 448 88 min cylinder_upright: "a cylinder is lying on its side on the table; stand it upright on top of the wooden box" 5 (schema; timeout, twice; predicate true at start) no 5 160 67 min colour_row: "line up the red, green and blue blocks in a row along the y axis, in that order" 2 (timeout) no 4 483 15 min

All 6 scenes were built and checked; 3 of 6 were solved. Model time includes queueing on the shared Ollama server.

size_tower: the scene the model wrote (blue large, green medium and red small block), solved in 6 turns and 423 steps. The model moves the large block to the centre, stacks the medium one on it, then places the small one on top. The episode ends with the hand still over the tower, so the small block is partly hidden by the fingers. The caption shows each turn's thought, code and printed result.

ball_cup: the red ball picked up and dropped into the fixed blue cup, in 3 turns and 159 steps.

slide_lid: the gripper pushes the lid along its slide joint until it overhangs the front of the box (the predicate asks for at least 4 cm of travel), in 2 turns and 87 steps.

The three videos are re-simulated on a fresh mujoco.panda_scene from the recorded actions. Each re-simulation gives the recorded task digest, step count and outcome, and the frames are rendered with Blender Cycles at 960x720.

Limitations.

  • 3 of the 6 scenes were solved, and only with privileged state.
  • The failures are the model's: it never opened the drawer, it did not turn the cylinder upright, and it lined the blocks up in the wrong direction. In the last two it called finish() without checking.
  • Single model calls took up to 26 min on the shared server, mostly queueing, and several builds lost an attempt to a timed-out call. The wall times say little about the method.

docs.title: Tool-calling agents
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

tools.llm (RFC-0007) gives a chat model the robot as typed tools and lets it call them natively, one checked action at a time: it measures freely (locate, grasp_options, pixel_to_world, calc, ...), and every action (grasp, place, move_tcp, ...) is a proposal that runs through the kernel and the safety shield and comes back as a measured receipt with fresh images. Refused actions that moved nothing cost no decision; handles measured before the robot moved are refused as stale; the task's own check is the verdict.

uv run hylo preflight --model ollama:qwen3.5:35b-a3b --vision          # text, image, tool call, tool result
uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/tools_llm/run_tools_llm.py run --out runs/tools-llm --episodes 3
uv run hylo watch runs/tools-llm/<run>                                  # follow or replay an episode
uv run hylo seal runs/tools-llm/<run>                                   # hash chains, inventory, read-only

qwen3.5:35b-a3b (vision, reasoning off, local, $0), zero-shot, cameras front / side / wrist with the environment's segmentation, validation split, 3 episodes per task:

Task Success Decisions (mean) Model calls (mean) Tokens in / out (mean) Wall s (mean) pick_place 2/3 2.3 6.3 46,896 / 932 133 put_in_bowl 3/3 2.0 4.7 32,111 / 436 48 stack 3/3 3.3 8.7 73,884 / 1,138 122 push_to_zone 0/1 12 (8 more refused) 29 377,227 / 7,999 962

push_to_zone was stopped after its first episode (it ran out of its 600 steps); press_by_number and sort_by_colour were not run for this page.

stack, seed 10000: locate both blocks, choose a grasp option, grasp, locate the target block again (the earlier handle is stale after the motion), place on it; five model calls, three decisions. Re-simulated from the trace, captions from the agent's turns and the condensed tool results.

The evidence a run keeps: every trace line is hash-chained (prev, h), so hylo seal refuses a run whose lines were changed, removed or reordered and hylo seal --verify lists any file changed after sealing (the stack run above: 3 episodes, 531 to 2,124 chained lines each, 45 files sealed). Model prompts are recorded by layer digest (protocol, evidence rules, boundary, embodiment card) with the tool surface's digest. hylo chats turns the successful, unsteered conversations into training records.

What the runs show.

  • The model asks for a grasp option, executes it, re-locates the place target after the motion and places in two decisions on pick_place and put_in_bowl; stack takes three.
  • An agent's own finish(success) is not the verdict: in one pick_place episode the model reported success after place, and the task's check (object resting on the plate) said failure.
  • Without a push verb, push_to_zone has to be improvised from straight move_tcp motions; an early version of the agent let the model repeat the same refused rotation for 60 calls, so identical refused actions now count as repeated and three in a row end the episode.

docs.title: Perturbed LIBERO
docs.text:
Seven perturbations of the official LIBERO scenes, declared on the task (benchmark params: perturb):

libero_goal "put the bowl on the plate": original; position (the bowl trades places with the cream cheese box); task (a rewritten goal: the cream cheese box on the plate, checked by LIBERO's own BDDL predicate); language (a paraphrase); object (recoloured); camera (moved about its view axis); noise (pixel noise and a glare spot); robot_init (the arm starts from offset joints).

27 of the 40 tasks of libero_spatial, libero_object, libero_goal and libero_10 have a goal rewrite (single On / In goals onto a named object); each instruction has three paraphrases written by qwen3.5:35b-a3b and kept only when they contain every object and place word of the original. The perturbations are implemented and tested on the simulator (the picture above, and the goal rewrite checked by LIBERO's own predicate); tools.llm has not been evaluated on them yet.

docs.title: Tool agents two arms and a humanoid
Two arms and a humanoid
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

The same toolkit drives robots with more than one arm and with multi-finger hands. Two environments on MuJoCo Menagerie models (fetched at a pinned commit, never vendored): mujoco.aloha_table, two arms at a table, and mujoco.g1_table, the Unitree G1 with its three-finger hands, pelvis fixed, working at a table. Programs pass arm= to the arm-specific verbs, and robot.run({"left": plan_l, "right": plan_r}, sync=True) runs both arms in one motion, checked at every step for the arms touching each other. For the hands, hand_grasps(..., kind="power") or kind="pinch" proposes multi-finger grasps.

uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/programs/run_programs.py --suite bimanual --out runs/bimanual-programs
uv run python harness/adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/programs/run_programs.py --suite humanoid --out runs/humanoid-programs
Task What makes it a two-arm or hand task Privileged oracle Camera-only program ALOHA handover the bar starts where only one arm reaches; the zone is where only the other reaches 1.00 1.00 ALOHA lift_box the box is too wide for one gripper; lifted level by its two handles for one second 1.00 1.00 ALOHA two_bins a 260-step limit; one arm after the other takes 407 to 489 steps 1.00 1.00 G1 pick_place a three-finger power grasp 1.00 0.80 G1 two_hands one block per hand at the same time, 340-step limit (one after the other: 408 to 424 steps) 0.90 0.50 G1 press_button press a button with the hand 0.90 1.00

Validation split, 20 episodes per task. After the toolkit gained these features, the six Panda programs still score 1.00 on all tasks.

Top left: ALOHA handover; the left arm brings the red bar to the middle, the right arm takes its free end and puts it in the orange zone (Blender Cycles). Top right: two_bins; both arms place their blocks at the same time. Bottom left: G1 pick_place, the green block onto the plate (Blender Cycles). Bottom right: G1 two_hands, one block per hand. All are camera-only programs on validation seeds, re-simulated from the traces.

Limitations.

  • No two-hand lift on the G1: the three-finger hands could not hold a box level (squeezed between the palms, or by flat or bar handles), so that task was replaced by two_hands.
  • The G1 presses with its closed hand; pointing one finger down was reachable over too little of the table.
  • The G1 hands needed physics adjustments: no collision between a hand's own palm and fingers, two finger servos capped at half their torque, and gravity compensation on the arms. The ALOHA bar is light (30 to 60 g) with extra torsional friction, so an end grasp holds it.
  • The G1 reaches only a narrow strip of the table (x 0.22 to 0.32 m, |y| up to 0.25 m), and its programs are weaker than the oracle: two_hands at 0.50 mostly misses the first grasp of one hand and then runs out of steps.
  • The programs were written by hand while looking at these tasks; segmentation comes from the simulator.

docs.title: Tool agents what does not work yet
What does not work yet
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

  • Scene builder: 3 of 6 scenes solved, and only with privileged state. The other three failed on the model's side: the drawer was never opened, the cylinder was not turned upright, and the row was laid out in the wrong direction.
  • Replay to simulation: only our own Panda episodes reproduce. None of LIBERO (3 episodes), DROID or the human video does.
  • Motion studio: the motions fall over under physics. Five of six fall within 1.7 s without the ankle strategy, and the sixth, a 1 s hold, has its centre of mass outside the support.
  • Code as policy: local models solve no push or press task, and from-scratch research sessions froze no program.
  • Humanoid: the G1 cannot lift a box with both hands, and its camera-only programs score 0.50 on two_hands.
  • LIBERO: the comparison with SmolVLA uses privileged segmentation; on libero_10 the microwave task fails 0/10 and flat boxes slip out of the grasp.
  • Program improvement: improving a working parent succeeds, but writing a program from scratch in a research session does not yet work with local models.
  • Tool-calling agents: push and press tasks have no dedicated verbs and are improvised from move_tcp; the model's finish(success) is often wrong, which is why it never decides.
  • Worlds: the quadruped trot is open-loop (turn rates differ by robot); the Crazyflie is slow because of its weak moment actuators; humanoids walk only under a pretrained policy on the leg models it was trained for (the 29-joint G1 and the full H1 cannot stand by themselves); people are kinematic and stop rather than step aside.
  • Chat-built worlds: the model writes scenes in small steps and fixes overlaps, but it also weakened its own check until it passed, and reported a lift it never measured; role campaigns check a fixed goal for this reason.

docs.title: Worlds
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

All program and tool experiments

A stage (RFC-0008) is a scene written as entities with revisions: shapes and meshes, robots from 24 packs, cameras, lights and people. A world is a MuJoCo simulation built from one revision; every action names the world generation it was decided on and returns a receipt measured in the simulation. The same 21 tools serve a chat model (hylo world chat), the Studio, coding agents (hylo mcp) and role campaigns (hylo roles).

uv run python bench/adapters/hylo-env-mujoco/examples/world/showcase.py --out runs/world-showcase   # the videos below
uv run hylo world chat "a table with a red cube, a Panda that picks it up, a Go1 walking past" --vision
uv run hylo mcp --surface mujoco.world --param stage=lab
Scene What runs Measured (receipts and checks) Quadrupeds Go2, Go1, A1, Spot: an open-loop trot, then a turn, all in the same steps 0.78, 1.27, 1.22, 1.31 m forward in 4 s, heading within 1.1 degrees; turns of 50, 79, 75, 37 degrees; all upright Humanoids G1 and H1 leg models under pretrained walking policies (numpy LSTM, weights read without executing them) G1 2.23 m and H1 2.03 m in 5 s (0.45 and 0.41 m/s for 0.5 commanded); then turns of 122 and 120 degrees; both upright Drones Crazyflie 2 and Skydio X2 flying three waypoints each X2 within 6 mm of every waypoint; Crazyflie within 0 to 48 mm (its moment actuators are weak, so its gains are scaled down) Arms a Panda picks a cube onto a plate; a UR5e with a mounted Robotiq gripper and a TidyBot base move at the same time gripper closed on the cube (holding), check near(cube, plate) and settled satisfied Crowd four people on routes around two crates while a Go1 trots across no person touched anything; 7.7 to 10.2 m walked each, around the crates and the dog; the Go1 2.41 m Dataset export while the Panda moves: two cameras, six frames each 12 samples: RGB, depth in metres, segmentation by entity, camera pose and world state per frame

Recorded through the world tools (act with record), MuJoCo rendering on the CPU. Last tile: three exported frames of the top camera (RGB, depth, segmentation by entity).

The Studio's World page on a chat session's stage: entities, a free view to orbit, actions and checks by hand, and the session's transcript.

A chat model building a world. qwen3.5:35b-a3b was asked for a table with a red cube, a Panda next to it, a Go1 1.5 m away, the Go1 to walk 1 m, the cube to be picked up and lifted 10 cm, and a check. Two sessions, 26 and 60 model calls:

  • First: it built the scene in a few stage edits after two rejected patches, fixed an overlap the build reported, and walked the Go1 about 1.2 m. The cube, however, had no body, so it was fixed in place: the gripper closed on it but nothing could lift it. The model's check (cube 9 cm above the table) failed; it lowered the threshold to 5 cm until the check passed, and reported a 19 cm lift it never measured.
  • Second, after world_build started listing the entities that are fixed in place: it made the cube movable, but then spent all its remaining calls moving the Panda between the floor and the table top (43 stage revisions) and never ran an action.

Neither session lifted the cube. Both are traced and can be replayed with hylo watch runs/world-chat/demo1.

Role campaigns. hylo roles run with a scripted worker (the test campaign): the dev task's acting calls become a recipe skill keyed by the failure the task started with (NOT_LIFTED), a model-free replay on a fresh copy of the stage verifies it, and the held-out task is offered the skill and solved. Every call is in a ledger with its argument digest and receipts.

docs.title: Tool-using agents
docs.text:
Source

Reproduction record from hylo-harness: adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/README.md. Every number on this page was measured by the scripts next to it; run them to reproduce.

Agents that act by writing Python against a small set of robot and perception tools, instead of outputting joint commands directly (RFC-0006). Each tool call that moves the robot goes through the kernel and its safety shield, and every model turn and every tool call is a trace event. This page collects the workflows that are finished, with the numbers their recorded runs gave, the videos those runs produced, and what does not work yet.

Common setup, unless a section says otherwise:

  • one shared 128-thread CPU workstation, no GPU;
  • local language models through Ollama: qwen3.5:35b-a3b (vision) and gpt-oss:20b (text only), at $0;
  • the task's score is never shown to the model;
  • every robot video is re-simulated or played back from the recorded run (its actions or joint trajectory); none is a separate rollout.
Workflow Headline Section Robot toolkit and programs Six hand-written Panda programs that use only cameras and segmentation: 1.00 on every task (20 validation episodes each) Robot toolkit Two arms and a humanoid ALOHA (two arms) and Unitree G1 (dexterous hands): camera-only programs solve 3 of 3 two-arm tasks at 1.00; G1 programs 0.80, 0.50 and 1.00 Two arms and a humanoid Program improvement A program written by gpt-oss:20b passes the gate: 0.95 against 0.50 for its parent (p = 0.002), and 1.00 against 0.60 on held-out Program improvement Scene builder 6 of 6 scenes written from text pass the checker; 3 of 6 are then solved by qwen3.5 with privileged state Scene builder Free-form scenes The model writes scene programs (any robot, cables, cloth, joints) checked by building, settling, reach and a scripted demo; not run yet Free-form scenes Replay to simulation All 5 of our own Panda episodes reproduce in physics (2.7 to 8.0 mm mean object error); 0 of 5 external episodes do Replay to simulation Motion studio 6 requests (text, image, video) become kinematically clean Unitree G1 motions; none stays balanced under physics (five fall within 1.7 s) Motion studio Motion characters and free mode Eight target characters (five Menagerie humanoids, a capsule figure, two CC0 rigged characters) and a free mode where the model writes its own pipeline; not run yet Motion characters and free mode LIBERO robot contract Programs: 0.98 on libero_spatial, 0.96 on libero_object, 0.81 on libero_goal, 0.66 on libero_10 (SmolVLA: 0.70, 0.66, 0.78, 0.42); qwen3.5 writing code: 4 of 7 LIBERO Perception and motion tools 9 tool adapters (SAM 3, MoGe-2, GeoCalib, Kimodo, Blender, ...) run on the CPU; 3 of them only on their fallbacks Perception and motion tools Live code-as-policy runs Local models solve pick-and-place-type tasks zero-shot (gpt-oss:20b 14/15); with the promoted skill offered, gpt-oss solves 10/10 stack episodes in one turn Live code-as-policy runs Tool-calling agents qwen3.5 through typed tools, one checked action at a time: 8 of 9 episodes on pick_place, put_in_bowl and stack; hash-chained, sealed runs; seven LIBERO perturbations Tool-calling agents Worlds 24 robot packs in stages a model edits: four quadrupeds trot, two humanoids walk under pretrained policies, two drones reach waypoints, an arm picks onto a plate, people walk around obstacles Worlds

docs.title: Video-memory checks
docs.text:
The recorded 2026-11-04 integration checked 18 sampling comparisons against pinned upstream code. Five GPU comparisons with batch 2 matched prepared inputs, subtask text and action chunks bitwise. The Hylo memory bridge completed 8/8 RoboMME regression episodes across PickXtimes, VideoUnmask, PickHighlight and PatternLock.

Those episode IDs had already been observed. This establishes implementation regression, not a fresh held-out success estimate or improvement over another memory method. The native agent lifecycle has CPU coverage; a full native Hylo kernel-to-RoboMME evaluation remains unverified. Longer windows, alternative frame selection and background prefill are possible experiments, not implemented or validated improvements.

docs.title: libero10_critic
docs.text:
SmolVLA on LIBERO-10: sample 4 chunks per decision, execute the one a learned chunk critic values most (hylo.agents.critic, model in hylo.instruments.critic). Train the critic first: uv run python -m hylo.learn.critic --runs runs/... --task-prefix libero/libero_10/ \ --image-camera agentview --out runs/critics/<name> and reference it by id (hylo store ref runs/critics/<name>). l10-v1 predates manifests and was adopted without a record of its training runs: it runs here, but the RSI gate refuses it in a candidate (unknown provenance).

uv run hylo run bench/examples/configs/libero10_critic.yaml
bench/examples/configs/libero10_critic.yaml 
# SmolVLA on LIBERO-10: sample 4 chunks per decision, execute the one a learned chunk critic values most
# (hylo.agents.critic, model in hylo.instruments.critic). Train the critic first:
#   uv run python -m hylo.learn.critic --runs runs/... --task-prefix libero/libero_10/ \
#       --image-camera agentview --out runs/critics/<name>
# and reference it by id (`hylo store ref runs/critics/<name>`). l10-v1 predates manifests and was adopted without
# a record of its training runs: it runs here, but the RSI gate refuses it in a candidate (unknown provenance).
schema_version: hylo.experiment/v0.1
name: libero10-critic
benchmark: {type: libero, split: search_val, params: {suite: libero_10, protocol: rsi, replicates: 1, gate_looks: 3}}
env:
  type: libero
  remote: {runtime: libero-sim}
agent:
  type: remote
  params:
    ref: lerobot.critic_steered
    runtime: lerobot
    params:
      repo_id: lerobot/smolvla_libero
      num_threads: 3
      steering: {n_samples: 4, selector: gripper_vote_medoid, execution_steps: 25, seed_noise: true}
      critic: {path: "artifact:l10-v1@7934d463d67ad242", beta: 0.5, within_vote: true}
trace: {record_privileged: true, image_every: 5}
workers: 12
output_dir: runs

docs.title: mujoco_online_cem
docs.text:
Online learning as a candidate generator: the CEM learner (packages/hylo-plugin-examples) searches the controller gain by rolling out on the search split, seals its result with every rollout run in the provenance, and the proposer turns the best gain into a candidate that the gate judges on unseen init states.

uv run hylo evolve run plugins/examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml
plugins/examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml 
# Online learning as a candidate generator: the CEM learner (packages/hylo-plugin-examples) searches the controller
# gain by rolling out on the search split, seals its result with every rollout run in the provenance, and the
# proposer turns the best gain into a candidate that the gate judges on unseen init states.
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-online-cem
experiment: ../configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi}, agent.params.kp: 0.02}
proposer:
  type: learn
  params:
    learner: examples.cem
    online: true
    out_root: runs/evolve/mujoco-online-cem/learned
    params: {space: {kp: {path: params.kp, low: 0.01, high: 1.0, init: 0.05}}, population: 5, iterations: 3}
    patch: {agent.params.kp: "{metrics.best.kp}"}
    hypothesis: "a gain of {metrics.best.kp} found by CEM on the search split reaches more targets in time"
cycles: 1
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-online-cem

docs.title: mujoco_steps_gate
docs.text:
The gate's statistic is a plugin. Both gains always reach the target, so a success-based gate (McNemar) has no discordant pairs; a sign test on steps (lower is better) promotes the faster one. Vetoes stay on success and safety. Try {type: examples.min_effect, params: {min_effect: 0.1}} from packages/hylo-plugin-examples as well.

uv run hylo evolve run plugins/examples/evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml
plugins/examples/evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml 
# The gate's statistic is a plugin. Both gains always reach the target, so a success-based gate (McNemar) has no
# discordant pairs; a sign test on steps (lower is better) promotes the faster one. Vetoes stay on success and
# safety. Try {type: examples.min_effect, params: {min_effect: 0.1}} from packages/hylo-plugin-examples as well.
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-steps-gate
experiment: ../configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi}, agent.params.kp: 0.1}
proposer: {type: rule.gain, params: {path: agent.params.kp, factors: [2.0]}}
protocol: {gate_test: {type: sign, params: {metric: steps, direction: lower}}}
cycles: 1
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-steps-gate

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Script What it does bench/examples/policies/compare.py Every reference policy family on MuJoCo planar reach: demonstrations -> learners -> scorecards -> leaderboard. bench/examples/rsi_demo.py End-to-end offline improvement loop on MuJoCo planar reach.

docs.title: First improvement
docs.text:
Compare two controllers, run a campaign that improves a weak one, and serve the promoted version. This is a complete CPU improvement loop; it changes controller parameters without training a model.

You need the installed workspace and the quickstart. Run commands from bench/. From the workspace root:

cd bench

docs.title: 1. Compare
docs.text:
An evaluation protocol fixes everything except the agent being scored. mujoco-reach is 100 episodes: a fixed and a random target, 50 held-out seeds each.

uv run hylo bench list
uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name ik-0.3 \
    --policy '{"type": "baseline.planar_ik", "params": {"kp": 0.3}}'

The run ends with the scorecard's path and its success rate:

{
  "scorecard": "scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.3.json",
  "success_mean": 1.0,
  "success_ci95": [0.963, 1.0],
  "n": 100
}

Score a second policy, then rank and compare the two:

uv run hylo bench run mujoco-reach --name ik-0.05 \
    --policy '{"type": "baseline.planar_ik", "params": {"kp": 0.05}}'
uv run hylo bench leaderboard        # every scorecard under scorecards/, per protocol, best first
uv run hylo bench compare scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.05.json scorecards/mujoco-reach/ik-0.3.json

### mujoco-reach v1  (`a76c7037efb84660`)

| # | policy | success % | 95% CI | episodes | mean steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ik-0.05 | 100.0 | 96.3–100.0 | 100 | 68 |
| 2 | ik-0.3 | 100.0 | 96.3–100.0 | 100 | 36 |

Both policies succeed on all 100 episodes, so they tie, and ties are listed by name. ik-0.3 needs about half the steps. compare pairs the scorecards episode by episode for a one-sided exact McNemar test. Neither policy wins an episode the other loses, so p = 1.0:

{"candidate": "ik-0.05", "baseline": "ik-0.3", "n_pairs": 100, "candidate_wins": 0, "parent_wins": 0, "p_value": 1.0}

More in benchmarking.

docs.title: 2. Improve
docs.text:
A campaign tries changes to a config and keeps one only if it beats the current version on episodes it was not chosen on. Here the IK controller starts with the weak gain kp: 0.02, and a rule-based generator proposes 2× and 4× the gain:

bench/examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach-gain
experiment: ../configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {agent.params.kp: 0.02, workers: 16, benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi, gate_looks: 2}}
proposer: {type: rule.gain, params: {path: agent.params.kp, factors: [2.0, 4.0]}}
protocol: {alpha: 0.05, gate_looks: 2, stage1_pairs: 20}
cycles: 3
stop_after_no_progress: 1
approval: auto
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain

The generator is configured under proposer, and the top-level protocol: block holds the gate settings, not an evaluation protocol. benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi} gives the campaign its four splits: search, search_val, gate and heldout.

uv run hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml

[cycle 1] parent = base config
[cycle 1] parent-search                      search     success=0.450 n=80
[cycle 1] parent-search_val                  search_val success=0.400 n=40
[cycle 1] cand-8786c03a32-search_val         search_val success=1.000 n=40
[cycle 1] cand-dca7bbd596-search_val         search_val success=1.000 n=40
[cycle 1] parent-gate                        gate       success=0.350 n=40
[cycle 1] cand-8786c03a32-gate               gate       success=1.000 n=40
[cycle 1] cand-8786c03a32-heldout            heldout    success=1.000 n=40
[cycle 1] parent-heldout                     heldout    success=0.400 n=40
[cycle 1] done: promoted=cand-8786c03a32 heldout={...}
[cycle 2] parent = cand-8786c03a32
...
[cycle 2] done: promoted=None heldout=null
{
  "cycles_done": 2,
  "stopped": "no promotion in 1 consecutive cycles",
  "out_dir": "runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain"
}

Timings are left out above. Cycle 1 promotes a candidate: on held-out episodes, success rises from 0.40 to 1.00 in this run (24 wins, no losses, 40 pairs). Cycle 2 finds nothing better, so the campaign stops (stop_after_no_progress: 1). Candidate ids differ from run to run. Check the result:

uv run hylo evolve status examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml

Among other fields, the status shows the active version and the change it makes to the base config:

{
  "active": "cand-8786c03a32",
  "effective_patch": {"agent.params.kp": 0.04},
  "pending_approval": null
}

The campaign writes its active version to runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain/active.json, which step 3 serves. hylo evolve rollback would undo the promotion (campaigns); keep it for now.

docs.title: 3. Serve
docs.text:
A policy server serves a campaign's active version and follows later promotions and rollbacks. It needs no hardware:

uv run hylo serve policy --campaign runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain      # port 8000 by default; Ctrl+C stops it

[policy] ws://127.0.0.1:8000/wc and /openpi (version cand-8786c03a32)

A workcell next to a robot connects to this server; see Deployment.

docs.title: 4. Inspect
docs.text:
Studio shows the runs, episodes and campaigns from the steps above. Build its web UI once (optional setup), then start it from bench/:

uv run hylo playground          # http://127.0.0.1:8765

It shows runs/ and examples/ of the directory it starts in. Open Runs & replays to step through an episode, and Self-improvement to follow the campaign (Studio).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page sets up a workspace that can run the quickstart, and checks that it works.

You need Linux, Python 3.10 or newer and uv. The first CPU experiment needs no GPU, language model, camera renderer or downloaded weights. Run the setup commands below from the new workspace root.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
Clone the harness into a new directory and run its bootstrap script there:

mkdir hylo && cd hylo
git clone https://github.com/HyloAI/hylo-harness.git harness
HYLO_GIT_BASE=https://github.com/HyloAI harness/dev/bootstrap.sh

The script clones bench, serve, studio, plugins and docs next to the harness. It writes a pyproject.toml that makes this directory a uv workspace, and runs uv sync, which installs every package, editable, into .venv. The deployments template is cloned separately; see deployment. Rerun the script after you add or remove a repository.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
Register bench/runs as this machine's store. The quickstart writes its runs there:

uv run hylo store init bench/runs      # recorded as `store:` in ~/.config/hylo/profile.yaml
uv run hylo store ls

$HYLO_STORE, when set, overrides the registered store. Profiles has the full lookup order.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
uv run hylo --help              # the subcommands of the installed packages
uv run hylo plugins             # every plugin: group, name, contract version, maturity, licence

hylo plugins should list mujoco.planar_reach and baseline.planar_ik; the quickstart uses both. To run the tests, see testing.

docs.title: Optional setup
docs.text:
Only follow these when your chosen task needs them:

  • Studio web UI.
  • Camera rendering.
  • Strategy development tools.
  • LIBERO and LeRobot policies.
  • A subset of the repositories.

For example videos or figures, run uv sync --group demo from the workspace root. To build the docs, use uv sync --group docs. The default dev group contains the test tools.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Run your first experiment. Setup is complete when hylo plugins lists the two plugins above.

docs.title: Optional environments
docs.text: Set up only the components needed by your next task. Complete Installation first. Run commands from the workspace root, unless a step changes directory.

docs.title: Studio web UI
docs.text:
Studio's web UI must be built once before hylo playground can show it. Without the build, Studio answers only "frontend not built". The build needs Node.js 18 or later:

cd studio/web && npm install --ignore-scripts && npm run build && cd ../..

docs.title: Camera rendering
docs.text:
MuJoCo comes with bench and needs nothing else for experiments. Camera rendering, used by the table-reach vision variant and by figures, needs an OpenGL backend. On a machine with a GPU, set MUJOCO_GL=egl.

Without a GPU, install CPU-only OpenGL (OSMesa). The script assumes Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64 and installs into ~/.local/mesa without root:

bench/scripts/install-osmesa-user.sh

Then set:

export MUJOCO_GL=osmesa
export PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/.local/mesa/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu

docs.title: Program tools
docs.text:
The workspace discovers hylo-manip, hylo-code-agents and hylo-tools alongside the other packages. Reference programs need the robot assets and camera rendering above, but no chat model. Assets are cached on first use. Model-written programs and research sessions additionally need a supported chat backend, such as Ollama or an API configured in the model specification. A local model must already be available at that endpoint.

Heavy perception and motion tools use uv worker environments: their first call can install separate dependencies and download weights. Some primary backends require model access or registered body-model files; the tools expose fallbacks and record the backend actually used. See Programs and the environment variables.

robosuite and RoboCasa have their own setup scripts under bench/envs/robosuite and bench/envs/robocasa. They are optional; the existing CPU quickstart does not require those runtimes or a language model.

docs.title: LIBERO and LeRobot
docs.text:
LIBERO and LeRobot need package versions that conflict with the workspace, so they run in their own venv inside bench, through two named runtimes.

  1. Install OSMesa as in camera rendering. LIBERO renders with it.

  2. Build the LIBERO venv:

    bench/envs/libero/setup.sh

    The script builds bench/envs/libero/.venv (Python 3.12, CPU) with LIBERO and lerobot[smolvla]. It downloads the LIBERO assets (lerobot/libero-assets, research use only) and writes a non-interactive LIBERO config.

  3. Check the two runtimes the script registered:

    uv run hylo profile show
    Runtime What runs there Environment libero-sim the LIBERO simulator (env.remote: {runtime: libero-sim}) OSMesa variables, LIBERO_CONFIG_PATH, thread limits lerobot LeRobot policies (agent: {type: remote, params: {runtime: lerobot}}) HF_HOME=bench/envs/hf-home, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

  4. Download model weights. The lerobot runtime runs offline and loads weights only from bench/envs/hf-home. setup.sh downloads none. Put each checkpoint into that cache once. SmolVLA for LIBERO also needs its vision-language backbone, HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct:

    cd bench
HF_HOME=envs/hf-home envs/libero/.venv/bin/python -c "from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download; \
    [snapshot_download(r) for r in ('lerobot/smolvla_libero', 'HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct')]"

    Weight licences differ from the code's; the plugin catalogue lists them.

docs.title: Partial workspace
docs.text:
The workspace covers whichever repositories are present; tests that need a missing one skip.

Checkout What you can run harness contracts, the episode loop, learners and campaigns, on the testing.* test plugins harness + bench MuJoCo and LIBERO experiments, protocols, scorecards, leaderboards, the examples harness + serve policy servers and workcells harness + studio Studio (building its web UI needs Node.js 18 or later) harness + plugins the example plugins, written the way a third party would

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Run a controller on MuJoCo planar reach and inspect its results. A two-link arm moves its fingertip to a target. This CPU example checks that execution and recording work before you try a model or a robot skill.

Complete Installation, then run the commands from bench/:

cd bench

docs.title: 1. Run
docs.text:
An experiment config names a benchmark and its split, an environment and an agent:

bench/examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
schema_version: hylo.experiment/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach
benchmark: {type: mujoco/reach-v0, split: validation}
env: {type: mujoco.planar_reach}
agent: {type: baseline.planar_ik, params: {kp: 0.3}}
output_dir: runs

uv run hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_reach.yaml

Each episode is printed as it ends ([20] mujoco/planar_reach_random seed=10009 success (32 steps)), then the run's metrics:

{
  "run_dir": "runs/mujoco-reach-validation-2342f91d706e83e9-eaf39f",
  "config_digest": "2342f91d706e83e9",
  "success_mean": 1.0,
  "safety_interventions_mean": 0.0,
  "steps_mean": 35.25,
  "n_episodes": 20,
  "n_scored": 20
}

The run directory contains the results and traces. Its random suffix will differ on your machine.

docs.title: 2. Inspect
docs.text:
Use the run_dir printed above to read a run. Its last six characters are random, so yours differs (what a run contains):

uv run hylo trace <run_dir>                  # the metrics, then every episode id
uv run hylo trace <run_dir> <episode_id>     # one episode, for example mujoco.planar_reach_fixed-s10000-2749d014

For one episode, hylo trace counts the events and prints the episode's end record. The trace holds every action the agent proposed (agent.chunk), what the safety shield decided (safety.review) and what was executed (action):

Counter({'observation': 31, 'agent.chunk': 30, 'safety.review': 30, 'action': 30, 'step.result': 30,
         'privileged.state': 30, 'episode.start': 1, 'episode.end': 1})
{
  "status": "success",
  "success": true,
  "steps": 30,
  "termination_reason": "terminated",
  "safety_interventions": 0
}

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: A completed run contains 20 scored episodes. In the recorded reference run all 20 succeed, with no safety interventions and an average of 35.25 steps. hylo trace lets you inspect what was proposed and executed. See Experiments for the files and event types.

The evaluation, campaign, serving and Studio steps are in First improvement.

docs.title: Module Dependency Graph
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/dependency-graph.md.

The runtime core remains independent of simulators and models. Strategy development adds robot tools and program agents above that core; environments remain in bench and heavy model tools run in their own worker environments. dev/test_boundaries.py enforces installed package dependencies and cross-repository imports.

docs.title: 1. Package dependencies
docs.text:
flowchart BT
  eval[hylo-eval] --> core[hylo-core]
  agents[hylo-agents] --> core
  memory[hylo-memory] --> core
  manip[hylo-manip · MuJoCo kinematics] --> core
  tools[hylo-tools · model workers] -. optional integration .-> manip
  llm[hylo-reasoner-llm] --> core
  learn[hylo-learn] --> core & eval
  evolve[hylo-evolve] --> core & eval & learn
  code[hylo-code-agents] --> core & agents & manip & tools & llm & memory & evolve & eval
  envs[bench environment adapters] --> core
  studio[Studio] --> core & eval
  serve[Serve] --> core

Selected relationships are shown; dev/test_boundaries.py contains the complete allowed dependency table. hylo-tools declares manipulation integration as an optional dependency. hylo-manip deliberately uses MuJoCo for its current kinematics/collision backend even when the environment is remote; the core contracts do not.

Dependency rules

  1. hylo-core imports no other Hylo package. Robot and scene descriptions are simulator-independent data.
  2. The harness imports no leaf repository. Bench, serve, studio and plugins never import one another.
  3. Decision-making, memory, measurement and development remain separate packages; optional components load only when requested. The robot-side serve packages declare only core by default.
  4. MuJoCo imports are allowed in hylo-manip, the MuJoCo environment adapter, hylo-tools and code-agent workflows as listed by the boundary lint. Torch and conflicting model dependencies stay in policy/tool worker environments.
  5. Cross-repository runtime contracts live in core. Studio reads producer-owned research JSON/JSONL records without importing their producer; changes to these records must preserve tolerant readers.

docs.title: 2. Runtime process topology
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph main[Main process - Hylo venv]
    RUN[EvaluationRunner] --> K[Kernel]
    K --> AG[Agent<br/>Reasoner/Policy/Memory]
    K --> SH[SafetyShield]
    K --> TR[(Trace)]
  end
  subgraph envp[Env process - benchmark-specific venv/container]
    ES[EnvServer] --> SIM[LIBERO / RoboCasa / ManiSkill]
  end
  subgraph polp[Policy process - model-specific venv/container, GPU]
    PS[openpi / LeRobot / vla-eval model server]
  end
  subgraph llm[External API]
    LLM[LLM/VLM endpoint]
  end
  SH -- JSON lines / WS --> ES
  AG -- openpi WS msgpack --> PS
  AG -- HTTPS --> LLM

In Served mode the topology is inverted: the vla-eval benchmark container owns the loop, and our process acts as the model server:

flowchart LR
  BC[vla-eval benchmark container<br/>Orchestrator owns the loop] -- OBSERVATION --> ADP[hylo-bridge-vlaeval<br/>ModelServer adapter]
  ADP --> AG[Agent] --> SH[SafetyShield] --> ADP
  ADP -- ACTION --> BC
  ADP --> TR[(Trace)]

docs.title: 3. Summary of how external projects are depended on
docs.text: External project Method Target package MuJoCo PyPI dependency hylo-env-mujoco LIBERO / RoboCasa / ManiSkill PyPI/source dependency in a separate venv hylo-env-* (server side) vla-evaluation-harness Protocol-compatible + run its containers hylo-bridge-vlaeval openpi Protocol-compatible (no import) hylo-policy-openpi SimpleMemVLA Optional frozen model runtime and independent video-memory option hylo-policy-simplememvla, hylo-memory LeRobot Optional dependency + data format export hylo-policy-lerobot, hylo-eval (exporter) inspect-robots Port code (MIT, with attribution) hylo-core (safety/compat parts) RPent Port the tool layer (Apache-2.0, with attribution) hylo-agents (tools) Zetta Borrow schema design, rewrite hylo-evolve LangGraph / DSPy Optional dependency hylo-reasoner-langgraph / hylo-evolve-dspy Spark-DSG / mem0 / Graphiti Optional dependency hylo-memory-*

docs.title: 1. Hierarchy
docs.text:
Experiment ──▶ Evaluation Run (benchmark × split) ──▶ Episode (TaskInstance) ──▶ Step
   │                    │                                  │                       │
 config digest      run_id, manifest                 episode_id, seed          seq, sim_time

docs.title: 2. Driven mode (default): the Kernel owns the loop
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant R as EvaluationRunner
  participant K as Kernel (EpisodeRunner)
  participant A as Agent
  participant X as ChunkExecutor
  participant S as SafetyShield
  participant E as Environment
  participant T as Trace (via EventBus)

  R->>K: run(TaskInstance)
  Note over K: compat check already done at bind time (failure = IncompatibleComponents, run does not start)
  K->>T: episode.start {task digest, seed, split, agent components, guards}
  K->>E: reset(task)
  E-->>K: Observation (includes actual instruction)
  K->>T: observation
  K->>A: reset(EpisodeContext{emit, seed, env_spec})
  loop until terminated / truncated / max_steps
    alt executor is empty
      K->>A: act(obs)
      A-->>T: agent.decision / memory.retrieval (via ctx.emit)
      A-->>K: ActionChunk
      K->>K: measure latency, exceeds act_timeout_s → AgentTimeout
      K->>X: load(chunk)
      K->>T: agent.chunk
    end
    K->>X: next()
    K->>S: review(action)
    S-->>K: approved (+ modified/reasons) or SafetyAbort
    K->>T: safety.review, action
    opt modified
      K->>X: clear() — plan is invalidated, replan at next step
    end
    K->>E: step(approved)
    E-->>K: StepResult(obs, reward, terminated, truncated, success, info)
    K->>T: step.result, observation, privileged.state (Trace only)
    K->>A: on_step(result)
  end
  K->>T: episode.end {status, success, steps, reason, safety_interventions}
  K->>A: on_episode_end(outcome)
  A-->>T: memory.write (via ctx.emit)

docs.title: 2.1 Status and errors
docs.text: Situation episode status Scored? Prototype behavior Task judged successful success 1 ✓ Steps exhausted or truncated failure 0 ✓ Agent raises an exception / times out error Abstain ✓ Env reset/step exception infra_invalid Abstain ✓ Simulation divergence (MuJoCo BADQPOS/QVEL/QACC) infra_invalid Abstain ✓ Guard rejection (NaN, rotation out of bounds, any modification in real-robot mode) safety_abort 0 + safety event ✓ Incompatible at bind time run does not start — ✓

docs.title: 2.2 Chunk execution
docs.text:
ActionChunk(actions[T], execution_steps): after executing execution_steps steps, act is called again. If SafetyShield modifies any action → the queue is cleared to force a replan (the plan has diverged from reality).

Timing (RFC-0005, part of what an experiment measures) selects how policy time relates to robot time, in the one loop that evaluation and deployment share: - sync (default): the above; the world waits for every act. - realtime: a chunk is requested when at most refill_steps actions remain (earlier when recent latency needs it); a chunk computed at step s and merged at step t has its first t - s actions dropped; an empty queue executes a hold action; a watchdog aborts after max_hold_steps holds. Clock virtual (deterministic: latency measured or fixed by latency_s, the steps it covers run before the merge) or wall (the policy in a worker thread, the loop paced at the control rate). The workcell (hylo-serve) runs this mode; a benchmark protocol can score it (libero-10-heldout-realtime). Temporal ensembling is an agent (temporal_ensemble), not a loop variant.

docs.title: 2.3 Clock and timeouts
docs.text:
• act latency is measured after the fact; exceeding act_timeout_s yields AgentTimeout (soft timeout).
  • v0.2: hard timeouts for remote policies are guaranteed by client deadlines; hard timeouts for in-process policies require thread/subprocess isolation.
  • Real robot: when EnvCapabilities.self_paced=True, the Environment is responsible for wall-clock pacing and the Kernel does not sleep; the Reasoner must be asynchronous (see §4).

docs.title: 3. Served mode: an external harness owns the loop
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as vla-eval Benchmark container
  participant V as hylo-bridge-vlaeval (ModelServer)
  participant A as Agent
  participant S as SafetyShield
  participant T as Trace
  B->>V: EPISODE_START {task}
  V->>A: reset(ctx)
  V->>T: episode.start (mode=served)
  loop
    B->>V: OBSERVATION
    V->>T: observation
    V->>A: act(obs)
    A-->>V: ActionChunk
    V->>S: review(each action)
    V->>T: agent.chunk, safety.review, action
    V-->>B: ACTION
  end
  B->>V: EPISODE_END {success}
  V->>T: step.result(final), episode.end

Differences: no per-step step.result information (only the final success), no privileged state, no snapshot. Therefore Served mode runs cannot be used for shadow replay, nor as the sole evidence for the RSI validation split. The EvalLog records mode=served.

docs.title: 4. Dual-rate Agent (v0.2 design)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant K as Kernel (control rate, e.g. 20 Hz)
  participant P as Policy
  participant Q as Reasoner (async, 0.1–2 Hz)
  K->>P: act(obs) every chunk
  K-->>Q: trigger(event) [episode_start, subgoal_reached, failure_signal, periodic]
  Q-->>P: update subgoal / instruction (atomic swap)
  Note over P: Policy always uses the most recently committed subgoal; the Reasoner does not block the control loop

The prototype implements a synchronous version (the Reasoner is triggered and executed inside act), which is sufficient to validate the interface and Trace semantics.

docs.title: 5. Passive observers and online critics
docs.text: Non-critical Event Bus subscribers (real-time visualization, online critics) are detached on failure without affecting the episode [Validated in prototype]. Online critics (Zetta-style TemporalCritic) are implemented in v0.3 as Agent components, not Kernel components: what they output is a "suggested recovery", and the final action still passes through SafetyShield.

docs.title: Experiment configuration
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/experiment-schema.md.

Fields of hylo.core.config.ExperimentConfig, using schema hylo.experiment/v0.1. For a complete workflow, see Run experiments. The Configuration API documents the Python models; Data formats & schemas provides the generated JSON Schema.

docs.title: Fields
Component placement
docs.text: env.remote accepts runtime, python and env. A named runtime resolves through the machine's execution profile; explicit python and env values override that runtime. A remote agent carries placement settings in its params.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text: timing controls how policy time relates to environment time. See experiment timing for execution semantics and Timing for every field and default.

docs.title: Digest and run manifest
docs.text:
config_digest is the first 16 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the canonical JSON produced by ExperimentConfig.measured(). The measured configuration follows these rules:

  • Exclude output_dir and workers.
  • Normalize env.remote to null, so environment placement does not change the digest.
  • Remove runtime, python and env from the params of components whose type is remote, recursively.
  • Omit timing only when it equals the complete default Timing model; non-default timing is measured.
  • Retain other configuration fields, including name, seed and tags.

docs.title: Reproducibility levels
docs.text: A matching digest identifies the measured configuration. It does not establish identical code, model weights, assets or results. Use Validation for measured reproducibility evidence.

docs.title: Run Manifest (<run>/manifest.json)
docs.text: The run manifest records run_id, configuration and trace schema versions, the measured configuration and digest, creation time, Git SHA, Python/platform information and selected package versions. Store references add pinned artifact records. Callers may add further manifest fields.

docs.title: Seeds
docs.text: The benchmark supplies each episode's task and seed. Split definitions belong to the benchmark; do not infer held-out seeds from the experiment-level seed. See evaluation protocols for the fixed conditions used to compare agents.

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text: cfg.with_overrides({"agent.params.kp": 2.0}) applies dotted-path values and validates a new ExperimentConfig. Its digest changes when the measured configuration changes. Use Run experiments for command-line overrides.

docs.title: Output layout
docs.text:
runs/<run_id>/
├── manifest.json
├── evallog.json
├── episodes/<episode_id>.jsonl
└── blobs/

manifest.json records configuration and runtime provenance. evallog.json records the benchmark, agent, aggregate results and episode samples. Episode traces reference array data in blobs/. See Runs and traces for inspection and replay.

docs.title: Extending Hylo
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/extending.md.

Everything that varies between methods is a plugin: a class that satisfies a small contract, registered under a name through a Python entry point (or referenced as module:attr). A plugin package never modifies Hylo. The examples below live in the plugins repository (hylo-plugins: packages/hylo-plugin-examples, module hylo_examples), written the way a third party would; run them from that repository (they use MuJoCo planar reach from hylo-bench).

docs.title: 1. Start a plugin
docs.text:
hylo plugin new learner my-recap          # also: policy, agent, guard, gate_test, online_learner, datasource, judge, generator
uv pip install -e plugins/hylo-plugin-my-recap
uv run pytest plugins/hylo-plugin-my-recap/tests          # the template passes its conformance check as generated
hylo plugin check learner my-recap                        # same check from the CLI, on any registered plugin
hylo plugins                                               # every plugin: contract version, maturity, licence

Environments and agents are checked with hylo conformance CONFIG [--agent].

Each plugin group is a versioned contract (hylo.policy/v0.1, ...; hylo.core.plugins.CONTRACTS). A plugin package declares what it implements in one dictionary, registered under the hylo.meta entry-point group (the template generates it):

META = {"contracts": {"learners": "hylo.learner/v0.1"}, "maturity": "unverified",
        "plugins": {"learners/my-recap": {"weights": "...", "notes": "..."}}}     # per-plugin overrides, optional

Maturity is implemented (run end to end on its target, with recorded runs), unverified, or needs-hardware; weights names the licence of model weights the plugin needs, the code licence is license in pyproject.toml. The registry refuses a plugin that declares another major version, or a newer minor version, than the core implements; hylo plugin check warns when a declaration is missing.

simulators, robots hylo conformance policies ChunkPolicy: spec / reset / default_execution_steps / sample(obs, seeds, noise_scale) -> (N, T, A) (core/policy.py) policy.knn, policy.bc, policy.flow,
