search, on-policy RL, iterative self-training) hylo plugin check online_learner instruments SuccessJudge.judge(trace), ValueModel, WorldModel (core/instrument.py) judge.trace, judge.vlm measuring and labelling hylo plugin check judge, then hylo calibrate datasources DataSource.episodes() -> ExternalEpisode with origin, licence (core/learning.py, core/datasource.py) lerobot.dataset, video.frames, video.files demonstrations, videos, other robots hylo plugin check datasource generators propose(diagnosis, cfg, parent_id, archive) -> [(Candidate, hypothesis)] (evolve/protocol.py) rule.*, llm.steering, experience, learn how candidates are proposed hylo plugin check generator gate_tests GateTest.compare(candidate, parent) -> PairedComparison, metric (eval/stats.py) mcnemar, sign, paired_permutation, examples.min_effect the statistic the gate decides with hylo plugin check gate_test guards review(action, ctx) -> GuardVerdict, name (core/safety.py) delta_limit, workspace, norm_limit, keep_out, examples.slow_zone safety rules hylo plugin check guard memory MemoryStore, ActionMemory (core/memory.py, core/experience.py) action_bank, skill_library, lesson_book, sqlite experience stores conformance kit check_memory_store scorers, benchmarks Scorer (core/scoring.py), a factory returning a Benchmark (core/benchmark.py) success, steps, mujoco/reach-v0, libero metrics, task sets – reasoners, choosers, planners, reflectors Reasoner, Chooser, Planner, Reflector (core/reasoning.py) testing.rule_landmark, chooser.llm, planner.llm, llm.reflector deliberation, object choice, subgoal planning, lessons from campaigns – surfaces a factory returning a Surface of ToolDefs (core/tooling.py) mujoco.world tools for models, people and coding agents: anything callable through hylo world chat, hylo mcp, the Studio and hylo roles Surface.call checks every call against its schema

docs.title: 3. What a plugin gets for free, and what it cannot change
docs.text:
For free: - store ids: configs reference artifacts as artifact:<name>@<digest>, resolved to this machine's path when your plugin is built (hylo store, hylo.core.store); your plugin receives a path as before; - the split guard: learners read development data only. Gate and held-out runs are refused at build time and again at the gate. - sealing and provenance; - running in any venv (launch); - resumable jobs; - the gate (cascade, sequential looks, Holm, regression and safety vetoes, held-out report); - traces, replay, A/B comparison; - the playground.

By design, a plugin cannot change: - the protected configuration scopes (safety, benchmark, trace, scoring); - the mandatory safety guards (finite check first, bounds clamp last); - the rule that only the gate activates a behaviour artifact, and that instruments are trusted only after calibration.

Candidates are configuration patches and can reference sealed program artifacts. Program agents and research sessions execute model-generated code with AST validation and a restricted Python namespace in the host process. These restrictions do not provide operating-system isolation. Campaign approval controls promotion after candidate evaluation; see program execution boundaries.

docs.title: 4. Worked examples (all runnable)
docs.text: Example Files Run A guard plugin that slows the robot inside a zone hylo_examples/guards.py, examples/configs/mujoco_guarded.yaml hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_guarded.yaml A gate on steps instead of success; a practical-significance gate hylo_examples/stats.py, examples/evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_steps_gate.yaml An online learner (cross-entropy method) as a candidate generator hylo_examples/online.py, examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_online_cem.yaml A policy written from scratch, and a mixture of registered policies, steered hylo_examples/policies.py, examples/configs/mujoco_mixture.yaml hylo run examples/configs/mujoco_mixture.yaml One reference policy per family, trained and scored on MuJoCo reach (bench) examples/policies/ in hylo-bench uv run python examples/policies/compare.py An offline learner, a judge, a data source, a generator, a policy, an agent hylo plugin new <group> <name> templates uv run pytest <package>/tests

docs.title: 5. Policies: one contract, many families
docs.text:
An agent is what the kernel runs; a policy (policies group) is the model inside it. Any policy plugin runs with {type: policy, params: {policy: SPEC}}, ACT-style with temporal_ensemble, or steered (seeded noise, sample-and-select, recovery rules) with {type: steered, params: {sampler: SPEC}}, and the reference policies of hylo-policies cover one example of each family (examples/policies/):

Family Published methods Here Retrieval VINN policy.knn Regression BC with action chunks BC, BC-RNN, ACT's chunking policy.bc; ACT's temporal ensembling is the temporal_ensemble agent Diffusion / flow matching Diffusion Policy, pi0, SmolVLA, GR00T's action head policy.flow (flow matching); the LeRobot ones via lerobot Tokenized actions RT-1, OpenVLA, VQ-BeT, pi0-FAST policy.tokens (binned, independent heads) Model-based planning MPC, PETS, TD-MPC policy.mpc over a world_model.state artifact Large VLAs pi0 / pi0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.5, OpenVLA lerobot (any LeRobot policy by repo id), openpi (an openpi server), or a new policy plugin

docs.title: 6. Mapping published methods onto the extension points
docs.text: Method Plugins V-GPS, RoboMonkey (re-rank sampled actions) a learner for the value model, plus an agent that samples and selects Retrieve-then-Steer, DSRL (offline) a learner that builds a bank, plus a prior / noise steering agent Expert iteration, BC, RECAP (offline) a data source and labeler if needed, plus a learner producing weights SimpleVLA-RL / GRPO, DSRL (online), RECAP (iterative) an online learner: policies() returns the current policy, update() takes a step from the rollouts' traces GEPA, Eureka (prompt / reward search) a generator: prompts and reward weights are configuration values RoboArena-style pairwise evaluation a gate test on a preference metric FAIL-Detect / SAFE an instrument for the detector; a guard to act on it A new robot or simulator an environment (or a LeRobot Robot, through lerobot.robot) A new policy family (GR00T, OpenVLA, ...) an agent adapter, or serving it behind the openpi protocol

docs.title: 1. Design sources
docs.text: Source Borrowed Discarded inspect-robots registry.py importlib.metadata entry points; auto-loading can be disabled via an environment variable — vla-eval module:Class references written directly in YAML, lazy import No entry points, no capability declarations RPent / XPolicyLab — Directory name as plugin (no version, no metadata)

docs.title: 2. Plugin groups
docs.text:
Every contract is defined in hylo-core (module in brackets), so a plugin of any group depends on hylo-core alone.

Group (entry point group) Contract (hylo-core module) Examples hylo.envs Environment (core.env) testing.point_reach, mujoco.planar_reach, libero hylo.agents Agent or a factory returning one (core.agent) testing.p_controller, policy, steered, lerobot.steered hylo.policies ChunkPolicy (core.policy) policy.flow, policy.bc, lerobot hylo.reasoners Reasoner (core.reasoning) testing.rule_landmark hylo.choosers Chooser (core.reasoning) chooser.rule_color, chooser.llm, chooser.vlm hylo.planners Planner (core.reasoning) planner.identity, planner.llm hylo.reflectors Reflector (core.reasoning) llm.reflector hylo.memory MemoryStore / ActionMemory (core.memory, core.experience) sqlite, action_bank, lesson_book hylo.scorers Scorer (core.scoring) success, steps, safety_interventions hylo.gate_tests GateTest (core.scoring) mcnemar, sign, paired_permutation hylo.benchmarks a factory returning a Benchmark (core.benchmark) testing/reach-v0, mujoco/reach-v0, libero hylo.generators Proposer (core.improvement) rule.gain, rule.steering, llm.steering, learn hylo.learners Learner / OnlineLearner (core.learning) critic.chunk_value, policy.flow hylo.instruments SuccessJudge / ValueModel / WorldModel (core.instrument) judge.trace, judge.vlm hylo.datasources DataSource (core.learning) video.frames, lerobot.dataset hylo.guards Guard (core.safety) delta_limit, keep_out hylo.surfaces a factory returning a tool Surface (core.tooling) mujoco.world

docs.title: 3. Resolution rules
docs.text:
registry.resolve(group, "testing.point_reach")              # 1. explicitly or lazily registered name
registry.resolve(group, "my_lab.envs.kitchen:KitchenEnv") # 2. if it contains ":", import as module:attr
# 3. on a name miss, load Hylo.<group> entry points (only once; HYLO_NO_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 disables)
registry.build(group, {"type": "...", "params": {...}})   # factory call
  • Lazy: builtin.py registers string references with register_lazy, so import Hylo does not import MuJoCo [Validated in prototype].
  • Diagnosable errors: an error for an unknown name lists the known plugins [Validated in prototype].

docs.title: 4. Plugin metadata
docs.text:
A distribution declares metadata through a hylo.meta entry point pointing to a lightweight META dictionary. The registry exposes each plugin as PluginMeta (hylo.core.plugins), including its contract version, maturity, licence and weights information. For example, the declaration can contain:

META = {
    "contracts": {"policies": "hylo.policy/v0.1"},
    "maturity": "unverified",
    "plugins": {"policies/my_policy": {"weights": "per checkpoint"}},
}

The registry refuses an incompatible declared contract version. Undeclared plugins can still load; hylo plugin check warns about the missing declaration. hylo plugins lists installed metadata without loading heavy plugin implementations. The code licence comes from the distribution's package metadata.

docs.title: 5. Isolation levels
docs.text:
Level When to use Mechanism in_process Pure Python, dependencies compatible with the main environment Direct import subprocess Dependency conflicts, but a separate venv can be created on the same machine RemoteEnvironment(ref, python=<other venv>) [Validated in prototype] container System-level dependencies (EGL/Vulkan/CUDA/Isaac) or untrusted code Same protocol, via docker exec / network endpoint

The protocol layer forbids pickle; array encoding/decoding only allows bool/int/uint/float dtypes [Validated in prototype].

docs.title: 6. Conformance Kit
docs.text:
Each plugin group provides a set of conformance tests (conformance/) that third-party adapters must pass:

  • Environment: spec() does not trigger simulation construction; two resets with the same seed yield the same obs; success vs terminated semantics; simulation error → truncated + info.sim_error; if snapshot is declared, stepping after restore is consistent step by step.
  • Agent/Policy: spec() matches the actual output dimensions; no cross-episode residual state after reset (except declared memory); ActionChunk shape.
  • MemoryStore: deduplication, key invalidation, as_of, radius queries, forget soft delete.
  • Scorer: depends only on the Trace (can run without env/agent).

The corresponding test cases in the prototype's tests/ are the embryo of the conformance kit.

docs.title: 7. Tool surfaces
docs.text: A surface (hylo.surfaces, contract hylo.tools/v0.1 in core.tooling) is a set of tools a model or a person can call: each ToolDef has a name, a kind (read, act or end), a structured description and a closed JSON Schema for its arguments. Surface.call checks the arguments, runs the tool and returns either a result or a structured ToolError (code, message, field, whether a retry can help). Surface.digest() identifies the declarations a run used. Surfaces are served unchanged by hylo world chat (a chat model), hylo mcp (coding agents over MCP), the Studio's World page and hylo roles.

docs.title: Interface: Agent / Policy / World Model
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/agent.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Packages: hylo-core (Agent protocol) + hylo-agents [Validated in prototype]

docs.title: 1. Agent (the only intelligence abstraction the Kernel knows about)
docs.text:
class AgentSpec(Contract):
    name: str; version: str
    required_state: tuple[str, ...]; required_cameras: tuple[str, ...]
    action_semantics: ActionSemantics | None
    action_dim: int | None
    components: Mapping[str, str]          # {"policy": "openpi.pi05@<ckpt>", "reasoner": "...", "memory": "..."} → written to the Trace
    weights_license: str | None            # required for learned policies

@dataclass
class EpisodeContext:
    episode_id: str; task: TaskInstance; env_spec: EnvSpec; seed: int
    emit: Callable[[str, Mapping[str, Any]], None]   # writes to the Trace (source="agent")

class Agent(Protocol):
    def spec(self) -> AgentSpec: ...
    def reset(self, ctx: EpisodeContext) -> None: ...
    def act(self, observation: Observation) -> ActionChunk: ...
    def on_step(self, result: StepResult) -> None: ...
    def on_episode_end(self, outcome: EpisodeOutcome) -> None: ...

Constraints - The Agent never gets the SafetyShield, an Environment handle, or privileged state. - After reset, no state from the previous episode may remain, unless it is an explicitly declared Memory (conformance test item). - Bind-time compatibility check: a mismatch in control_mode / rotation_repr / dimension / required keys = error (not a warning) [Validated in prototype].

docs.title: 2. ActionChunk and ChunkExecutor
docs.text:
class ActionChunk(Contract):
    actions: np.ndarray            # (T, *action_shape)
    execution_steps: int | None    # replan after executing this many steps (LeRobot ChunkPolicySpec: prediction ≠ execution)
    provenance: Mapping[str, Any]  # model id, checkpoint, latency, reference to raw/unnormalized output

ChunkExecutor (inside the Kernel) handles queuing and replanning; swappable strategies in v0.2: OpenLoop (default), TemporalEnsemble, RealTimeChunking, AsyncPrefetch. This unifies openpi's ActionChunkBroker, LeRobot's select_action queue, and vla-eval's ensemble in one place.

docs.title: 3. Policy (fast system)
docs.text:
class PolicySpec(Contract):
    name: str; version: str
    input_features: Mapping[str, FeatureSpec]     # LeRobot FeatureSpec semantics (type, shape, names, semantics)
    action_semantics: ActionSemantics
    prediction_steps: int; execution_steps: int
    control_hz: float | None
    weights_license: str

class Policy(Protocol):
    def spec(self) -> PolicySpec: ...
    def reset(self, ctx: EpisodeContext) -> None: ...          # must also reset the pre/post processors (LeRobot lesson)
    def act(self, obs: Observation, instruction: str | None) -> ActionChunk: ...
    def invalidate(self) -> None: ...                           # instruction changed mid-episode: drop the action queue, keep memory (LeRobot drop_queued_actions)
Implementation Approach v0.1 PControllerAgent, PlanarIKAgent, PGoalPolicy in-process baselines ✅ prototype OpenPIRemotePolicy openpi WS wire protocol (msgpack-numpy, metadata in first frame); obs key mapping and image preprocessing configured on the client P1 LeRobotPolicyAdapter make_policy + processors; chunk_inference_spec() → PolicySpec; policies without chunk support degrade to StepwisePolicyAdapter P2 VlaEvalModelServerPolicy connects to vla-eval's 17 model servers P2

docs.title: 4. ComposableAgent (reference composition)
docs.text:
class ComposableAgent(Agent):
    def __init__(self, policy: GoalPolicy | Policy, reasoner: Reasoner, memory: MemoryStore | None,
                 triggers: ReasoningTriggers, world_model: WorldModel | None = None): ...
  • The Reasoner is trigger-driven (episode_start, perception_change, subgoal_reached, periodic; v0.2 adds failure_signal, low_confidence) [Validated in prototype].
  • Emits agent.decision when the Decision changes; Memory retrieval emits memory.retrieval [Validated in prototype].
  • Prototype result (testing/reach-v0 validation, 100 episodes): composite Agent with memory success 1.00; best pure baseline 0.62 (cannot complete the briefly-visible and landmark tasks).

docs.title: 5. World Model (interface in v0.2, implementation in v0.3)
docs.text:
class WorldModel(Protocol):
    def spec(self) -> WorldModelSpec: ...           # observation/action spaces, prediction horizon, whether latent
    def encode(self, obs: Observation) -> Latent: ...
    def predict(self, latent: Latent, actions: np.ndarray) -> Prediction: ...   # predicted observation/latent + uncertainty
    def reward(self, latent: Latent, task: TaskSpec) -> float | None: ...        # optional

class WorldModelEnvironment(Environment):           # wraps a World Model as an Environment
    """Runs episodes "in imagination" with the same Kernel, same Agent and same Scorer: used for planner candidate evaluation,
    cheap pre-screening of RSI candidates (cannot replace the validation gate), and sim-vs-model consistency studies."""

This is one of the differentiators between Hylo and existing projects: the world model is treated as a first-class evaluable object, not as a private implementation detail of the planner.

docs.title: Interface: Benchmark / Task / Scorer
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/benchmark.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Packages: hylo-core (TaskSpec) + hylo-eval [Validated in prototype]

docs.title: 1. Task
docs.text:
InitSpec = SeedInit | InitStateRef(uri, count) | SnapshotInit(uri)

class Predicate(Contract):
    kind: Literal["builtin", "expr", "callable"]   # builtin name | declarative expression (BDDL goal) | "pkg.mod:Class.method"
    name: str = ""; expr: str | None = None; ref: str | None = None

class TaskSpec(Contract):
    id: str; version: str
    instruction: str                     # static text or template; the actual text is produced by env.reset
    init: InitSpec
    success: Predicate
    max_steps: int
    params: Mapping[str, Any]            # task parameters passed to the Environment
    tags: tuple[str, ...]
    def digest(self) -> str

class TaskInstance(Contract):
    spec: TaskSpec; seed: int; episode_index: int; split: str
    @property
    def key(self) -> str                 # "{id}#{seed}": primary key for paired comparison across versions

LIBERO mapping: InitStateRef("libero://libero_10/<task>.pruned_init", 50), Predicate("expr", expr=<BDDL :goal>). RoboCasa mapping: SeedInit or SnapshotInit, Predicate("callable", ref="robocasa...:<Task>._check_success"), instruction is a template.

docs.title: 2. Benchmark
docs.text:
class Benchmark(Contract):
    id: str; version: str
    tasks: tuple[TaskSpec, ...]
    splits: Mapping[str, tuple[int, ...]]     # train / validation / heldout → seeds; reusing seeds across splits is forbidden at construction
    requires_privileged: bool = False          # whether scoring depends on privileged information (written to EvalLog)
    metadata: Mapping[str, str]
    def instances(self, split: str) -> list[TaskInstance]
    def digest(self) -> str

v0.2 adds: the TaskProvider protocol (dynamic/procedurally generated tasks, e.g. RoboCasa layout sampling), episodes_per_task, per-task max_steps overrides, and upstream commit and asset hashes for external benchmarks.

docs.title: 3. Scorer / Grader
docs.text:
class Score(Contract):
    value: float | None              # None = abstain (infra failure, agent error); excluded from the mean
    explanation: str = ""
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any] = {}

class Scorer(Protocol):
    name: str
    def score(self, trace: EpisodeTrace, task: TaskInstance) -> Score   # reads the Trace only

class Grader(Protocol):              # v0.2: captures external judgments (human, VLM, simulation oracle), written as grade events in the Trace
    name: str
    def grade(self, trace: EpisodeTrace, task: TaskInstance) -> GradeEvent

Built-in Scorers: success, safety_interventions, steps [Validated in prototype]. v0.2: success_once, success_at_end (ManiSkill semantics), latency_p95, vlm_judge (Grader).

Scorer and Grader are separate (from inspect-robots): a Grader may have side effects (calling a VLM, asking an operator) and writes its judgment as an event; a Scorer is always a pure function, so historical Traces can be re-scored at any time.

docs.title: 4. EvaluationRunner and EvalLog
docs.text:
def evaluate(benchmark, split, *, env_factory, agent, run_root, safety, scorers, manifest) -> EvalResult

EvalLog (hylo.evallog/v0.1):

{
  "version": "hylo.evallog/v0.1", "run_id": "...",
  "benchmark": {"id", "version", "digest", "split", "requires_privileged"},
  "agent": {"name", "version", "components"},
  "results": {"success_mean": 1.0, "safety_interventions_mean": 0.03, "steps_mean": 38.3, "n_episodes": 100, "n_scored": 100},
  "samples": [{"key": "testing/reach_fixed#10000", "task_id", "seed", "episode_id", "status", "scores": {...}, "trace": "episodes/<id>.jsonl"}]
}

v0.2: the top-level structure aligns with the inspect-robots EvalLog (eval/results/stats/samples) so that its view tool can be reused; sharding/resume adopts vla-eval's SQLite work queue pattern.

docs.title: 5. Statistical comparison
docs.text:
def paired_compare(candidate: Mapping[key, float|None], parent: Mapping[key, float|None]) -> PairedComparison
#   drops pairs where either side abstained; returns n_pairs, candidate_wins, parent_wins, one-sided exact McNemar p

One-sided exact McNemar (the same test as Zetta gating.py) [Validated in prototype: 5:0 → p=1/32].

docs.title: Interface: Environment
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/environment.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Packages: hylo-core (protocol) + hylo-env-* (implementations) [Validated in prototype]

docs.title: 1. Protocol
docs.text:
class Environment(Protocol):
    def spec(self) -> EnvSpec: ...                       # must be cheap and side-effect free
    def reset(self, task: TaskInstance) -> Observation: ...
    def step(self, action: Action) -> StepResult: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

# Optional capabilities: declared in EnvSpec.capabilities, with the corresponding protocol implemented
class Snapshottable(Protocol):
    def snapshot(self) -> bytes: ...
    def restore(self, blob: bytes) -> None: ...

class PrivilegedStateSource(Protocol):
    def privileged_state(self) -> dict[str, Any]: ...   # goes into the Trace only; the Kernel never passes it to the Agent

class Renderable(Protocol):                              # v0.2
    def render(self, camera: str, *, width: int, height: int) -> np.ndarray: ...

class BatchedEnvironment(Protocol):                      # v0.3: ManiSkill GPU / Isaac Lab / mujoco.batch
    def reset_batch(self, tasks: Sequence[TaskInstance], env_ids: np.ndarray | None = None) -> BatchedObservation: ...
    def step_batch(self, actions: np.ndarray) -> BatchedStepResult: ...

docs.title: 2. Data types
docs.text:
class EnvSpec(Contract):
    name: str; version: str
    observation: ObservationSpec        # state: {key: shape}, cameras: {name: (H,W,C)}, units, has_instruction
    action: BoxSpace                    # shape, low, high, semantics: ActionSemantics
    control_hz: float
    capabilities: EnvCapabilities       # seedable, snapshot, render, privileged_state, batch_size, self_paced, real_robot

class ActionSemantics(Contract):
    control_mode: Literal["joint_pos","joint_delta","joint_vel","eef_delta_pos","eef_delta_pose","eef_abs_pose","planar_vel"]
    frame: str = "base"
    rotation_repr: str | None = None    # axis_angle | quat_xyzw | rot6d
    gripper: str | None = None          # binary_close_positive | continuous_open01 ... (vocabulary follows vla-eval DimSpec.format)
    dim_labels: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    max_step: tuple[float | None, ...] | None = None

class Observation(Contract):
    state: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]     # canonical keys and units (aligned with LeRobot / inspect-robots CANONICAL_STATE_UNITS)
    images: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]    # HWC uint8, orientation already corrected (the LIBERO/RoboCasa [::-1] is done inside the adapter)
    instruction: str | None             # the instruction actually produced by the Environment (RoboCasa generates it dynamically per episode)
    time: float
    extra: Mapping[str, Any]

class StepResult(Contract):
    observation: Observation
    reward: float | None
    terminated: bool                    # episode ended naturally (success or unrecoverable failure)
    truncated: bool                     # external truncation (time limit, simulation error)
    success: bool | None                # Task predicate result, independent of terminated
    info: Mapping[str, Any]             # conventional keys: distance, sim_error, fail_reason

docs.title: 3. Semantic constraints (conformance test items)
docs.text:
1. spec() does not build the simulation (ManiSkill doing a real reset in its constructor to derive the obs space is a counter-example).
  2. Two reset calls on the same TaskInstance (same seed) produce the same initial observation (when seedable=True).
  3. success is decided by the Task; terminated/truncated only describe the lifecycle. The adapter is responsible for mapping upstream semantics:
Upstream Upstream semantics Mapping LIBERO done = success success=done, terminated=done, truncated=steps>=max RoboCasa _check_success(), never terminates success=_check_success(), terminated=success (configurable), truncated=steps>=horizon ManiSkill terminated = success \| fail success=info.success, terminated=success or fail, info.fail_reason MuJoCo (our own Task) none we implement it; divergence → truncated=True, info.sim_error
  1. Numerical simulation errors must be surfaced as truncated + info.sim_error, never silently (MuJoCo silently resets MjData on divergence). The prototype handles BADQPOS/BADQVEL/BADQACC [Validated in prototype].
  2. When snapshot=True is declared, the subsequent trajectory after restore(snapshot()) is bit-identical [Validated in prototype: MuJoCo].
  3. Action arrays are interpreted according to BoxSpace.semantics.dim_labels; composite actions (RoboCasa 12-D) must be mapped by named components; relying on flat ordering is forbidden.

docs.title: 4. Remote environments (EnvServer protocol hylo.envserver/v0.1)
docs.text:
• Transport: JSON lines over subprocess stdin/stdout (v0.1); v0.2 adds a WebSocket transport to support containers.
  • Handshake: the server first sends {"hello": "hylo.envserver/v0.1"}; a version mismatch raises EnvironmentFault.
  • Request: {"id", "method": spec|reset|step|privileged_state|close, "args"}; response: {"id", "ok", "result"|"error", "traceback"}.
  • Encoding: contracts are pydantic models, so the wire format is model_dump(mode="json") / model_validate; ndarray → {"__nd__", dtype, shape, b64}, only b/i/u/f dtypes allowed; no pickle.
  • Remote and in-process execution of the same episode produce step-by-step identical results [Validated in prototype].

docs.title: 5. Adapter inventory
docs.text: Adapter Runs in v0.1 Notes testing.point_reach in-process ✅ prototype 5 task types: reach/push perturbation/briefly visible/landmark mujoco.planar_reach in-process ✅ prototype own MJCF + Task; snapshot; divergence detection libero.* EnvServer (py3.8 venv) P1 BDDL → Predicate(kind="expr"); init states → InitStateRef vlaeval.* Served mode P1 see execution-lifecycle §3 robocasa.*, maniskill.* EnvServer P2 isaaclab.* container + Batched P3

docs.title: Interface: Improvement (Evolution Layer)
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/improvement.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Package: hylo-evolve [Validated in prototype] Based on: our research notes

docs.title: 1. Closed loop and split discipline
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Execute: parent = registry.active
  Execute --> Diagnose: search split traces
  Diagnose --> Generate
  Generate --> StaticCheck
  StaticCheck --> Rejected: protected scope / schema
  StaticCheck --> Selection: search_val cascade
  Selection --> Rejected: candidate not selected
  Selection --> Validate: independent gate
  Validate --> Rejected: gate failed
  Validate --> HeldOut: gate passed (best)
  HeldOut --> Approval: report only, not used for selection
  Approval --> Promoted: approved
  Approval --> Archived: declined
  Promoted --> RolledBack: rollback()
  Rejected --> Archived: retain evidence
Split Purpose Data boundary search diagnosis and candidate development deployment observation requirements depend on the configured tools and diagnosis search_val candidate screening and selection separate from search cases gate confirmatory paired test separate from candidate development and selection heldout report only not used for candidate selection

This is the current run_cycle campaign protocol. The older improvement_cycle prototype uses train/validation/heldout; its example results below should not be read as the current four-split protocol. Proposers receive the archive and must control what reaches a model; the interface itself does not isolate arbitrary plugins from historical evaluation fields.

docs.title: 2. Data types and protocols
docs.text:
class Candidate(Contract):
    patch: Mapping[str, Any]          # v0.1: dotted-path config patch, e.g. {"agent.params.kp": 2.0}
    rationale: str
    parent_id: str | None             # must equal registry.active at promotion time (prevents stale candidates)
    generator: str                    # "name@version"
    kind: str = "config_patch"        # enabled: config_patch or code; other enum values remain disabled
    evidence: Mapping[str, Any]       # diagnostic references (bucket, episode ids)
    id: str
    def digest(self) -> str

class Proposer(Protocol):                                             # the `generators` contract (core.improvement)
    name: str
    def propose(self, diagnosis: Mapping[str, Any], cfg: ExperimentConfig, parent_id: str | None,
                archive: list[ArchiveEntry]) -> list[tuple[Candidate, str]]    # (candidate, hypothesis)

def diagnose(result: EvalResult) -> FailureReport                     # deterministic bucketing; v0.2 layers on LLM multi-hypothesis diagnosis
def check_protected_scope(c: Candidate) -> None                       # violation → ProtectedScopeViolation
def run_cycle(base_cfg, registry, archive, proposer, evaluate, diagnose, *, protocol, approve) -> CycleReport
                                                                      # campaigns: cascade + sequential gate (RFC-0002)
def improvement_cycle(base_cfg, registry, proposer, evaluate, *, approve) -> CycleReport
                                                                      # one cycle on train / validation / heldout splits

class CandidateRegistry:
    def register(c); def promote(id, *, gate, approved_by); def reject(id, *, gate)
    def rollback(*, reason, by) -> str | None
    def lineage() -> list[str]; def effective_patch() -> dict; def ledger() -> list[dict]
    active: str | None

docs.title: 3. Validation gate (Gate)
docs.text:
After selection, the current campaign checks:

  1. A paired gate test on matching episode keys. The default is one-sided exact McNemar on success, with alpha=0.05, Holm correction across selected candidates and optional alpha spending across configured gate looks. A custom gate_test can select another metric.
  2. Per-task success regression no greater than max_task_regression (default 0.15).
  3. Mean safety-intervention increase no greater than max_safety_increase (default 1.0).

The default success test requires evidence favoring the candidate; arbitrary gate plugins have their own comparison semantics. A general cross-benchmark regression suite and a latency_p95 promotion veto are not implemented by ProtocolConfig. The older prototype has different defaults. See hylo.evolve.protocol.ProtocolConfig for current options.

docs.title: 4. Protected scope (Protected Scope)
docs.text:
Config prefixes a candidate must not modify: safety, benchmark, trace, scorers, evolution, schema_version, env [Validated in prototype]. Reason: to prevent "raising the score by relaxing safety constraints or modifying the evaluation". In the prototype demo, an adversarial generator proposing safety.max_delta: 10.0 is rejected outright.

Current implementation boundaries:

  • The kind allowlist enables config_patch and code. Code candidates may change only the agent, cannot contain inline source and must reference a sealed program artifact.
  • Code agents use the configured restricted Python namespace and tool path. This is not a universal subprocess/container, read-only-filesystem or network-isolation guarantee for arbitrary proposer plugins. Observation permissions depend on the toolkit.
  • EvolveConfig.approval defaults to auto. Configure manual for reviewed deployment; a passing candidate then waits for explicit approval. The campaign does not independently detect hardware and force that setting.

docs.title: 5. Registry and Rollback
docs.text:
• Versions are immutable: versions/<id>.json (including digest, parent).
  • ACTIVE pointer; effective_patch() composes patches along the lineage from oldest to newest.
  • All operations are written to an append-only ledger.jsonl: register / promote / reject / rollback [Validated in prototype].
  • The online Agent only reads the active version and writes it into the Run Manifest at startup.

docs.title: 6. Prototype demo results (examples/rsi_demo.py)
docs.text:
Step Result Parent version (kp=0.5) train / validation success 0.033 / 0.083 Diagnosis {timeout_far: 13, timeout_near: 16} Adversarial candidate safety.max_delta=10 rejected (protected scope) Candidates kp=1 / 2 / 4 validation 0.767 / 1.000 / 1.000, all pass the gate kp=2 selected, held-out (report only) 1.000 vs parent 0.050, 57:0, p≈7e-18 promote → rollback effective patch {kp: 2.0} → {}; ledger records the rollback

Note: this demo validates the process and interfaces; gain tuning on the test double (and on MuJoCo reach) does not represent the real difficulty of RSI.

docs.title: 7. Phase-guided program evolution
docs.text:
The optional harness.program generator in hylo-code-agents independently implements a HarnessPAI-inspired strategy: propose an observable phase plan, repair an executable program on development cases, then seal the program together with evidence-linked repair notes. Completed program revisions are evaluated automatically within the submission budget; unchanged revisions and explicit submissions are not duplicated. It reuses the existing campaign gate and registry; solving development cases does not activate the candidate. No upstream HarnessPAI code is included.

PhaseRepairMemory retrieves notes only from active promoted program lineages. A note must cite failed and successful development replays of the same case, and its content is covered by the program artifact digest. Rollback removes the retired branch from recall. The containing program has gate evidence; transfer of an individual note remains unverified. Phase completion and handover logic are generated code, not a centrally interpreted phase graph. A frozen VLA can only be called through a toolkit that actually exposes one.

Implementation, configuration and verification details are maintained in adapters/hylo-code-agents/examples/harness_evolution/README.md.

docs.title: Interface: Memory
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/memory.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Memory backends and their consumers meet through contracts in hylo-core. Choose the contract that matches the information and lifetime you need; spatial records, ordered events, video history and reusable experience have different APIs. Use memory provides the user-facing entry points.

docs.title: Spatial and semantic records
docs.text:
MemoryItem holds typed content with optional identity, entities, scope, pose and time. MemoryKind includes working, episodic, semantic, spatial and skill; these are record labels, not interchangeable backend implementations. A skill-labelled memory item does not replace a skill-library record or its verification rules.

Type Important fields MemoryItem kind, content, key, payload, entities, scope, pose, event_time, valid_from, confidence, source, id Pose frame_id, three-dimensional position, optional quaternion orientation in xyzw order TimeSpan start, optional end, and clock (sim or wall) MemoryQuery kind/key/text/entity/scope filters, time_range, as_of, clock, near, include_invalidated, k Hit the item, score, scoring details and optional valid_to

Queries must use compatible frames and clock domains. See Spatial memory for invalidation, duplicate evidence and historical queries, and the core memory API for exact fields and defaults.

docs.title: Store protocol
docs.text:
class MemoryStore(Protocol):
    def write(self, items: Sequence[MemoryItem]) -> WriteResult: ...
    def query(self, q: MemoryQuery) -> list[Hit]: ...
    def forget(self, q: MemoryQuery) -> int: ...
    def snapshot(self) -> str: ...

write reports ADD, INVALIDATE or SKIP_DUP. forget expires matching records; it does not erase audit history. snapshot identifies the stored content. The SQLite backend implements this protocol. Callers scope observations to their episode and emit memory events so retrieval and writes can be inspected in the trace.

docs.title: Other memory interfaces
docs.text:
Component Interface and consumer Lifetime Bounded working store WorkingMemory.put/get/clear/items; a reasoner's scratchpad clear at episode boundaries Event memory EpisodeMemory.reset/append/recall/close; an observation extractor and an event-memory agent exact recall within a task/episode scope Video history SimpleMemVLAHistory; the compatible video-conditioned model runtime session-owned frames and caches, cleared at reset/end Action bank ActionMemory; a compatible policy's sampling/steering path sealed development artifact, frozen during evaluation Skill library SkillLibrary; the consumer for each skill kind versioned experience, frozen during evaluation Lesson book LessonBook; an experience-aware proposer curated development experience

Event memory requires an extractor: the journal does not infer facts from images. Video memory uses streaming frame history rather than MemoryStore. Its native model integration has separate checkpoint, embodiment and runtime requirements.

Skills have proposed, verified, refuted and deprecated states. Campaign-derived skills carry gate evidence; recipe skills carry model-free replay evidence. These checks establish different claims. Use the skill-library rules for the evidence and permitted consumers.

docs.title: Lifecycle and observability
docs.text:
• Reset or select an episode scope before recording observations. Do not expose another evaluation episode's history.
  • Emit memory.write and memory.retrieval events from the consuming integration where applicable.
  • Keep persistent action banks, skill libraries and lesson books frozen while evaluating an agent.
  • Episode-local spatial, event and video history can update from permitted observations during evaluation.
  • A content digest identifies stored evidence; it does not establish perception accuracy or a performance gain.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Use conformance and lifecycle checks for the interface, then compare complete agents under matching task and observation conditions. Memory results and video-memory integration checks describe their measured scope separately.

docs.title: Interface: Reasoner / Planner / Tools
docs.text:
Source

Maintained in hylo-harness: docs/interfaces/reasoner.md.

See the interface notes index for design context and links to current APIs. Versioned proposals and prototype results below retain their original scope.

Package: hylo-reasoners (rule-based, hylo.reasoners.rules); contract in hylo-core [Validated in prototype: synchronous, rule-based]

docs.title: 1. Role split
docs.text:
Role Frequency Input Output Examples Reasoner event-triggered (0.1–2 Hz) observation, working memory, long-term memory, trigger reason Decision VLM/LLM, rules, LangGraph graph, DSPy program Planner called by the Reasoner, or is the Reasoner goal, world state, skill library, World Model subgoal/skill sequence symbolic planning, MPC, LLM planning Policy every control step observation + current subgoal/instruction ActionChunk VLA, diffusion policy, controller

v0.1 treats the Planner as one implementation of a Reasoner (no separate protocol); once a planner appears that needs to be swapped independently (e.g. World Model-based MPC), v0.2 will split out a Planner protocol.

docs.title: 2. Protocol
docs.text:
class Decision(Contract):
    kind: str                         # "subgoal" | "instruction" | "skill" | "abort" | "ask_human"
    output: Any                       # pose, language instruction, SkillCall(name, args) ...
    rationale: str                    # human-readable rationale (LLM thinking summary; rule name)
    trigger: str
    component: str                    # "name@version", written to the Trace
    inputs: Mapping[str, Any] = {}    # references (observation seq, retrieval hit ids), for diagnostics

@dataclass
class ReasonerContext:
    task_id: str; episode_id: str
    working: WorkingMemory
    memory: MemoryStore | None
    emit: Callable[[str, Mapping[str, Any]], None]
    tools: Toolkit | None = None      # v0.2

class Reasoner(Protocol):
    name: str
    def begin(self, rctx: ReasonerContext) -> None: ...                       # episode start: retrieve long-term memory
    def deliberate(self, obs: Observation, trigger: str, rctx: ReasonerContext) -> Decision: ...
    def end(self, success: bool | None, rctx: ReasonerContext) -> None: ...   # episode end: write memory

v0.2 async variant: async def deliberate(...), run by ComposableAgent in a background task; the Policy uses the most recently committed Decision (see execution-lifecycle.md §4).

docs.title: 3. Tools (v0.2, port of RPent)
docs.text:
RPent's tool layer is currently the implementation best suited to "LLM invoking physical capabilities"; we plan to port it (Apache-2.0, with attribution):

@tool(readonly=True)
def locate(object_name: str) -> Pose: ...          # perception/memory query: can run in parallel
@tool(readonly=False)
def run_policy(instruction: str, max_steps: int) -> SkillResult: ...   # physical action: serial FIFO
  • Single source: the same decorator generates both the model-visible JSON schema and runtime validation.
  • Scheduling: read-only tools run in parallel, write tools run serially; cancellation waits for a safe point.
  • Key difference from RPent: every action produced by a tool still goes through the Kernel's SafetyShield; the LLM has no Bash/file-write permission; the tool allowlist is set by the experiment config and cannot be expanded by RSI candidates.
  • Success is decided by the Task, not by the LLM's own finish claim.

docs.title: 4. Adapters
docs.text: Adapter Description Version testing.rule_landmark prototype reference implementation: visible → go to goal; otherwise recall → go to recalled position (if reached but not visible, judge the memory stale and forget it); otherwise explore ✅ prototype llm.openai_compatible any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (including local vLLM); structured output → Decision; images via base64 v0.1 P1 llm.anthropic / other vendors official SDKs v0.2 langgraph.graph wraps a compiled StateGraph as a Reasoner; thread_id = episode_id; only references in state (no images); checkpointer used for planner-level replay v0.2 dspy.program loads DSPy-optimized JSON program state (loading .pkl is forbidden) v0.2

docs.title: 5. Observability requirements
docs.text: Each deliberate produces at least one agent.decision event (when the output changes), containing: kind, output, rationale, trigger, component; LLM adapters additionally record model, prompt_hash, tokens_in/out, latency_s, and (if enabled) store the full prompt/response in a blob. This is the basis for RSI to diagnose "reasoning error vs execution error".

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Look up a command, configuration field, tool, Python symbol or stored format. Start with a User Guide for a complete workflow.

You need Reference Command arguments and defaults CLI YAML fields, runtime settings or environment variables Configuration Stage fields, robot controls, goal checks or camera tools Worlds & tools Memory fields, retrieval settings and skill status Memory & skills Python classes, functions and plugin contracts Python API Versioned records and JSON Schemas Data formats & schemas Available plugin names, implementations and declared maturity Plugin catalogue

The Python API package index lists every package and its modules. Developer interface notes explain integration semantics; extension tutorials walk through an implementation. For runnable configurations, use the example catalogue.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Choose the configuration you are editing. Each reference lists its fields, defaults or lookup rules.

Configuration What it controls Experiment environment, agent, benchmark split, timing and recorded outputs Campaign candidate generation, evaluation gates, approval and cycle budgets Execution profile this machine's named Python runtimes and store location Environment variables paths, rendering, model caches and process settings Evaluation protocol the fixed conditions used to compare agents Workcell environment, policy endpoint, timing and recording on a robot computer

An experiment describes what is measured; an execution profile resolves where components run. A workcell's runtime block configures episode timing. It is distinct from a named runtime in an execution profile.

Use Run experiments or Deployment for setup steps. Data formats & schemas provides machine-readable contracts; Configuration API documents the Python objects.

docs.title: Memory reference
docs.text: Fields, queries and storage rules for memory backends and skill libraries. For setup and examples, start with Use memory.

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
Every fact is a memory item:

Field Meaning kind spatial, episodic, semantic, working or skill content a short text description key the identity of the thing described, for example <episode>:obj_0; a newer item with the same kind and key replaces it pose a position (and optional orientation) in a named frame, such as table event_time when it was observed: a start, an optional end, and the clock (sim or wall) payload structured data, for example {"rgb": [0.85, 0.1, 0.1]} entities, scope the entities it is about; the task, robot or episode it belongs to confidence, source how sure the writer was; which component wrote it

docs.title: Writes and invalidation
docs.text:
Time is kept twice: when the fact was true in the world, and when it was recorded. Writing an item has one of three effects, reported back to the writer and in the memory.write trace event:

  • ADD: a new fact.
  • INVALIDATE: an earlier fact with the same kind, key, exact scope and clock stops being valid from the new item's time. It is not deleted: a query "as of" an earlier time still finds it.
  • SKIP_DUP: the same typed evidence is already stored and valid. Scope, event time, pose orientation and provenance participate in its identity, so repeated-looking observations are not automatically duplicates.

forget marks matching items as expired (for example, a remembered location that turned out to be empty). Nothing is ever removed from the file. Forgetting applies all query filters, including scope, entity and exact spatial radius; k limits retrieval, not how many matching records expire. Backdated keyed replacements are rejected atomically. Append late evidence without a key instead of rewriting history.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Query field Effect kinds, key restrict to these kinds or this identity text items whose content contains the text entities, scope any of these entities; all of these scope values near within a radius of a pose (same frame); closer items score higher time_range observed during this interval as_of what was valid at that time, including facts that were invalidated later clock restrict to sim or wall; select it when interpreting numeric time filters include_invalidated also return replaced facts k at most this many hits (default 10)

Each hit has a score (confidence and, for spatial queries, closeness) and the time it stopped being valid, if it did.

How it is stored

One table, items, with an index on kind and key, one on frame and position, and one on content hash. Each row keeps both time axes:

Columns Holds t_start, t_end, t_clock when the fact was observed and its clock domain valid_from, valid_to when it was true; valid_to is set when a newer item with the same key arrives recorded_at, expired_at when it was written; when forget expired it frame_id, px, py, pz, orientation frame and pose; position supports the prefilter and exact radius check content_hash for duplicate detection

snapshot() uses the hylo.sqlite/v2 digest over all rows, including expired records, complete intervals and provenance. It is not comparable to the earlier snapshot algorithm. Opening a legacy store adds clock/orientation columns and rehashes its records; unknown historical orientations cannot be recovered.

docs.title: Retrieval settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning k 10 segments retrieved same_task true retrieve only from the same task sim_floor 0.9 minimum cosine similarity; calibrate it against the bank's build report temperature 0.05 softmax temperature over similarity when weighting segments dtw_mad 2.0 how far from the others a segment may be before it is dropped compare_steps the execution steps prefix length compared between segments t0_min, t0_max 0.1, 0.7 the range of start times; smaller is a stronger bias fixed_t0 none ignore confidence and always start here (for ablations) dispersion_scale 0.5 disagreement at which confidence roughly halves gripper_dim −1 the action dimension treated as the gripper

Configure action memory.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
The book is never rewritten as a whole. A reflector model proposes operations, and the book applies them by fixed rules:

Operation Effect ADD a new lesson; if an active lesson in the same scope has a near-identical title, it is upvoted instead UPVOTE, DOWNVOTE one more helpful or harmful count, with the episodes as evidence EDIT new content; the counts are kept RETIRE removed from retrieval, kept in the file

A lesson whose harmful count reaches its helpful count plus two retires itself. Invalid operations are reported, not applied. Every applied operation is appended to the log with its time and source.

What the reflector sends (the format) 
[{"op": "ADD", "scope": "global", "kind": "pitfall", "title": "Closing before the fingers surround the block",
  "content": "Failed episodes close the gripper above the block and lift nothing; successes descend until the block is between the fingers.",
  "evidence": ["<episode id>"]},
 {"op": "UPVOTE", "id": "L3f2a9c1d", "evidence": ["<episode id>"]}]
What the book logs (the format; ids are content hashes of scope and title) 
{"t": 1793560000.0, "source": "reflect:<run>", "op": "ADD", "id": "L5b07e2aa"}
{"t": 1793560000.0, "source": "reflect:<run>", "op": "UPVOTE", "id": "L3f2a9c1d"}
{"t": 1793563600.0, "source": "credit:cand-1c3f4ceacb", "op": "DOWNVOTE", "id": "L3f2a9c1d"}

A vote that retires a lesson carries "retired": true. The source keeps the book idempotent: a reflection or a credit already in the log is not applied again when a campaign resumes.

docs.title: A lesson
docs.text: Field Meaning kind strategy (what successful episodes did) or pitfall (a failure pattern to avoid) scope global, or task:<id> for one task title, content at most 12 words; at most 60 words helpful, harmful votes: from the reflector when new episodes confirm or contradict it, and from the outcomes of candidates that relied on it evidence the episodes it was drawn from or confirmed by (the last 20) status active or retired

docs.title: Skill kinds
docs.text:
Kind Body Applied by steering a partial steering configuration (samples, noise scale, execution steps, ...) the skills agent, merged into the steered agent it wraps recovery trigger rules for the steered agent (what to do when progress stalls) the skills agent, appended to the agent's rules plan subgoal templates with slots, such as pick up the {a} the skills agent, through a subgoal planner weights a configuration patch that points to other weights an improvement campaign, as a candidate configuration program a sealed solve(robot) program: path, digest and entry point code.llm, as skills.<name>(robot) recipe the tool calls that solved a world task, by surface role campaigns, offered when a goal fails for the same reasons

Every skill also has a name, a version, a description (what a language model reads first), a trigger, a status, usage verdicts and its evidence.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
A trigger says when a skill applies. All parts that are set must fit.

Part Fits when instruction_pattern a regular expression matches the whole normalised instruction; named groups become slots, for example put both the (?P<a>.+) and the (?P<b>.+) in the basket task_tags the task has all of these tags env the environment has this name reason_codes a goal check failed with all of these reason codes (NOT_LIFTED, DISTANCE_NOT_MET, ...)

Only verified skills match. When several fit, the most specific comes first (a pattern before tags before the environment alone), then the one with more useful than misleading verdicts. Program skills have no pattern; they are ranked by how close the instruction is to the skill's description and to the instructions it was developed on.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
New skills start as proposed. Only evidence moves them on, and no other transition is allowed:

Evidence Status a campaign promoted the candidate (it passed the gate) verified, with the gate's effect, p-value and pairs the gate failed with no gain, or the candidate was rejected early refuted the gate failed with a gain that was not significant, or the candidate was archived stays proposed, with its numbers attached (worth retesting with more episodes) a promoted program fails revalidation later deprecated a recipe's model-free replay achieves the goal verified

Refuted skills stay in the library, so a proposer can see what was tried and failed. Separately, each use can be marked useful, misleading or not_applicable; these verdicts accumulate per version and break ties.

docs.title: Worlds & tools
docs.text:
Stage fields, robot packs, controls and goal checks. Start with Create and run a world for a complete example. Worlds explains the concepts.

Look up Section Entity fields, revisions and storage Stages Supported robots and controls Robot packs Actions, receipts and generation checks Actions Goal predicates and failure reasons Goal checks Images, depth, segmentation and export Cameras and data Human entities and routes People

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
A stage is a list of entities, each with a pose and one kind of content:

Content Fields shape box, sphere, cylinder, capsule or plane, size (half extents for boxes), colour mesh an obj or stl file and a scale; collision geometry from collision body for shapes and meshes: dynamic: true makes it movable, mass or density, friction robot a pack name, base fixed or free, mount onto another entity's body, start joints camera field of view and image size; it looks along its own −z axis (look_at builds a pose) light, human a light; a walking person with a route, speed and height Two stored stage entities 
{"id": "panda", "parent": null, "pose": {"pos": [0.0, 0.0, 0.4], "quat": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]}, "locked": false,
 "robot": {"pack": "panda", "base": "fixed", "mount": null, "joints": {}}}
{"id": "cube", "parent": null, "pose": {"pos": [0.5, -0.15, 0.42], "quat": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]}, "locked": false,
 "shape": {"type": "box", "size": [0.02, 0.02, 0.02], "rgba": [0.85, 0.15, 0.12, 1.0]},
 "body": {"dynamic": true, "mass": 0.05, "density": 500.0, "friction": 1.0}}

Every change is a patch against the revision you read (add, remove, update, reparent). A patch written against an older revision is refused, so two editors cannot overwrite each other; a locked entity refuses changes. Every revision is kept and any one can be restored.

Where a stage lives on disk 
runs/stages/lab/
  current.json        the newest revision (schema hylo.stage/v0.1)
  history/            every revision: rev-00000.json, rev-00001.json, ...
  log.jsonl           one line per revision: {"revision": 1, "digest": "027d6619eba572c8", "author": "model", "entities": 8, ...}

uv run hylo stage new lab                       # in runs/stages (or $HYLO_STAGES)
uv run hylo stage patch lab patch.json          # {"expected_revision": 0, "ops": [{"op": "add", "entity": {...}}]}
uv run hylo stage history lab
uv run hylo stage restore lab 3

A shape or mesh without body: {dynamic: true} is fixed in place. Free-base robots (quadrupeds, humanoids, drones) take x, y and yaw from their pose and their height from the pack.

docs.title: Robot packs
docs.text:
Family Packs Actions Arms panda, ur5e, ur10e, iiwa14, xarm7, so101, vx300s, aloha joints, gripper, tool pose Gripper and hands robotiq_2f85 (mount it on an arm), leap, allegro, shadow gripper, joints Quadrupeds go2, go1, a1, spot joints, walk Humanoids g1, h1, t1; g1_legs, h1_legs with walking policies joints; policy Drones crazyflie, x2 fly Mobile manipulator tidybot base, joints, gripper, tool pose

Robot models come from MuJoCo Menagerie (and the two policy leg models from Unitree's training repository), fetched at a pinned commit on first use and checked file by file against recorded digests; nothing is vendored. The packs tool lists each pack's controls and status.

docs.title: Running a world
docs.text:
Build the newest revision with world_build; it reports the robots with their controls, the cameras, which entities are fixed in place, and any parts that overlap at the start. Then act:

Action What it does The receipt measures joints moves joints (or actuators) to targets over a duration the largest joint error gripper open, close, or a fraction opening, and holding when the fingers stop on something tcp moves an arm's tool point to a position (and orientation; by default it keeps the current one) joint error at the end walk a quadruped trot, forward speed and turn in −1..1 distance, turn, whether it stayed upright policy a pretrained walking policy with a velocity command distance, speed, turn, upright fly a drone to a position and heading distance from the target base a mobile base to x, y, yaw joint error hold keeps still (drones hover) —

Every action names the world generation it was decided on; after a rebuild or reset an old action is refused as stale. Actions for different robots in one call run in the same simulation steps. Time passes only during actions and advance. act and advance can record a video.

Pretrained policies are read from their files as tensors and run with numpy; nothing in a weights file is executed. Before running one, the world compares what the policy expects (robot, joints, drive, timestep) with the robot and refuses on any difference. policies lists them and reports such differences.

docs.title: Checking goals
docs.text:
check evaluates a goal on the world without stepping it. Atoms: in_box, near, apart, above, contact, no_contact, joint_range, settled, upright, lifted, reachable, no_penetration; combined with all, any and not.

{"op": "all", "terms": [{"op": "lifted", "entity": "cube", "min_z": 0.5},
                        {"op": "near", "a": "cube", "b": "arm", "max_m": 0.05}]}

A failed atom returns what was expected, what was measured and a reason code (NOT_LIFTED, DISTANCE_NOT_MET, CONTACT_MISSING, ...). From a chat session, where the cube had not been lifted high enough:

{"ok": true, "satisfied": false,
 "failures": [{"atom": {"op": "above", "a": "cube", "b": "table", "min_m": 0.09}, "reason": "NOT_ABOVE",
               "expected": "height difference >= 0.09", "measured": 0.075}],
 "reasons": ["NOT_ABOVE"], "step": 6950, "generation": 2}

The reasons list is the failure signature that recipe skills are keyed by. gate checks a goal before work starts: it refuses goals naming missing entities and flags goals that already hold.

docs.title: Cameras and data
docs.text:
• capture: images from camera entities, all from the same step, with depth and segmentation by entity kept for pixel_to_world (a pixel as a world point and the entity it shows).
  • view: a picture from any viewpoint, without a camera entity.
  • lidar: a grid of rays over a camera's field of view or a horizontal ring; hits per entity.
  • camera_fit: a camera's pose from six or more world points and the pixels they appear at.
  • export: frames over time while actions run: samples.jsonl (step, camera pose and world state per frame), RGB png, depth npy in metres, segmentation png, and a calibration file.

Three exported frames of a top camera while the Panda moves: RGB, depth (nearer is brighter) and segmentation by entity.

For meshes, hylo tool physicalize MESH writes collision geometry the stage can use: one box, the convex hull, convex parts or voxel boxes, chosen from the mesh's shape, with its mass from volume and density.

docs.title: People
docs.text: A human entity walks its route (looping or not, with a pause at each waypoint), plans around the footprints of everything else, and stops for anything in front of it. The people tool sends a person somewhere, stops them or lets them walk on.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: An agent decides what a robot does from its observations and task instruction. Hylo supports agents that run policies, execute programs or ask a language model to call robot tools. They share execution, safety checks and recorded traces, so each approach can be evaluated under explicit task and observation conditions.

docs.title: Choose an agent
docs.text:
You want to Start with Guide Run an existing model or controller a policy agent Policies Give a policy subgoals, memory or steering a composed or steered agent Policy agents Run a compatible frozen VLA with episode video history simplememvla Video memory Execute a hand-written or frozen task program code.program Programs Let a model write task code during an episode code.llm Programs Let a model call typed robot tools one step at a time tools.llm Tool-calling agents

A policy is a model or controller used by an agent. The agent decides how to use its output, including chunk execution, steering and planning. A research session is a development process that produces a program; the resulting program can then run through code.program without model calls.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
A policy maps observations to proposed actions, often as a chunk of future steps. The agent decides how much of that chunk to execute before observing again. It can also sample alternatives, use a critic, apply recovery rules or retrieve a memory prior when the policy supports those interfaces. Shorter chunks allow more frequent feedback; longer chunks reduce inference calls but commit to more actions before replanning.

A composed agent can separate slower reasoning from the control policy: a reasoner chooses a target or subgoal, while the policy produces the motion. Keeping these components inside the agent lets a direct action model and a planner-driven model use the same episode loop. A technique requiring flow sampling, video context or a critic still needs a compatible policy; composition does not supply missing model capabilities.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text: A program expresses task logic explicitly: perceive, choose a target, call robot tools, inspect the result and branch or retry. code.program runs an existing program; code.llm asks a model to write code during an episode. Developing and freezing a program moves model calls into development, so later execution can reuse the same logic without generating it again. Its behaviour still depends on new observations, tool results and the conditions covered by its tests. Code execution uses the restrictions described in Security.

docs.title: Tool calls
docs.text:
A tool-calling model alternates between observations and typed requests. Read tools can measure targets or compute grasp options without moving the robot. An action is submitted separately, executed through the episode kernel and safety checks, and answered with a measured receipt. The model sees the effect before choosing its next action.

Target and grasp handles are tied to the observation that produced them. After motion, stale handles are refused and the model must measure again. This prevents old coordinates from being treated as current facts. The task's own check determines success independently of what the model reports when it finishes.

docs.title: Execution and evidence
docs.text:
The episode kernel binds an agent to an environment, checks their action compatibility, obtains observations, asks the agent for actions and passes executed steps through the safety shield. Traces record proposed and executed actions, interventions and outcomes. Scorers read that record, allowing different agent types to be evaluated under the same protocol.

Observation privileges and timing remain part of the comparison. In synchronous execution the world waits for inference; in realtime execution it continues and stale actions can be dropped. Two agents are comparable only when the task, permitted observations, controller and evaluation conditions support the comparison. A shared execution path alone does not make different benchmark results interchangeable.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Agents act in an environment: a benchmark, a world or a robot adapter. The environment supplies observations and actions; task checks and evaluation establish the outcome.

Memory supplies observations and experience to the components that can use them. Skills provide reusable procedures or changes with stated applicability. Support depends on the agent and skill kind: a code agent can call program skills, while role campaigns offer recipes after matching goal failures. The skill library documents each consuming path.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
Record an experiment, inspect its traces and compare agents under a fixed evaluation protocol. Declare observation privileges and task conditions in the comparison. A campaign can propose and test changes to an existing agent as part of Physical RSI.

Program agents execute generated code with in-process restrictions; read the execution boundaries. Measured successes and current failures are recorded in the Validation records.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
A campaign improves an experiment's agent one tested change at a time. Each cycle asks a generator for candidate config changes and promotes at most one, only if a paired test against the current version (the parent) on init states not used for selection confirms it. Promotion is automatic by default. Set approval: manual for anything that will run on hardware.

One cycle. The promoted candidate is the next cycle's parent.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Commands on this page run from bench/. This is the quickstart's campaign:

examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml
schema_version: hylo.evolve/v0.1
name: mujoco-reach-gain
experiment: ../configs/mujoco_reach.yaml
experiment_overrides: {agent.params.kp: 0.02, workers: 16, benchmark.params: {protocol: rsi, gate_looks: 2}}
proposer: {type: rule.gain, params: {path: agent.params.kp, factors: [2.0, 4.0]}}
protocol: {alpha: 0.05, gate_looks: 2, stage1_pairs: 20}
cycles: 3
stop_after_no_progress: 1
approval: auto
out_dir: runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain
  • proposer: the generator.
  • protocol: the gate settings.
  • benchmark.params.protocol: rsi: the campaign's split scheme.
cd bench
uv run hylo evolve run examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml
uv run hylo evolve status examples/evolve/mujoco_reach_gain.yaml

The experiment path is resolved against the campaign file. out_dir is resolved against the working directory, so run every hylo evolve command for a campaign from bench/. That also keeps the campaign inside the store. If you ran the quickstart, status shows its result and run continues the same campaign from its state file, up to cycles. --set KEY=VALUE overrides a key of the campaign config.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
hylo evolve status prints the campaign state, the active version and its lineage, the combined patch, any pending approval, and the archive size. stopped says why the campaign ended: all cycles done, no promotion in N consecutive cycles, budget exhausted or waiting for manual approval.

runs/evolve/mujoco-reach-gain/
  evolve_config.json        the config as run
  campaign_state.json       cycles done, history with held-out results, why it stopped
  archive.jsonl             every candidate: patch, hypothesis, stages reached, verdict, evidence
  registry/                 the promotion ledger (ledger.jsonl) and the active candidate (ACTIVE)
  active.json               the active version as an agent spec, which deployment reads
  cycle-01/                 the cycle's runs and cycle_report.json
  pending_approval.json     only while a candidate waits for manual approval

Archive verdicts: rejected (stage 0 or 1), archived (not sent to the gate), gated_fail, gate_passed (confirmed, not promoted, for example while waiting for approval) and promoted. Ids and paths in the archive and ledger protect the runs and artifacts they name from deletion (store).

docs.title: Candidate evaluation
docs.text:
The parent runs on search, and its failures are sorted into buckets. The generator returns up to max_candidates config patches, each with a hypothesis. The cascade (stages 0 to 2) screens them, and the gate (stage 3) confirms the best against the parent:

Stage Runs on What happens 0 nothing yet stage-0 checks: reject patches that touch a protected section, are invalid or already archived, or reference (by store id, or by a path inside a sealed artifact) an artifact that was modified, built from gate or held-out runs, or (for behaviour artifacts) is of unknown provenance; a path to a directory without artifact.json is not checked; optional world-model pre-screen 1 the first stage1_pairs pairs of search_val reject when the parent leads by stage1_max_deficit wins or more 2 all of search_val keep candidates that win more pairs than they lose; the best gate_top_k go to the gate 3 gate, then gate_r1, ... paired test against the parent (McNemar by default), Holm-corrected across candidates, with sequential looks, futility stopping, and regression and safety vetoes report heldout the first candidate that passed and the parent, paired; recorded with used_for_selection: false

Then, with approval: auto, the candidate becomes the active version and the next cycle's parent. With approval: manual the campaign stops and waits. Candidates and parent share seeds and policy noise, so every comparison is paired.

Candidates may not change the protected settings. Timing and agent code are not protected.

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
A campaign needs four disjoint splits, which the rsi split scheme provides.

Split MuJoCo reach seeds LIBERO init states Used for search 30000–30039 0–19 diagnosis and learning search_val 30040–30059 20–29 selection (stages 1 and 2) gate 30060–30079 30–39 confirmation (stage 3) heldout 30080–30099 40–49 the report

LIBERO's boundaries are rsi_bounds (default [20, 30, 40]). On MuJoCo reach every seed runs on both tasks.

docs.title: Split access
docs.text:
Split Runs read by Results visible to search diagnosis; generators, through the diagnosis; learners generators search_val the cascade; learners; the learn generator, which trains on the cycle's search and search_val runs by default generators, through the archive gate, gate_r1, ... the gate generators, through the archive heldout the report only: the cascade and the gate never read it the approver, in pending_approval.json; generators, through the archive entries of promoted candidates

The gate reuses its init states every cycle, so after cycle 1 generators have seen gate results on them. The experience generator and lesson books use these results on purpose.

docs.title: Held-out sets
docs.text: Benchmark Held-out scored by the protocol Held-out a campaign reports on MuJoCo reach mujoco-reach: the standard heldout split, seeds 20000–20049 rsi heldout: seeds 30080–30099 LIBERO-10 libero-10-heldout: init states 40–49 rsi heldout: init states 40–49, the same states

docs.title: Gate looks
docs.text: With gate_looks: K the gate tests up to K times, stopping early once a candidate passes or no longer leads. Each further look runs a replicate of the gate split (gate_r1, ...). On LIBERO it reuses the gate init states with new policy noise. On MuJoCo reach it uses new seeds (gate_r1 is 30160–30179). Set the same value twice: benchmark.params.gate_looks makes the benchmark provide the replicates, and the gate_looks gate setting makes the gate use them.

docs.title: Generators
docs.text:
Generators are generators plugins:

Generator Proposes rule.gain scaled values of one numeric config path rule.steering steering rules (resample, back off) from failure buckets such as stalls and regrasps llm.steering steering patches from a local LLM that reads failure traces (hylo-proposer-llm, through Ollama) learn trains an artifact with a learner each cycle and patches the config to use it; {artifact} in the patch template becomes its store id when the artifact lands inside the store, else its path critic.chunk_value trains a chunk critic and proposes critic steering experience wraps another generator and gives it lessons and skills built from the archive selftrain.expert_iteration fine-tunes the policy on its own successful episodes

How far each is tested: plugin catalogue. To write your own, run hylo plugin new generator NAME and see adding a generator.

docs.title: Program candidates
docs.text:
Developing a first program and comparing a revision with a baseline have different evidence requirements. Use Program skills for development and independent evaluation; use a campaign to compare a proposed change with the current version and promote it through the gate.

The research.llm generator develops code on search cases, optionally starting from a code.program parent. It freezes a qualifying submission as a program artifact and proposes a code candidate. The same cascade, paired gate, held-out report and approval path apply. A program that succeeded during development has not yet passed these checks. Follow Program skills for the development and reuse steps.

For experimental phase-guided repair and note recall, see Program repair.

Proposer Changes Training rule.gain, rule.steering, llm.steering Runtime parameters or steering None experience Supplies lessons and skill evidence to an inner proposer Depends on the inner proposer research.llm Executable program None harness.program Phase-guided program and repair notes None critic.chunk_value Action-chunk ranking around a frozen policy Critic training learn, selftrain.expert_iteration Learner artifacts or policy checkpoint Explicit training path

Select one proposer through proposer.type; additional packages provide the model-based options. These choices do not automatically combine into one algorithm. See the campaign API for implementation details.

docs.title: Version control
docs.text:
In the Studio: each candidate's path through the cascade, a campaign whose candidates all failed the gate, a candidate approved by hand, the rollback form, and the parent and promoted version paired on held-out states.

uv run hylo evolve approve runs/evolve/my-campaign          # recorded with your user name
uv run hylo evolve run runs/evolve/my-campaign              # continue after approval
uv run hylo evolve rollback runs/evolve/my-campaign --reason "regression seen on the robot"
uv run hylo evolve shadow runs/evolve/my-campaign --candidate cand-9147236d7d
uv run hylo evolve status runs/evolve/my-campaign --publish  # also rewrite active.json

The target is the campaign config or the campaign directory.

  • With approval: manual, a candidate that passes the gate waits in pending_approval.json and the campaign stops. hylo evolve approve promotes it. Run hylo evolve run again to continue.
  • rollback restores the parent of the active version. The ledger records who did it and why (--reason).
  • shadow runs the active version with the candidate riding along: it sees every observation but never acts. The report says how often and how far it would have acted differently. Run it before trying a candidate on a robot. The candidate may change only agent.* keys.

docs.title: LIBERO campaigns
docs.text: examples/evolve/ has three campaigns on frozen SmolVLA in LIBERO-10: libero10_steering.yaml (rule-based steering), libero10_llm.yaml (an LLM proposes steering) and libero10_selftrain.yaml (expert iteration, manual approval). They need envs/libero/setup.sh. libero10_steering.yaml and libero10_llm.yaml set budget_s: 28800 (8 hours), libero10_selftrain.yaml 43200 (12 hours): no new cycle starts after that. It is a limit, not an estimate.
